  • Spenso’s threads and the package-scoped Symbolica key (fixed 2026-10-23). LoopSlice.generate of g g > g g g g deadlocked in the CT lowering (ct_line_insertions._line_factor → custom_propagator_components → TensorNetwork.execute, no CPU, every thread in a futex wait). Cause: pyAmpliCol’s library key unlocks Symbolica only for frames of the package (symbolica.set_library_key, has_library_unlock_frame); Spenso’s Rayon workers carry no such frame (Symbolica’s own pools carry the caller’s unlock with the crate-private InheritedLibraryUnlock), so the first LicenseManager::check of each worker asks has_library_unlock_frame, which waits for the GIL in Python::try_attach while the calling thread holds it and waits for the workers. It happens whenever Spenso parallelises a network before any license check has run on a Python thread, even with a valid personal key in SYMBOLICA_LICENSE (that key is only validated by the first such check; test processes always make one, so the suites never saw it). The same deadlock was the earlier “unexpanded clone numerator does not finish”. Fix (pyamplicol.licensing.ensure_spenso_thread_policy): once per process, before its first tensor network (called by the model-compilation Symbolica namespaces compiler_symbolica._ensure_symbolica and tensors._ensure_symbolica; the import itself checks no license, test_public_import_laziness; the built-in SM lowering builds only small networks, which Spenso’s workload heuristic keeps serial, and its sources are digested into the packaged built-in model, so it is left alone), the package asks is_licensed() on a thread without frames of the package (which also validates a personal key) and sets Spenso’s symbolic parallelism to serial without a thread-wide key. Tests: test_symbolica_thread_license.py (the probe’s frames; the import leaves Spenso alone and the first namespace sets it serial, in a subprocess without a personal key) and, end to end, test_six_gluon_generation_completes_without_a_personal_key (nightly: g g > g g g g on both routes without SYMBOLICA_LICENSE, asserting the serial policy; its script makes no Symbolica call outside the package, since without a key such a call takes the user’s one restricted Symbolica thread, which the native loop module’s own Symbolica then cannot start: an abort, a separate limitation of unlicensed use). Serial costs nothing measurable here (g g > g g g g generation 322 s serial against 341 s parallel). Upstream (prepared, not yet filed; workspace/reports/engine-v2/upstream/symbolica-library-unlock/): a reproducer whose only use of pyAmpliCol is the import that registers its key (repro_deadlock.py: a Dirac chain network executed in parallel from the package’s globals hangs, serial finishes; it also hangs with a personal key), the focused Symbolica fix f39c76f on 9cdc2949 (has_library_unlock_frame returns false without attaching on a thread without a Python thread state; branch fix/library-unlock-frame-no-attach in workspace/worktrees/symbolica-unlock-no-attach), verified on a rebuilt community wheel (builds/community-unlock-fix-python: no hang; with a personal key the parallel run completes, with the library key alone it aborts at once on Symbolica’s restricted-thread rule), and the issue text (ISSUE.txt) with the two follow-ups: public InheritedLibraryUnlock so that Spenso carries the caller’s unlock into its Rayon jobs, and Spenso’s Auto resolving to serial under a library unlock alone. Filing the issue and PR (draft) is left to the coordinator. pyAmpliCol’s serial policy stays until both land.

  • Production form: the closure (decision for WP3.1, 2026-10-23). The tree-route program (form 1: complete tree programs of the lowered model, Born × CT per squared order) cannot carry the multi-trace colour state. Its colour is that of the tree runtime’s sectors (ProcessLCSectorKind Singlet, OpenLines, SingleTrace in the Rust recurrence; single-trace and open-line words in the Python lanes) and of their full-colour contraction, so a CT amplitude with a closed trace next to its open word (the δδ part of the four-gluon R2; a d-symbol or identity vertex taking the U(1)-projected gluon of a quark line) has no sector to land in. In form 1 the four-gluon R2 and the g g g V R2 therefore stay residual (test_lowered_couplings_are_exact_model_expressions: the only reasons left are multi-trace colours), and every QCD request with four or more gluon lines (gg→gggg, gg→ggggg, uu~→ggggg, gg→tt̄gg, …) would be refused by a residual-free production rule. Lifting that needs new multi-trace sector kinds, their replay certificates and their colour overlaps in the recurrence’s full-colour contraction: a tree-engine feature (L), not a CT one. The closure (form 2) has no residual rule for loop_sm, is graded by N_c for LC/NLC, shares the Born’s root closure and kernels, and is the slice’s default. Form 2 is the production form; WP3.1 should build its CT program natively as loop-request blocks of the lowered model (the T2 strategy, with closed traces and closed lines in the colour state of the CT = 1 currents, BlockColourFlow.traces/lines and generation/dag_color.py being the reference) plus the native root closure of I4, and keep form 1 as a test of the lowering. Under REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM H the Python DAG can generate that program at seven legs on WP3.1’s T1 path (4 min at uu~→ggggg, 54 min and 55 GB peak at gg→ggggg for the program, its root-closure terms unmeasured, “Generation cost” above; the earlier “> 18.5 min and > 16 GB” of the WP3.1 plan §2.4(c) was a run killed at its 1,150 s bound), so T2 and the native colour port below are an optimisation of generation, not a precondition of residual-free counterterms at seven legs.

  • What a native builder of the CT program must carry (WP3.1 I5R/T2; coordinator decision D3, 2026-10-23). The CT program is an ordinary loop-request program of the lowered model, so no CT-specific vertex code is needed; a native builder must reproduce the items below, each defined by its Python reference. Oracles, in this order: the block set of ct_closure.CountertermBlocks.build (keys with field, orders, word, chirality and auxiliary kind, plus the colour state and Block.wick_sign) for gg→ggg, uu~→dd~gg, gg→uu~γg, uu~→γggg, gg→tt̄gg and the two-point synthetic model; then O6 against the site closure (test_loop_v2_ct_closure.py, test_loop_v2_ct_two_point.py, test_loop_v2_ct_cancellation.py).

    1. Program. Reachability: every leg set without leg 1, except the set of all legs but leg 1 (ct_closure.RootReachability): no root term reads it (a root attaches at least two currents; a two-point insertion next to leg 1 is on an external line). Leaving it out removes 80 % of the program’s interactions at gg→ggg (110.8 k → 21.7 k) and 18 % at uu~→ggggg (2.24 M interactions, 181 s, 4.0 GB, measured before). The sets of one leg fewer then feed no interaction, so the runtime schema gives them their propagated value anyway (propagated_currents, the hunk of WP3.1 I1a on work/v2-generation-scale, byte-identical; ct_closure.program_propagated_currents; the oracle tests/unit/loop_v2_stage_rows.stage_rows takes the same option). Order limits: CountertermRecursion.coupling_order_limits (physical orders bounded by the Born and loop orders, PYAMPLICOL_CT_INSERTION ≤ 2; slot orders unlisted, at most one per current, ct_closure._slot). The lowered model’s full-kernel variant (model_tree_kernel_variant). Couplings are derived model couplings; the rule multiplicities and slot switches are integer runtime parameters (CountertermRecursion.parameter_values). The non-vanishing assumptions under which CoefficientLowering resolved cond and reglog (CountertermModel.assumptions) are checked against the runtime parameters before an evaluation (CountertermModel.check_parameters): parameters that make one vanish (a mass set to zero, say) are refused, never evaluated. Status (ct-assume-fix, 2026-10-23): a helper argument free of model parameters (numbers, builtin constants and functions: loop_qcd_qed_sm’s reglog(2π), whose assumption 2*𝜋 check_parameters could not decide, so every recursion-route evaluation of that model failed) is decided when lowering (ct_recursion.decide_constant: numbers exactly, other constants numerically at 40 and 80 digits, undecidable ones refused) and is never an assumption; an assumption keeps only its parameter-dependent factors, the untaken branch of a cond is not resolved, and check_parameters decides every assumption the same way, refusing vanishing, singular and undecidable values (test_constant_factors_are_decided_not_assumed). Finite-only mode (REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM B) must skip every current and interaction that feeds only pole slots, not only zero their switches: a CT = 1 current carries at most one slot order, so the currents of the pole slots (UV_local ε⁻¹ and ε⁻²; 18 % of the interactions at gg→ggg for ε⁻¹) and everything that reaches only them are left out of a finite-only evaluation, by a per-slot reachability mask of the one program or by a finite-only program in the same artifact. The slot switches stay the API’s switch (the four-valued pole selection maps onto parameter_values(poles=has_poles(selection)), §12.4 “Counterterm slots”); the Python CT program (the per-point Python path) only zeroes them and skips the closure terms of the pole slots. Measured on that path (gg→ggg, recursion route, binary64, two CT-level points): 9.1 s with poles against 5.2 s finite-only; the program’s rows, pole-slot currents included, take 0.2 s of either (2 %; the ε⁻¹ currents are 17 % of the program’s interactions), the closure terms 4.1 s against 2.65 s, the coupling program 1 ms. Skipping the pole-slot currents is therefore worth it only natively. Owner: WP3.1 (open item of WP2.2). As built (generation-scale-2, I5 proper, TREE_SCHEMA 4): the counterterm program’s interaction program records its slot table and per-slot reachability masks, the record A5 emits natively (dag/program.rs, rule 3). counterterm_trees.slots lists per CT slot its pseudo-order, component, ε power and N_c grade (native_trees.counterterm_slots, CountertermRecursion.slots order); interactions.masks lists slot sets (masks[0] every slot, masks[1 + s] slot s alone, slot_mask_table) and each step’s accumulator_masks the set its result current reaches (slot_masks: a current with one insertion carries its slot’s order and reaches that slot only; a CT = 0 current feeds every slot; two slots on one current are refused). The native runtime derives the finite-only skip per slot set (loop_v2::trees::load_interactions: an interaction or output whose current reaches no slot of ε power 0 is skipped), exactly TREE_SCHEMA 3’s per-step pole lists: converting the new record back to those lists reproduces the stored seven-leg P-ct digests (u u~ > g g g g g 7aa25d0a…, g g > g g g g g 28213864…, both lanes; S1″ unchanged; new P-ct 36d23c48… and 276d98d5…). Reachability through the CT = 0 currents is every slot (they are shared by every insertion); a finer per-current reachability needs the root closure’s reads, which A6 brings natively. Measured saving (poles="none" against "all", B = 128, one thread on an idle core, frozen G1 streams, finite parts bitwise equal), stage-isolated (the evidence audit’s nine repetitions; the totals of three repetitions spread by ±3-5 % and are no measure of it): the native trees stage 122.7 → 102.4 ms/pt at g g > g g g g (32,720 of 240,120 CT interactions skipped) and 9.51 → 7.89 ms/pt at u u~ > g g g g (10,432 of 70,968), i.e. −5.0 % and −2.0 % of the total per point (total medians −4.9 % and −2.2 %); reduction and dressing do not change. The skipped set is the one TREE_SCHEMA 3’s per-step pole lists already skipped: I5 proper re-encodes the record, it adds no new skip.

    2. Colour state of a current (generation/dag_color.ColorState, rules in ColorEngine._loop_block_flows). It is the open word plus two sorted sets: closed traces (adjoint labels, rotated to the smallest; (t₁ … tₙ) is tr(τ^{t₁} … τ^{tₙ}), so a closing’s trace is its joined word read backwards) and closed lines (strings from a fundamental to an antifundamental label). A merge unites its inputs’ traces and lines. A colour-singlet input of a merge into an adjoint current or of a closing (_loop_block_absorbing_sides: the U(1)-subtraction auxiliary, an identity contact line, a boson of a quark pair) adds its complete strings as closed lines (_loop_block_split_singlet_strings). The identity alone is dropped, and the trace of one gluon current without a quark line vanishes. A colour-identity vertex closing two adjoint currents into a singlet turns the joined word into a closed trace, or into closed lines when it holds fundamental labels. Input orders (_loop_block_trace_orientation_allowed): a closing keeps the smaller first label on the left; so does a merge of two colour singlets into a colour singlet whose inputs both carry coloured labels (WWA, WWZ or HZZ joining the bosons of two quark lines, a four-point contact’s partial or final merge): both orders would concatenate the same complete strings into two words of one colour factor, which the loop seeds count as two blocks, each holding the vertex’s trees (lit-ew-blocks, F-A: example 2’s e^6 loop); with an input without coloured labels the singlet rule (_singlet_order_allowed) keeps one order, so every merge of a four-point colour-singlet contact keeps one and the contact enters a block current once per assignment of its legs, as in the Born (_singlet_contact_orientation_allowed); an absorbed singlet stands on the right; U(1)-projection singlets keep both orders, and a closing that takes the auxiliary keeps the pattern whose replaced input has the larger first label. The native builder (loop_v2::dag::colour::trace_orientation_allowed) applies the same rule on the same keys (both words’ coloured labels and the vertex).

    3. Colour rules of the lowered vertices (models/ct_color_flow.tree_colour_source): d-symbols (on three adjoint legs, alone or with one colour-singlet leg), d·d, d·f and f·f products over one summed index, and Identity·Identity on four adjoint legs. The U(N) contact split of d·d is d·d + (2/N)δδ, with the U(1) term subtracted in the coupling (_without_u1_terms). Contact splits trilinear-identity and identity-singlets (models/compiler_contacts.py). N_c-graded couplings (split_color_grades) and whole-rule continuation rows (whole_rule_rows).

    4. U(1) projection (models/compiler_color_flow.synthesize_u1_projections, vertices suffixed ::u1-projection). Absorption copies have colour weight −c. Production copies have −c and the exact 1/3 in the coupling. Identity contact lines are colour-singlet clones of the adjoint contact line, read by copies of the d-symbol final stages. Closings replace their right input only. The projection is all or nothing per model (ct_closure.u1_projected); otherwise a leaking request fails closed (UnprojectedU1Error).

    5. Signs (loops/v2/blocks._connection_parities). The connection parity counts only open-word endpoints, and no merge of a singlet into a non-fermion current. The auxiliary’s sign is the projection copies’ weight.

    6. Clone lines (models/ct_line_insertions.lower_line_insertions). Each (X, Y, orders of Π, slot) class has an oriented clone pair with the model-supplied propagator N_out Π N_in/(D_in D_out) (engine widths in D) and records with M = W = 0. The vertex copies carry half of Π’s orders and the insertion and slot orders once. A clone current’s block key carries the field it is read as (CountertermLoweredModel.line_fields; CountertermBlocks.clones). The Weyl factor κ sits on the copies of C̄ (line_factors) and is a closure scale at a ROOT_LINE. Dirac-forced Weyl fields (dirac_fields) have model-supplied standard propagators, so their sources, currents and clone lines are Dirac spinors; the root reads them through chirality-0 kernels.

    7. Root closure (CountertermClosure.build, the CT part of I4). The terms are ROOT_VERTEX; ROOT_LINE, with the other half of Π’s orders and κ; ROOT_COUNTERTERM, on the CT-root sites (CountertermClosure.root_sites: the partitions with leg 1 as one block, the rule’s fields on CT = 0 currents, the loop orders, multiplicity M_rule from CountertermRecursion.admission; Laurent powers per rule _powers); and whole-rule continuation terms (assemble._whole_rule_terms). Each term has an exact colour at any N_c grade. The lowered model’s cancelled cells are skipped (CountertermModel.unlowered). A request admitting an unlowerable rule whose vertex can enter one of its trees is refused (CountertermRecursion.residual, UnloweredCountertermError); inert rules (CountertermRecursion.inert) are not listed.

    8. Admission and veto (§6.2). admitted_alternatives(rule, particle_veto, corrections, species_orders) per rule (the model’s perturbative species facts, no loop routing); the vetoed particles are the tree engine’s ignored_particle_ids (both charge states, blocks.vetoed_particle_ids) of the program’s DAG and are excluded from the lowered model’s vertices.

    On the T1 path (the Python loop-request DAG lowered to the eager plan, WP3.1 §3.5) items 2–6 stay in Python generation: block colour states feed only the root closure’s exact colour tensors, and the native evaluation needs the kinematic recursion with each interaction’s scalar colour weight. The eager lane already evaluates the lowered model (custom clone propagators, derived couplings with runtime multiplicities and switches): the form-1 O6 tests run both lanes (test_recursion_equals_site_closure[*-eager]). T1 therefore carries form 2 without the native colour port, at the cost of the Python CT program (“Generation cost” above). Per point, the program costs about six times its CT = 0 part (gg→ggg: 21.7 k interactions, of which CT = 0 3.6 k, R2 10.7 k with its clone lines, UV_local ε⁰ and ε⁻¹ 3.7 k each; with the set of all legs but leg 1 it was 110.8 k). Its currents per slot are separate, so finite-only evaluation skips the currents that feed only pole slots (UV_local ε⁻¹: 17 % of the interactions at gg→ggg; item 1); a zero slot switch alone, as in the Python CT program, still computes them.

    Native builder (WP3.1 Rust migration A3, work/v2-native-dag; switched on in A4, below). loops/v2/dag_input.native_counterterm_blocks(recursion, process, ignored_particle_ids=...) is the twin of CountertermBlocks.build: the Rust loop-request builder (rusticol-core loop_v2::dag) over the CT-lowered model’s tables, with RootReachability, the program’s order limits and the vetoed particles (items 1 and 8), carries items 2-6 through the model tables and the loop-block colour engine (multi-trace states, U(1)-projection copies and closings, connection signs, clone-line blocks keyed by line_fields, Dirac-forced fields); the DAG scan of the U(1) leakage check runs natively (ct_closure._u1_leaking asks the NativeDag handle, NativeDag.u1_leaking). The CT program’s closed colour components make currents share evaluation contracts, so the builder carries the value-equivalence derivation of assign_recursive_current_evaluation_reuse in the oracle’s bit-exact binary64 arithmetic (loop_v2/dag/exact.rs: CPython’s math.fsum and complex division, exact rationals where Python uses Fraction; term vectors in Python’s key order). The inert rule stays a Python generation-side record (§6.2). Oracles (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_native_dag.py): the derivation value by value against _derive_current_value_equivalences on A0’s electroweak fixture, on copies scaled by complex, non-unit and inexact factors, and on guard copies in which each fail-closed guard of the oracle decides one class (the exactness proof of a projective factor, fsum, the round-trip check of the lookup key, the coefficient-by-coefficient scaling check; the class moves when the oracle drops that guard); the whole CT GenericDAG, its flat-record digest, blocks and clone lines equal on g g > g g g (default tier), on g g > u u~, u u~ > d d~ g(g), g g > u u~ γ g, u u~ > γ g g g, g g > t t~ g g, a top veto, u d~ > e+ ν g, e+ e- > e+ e- (no coloured leg: the engine’s colour-sector branch) and the two-point synthetic model (physics tier, the U(1) scan with the projection gate off), and at six legs (nightly; there a child without a Symbolica key also runs V2Dag.build, V2Dag.reuse on the scaled and guard copies, whose non-unit factors take the exact-rational path, and V2Dag.u1_leaking, equal to the oracle). Seven legs (stage-isolated S1″, tools/loop_v2_dag.py s1pp --blocks native): u u~ > g g g g g 248,938 currents and 2,105,180 interactions, S1″ 8eeca050… in both lanes, CT program 141 s (Python) against 5.4 s (native), process peaks 2.79 GB against 0.78 GB; g g > g g g g g 1,027,618 currents and 9,749,220 interactions, S1″ ae1a90e9…, CT program 631 s (Python) against 21.0 s (cold; 22.1 s warm), process peaks 12.0 GB against 2.99 GB, the Born included (records workspace/tmp/native-dag/oracle/a3/, native lane re-run on the immutable build loop-native-native-dag-79674311: the same digests and counts, 5.8 s and 21.8 s). Below six legs the native stage is slower than the Python one (rule 8, measured 2026-10-24): its Θ(model) input tables (dag_input.dag_input, _vertex_row) query every vertex and chirality triple of the lowered model, and CompiledUFOModel.allowed_quantum_flows runs a symbolic Weyl-projection check on each (_weyl_projection_is_nonzero, cached per model instance, which native_counterterm_blocks builds afresh), where the Python recursion pays it only on the vertices it reaches. u u~ > a a g: CT program 4.98 s native against 0.13 s Python (1,559 vertex rows; under cProfile 10.8 s of the native 11.4 s are the tables, 10.2 s of them the projection check); g g > g g g 2.7 s against 1.4 s (1.55 s against 1.45 s in an audit run); the gain starts at six legs (g g > g g g g 28.2 s against 2.5 s). Before the A4 switch the tables must be cached per lowered model, restricted to the request’s reachable species, or built in Rust. Done for the projection check (ct-perf third increment above): native_counterterm_blocks builds over CountertermLoweredModel.tree_model(), whose Weyl-projection support comes from the lowering cache; the tables take 0.06–0.07 s at six legs. The production call sites switch in A4, after G-int.

    Switch (WP3.1 Rust migration A4, work/v2-native-dag; dag_input.NATIVE_DAG = True). The one flag of the stage (RUST-MIGRATION rule 1) puts the native builder in production: the loop-block DAG of build_tree_blocks (dag_input.loop_request_blocks, the switch glue; one call line in build_tree_blocks) and the CT program of CountertermBlocks.build (dag_input.native_counterterm_blocks) are built in Rust, and so are their queries: the Ward-kernel and coloured-width scans (blocks.propagated_species, read by ward_breaking_fields and artifact.coloured_widths) and the DAG scan of the U(1) leakage check (ct_closure._u1_leaking, which keeps its model-level gates). With the flag off the tree engine’s loop-request mode runs; it stays the oracle. TreeBlocks.blocks_dag is then a dag_input.NativeDag handle standing in for the GenericDAG: it passes isinstance(dag, GenericDAG) (the per-point TreeRows’ StageCompilationInput), pickle and copy take the decoded DAG, and the first read of a GenericDAG attribute decodes it once (decode_count, rule 9), after which the decoded fields are the handle’s own attributes (the consumers read dag.currents in their loops). Once generation’s queries are answered (blocks, propagated species, U(1) leakage; kept on the handle) the native columns are released; a later read rebuilds them from the kept input tables (deterministic, rebuild_count), so generation does not hold them to its end. The decode shares equal values as the compiled DAG does (couplings, colour weights and factors by bit pattern, ids, label tuples, words): the decoded CT DAG of u u~ > g g g g retains 48 MB against 74 MB for the tree engine’s. The Θ(model) input tables cover only the species the recursion can reach (a fixed point from the legs over the usable vertices within the order limits), and the model-only part of each vertex row (the Weyl-projection probe of allowed_quantum_flows, colour weight, kernel equivalence, coupling identities) is kept per compiled model and runtime parameters: u u~ > d d~ g loop-block tables 0.62 → 0.036 s; the CT program’s tables 0.03 s at six legs. A request with a feature the builder lists as not covered (dag_input.NATIVE_FALLBACKS: eleven NativeFallback records, each with its key, owner and follow-up; NativeDagUnsupported.feature is the key, the Rust builder’s four refusals included: a NaN colour weight, more than 64 source states, two vertex rows sharing a kind, a leg label above 64) takes the tree engine with a warning, TreeBlocks.dag_fallback names it ("<key>: <refusal>") and dag_input.fallback_record(slice) collects a slice’s; a refusal of no listed feature is raised (rule 2: fail closed); no control needs a fallback. Each listed feature is refused for real in test_native_tables_refuse_each_listed_feature (the model’s answers, the process or the native tables changed in one place on u u~ > d d~ g), and the switch sites’ fallback and raise in test_native_stage_falls_back_with_a_record. The generation record names every fallback (rule 2; slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-25 ~12:50 item 1): GeneratedProcess.native_fallbacks (the slice’s fallback_record) is the artifact’s generation_filters["native_fallbacks"], written only when non-empty, so an artifact without a fallback keeps its bytes. The tables fail closed (NativeDagUnsupported of no listed feature, raised) for a usable reachable vertex with a negative coupling order in a limited name: the oracle bounds each current’s accumulated orders, which a negative order can bring back within a limit, while the tables prune vertices by their own orders, which is exact for non-negative orders only (no model of the slice has one). The native stages report their start and finish to the request’s progress_callback ({"step": "native-dag", "stage": "loop-blocks" | "counterterm-program", "state": "start" | "done" | "fallback"}, done with the current, interaction and block counts, or fallback with the listed feature before the tree engine reports its own steps; dag_input.native_progress). LoopSlice.generate and export_plan decode nothing; the native-trees export decodes exactly the two A5 consumers (the slice’s and the CT program’s tree rows and interaction programs; A5’s CT emission below removes the second). The builder is sequential, so 1 and N threads give the same columns (rule 5). Cache state (slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-25 ~06:30; workspace/tmp/native-dag/fix2/determinism/): g g > g g and u u~ > d d~ g generated twice from empty PYAMPLICOL_CACHE_DIR directories and twice warm give byte-identical plans in all four runs, and native members identical between the two cold and between the two warm runs, equal to the slice’s (8b52179b, A4 off) cold and warm. Cold and warm differ in parameters.bin only, on the slice as well (not A4’s): native_trees._parameter_program passes the scalar library’s helper definitions (library._bodies, in the order the process history first parsed them: a fresh UFO compile and the cached compiled model, *.pyAmplicol-model.json, parse in different orders) to assemble._canonical_stage, which numbers function heads positionally, so a helper is pyamplicol_v2_canonical::c25 cold and c31 warm (8 bytes in 2.9 kB; the evaluators compute the same). Sorting the helpers by their canonical head name before _canonical_stage makes cold and warm byte-identical (checked on the slice; patch fix2/determinism/sort_helpers.patch, for the owner of _parameter_program). Re-checked after the lc-perf merge (8126d301, workspace/tmp/native-dag/fix4/determinism/): the plans are byte-identical in all five runs (two cold, two warm, and the flag-off Python route warm), the native members identical between the two cold and between the two warm runs, the flag-on warm members equal the flag-off Python route’s member for member, and cold and warm still differ in parameters.bin only (the same cause; the patch still applies). Oracles (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_native_dag.py): the switched build_tree_blocks and CountertermBlocks.build against the oracle stages (blocks, S1′/S1″, the Ward, coloured-width and U(1) queries without a decode, one counted decode on the first attribute read) and the listed fallbacks with their record (default tier, 19 s); the photon/Z and top-width controls (u u~ > e⁻e⁺ g g, g g > u u~ γ g, e⁺e⁻ > u u~ g, g g > t t~ g) and a recursion-route LoopSlice.generate whose S1, S4, S5, S8 (also with native trees), S1′, S1″, S2 and P digests equal the oracle route’s (physics tier); the O6 files and the recursion-against-sites tests of test_loop_v2_ct_recursion.py run on native blocks. Seven legs, production stages under the flag (tools/loop_v2_dag.py, records workspace/tmp/native-dag/oracle/a4/, on the A4 head and again after the slice merge): S1′ and S1″ equal the stored Python digests (g g > g g g g g S1′ 9d274adf…, S1″ ae1a90e9…; u u~ > g g g g g 198f439b…, 8eeca050…) with every count, no fallback and no decode. Python → native: loop-block DAG and blocks 498.9 → 10.0 s (11.9 s warm; g g > g g g g g, process peak 10.27 → 1.59 GB) and 42.2 → 0.85 s (0.96 s warm; u u~ > g g g g g, 0.93 → 0.30 GB); CT program 631.1 → 20.6 s (19.1 s warm; process peak, Born included, 12.0 → 2.66 GB) and 141.0 → 4.5 s (4.3 s warm; 2.79 → 0.78 GB).

    The recursion now beats the oracle on the artifact build at g g > g g g g (0.97×; peak +1.6 %) but not at u u~ > g g g g (1.09×, peak 1.27×) or g g > t t~ g g (1.07×, 1.14×); LoopSlice.generate alone is 1.06×, 1.05× and 1.08× (peaks 1.05×, 1.05×, 1.12×). What remains is not A4’s: the CT program’s Python tree rows and interaction program in the export (A5’s CT emission, which RUST-MIGRATION §3.A sequences after generation-scale-2’s I5 proper record), now behind a decode of the native DAG (0.98 / 0.82 / 3.10 s); the bind’s colour reductions (0.15 / 0.65 / 5.74 s; A6 keeps reduce_network in Python); the warm lowering (0.46–0.84 s).     CT program emission (WP3.1 Rust migration A5, its counterterm part, brought forward to close parity; work/v2-native-dag; dag_input.NATIVE_PROGRAM = True). The native-trees export builds the counterterm program’s interaction program from the native CT DAG (V2Dag.program, rusticol-core loop_v2/dag/program.rs) instead of the Python TreeRows (runtime schema) and native_trees._interaction_program on the decoded DAG, which stay the oracle; they run with the flag off and for a CT DAG the tree engine built (an A4 fallback). The dispatch is the first line of native_trees._CountertermTrees.of (A5’s call site, RUST-MIGRATION §5.2): dag_input.native_counterterm_trees returns only the parts (rows, value slots, momentum slots, source fill, interaction program, saved kernels) and of builds the record and the dataclass for both routes, so a field added to of reaches the native route too (the A5 test compares every field). native_interaction_program and the oracle _interaction_program build their kernels with one recipe, the helpers of native_trees (_kernel_model, _vertex_kernel, _propagator_kernel, _saved_kernel: model expressions with the kernel functions inlined, canonical symbols, exact evaluators, TREE_SCHEMA 3 shapes; slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-25 ~12:50 item 3), so a change to the recipe reaches both lanes. Only dag_input._retained_functions still mirrors code of the oracle, the retention tail of stage_parameters._specialize_stage_symbolica_functions (not package A’s file; the native lane inlines all kernels in one call and then keeps each kernel’s functions); the default-tier A5 test compares every kernel byte for byte. lc-perf’s TREE_SCHEMA 3 (eae925f9) was mirrored in 92fa498a, before the helpers. Rust lays out the runtime schema of a loop-request DAG whose every non-source current is propagated (ct_closure.program_propagated_currents; the slice’s TreeRows(dag) is not such a DAG): one value slot per current (source, or propagated / unpropagated by the model’s propagator of its particle and chirality), the momentum slots by (bit count, mask), one stage per result size; and it emits the steps (rows, accumulators, outputs, and the rows and outputs of the epsilon-pole slots that finite-only evaluations skip), the colour weights interned in first use, and the kernels in first use. Python keeps the model algebra (rule 4). Each kernel is compiled from the representative the oracle compiles it from, by the oracle’s recipe: the model’s component expressions on canonical symbols, saved as exact Symbolica evaluators, with the kernel functions inlined in one _specialize_stage_symbolica_functions call over all kernels instead of one per kernel (built in the oracle’s order, so the functions and their wildcards come out the same). 6.2 Admission: plain tree-level insertions (REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM J)¶

A counterterm contribution is an ordinary tree-level contribution of the CT-lowered model with exactly one CT vertex (the insertion order, §6.1). Its admission is

  • the requested coupling orders: the program’s order limits and the loop orders of the request (§6.1 item 1), which also exclude every rule above them (inert);

  • a rule of a selected correction (rule.perturbation_type; a UVtree rule also needs a selected correction among its own orders);

  • a loop of a selected correction (WP3.2 EWI-3, Q3): every particle of the alternative is perturbative in a selected correction (the model’s perturbative_species_orders, MadLoop’s is_perturbating, the eligibility of the families’ loop lines; a species without facts is no loop species). The UFO declares no correction type of a CT vertex (perturbation_type is None for every rule of loop_sm, loop_qcd_qed_sm and G_μ), so this is what tells the QCD correction of the photon vertex (the R2 of u u~ a with a u-gluon loop, orders QCD² QED) from the QED one (its u-photon UV counterterm) when a mixed-order Born admits both by coupling orders (u u~ > d d~ with QED corrections). With the families’ loop species in the catalogue (EWI-1), the photon-only QED corrections of that request generated, their bare and counterterm UV poles cancelling (ladder rung uudd_qed_photon_uv of test_loop_v2_ew.py, binary64; an identity of poles, which takes the field factors’ UV part as the remainder); since WP3.2 EWI-5 they are refused before any tree (listed veto-unlabelled-counterterms, “Listed generation refusals”: loop_qcd_qed_sm’s electroweak counterterm labels are nominal). loop_sm’s QCD admission is unchanged rule by rule. This third criterion refines REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM J’s literal admission list (coupling orders, exactly once, particle_veto) without any loop matching; it awaits the coordinator’s ratification as an implementation note of ADDENDUM J (ew-ct fix round 1);

  • the particle veto: every loop-content alternative of the rule (its UFO loop_particles, |PDG| codes; an empty one is a wildcard) that holds a vetoed particle is dropped, all others are kept. M_rule is their number (ct_recursion.admitted_alternatives).

Inert vertices (coordinator decision 2026-10-23, REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM J). The admission does not ask whether a tree of the request can hold the rule’s vertex: a lowered vertex that none can hold simply never enters the program’s DAG. A rule the lowering cannot lower (§6.1 “Not lowered”) is checked: when its vertex cannot enter any tree of the request’s CT program it is inert. It contributes nothing, needs no lowering and is recorded as inert with its reason (CountertermRecursion.inert, LoopSlice.counterterm_program.recursion); the artifact’s generation record keeps it as the process’s generation filter counterterms_inert (rule name → reason, in artifact.json extensions.generation.concrete_processes[].filters, next to particle_veto; model names only, no path, no native schema involved). Otherwise the request is refused. “Can enter” is the tree engine’s own reachability over the request’s legs, order limits and particle_veto (ct_closure.InsertionReachability): the tree engine’s forward species and coupling-order sweep (generation.dag_reachability._species_coupling_orders_by_mask, the same function the DAG compiler’s closure-order reachability runs, here without its colour-engine and leg-set filters) over the CT program’s model, order limits (insertion order 0) and vetoed particles gives the insertion-free currents of every leg set, and a vertex of fields f₁…f_n and orders o enters a tree iff the legs split into n blocks whose currents enter its fields with orders that sum with o to within the program’s limits; a single leg is the external particle. The program reads a vertex in one of two ways, told apart by the block of leg 1. With leg 1 alone the vertex is a CT root, which reads each block by its incoming field like the Born closure: the current entering a leg of field f is the particle anti(f). Otherwise it is an insertion inside a current of the program’s DAG, which the tree engine reads with the current of particle p on the UFO leg of p (models.compiler_entry._compile_oriented_kernels): the current entering a leg of field f is f, and the block holding leg 1 is the rest of the tree re-rooted at the vertex (its root’s ordinary vertex read through its conjugate, which a Hermitian vertex set holds). The two readings differ only for vertices whose fields are not closed under conjugation: in u d~ > e+ ve g the R2 of [u~ d W+] sits inside the current of legs 1 and 5 (the kernel the DAG uses for d + W+ → u) and that of [d~ u W-] at the root. A two-point vertex needs two blocks of at least two legs: the CT program puts two-point insertions on internal lines only (a clone line is never external, and an external line takes the particle’s field factor, §6.5). The full leg set is swept too, as the root of a one-point vertex, should one ever reach the check. The sweep ignores colour, helicity and flavour-flow labels, so it over-approximates the currents and never declares a vertex that can enter a tree inert; no loop, site or witness is consulted. Goldstones: a tree model that absorbs them into the massive vectors (CompiledUFOModel.inactive_goldstone_names, unitary gauge) holds no Goldstone vertex, so every Goldstone CT vertex of that model is in no tree of any request: a two-point term on an absorbed Goldstone is not lowered and is inert (ct_line_insertions), a vertex term is lowered and never enters the DAG. The check (WP3.2 EWI-4b). Since EWI-4b only QCD-only requests take unitary trees: every request with electroweak loop species takes the model in ‘t Hooft–Feynman gauge (§6.8), where the Goldstones are explicit fields and their counterterms (the Goldstone Yukawa and mass counterterms, the Goldstone–vector mixings) are ordinary rules, lowered and admitted like any other. For a QCD-only request the absorbed policy accounts for the explicit Goldstone counterterms exactly when the two gauges agree: M5 compares b b~ > t t~ QED=2 [virt=QCD] with a massive b (an internal Z between massive currents; the ‘t Hooft–Feynman request admits and inserts the QCD counterterms of the G⁰ b b̄ and G⁰ t t̄ vertices, the unitary one cannot hold them) in both gauges (test_qcd_corrections_agree_in_both_gauges, nightly). It runs only when a request admits an unlowerable rule (0.02 s at four legs). Tests: test_insertion_reachability_is_sound_against_the_site_oracle (every rule the site oracle closes on the slice’s exact tree currents is reachable; quark vertices in g g > g g and gluon or vetoed-Z vertices in Drell-Yan are not), test_uncancelled_cells_in_no_tree_are_inert (an anomalous g g Z R2 is inert in u u~ > e- e+ with the cancelling model’s components, refused in u u~ > e- e+ g), test_insertion_reachability_tells_a_vertex_from_its_conjugate (u d~ > e+ ve: [d~ u W-] enters at the root and [e+ ve W-] inside the W+ current, their conjugates do not; u d~ > e+ ve g: [u~ d W+] enters too; u u~ > d d~: [g g] enters, the two-point quark vertices of its external lines do not), test_insertion_reachability_is_sound_against_the_program_dag (u d~ > w+ g: every rule of a CT vertex or clone line in the production program’s DAG and of its CT roots is admitted, [u~ d W+] inside a current and [d~ u W-] at the root), test_unlowerable_charged_vertex_in_a_current_is_refused (u d~ > w+ g with the R2 of [u~ d W+] made unlowerable is refused), test_qed_declaring_model_names_its_blockers (loop_qcd_qed_sm u u~ > d d~: the reachable recms rules are refused, the G0–A mixing is inert) and the nightly test_qed_declaring_model_joint_corrections_equal_legacy (g g > g g with QCD and QED corrections, every unlowerable EW rule inert, equals legacy).

Nothing else: no counterterm is matched to its loop counterpart. There is no witness table of divergent loop routings, no admission per routing or per leg mask, and no fallback to site closure. MadLoop’s matching (set_LoopCT_vertices) needs the loop graphs and is complicated and costly; for a consistent model it admits the same alternatives, since a CT vertex of given fields and orders that sits in a tree of the process has its one-loop counterpart in the process too, with the loop content of each non-vetoed alternative.

particle_veto is a public generation option ([generation] particle_veto, --particle-veto, GenerationConfig.particle_veto; model names, a name vetoes its antiparticle; v2 virtual generation only). It is stored with the plan v4 request record (SliceRequest.particle_veto, |PDG| codes) and in the generation filters. A vetoed particle is removed from every tree-level vertex of every generation step, so the loops, the trees and the counterterms stay consistent: the Born and the loop blocks (the tree engine’s ignored_particle_ids), the loop species and loop vertices (families.ModelLoopCatalogue(veto=...)), the CT program (its DAG and the lowered model’s vertices), the CT terms and the external-field terms with vetoed loop content. A vetoed particle cannot be external. With loop_sm, particle_veto = [t] is massless five-flavour QCD (no top loop, no top decoupling term in α_s and δZ_g): g g > g g equals NJet’s Nf = 5 virtual to 3·10⁻¹⁴ at ten points, and g g > g g g g at NJet’s first point to 1.5·10⁻¹⁴ (Born), 6·10⁻¹³ (poles) and 1.1·10⁻¹¹ (finite part), within the references’ own spread at six gluons (NJet against OpenLoops up to 7·10⁻¹¹; test_loop_v2_particle_veto.py, the six-gluon point nightly: an hour on the per-point Python inputs). It replaces the internal top-free switches (the NJet comparison’s ignored_particle_ids).

The site oracle (§6.6) keeps MadLoop’s matching through witnesses as an independent check of this rule: a witness is an admitted family routing with structural rank R_f ≥ 2N − 4 and signature (attached currents’ fields and leg masks, loop species set, loop orders); R2 and UVmass rules need a witness whose species set is one of their alternatives, UVloop rules any witness (alternatives as veto filters), UVtree rules none. O6 (closure with the plain rule = sites with witness admission) holds on every control and slice request (§6.1 “O6 and O1”).

6.3 Completeness¶

The model’s UV and R2 rules are taken as declared (its NLO declaration’s uv_complete and model_r2_complete): production does not check them against the loops, and nothing checks completeness at runtime (a missing R2 is finite and invisible to the poles). The IR-pole oracle (the Catani operator, O9) and the site oracle check it in tests and model development; the site oracle keeps the completeness check of design 3:

  1. Coverage rule (ct_sites._coverage, oracle). Every divergent witness family must be covered by an admitted rule for each eligible loop-species group, or by a certified zero. A divergent witness family has structural rank R ≥ 2N − 4, i.e. it is superficially UV divergent, which is the only case where UV poles and R2 occur in a renormalisable theory. Otherwise the oracle fails and names the uncovered signature (the sgluon bug, assessment R2). A model whose ranks make the divergent set unbounded (Δ ≥ 2 per propagator, effective theories) is refused by the oracle.

  2. Certified zeros.

    • Structural certificate (implemented, ct_sites.closed_fermion_zeros): a closed loop of one fermion f needs no rule when its colour factor is Tr_R(T^a) = 0 (one adjoint attachment, the rest singlets), or when charge conjugation cancels its two orientations (Furry: every vertex joining f, f̄ and an attachment is a pure vector current, the number of attachments is odd, and the colour trace is unchanged by reversing them, i.e. at most two adjoint attachments). Both need f’s model vertices to be three-point with one other field. Closed quark loops with one photon and two gluons are certified this way; a Z keeps its axial part, which R2_GGZ covers.

    • Cheap test: the summed 1PI numerator, including both fermion orientations, vanishes exactly at random exact points (Furry-type zeros).

    • Thorough test: the model certifier built on the retained direct-R2 path (loops/evanescent.py, evanescent_gauge.py, direct_kernels.py). Once per model, it computes R2 and UV poles of every admitted 1PI function with k ≤ k_max per loop species, and compares them with the UFO rules, both non-zero values and zeros. This is also the structural replacement for the string whitelist (assessment R6).

6.4 Contraction and component split¶

  • Contraction. CT = 1 amplitudes are contracted with the Born exactly like the Born square: A0† G A_CT per sector, plus rectangular overlaps for CT-only multi-trace states.

  • Kinds stay separate through slots. This reproduces the kept component vector [full, bare, UV, R2, UV_local, UV_fields] (rust/crates/rusticol-core/src/loop_execution.rs:188 CompleteLoopResult [V]) and the 19 totals, with full = bare + UV_local + R2 + fields and UV = UV_local + fields.

  • No extra loop factor. CT couplings already contain the loop factor, so no i/(16π²) is applied (physical_counterterms.py:848-849 [V-s]).

  • Allowed exact refactorings (contracts §2.5): fold currents per (site class, tensor) and drop identically zero currents.

6.5 External fields¶

  • Scalar δZ: for each external leg and correction, δZ/2 × the order-masked Born interference, keeping the semantics of physical_counterterms.py:877-905 [V-s].

  • Chiral δZ^{L,R} and mixing (δZ_{Zγ}, CKM): CT-tagged modified external sources in the tree recursion (CT = 1 sources). The field term is then the Born dual times that amplitude, which is generic for the electroweak members.

  • Tadpole CTs. The VEV-subtracted scheme has no tadpole CTs; one-point rules raise at preparation, as today (counterterms.py:259-260 [V-s]).

Status (WP2.2). Scalar δZ only (loops/v2/fields.py). Internal two-point terms of any chirality and mixing between fields of equal spin are lowered as clone lines (§6.1). Chiral and mixing external factors have no UFO format: the particle counterterm attribute carries one scalar per order key, and the NLOCT electroweak models (loop_qcd_qed_sm) keep it QCD-only and put the electroweak field renormalisation, chiral and mixing δZ included, into their vertex counterterms (on-shell residues are one). A model that declares such factors needs a format first (proposal: ExternalFieldRule.chirality ∈ {None, L, R} and a partner PDG). Plan:

  • Chiral, massless (Weyl) legs: a helicity selection. δZ_L multiplies quarks of physical helicity −1 and antiquarks of physical helicity +1, incoming or outgoing (ψ → P_L ψ; ψ̄ → ψ̄ P_R; the tree engine’s labels of crossed legs must be mapped), so the scalar mechanism restricted to the leg’s helicity rows is exact.

  • Chiral, massive legs: the projected source P_χ w (row spinors take the opposite projector), as a CT = 1 source.

  • Mixing: the Born with leg i’s field replaced by its partner, keeping leg i’s wavefunction. For legs other than 1 this is a CT = 1 source of the CT program (a partner source current with the leg’s wavefunction values); for leg 1 it is the root closure with the partner’s vertex entries.

  • Tests: loop_sm has no such rule, so they are synthetic: δZ_L = δZ_R reproduces the scalar term, and a partner with identical couplings reproduces it too.

Decays (M-FINAL MF-DEC-2). The decaying particle of a 1 → n request is an ordinary incoming leg: no rule reads the number of initial legs (MF-DEC-1’s interim decay-process refusal is retired), its field factor is the scalar δZ above (loop_sm’s particle counterterm, e.g. the top’s UVWfct_t_0) or, in the NLOCT electroweak models, part of the vertex counterterms (c_UVepemZ1EW holds δZ_ZZ and δZ_AZ), and the averaging is the tree engine’s (the decaying particle’s helicities and colours). The loops are amputated like any external leg’s, so its self-energy enters only through δZ, whose finite parts the NLOCT models write as recms(CMSParam == 1 and W != 0, x): in the real-mass scheme (CMSParam = 0) that is Re x, so the absorptive part of the decaying particle’s self-energy at its mass is dropped, which is MadLoop’s convention; its own width enters nothing unless the particle propagates, where the coloured-width and electroweak-width guards hold, and under the complex-mass scheme it must be zero (cms-external-width). Evidence: rows XX01–XX08 (tests/fixtures/loop/dec/manifest.json, tests/unit/test_loop_v2_dec_*.py: t > b w+ [QCD] and [QCD QED], z > e- e+ [QED], z > u u~ [QCD QED], w+ > e+ ve [QED], h > b b~ [QCD] with a massive b, t > b w+ g [QCD], z > u u~ g [QCD QED]) equal MadLoop’s quadruple-precision references per squared order (double-double within 1·10⁻¹³ at every point, 6·10⁻¹⁵ but for one Born of z > u u~ g), rule 4’s Catani poles (one massive coloured initial emitter, the QED operator with incoming charged legs) and rule 5 (the incoming top’s field factor) hold, Ward on t > b w+ g’s gluon, LC/NLC of the loop_sm QCD decays against the N_c scan, z > u u~ [QCD] against the time-like quark form factor, and the public route (stored artifact, native evaluate, O1 checks) on XX01 and XX07. No engine change was needed beyond the admission.

6.6 Test oracle: CT site closure¶

The site closure was the slice form of wave 1; it is now a test oracle only (SliceRequest.counterterms = "sites"; plan v4 refuses it), with the witness admission of §6.2. CT contributions are computed as sites:

  • A CT vertex V_r is applied at the root to m ∈ {2, …, k_max} CT = 0 block currents whose leg sets partition the legs (k_max from the model’s CT rules).

  • Partitions are unordered and assigned to the vertex’s field multiset. The UFO vertex is fully symmetrised, so each assignment counts once, which is the BG rule.

  • Internal two-point insertions are two-block sites with both blocks of at least two legs.

  • Colour comes from exact closure of the vertex colour with the block words.

Every one-CT tree has exactly one CT vertex and can be rooted there, so the site sum is exact and complete. It stays as the oracle for §6.1 (physics-judge graft 7) and for small processes. The CT-root terms of the production closure (§6.1 item 7) reuse its enumeration with the plain admission.

LC/NLC need these named invariants, which a UFO with numeric SU(3) colour does not provide (loops/model.py:1-7 [V]). LC/NLC therefore need a formal-N_c continuation: the model’s own (source-owned: QCDR2Continuation, loops/qcd_r2_color.py:30 [V], for QCD; a future EW or BSM declaration otherwise) or, for loop_sm, the one pyAmpliCol ships (below); a request reaching a counterterm vertex no continuation covers is refused (colour-declaration-coverage). FC always works (MASTER_PLAN §2.15; judge X1).

Shipped loop_sm declaration (M-QCD MQ-NC, as built). pyAmpliCol ships the formal-N_c data of MG5_aMC 3.7.0’s loop_sm (models/loop_color_declarations/loop_sm.json, written by tools/developer/build_loop_colour_data.py), so LC and NLC work on stock loop_sm without a hand-written declaration; full colour stays the default of loop requests (USER Q1, MQ-MODEL).

  • Coverage. All 103 counterterm vertices of loop_sm (the source’s 104th, V_R24G, is commented out in CT_vertices.py): 74 R2, 26 UV, 3 UVmass; 198 coupling entries continued by the identities C_A = N_c, C_F = (N_c²−1)/(2N_c), T_F = 1/2, N_col = N_c (with the scheme tie λ_HV = 1), the four-gluon R2 V_R2RGA by its two whole-rule recipes (gauge and fundamental-Dirac loop groups, loops/qcd_r2_color.py), and the six external-field factors (c, b, t: C_F; the gluon’s three heavy-quark groups: T_F).

  • Keys. Each vertex is keyed by a structural digest of the vertex as the source writes it (vertex_digest): counterterm type; particles by spin, colour, charge, mass and width parameters (never names or PDG codes); colour and Lorentz structures; coupling entries with their expressions and orders; loop-particle groups; and the definitions of every internal, counterterm and helper parameter the expressions read (external parameters by LHA address and type, never a value). Field factors likewise (field_digest). Vertex names, record positions, the model’s name and path never enter. A restriction lives in the source’s metadata (card values and the zeros it fixes), not in its declarations, so every shipped restriction has the same digests and resolves its surviving vertices (checked for all nine). Vertices of one structure (d and s quark R2 and UV) share an entry: 98 entries for 103 vertices.

  • Resolution. resolve_loop_color_declaration returns the source’s own declaration (metadata), else the shipped one at that source’s positions (resolve_shipped_declaration) when the source states the data’s loop scheme (its metadata’s loop declaration, which the public route attaches, else its shipped [loop.model] profile; a model sharing a few digests, e.g. loop_qcd_qed_sm with 3 of 499, gets none), else None. LC and NLC requests naming no declaration take it, on the public route (loop_service._prepare) and in LoopSlice.generate (assemble.resolve_request), and record it in the artifact like an explicit one; a full-colour request’s contraction choice still reads the source’s own declaration only.

  • Literature colour factors. Each entry states every coupling entry’s colour factor from the literature (textbook UV renormalisation; Draggiotis et al. 0903.0356 for the QCD R2; Garzelli et al. 0910.3130 for R2 with electroweak legs and QCD loops). test_loop_v2_nc_declaration.py proves each source coupling with the identities equal to its factor times an N_c-independent rest in every branch of its conditionals (a coupling with C_F written as 4/3 fails), and the model preparation proves the identities equal to the source at N_c = 3.

  • Guard. The listed refusal colour-declaration-coverage (refusals.require_declared_colour_rules, require_declared_colour_fields): an LC or NLC request is refused when its counterterm program can insert a vertex the declaration does not cover (reachability as for unlowerable vertices, ct_closure.InsertionReachability; an uncovered vertex no tree holds is left alone) or an external leg takes an uncovered field factor. Full colour reads the source couplings at N_c = 3 and is never refused for coverage, with or without a declaration. The example QCD subset (examples/loop/source_colour/loop_sm_qcd_subset.json) is refused on u u~ > e- e+ g(g), whose closed quark loops reach g g Z, g g g Z and g g g A; the tests and developer tools that used it there take the shipped declaration. The engine’s own alpha(0) photon field term is not a source factor and is not checked (electroweak, M-SM).

  • Independent oracles (test_loop_v2_nc_oracles.py; none reads the declaration; the N_c scan tests/unit/loop_nc_scan.py evaluates full colour at N_c = N with the declaration’s couplings): (a) NJet’s NJetNc (2.1.1, double-double, top-free, N_f = 5; tests/fixtures/loop/nc/njet_nc_scan.json) at N_c = 2, 4, 5, 6 on g g > g g and g g > g g g (direct mode, which keeps the N_c = 3 colour average) and on u u~ > g g g, u u~ > d d~ g and u u~ > u u~ g (BLHA mode, NJetNc, every point re-evaluated in double-double; BLHA divides by the colour average at N_c, so the fixture stores its values times avg(N_c)/avg(3)): Born and every Laurent coefficient within 1.8e-13 (gluon rows) and 3.5e-12 (quark rows) in binary64; (c) Catani’s operator at N_c = N (C_A, C_F, β₀ and the colour-correlated Borns at N, the Python correlators: the native C4 correlators are contracted at N_c = 3) against the poles of the renormalised virtual, which tests the UV counterterms’ N_c dependence (C_A fixed to 3 fails at 46 %); (d) the gauge-Ward check (§8.4) at N_c = 2 and 4 in double-double, which tests the R2’s N_c dependence (N_col fixed to 3 fails on u u~ > g g g at 1.7e-4 of the physical scale; on u u~ > e- e+ g the R2 satisfy their own Ward identity, so that row is a consistency check only); (b) BDK’s O14 for u u~ > g g g (test_loop_v2_colour.py, test_loop_v2_observables_nightly.py).

  • Campaign nc column (m-qcd PLAN §1.4 rule 7). test_loop_v2_nc_projection.py, per nc row (A01, A08, A09, A12, A13, A15, A18, A21, B03, C01, D05, E01, F01) at the campaign’s points: the row’s binding reference fixture (required/mqcd_references.json) gives points 0, 1, 2 at their μ_R and point 3 = point 0 at μ_R/2, its fixed parameters (5F rows on the default restriction with no_b_mass’s zero masses, ‘5F*’, until MQ-5F) and α_s; the default tier runs points 0 and 1 of A12 and D05, the nightly tier every other point (PLAN §4.2 also marks A01, A09 and C01 default: their projection runs nightly, the user’s fast-default-tier rule). LC, NLC and FC come from the production native path (native point inputs, as a stored artifact; the shipped declaration resolved from the model and handed to the request) in double-double and in native MPFR (50 digits), and are compared with the exact Laurent fit FC(N) = Σ_p c_p N^p of the N_c scan. The scan is loop_nc_scan request with "dressing": "native": the Python point inputs at N (trees, Born, colour cells, counterterm and field scalars) dressed and reduced natively at 60 digits, one generation per N for all of a row’s points; it equals the Python reference path’s own dressing within 7e-53 at N = 2 and 1/2 (A08, A12, A13, B03 point 0; nightly test on A12), which instead carries a precision-independent error at B03’s point 1 (bare loop 4e-25 off Catani at 60, 80 and 100 digits; the native carriers equal Catani to 1e-65; below the user’s ~1e-5 threshold, a HANDOFF §9 note only). The fit window holds the powers P_top − 2n_col .. P_top, n_col being the number of coloured external legs; two check nodes inside the fit nodes’ range must be reproduced, and the window’s two lowest powers must vanish. Every check is per point, per squared-order sector and per coefficient (PLAN §1.4), Born included: strictly relative, except a value that vanishes identically (|r| ≤ 1e-28 A) is held absolutely, |a − r| ≤ 1e-24 A, A = F_s = |B_s| α_s/2π (PLAN’s F_s rule at rule 7’s tolerance; |B_s| for a Born). Within 1e-24: no power above the sector’s P; on MPFR every component’s LC = c_P 3^P, NLC = Σ_{P−2..P} c_p 3^p, FC = FC(3); and the poles at the scan’s integer N equal Catani’s at N (oracle (c) on every row). In double-double the same identity for the Born (within 1e-24) and the virtual, in rules 4 and 6’s band max(1e-24, 10 E_DD) per coefficient (coordinator ruling 2026-10-29 ~10:15), E_DD that coefficient’s double-double estimate with stability.RECOMMENDED_CHECKS over the deviation’s own denominator (A for a value held absolutely): MPFR proves the identity exact (≤ 2.1e-59; C01 7.4e-37), so a double-double miss within 10 E_DD is double-double’s conditioning. Only A18 goes beyond 1e-24: its full-colour virtual finite part, 1.9e-24 / 7.2e-24 / 7.2e-24 at points 0, 2, 3 against E_DD 4.2e-24 / 1.6e-23 / 1.6e-23 (0.46x). Measured at all four points of every row (native dressing): double-double ≤ 3.2e-28 on every row but A18 (1.8e-25 at point 1) and B03 (2.3e-26); MPFR ≤ 2.1e-59 except C01 (7.4e-37); fit check nodes ≤ 1.7e-64 (C01 3.3e-40); Catani ≤ 3.9e-70 except the supplied-point rows C01 and E01 (≤ 1.3e-28: their 30-digit points are on shell to 1e-30, Catani takes the model masses); the values held absolutely lie below 1e-77 A, the smallest held relatively above 4.9e-4 A. Default tier: A12 and D05, about 100 s each; nightly rows 108-507 s, A15 1780 s. NC_COLUMN lists each row’s column: the projection ids (default rows also the nightly-points id) followed by its oracle ids.

6.8 Gauge and scheme¶

  • One gauge. Born, blocks, loop lines and CTs all use ‘t Hooft–Feynman gauge (ξ = 1) with explicit Goldstones and ghosts. Ranks then stay ≤ N, whereas unitary-gauge kμkν/M² terms would break rank ≤ N + 2. As built (WP3.2 EWI-4b): LoopSlice.generate takes the model in that gauge for every request with electroweak loop species (ew_policy.electroweak: a correction other than QCD or a colour-singlet loop species of a requested correction; ew_policy.feynman_gauge_model), refused with ElectroweakGaugeError on a model that cannot be (its source declares no gauge 1, or a bundle prepared in unitary gauge; ew_policy.require_loop_gauge in prepare_request_model, so the dry run reports it, which also refuses a massive vector loop species on a model not compiled in that gauge; MF-GM-HC P2: a source declaring only unitary gauge is no longer refused for every loop request). QCD-only requests keep the compiled model’s gauge: unitary by default (their validated trees; QCD plans byte-identical), ‘t Hooft–Feynman for a model compiled in it. The request’s gauge is its model’s (LoopSlice.compiled.ir.gauge), recorded in the artifact’s generation filters (gauge, off the default only); a regenerated artifact takes the same gauge from the same model and request. The tree API’s default is unchanged (unitary). Loop lines: massive vectors −i g, Goldstones and ghosts i (the UFO’s index-free numerator), every segment and numerator of degree ≤ 1 (test_feynman_gauge_loop_lines_keep_rank_at_most_n).

  • Complex-mass scheme. Complex masses and couplings are runtime inputs from the snapshot (R7). The fast NinjaRS engine accepts complex masses with real shifts and a real S-matrix (ninjars:fast/mod.rs:60-79 [V]). The known complex-mass master defects are risk 13 (§15). As built (M-SM MS-CMS, loops/model_cms.py). The declaration’s mass_scheme is "real-on-shell" or "complex-mass" (mass-scheme otherwise; [loop.model.scheme] mass_scheme stated alone selects it over the model’s own declaration, MadLoop’s set complex_mass_scheme True). "complex-mass" generates on MG5_aMC’s complex-mass model of the source: complex_mass_scheme ports Model.change_mass_to_complex_scheme (MG5_aMC 3.7.0 base_objects.py) on the exact UFO records, complex_mass_model applies the same decisions to the compiled tree payload. CMSParam = 1; per width parameter first met (source order) with a nonzero value at the card (fixed parameters, else the restriction card, else the source), an internal width takes re(), an external real mass M gets CMASS_M = sqrt(M² − iMΓ) with M and Γ staying real inputs, an internal mass is refused (cms-internal-mass: MG5’s PDG-24 input-scheme switch is SM-specific and not ported, m-sm PLAN §1.7); the YUKAWA inputs become their particles’ (pole) masses (cms-yukawa-input if a request fixes one), written in M and Γ so that no coupling reads the CMASS parameter whose sign the fermion-loop tree reading flips; a tied mass without a pole mass (a zero width at the card, as for every external top, EW-25, or loop_sm’s τ) gives its particles the real line mass LMASS_M := M (step 4b, ComplexMassScheme.lines, MS-CMS-N’s CM07 fix; not in MG5_aMC, values unchanged), so the couplings read M and the line LMASS_M, and conventions.LeafWeights._require_mass_free_couplings holds at every width (before step 4b a zero-width top on an EW or Yukawa loop line raised FermionSignError: G_μ g g > t t~ [QED], loop_sm t t~ > h h [QCD]); every other internal parameter is complex and reads CMASS_M in parameters, CT parameters, couplings and the field counterterms; every particle of a pole mass, Goldstones and ghosts included, propagates with it and width ZERO (so the [U8] width guards pass on that model); the UFO-standard principal reglog is bound ([U3]; reglog_convention = "source" keeps the G_μ override as a view). First oracle: MG5_aMC’s own CMS model (tools/loop_reference/mg5_cms_model.py) equals ours to ≤ 3.4·10⁻¹³ in every parameter, CT parameter, coupling and field counterterm (G_μ default and a0, loop_sm with Γ_t; test_loop_model_cms.py). Python inputs: assemble._model_masses(pole_masses=True) returns a pole mass as an exact complex; the loop propagators (_mass_values: M² − iMΓ to the working digits), the kernel constants and the Python reduction lanes take it; external legs and Catani’s emitters stay real (external states are stable, EW-25: cms-external-width). Policy keys (listed, shown by the dry run): mass-scheme, complex-mass-scheme (a model outside the transform’s assumptions), cms-internal-mass, cms-yukawa-input, cms-external-width, complex-fixed-parameter (both schemes: external parameters are real), and for real on-shell requests coloured-width and electroweak-width (the latter now also on the Born DAG in loop_service._v2_request). The conventions record (ew_policy.scheme_conventions) states mass_scheme = "complex-mass" with the pole masses, widths, Yukawa ties, reglog and CMSParam/LogSwitch/GfRedefinitionChoice (model_cms.convention_record; also for a QCD-only CMS request); non-CMS records are unchanged. The native point inputs take complex plan masses (MS-CMS-N, §11.1), so the public route stores complex-mass artifacts (model_cms.NATIVE_POLE_MASSES; a build without them refuses a request with a pole mass, complex-mass-scheme). Evidence (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_cms.py): Python inputs (LoopSlice.evaluate; double-double runs in the native executor, MS-CMS-N) = MadLoop CMS: CM10 (u d~ > w+ b b~ QCD=0 [QCD], loop_sm, Γ_t; QP, 4 points) AP(32) ≤ 6.8·10⁻¹⁴, binary64 ≤ 3.4·10⁻¹⁰; CM02 (u u~ > e- e+ [QCD QED], G_μ, every width; QP, 4 points, every sector) binary64 ≤ 1.0·10⁻¹³, AP(32) ≤ 8.8·10⁻¹⁵; CM05 (u u~ > e- e+ g [QCD QED]) binary64 ≤ 4.6·10⁻¹³, AP(32) ≤ 1.1·10⁻¹³; CM04 (g g > t t~ [QCD QED], Γ_t = 0: the top on its line mass, ymt := MT on the EW loop lines; QP, 4 points) binary64 ≤ 1.5·10⁻¹⁴, AP(32) ≤ 1.4·10⁻¹⁵; CM02, CM04 and CM05 check the engine’s set of sectors and their sum too; CM01 (e- e+ > mu- mu+ [QED], MadLoop double exports at the continuum, three Z-resonance points, zero widths and widths × 0.001 (electroweak-mumu-cms-small-width-control.json), both reglog conventions) ≤ 10⁻⁸ in binary64, double-double (the native executor with Python inputs) and AP(32), DD = AP(32) ≤ 10⁻²⁰ at every point, AP(40) = AP(60) ≤ 10⁻³⁰ at a Z-resonance point; CM09 (u d~ > e+ ve a [QCD QED], a0, the photon tagged: the conversion’s real part) = MadLoop CMS × MG5_aMC’s tagged-photon formula ≤ 10⁻⁸ (binary64 at 4 points, AP(32) at 1) (nightly: CM01, CM02, CM04, CM05, CM09). Generation: CM02 and CM05 176 s each, CM04 110 s. Default tier: loop_sm t t~ > h h [QCD] at zero widths equals real on-shell with ymt = MT, at the card and at a run-time MT, with Python inputs and as a stored public artifact. A derived mass on an external leg (the line mass, loop_sm’s MW) is read by the exact runtime’s sources at the point’s parameters (symbolica_exact._particle_mass; before, the value at generation: 2·10⁻⁴ off at MT = 172 on a card of 173, 3.8·10⁻⁴ on CM04’s Born). Generation cost: MG5_aMC restricts the transformed model by its restriction card, fixing the card’s parameters of value 1 (our loader fixes only zeros); the transform does the same (ComplexMassScheme.ones: the G_μ UFO’s TECHNICAL LogSwitch and GfRedefinitionChoice; its pole regulators epsUV and epsIR stay adjustable, MS-POLES §12.4: read only by the counterterms’ pole coefficients, they carry no dead branch, CM05 generates in 178 s against 176 s with them fixed). Left free, GfRedefinitionChoice’s dead re() branch carried complex conjugates of the pole masses into every resolved coupling (the 20 largest couplings × (ab + c) expand in 20 s to 646 MB of canonical text, against 0.03 s and 1 MB fixed), which made EW CMS generation 10-100× slower than real on-shell (CT lowering 256 s vs 41 s; the catalogue of u u~ > e- e+ > 25 min). Non-CMS plans, trees, parameter programs, kernels and Python binary64 virtuals are bitwise unchanged (loop_sm g g > t t~, u u~ > d d~; G_μ u u~ > e- e+ [QCD QED]).

  • No scheme choices in v2. The γ5 prescription and the finite terms are those of the model’s UV/R2 rules: loop_sm sets lhv = 1, and nothing is added to the four-dimensional numerator (MASTER_PLAN.md:1547-1556 [V]).

6.9 Direct-R2 bonus¶

The inherited per-diagram direct path stays, quarantined, for processes whose loops have at most four propagators. Its roles are validation and the model certifier (§6.3). v2 is model-R2 only.

The plan keeps the (k_μ², ε) monomial labels and the MuTensorNumerator ingress, so a future evanescent segment builder (X = Y + q·Z + μ·W, MASTER_PLAN §2.6) can feed the same tries. r2_strategy = "direct" is refused for other processes.

7. Colour¶

7.1 Representation¶

  • Colour flow. U(N_c) colour flow with explicitly graded U(1) pieces, so the dressed kinematics never depends on N_c.

  • Born basis. From build_color_plan (color/plan_build.py:17-24 [V]): single traces, open strings or products of these; optionally the DDM basis where the tree certificate applies.

  • Seed tables. K[c, b] = ⟨b|κ_c⟩, an exact Laurent polynomial in N_c with rational coefficients, computed by integer cycle counting (color/adjoint_kernel.py:36-62) or exact overlaps (color/connections.py:492) [V-s]. Fermion signs (§3.3) multiply the leaf weights, not K.

  • No Gram inversion. Loop colour is never decomposed into the Born basis; only overlaps are needed. This avoids the missing partial-contraction routine (tree report §8d) and the Idenso degree limits (assessment W3).

  • Born Gram. The Born–Born Gram matrix is needed only for the Born square and CT contractions.

7.2 Seed classes¶

  • Generic (default). As in §3.4: a per-skeleton colour-flow vector, term-factored. Per point, W_t(h) = Σ_b ⟨b|t⟩ conj(A0_b(h)) is computed once per distinct structure t, and then U0[s] = Σ_t c_{s,t}·W_t.

    • This is correct for any model whose coloured vertices lower to colour flow (Recola2 App. A method [L-s 1705.06053]).

    • Its cost grows with #skeletons × terms. For gg→ggggg FC it would be ≈0.7–2.4×10⁹ complex MAC per point [I], i.e. +0.4–2.4 s on Table 1a. The FC targets of the gluon-rich rows assume the certified compressions below, which is why WP2.4 builds the DDM and trace certificates first. The effect is negligible at 6 legs.

  • Certified compressions. Each needs a loop-level certificate: the model’s colour structures in the relevant orders, plus an exact colour-space identity on the smallest instance of the species pattern, plus the cited theorem.

    Class

    Seed per

    Gluon and ghost loops

    Ordering σ: Tr(F^{σ₁}…F^{σₙ}) (DDM) [L]

    Closed fundamental loops

    σ: Tr(T^σ)

    One quark line

    Quark ring: one class per proportional colour vector of its generalised arc word (WP2.4; the DDM (σ, L/R) q̄q ring [L] is not adopted, see below)

    Several quark lines

    Generic, or published decompositions when certified [L-s 1111.4193, 1310.0413, 1908.02695]

    With compression the per-point seed cost for gg→ggggg FC is ≈1.2×10⁸ complex MAC for 4 loop classes × 360 orderings [V-s Design 1 §5.1], about 2 % of dressing.

    The quark-ring compression leaves more classes than the DDM L/R form would. uu~→ggggg keeps 7,620 classes on its 120-element basis, against 2·5! = 240 L/R primitives. Its direct seed cost is therefore ≈7,620 × 120 × 64 helicity rows ≈ 6×10⁷ complex MAC per point, against ≈2×10⁶ for L/R [I]. That is about 6 % of the modelled FC dressing of that row (9.1×10⁸, Appendix B), before the FFT takes over the 74 certified loop orbits. The L/R re-expression is not adopted because rings already share one row per colour vector and a linear re-expression adds terms per skeleton to the dressing side. WP2.8 revisits it if G1 measures the seed share above that estimate.

  • Proportional classes (WP2.4). With compression, the seed table also merges classes whose colour vectors are proportional (colour._ClassKeys). These are quark rings of different arc words, and generic seeds equal to them. On uu~→ggg this cuts 315 classes to 99.

    • A quark ring is reduced once per relabelling of its external gluon labels (_ring_relabelling); keys, tensors and cells of the other members are relabelled. Measured compressed seed tables (Python, exact) [M]: uu~→gggg 828 classes on a 24-element basis in 10 s (53 s before); uu~→ggggg 7,620 classes on 120 elements from 103,770 skeletons in 176 s plus 11 s for the 74 certified FFT loop orbits (more than 40 min before; stopped).

  • Certificate predicate (WP2.4, interface to WP2.8). SeedTable.certified(combination) is true when every class of a seed is a Primitive whose compression is certified in the table; ColourSeeds.certified applies it per skeleton and is what ReferenceExecutor.run(..., certified=...) takes to admit schedule M at NLC and full colour. All gg→gg skeletons pass, uu~→dd~g only partly. The Python reference executor’s M still falls back to B on its structural check, because seed contents are not colour-ordered; the native schedule M splits certified skeletons into colour-ordered paths instead (loops/v2/merged.py, §5.6).

  • Closed-fermion orientation folding (Tr(σ) + (−1)ⁿ Tr(σᵀ) in one class) is used only when the attached vertices carry a C-parity certificate.

    • It is not used with Z or W attachments (judge finding 11). Those classes keep both orientations, and their dressing doubles.

    • The counts of Table 1a assume folding for the closed quark loops with QCD attachments (certified for loop_sm QCD vertices). Without folding, FC dressing of the gluon processes would be ≈1.75× (gluon loop plus three closed-quark classes doubled, with a massive b).

  • Native seed stage (WP3.1 Rust migration B, work/v2-native-seeds; RUST-MIGRATION.md §3.B). The seed table is built in rusticol-core loop_v2::generate::{seeds, networks, arena}; the Python stage (colour.build_seed_table / extend_seed_table with native_seeds.NATIVE off, native_seeds.python_oracle()) is its oracle.

    • Switch (rule 1): one dispatch at the top of colour.build_seed_table and colour.extend_seed_table (colour._native_seeds), so the main slice, the poles companion, the LC/NLC prune and the observables’ prune all take the native stage. Rule 2: the native stage covers every input the Python stage covers, so no feature keeps a per-request Python fallback; any native failure fails closed.

    • Per-skeleton work (B2/B3, phase 0): combinations, certificate bookkeeping, class keys, ratios, rows and class_of, class orders, the prune liveness. Python keeps what is per distinct object: each content’s compression (CompressedColour._content), the certificate check on the smallest instance and the cells (seed_cells, package C).

    • Exact reductions in-crate (networks.rs, phase 1): every distinct canonical quark ring (_reduced_primitive) and every generic seed (SeedColour.seed, the ring of the contents’ CompressedColour._exact_networks; each content’s network handed over as a product of distinct factors, its relabelled vertex structure and its attached blocks’ words, native_seeds._Networks.factored, expanded by seeds::factored_networks) is reduced natively, a faithful port of reduce_network (_join_strings, _Numbering, _fierz, _decode, the 1/sqrt(2) parity and ConnectedColorTensor’s normal form) in exact rationals with unbounded integer Fierz coefficients (symbolica Integer, a machine word until it needs more: no size cap, as the oracle’s Python integers), in parallel per need into an order-preserving collect (each result depends on its need only). The ring tensors fill _reduced_primitive’s cache (colour._NATIVE_REDUCED), so the cells read them (the Python _PrimitiveCells and package C’s NativeCells, both through Primitive.tensor / _reduced_primitive); native_seeds.NATIVE_REDUCTIONS off calls the Python reductions instead. No Symbolica licence call; Idenso/Spenso are not used because the stage’s oracle is this trace algebra and its output must be identical.

    • Plan deviation, ratified (coordinator ruling, slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-26 ~08:00: the in-crate reductions stay, Rust-first per HANDOFF §0.4, NATIVE_REDUCTIONS on, the Python reduce_network the oracle; the requirements audit of ff8b1b0e raised it): RUST-MIGRATION §3.B (B3) and PLAN I10/§3.4 keep the exact ring reductions in Python, batched, and rule 4 routes colour algebra beyond counting through Idenso/Spenso. Measured: the Python reductions alone take 33.7-37.7 s at uu~→ggggg FC (stage runs p1_uu7_fc, s5_uu7_fc, s5_uu7_fc_m2 under workspace/tmp/native-seeds/oracle/), above B’s 20 s share of I10, against 0.36 s in-crate (i10h_uu7_fc); at gg→ggggg FC the companion’s 43,200 generic seeds take 2.7 s in-crate. reduce_network is pyAmpliCol’s own Fraction trace algebra (pyamplicol.color.contraction_trace), with no Idenso/Spenso/Symbolica call, so the port reproduces the oracle’s normal form exactly; Spenso/Idenso would give another normal form and need a canonicalisation the Python stage does not have. Not in §3.B’s list: networks.rs, NATIVE_REDUCTIONS (default on) and the three-line hook in the read-only colour._reduced_primitive with its _NATIVE_REDUCED dict (rule 3: the oracle path is unchanged while the dict is empty, which python_oracle() ensures, also emptying the cache; past _reduced_primitive’s 2^14 entries an evicted ring is recomputed by reduce_network, equal and slower). The alternative, NATIVE_REDUCTIONS = False (the plan’s form), would fail B’s I10 share at uu~→ggggg.
