7.3 Seeds per point and FFT¶

U0 = A0† K. Leading colour is diagonal.

  • FC/NLC use direct exact-cast contraction, or the existing rectangular symmetric-group FFT where certified orbits exist (color/symmetric_group.py:362; Rust recurrence/symmetric_group_fft.rs [V-s]).

  • The auto | direct | fft policy and the reported algorithm are kept (MASTER_PLAN §2.16).

  • DoubleFloat and arbitrary precision use exact direct contraction.

  • Correlated FFT stays unsupported, as today.

  • Implemented (WP2.4). loops/v2/colour.seed_fourier finds the orbits of S_m on the external adjoint labels (all of them, or all but one when every coloured leg is adjoint) directly on the literal Born tensors and the seed classes: regular Born orbits, and complete loop orbits whose stabilisers carry signs (an adjoint ring is fixed up to (−1)ⁿ by its reflection). Each Born/loop orbit pair is certified on every exact cell, K[class(g), b(h)]·sign_g = k(h⁻¹∘g). Other pairs stay direct. The native V2SeedFourier (rust/loop-reduction/src/runtime/v2_seeds.rs, binding _loop.V2SeedFourier) contracts the certified pairs for a batch of helicity rows with SymmetricGroupFftPlan. Kernels are projected exactly per sector degree P and Born grade, then rounded once.

    • The slice’s SliceRequest.colour_contraction defaults to auto: binary64 at NLC/FC, with PointResult.colour_contraction reporting the algorithm. fft requires the FFT: it refuses a table without a certified pair and LC at generation, and it refuses, instead of silently contracting directly, every evaluation of the Python stage that contracts seeds directly (exact dressing, arbitrary precision, observable columns at ObservableSlice.of). Under auto, the Python stage’s exact dressing, DoubleFloat and arbitrary precision stay direct.

  • Native executor (M-QCD MQ-FFT, user 2026-10-28 ~15:35/~15:40). The production executor contracts the certified pairs with the FFT in its own carrier (rusticol-core loop_v2::fourier, the Python stage the oracle):

    • Record. plan_export.fourier_record maps slice.fourier’s orbits into the plan, structurally: per job (weight column of the slice’s own table over every basis element, i.e. the sector columns; Born order; loop order; Born N_c grade) the plan’s Born component of each Born-orbit element (-1: no seed weight reads it, its amplitude is zero for the FFT), the plan’s seed-class record and sign of each loop-orbit element (-1: no seed key reads the class at that order) and the certified pairs whose projected kernel is nonzero. It holds no weights. The plan v4 is unchanged (bytes equal under every policy); the record travels beside it (ExportedPlan.fourier, V2Executor(fourier=)) and is stored in the native process record (native_process, key fourier, the companion’s under scaleless), which the SDKs’ Rust runtime reads too (v2_runtime).

    • Certification at load (SeedFourier::load). The kernel k(x) of a pair is read from the plan’s exact weights of one recorded class (k(h⁻¹∘g₀) = s(g₀) K[c(g₀), b(h)]), and every recorded class of the orbit is checked on every Born element, K[c(g), b(h)] s(g) = k(h⁻¹∘g), exactly (rationals); a record that fails is refused. The covered (record, column, component) weights then leave the direct seed classes; the FFT adds s(g)·w(g) at the first element g of each class, w = Σ_a f_a ⋆ k_al with f_a(h) = conj(A0_{b_a(h)}). FFT and direct are equal before rounding by construction, whatever produced the record.

    • Transform. The tree engine’s SymmetricGroupFftPlan supplies the subgroup tower (Young’s orthogonal form, crate-visible levels with the integer axial distance of each generator); the forward and inverse transforms are rewritten generically over the carrier (real lanes: Re and Im of each SIMD lane), with the Young factors 1/r and sqrt(1 − 1/r²) and the inverse weights d_λ/m! formed in the carrier, so binary64, double-double and MPFR contract at their own precision (F[f ⋆ k] = F[f] F[k], one block product per pair). Tasks of 16 Born helicity rows per job run in parallel, the rows folded into the transform lanes (one tower walk for 16 rows × 2L reals); the pairs of a job are grouped per loop orbit at load. The exact carrier (numerators only, no square roots) contracts directly.

    • Policy. V2Options.contraction (Contraction::{Auto, Direct, Fft}): auto runs the FFT where the executor has a record, direct never, fft requires one; the report counts symmetric-group-fft seed jobs, from which PointResult.colour_contraction and the public VirtualColorContraction (regular_kernels = certified pairs) report the algorithm. NativeExecutor takes the request’s policy (fft without a record is refused at construction); the certified-scaleless companion runs auto (or direct). Stored observable column sets keep the direct contraction (their own seed records). A forced FFT the FFT cannot serve (no certified pair, LC, declared observables) is the listed generation refusal forced-seed-fft-unserved (refusals.LOOP_ADMISSION_REFUSALS, remedy auto), never a silent direct contraction.

    • Public route. color.contraction = "symmetric-group-fft" maps to fft (the v2 FFT needs no colour declaration at full colour); LoopV2ExecutionMetadata.color_contraction is auto | direct | fft. auto is not tuned per process: every certified pair takes the FFT.

    • Oracle of the contraction (V2Executor.seed_values, NativeExecutor.seed_values): the seeds U0 per point and seed key under auto, direct or fft, in every floating carrier. FFT and direct sum the same exact weights times the same Born components, so they agree to the contraction’s own rounding with no reduction behind it; the virtual’s comparison bounds the amplified difference only through the stability estimates.

    • Evidence (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_seed_fft.py): the seeds FFT = direct normwise per point within 2⁷ u in binary64 and double-double, and the virtual within both evaluations’ rounding envelope (10 (E_fft + E_direct) + 16 u S per Laurent coefficient; Born and local components bitwise), on g g > g g and u u~ > g g g (default tier, full colour), g g > g g at NLC, and nightly g g > g g g, g g > g g g g, u u~ > g g g g, g g > t t~ g g, g g > u u~ d d~ (two quark lines, S_2), g g > g g g g g (S_6) and u u~ > g g g g g (S_5); native FFT = the Python stage’s FFT; fallback (no certified pair: u u~ > d d~ g, and the three-quark-line u u~ > d d~ s s~, which has no external gluon; a three-line process with an orbit needs two external gluons, 2 → 6) reported direct; forced FFT in binary64, DD and MPFR; a record that does not certify is refused; the public route and the SDK runtime run and report the FFT.

7.4 Projection¶

For each virtual squared-order sector:

  1. P is the maximum N_c degree over all non-zero exact cells: seed cells for every class contributing to the sector, CT cells (with CT colour grades, physical_color.split_color_grades [V-s]) and field cells. P is structural and independent of helicity, ε and numerics.

  2. LC keeps degree P; NLC keeps P, P−1 and P−2, odd powers included; FC keeps all.

  3. N_c = 3 is substituted after projection, and the external average after that. N_f has degree 0.

Born sectors keep independent degrees. Truncation acts on the contracted cells K[c, b], never on a Gram matrix alone (contracts §2.6 caveat). Without a continuation, only FC is available (§6.7).

7.5 Leading colour, structurally¶

LC prunes skeletons before any numerics, by the face rule of the leading-colour report §4.1 [V-s, verified there against exact SU(N_c) overlaps].

Implementation.

  • Pruning. The trie builder applies the local rules: word admissibility through the tree engine’s LC segment tables (generation/dag_color.py:186-243, 1041-1076 [V-s]) extended by cut-terminated segments; the arc rule; no closed quark loops; no U(1) or Fierz-singlet currents. Each surviving class’s degree is then certified exactly from its seed table.

  • Seeds. LC seeds are diagonal: U0 = N_c^P·κ·conj(A0(σ, h)). There is no interference between orderings and no Gram matrix.

  • Strict-LC Born. The strict LC Born uses the graded Fierz and U(1) pieces (§3.2 item 4).

With a massive b the gluon-process ratios are 0.26 (dressing), 0.33 (families) and 0.27–0.30 (time), because FC then has one more closed-quark class. The inherited engine measures LC/FC ≈ 1, because it projects after computing everything (colour-measurements.json [V-s]).

The same face rule makes seeds composition-independent within an ordering, so schedule M is valid at LC without any decomposition theorem [I] (§2.2).

Native per-point inputs at LC (package lc-perf, 25 Oct; measured). With the WP3.1 native inputs (4e9b5a9e) LC was not cheaper than FC per point on five G1 rows (LC/FC 0.98–1.28, slower on four) and slower on gg→tt̄e⁻e⁺g (QCD, 1.21) and uu~→ggggg (1.19): the LC dressing was a third of FC’s, but its trees, Born and counterterm inputs cost more than FC’s (gg→gggg: about 930 of 1,033 ms against 650 of 913 ms). Three causes, all in native_trees.py and loop_v2::trees, none LC-specific code:

  1. Graded counterterm slots. The LC/NLC counterterm program carries each CT slot per N_c grade of its formal-N_c continuation (counterterm_slot_order(..., grade), §6.7), so it was larger than FC’s (gg→gggg: 764,800 against 499,160 interactions), and its closure formed every ket component, including those whose N_c powers lie below what the projection keeps. prune_program now drops the ket components no interference can read (_live_ket: no overlap cell the projection keeps), the closure terms left empty, then every current that no closure term and no plan block row reads (through other currents too), and the kernels no interaction uses (gg→gggg LC: ket 860 → 240, CT interactions 764,800 → 179,280; FC 499,160 → 240,120). The LC Born metric was already diagonal in the colour orderings (120 cells against FC’s 14,400 at gg→gggg) and the LC seeds diagonal (§7.2), so the squaring needed no change.

  2. Whole model blocks as kernel inputs. Every vertex and propagator kernel of both interaction programs took the whole model block of its state as inputs and copied it per row: 20 of a gluon vertex’s 36 inputs in the trees, 161–189 of 177–203 in the counterterm program (its model holds every coupling, multiplicity and slot switch of the request). A kernel now reads the model parameters its expressions hold (tree schema 3: the third entry of a kernel’s shape lists their indices into the state’s model block, read at state component model_offset + index).

  3. Latency-bound closures. The Born and counterterm root closures ran per point and Born row, each kernel monomial a serial chain of complex products. They now run over the batch in lanes of 8 points and the rest of the batch in lanes of 4, 2 and 1 (so no lane repeats a point; lane_runs), the lanes in fixed-size arrays, and for binary64 in AVX-512 or AVX2 when the running CPU has them (chosen at run time, never from the build host).

Values. By construction a lane performs one point’s operations in Complex<T>’s order (products and sums never fused, at every lane width and vector width), a pruned component only ever met zero metric cells, and kept currents sum the same interactions in the same order. Schema 3 is the one change that is not exact by construction: a kernel’s canonical stage (assemble._canonical_stage) now numbers its positional symbols over fewer model parameters, and Symbolica orders terms by the little-endian bytes of the symbol ids, which follows the position only below 256 symbols. A kernel whose stage had more symbols before could therefore sum its terms in another order, a binary64 rounding change within the LC oracles’ tolerance; none was found. Checked bitwise:

  • test_pruned_tree_program_is_bitwise_the_unpruned_one (LC, NLC, FC: every native input and the evaluation with and without poles; each case’s program strictly smaller), test_native_inputs_do_not_depend_on_the_batch (eleven points in one batch against each alone), test_closure_simd_widths_are_bitwise_equal (below);

  • native inputs plus evaluations (poles none and all) of 11-point batches against the slice 19083c10 on its own native: nine pairs up to six legs (gg→ggg LC/FC, uu~→ggg LC/NLC/FC, uu~→dd~g LC/FC, uu~→e⁻e⁺gg LC, gg→tt̄gg LC), the evidence audit’s 20 comparisons at gg→gggg and uu~→gggg (LC and FC; binary64, double-double, 40-digit arbitrary precision; poles none and all), and the three 2→5 rows at seven legs, LC and FC (uu~→ggggg, uu~→e⁻e⁺ggg, gg→tt̄e⁻e⁺g QCD; head ef400de5, 25 Oct 06:29–06:43 UTC): byte-identical value reprs in all.

Vector widths after relocation (§0.2). The binary64 closure kernels take AVX-512 or AVX2 by what the running CPU reports, so a relocated artifact may run a narrower width than its build host. RUSTICOL_TEST_KERNEL_SIMD=avx2|baseline caps the width of kernels::Simd, which the dressing, seed and interference kernels share, and never enables a feature the CPU lacks, and test_closure_simd_widths_are_bitwise_equal loads a stored native process (gg→gg LC, uu~→dd~g FC) in fresh interpreters capped at AVX2 and at the baseline: its native inputs and evaluations are bitwise those of the AVX-512 run. The Rust wide_closure_kernels_are_bitwise_the_baseline also passes in the release profile (cargo test --release -p rusticol-core --lib --features loop-v2 loop_v2::trees, the production build’s codegen settings), where the kernels are vectorised.

At gg→gggg the LC inputs split into the interaction programs 40.4 ms (FC 50.7), the closures 19.7 ms (FC 60.9) and the interferences 0.7 ms (FC 11.4). What is left of the LC inputs: the counterterm program recomputes the plain tree currents the trees’ program already holds (2,320 of its 6,736 outputs at uu~→gggg LC, about a sixth of its finite interactions), and the closure kernels are expanded monomial sums (a three-gluon closure: 72 monomials, 288 complex products, where a contracted form needs about 30; a factorised form changes the rounding). The interaction-program kernels are interpreted Symbolica evaluators until the binary64 plane applications of artifact-portability land.

Lane runs. A chunk of lanes costs about its instruction count whatever its width (gg→gggg, binary64 closures per chunk of 8 / 4 / 2 / 1 lanes: FC 487 / 449 / 350 / 249 ms, LC 154 / 169 / 125 / 91 ms), so a batch runs in lanes of 8 and its last points % 8 in one chunk of the narrowest width that holds them (lane_runs; padded lanes repeat the chunk’s last point and are dropped). B = 128 and B = 1 run as before (re-timed at 43befe28, 25 Oct 06:57–07:03 UTC during a test sweep, FC / LC ms: gg→gggg 398.6 / 167.0 at B = 128 (LC/FC 0.42) and 3,748 / 1,404 at B = 1 (0.37); uu~→gggg 84.8 / 39.5 (0.47) and 790 / 239 (0.30)); B = 9 at gg→gggg FC takes 764 ms of closures (8 + 1 lanes) against about 974 ms (2 × 487) with a padded second chunk of 8.

Pruning cost at export (Table 7.5c). prune_program is one linear pass: each closure block’s Born rows are marked once, up to the widest slot any term reads on it, the interaction rows are filtered and renumbered in place, and the counterterm record is left untouched when every ket component is read (full colour). Its first implementation appended one read per closure term, slot and Born row (about 14 M at gg→gggg FC) and copied every counterterm term and kept row. The pruned program is identical (JSON and saved kernels equal at gg→gggg and uu~→gggg, LC and FC). The pass stays in Python: at gg→gggg it takes 0.5 s, 2 % of the export (whose median grows by 0.8 s at FC and 0.2 s at LC), with an unchanged peak, and it moves to Rust with _CountertermTrees.of (A5), where the counterterm program is built, so that the dropped slots are never emitted.

The pass’s own traced allocation peak falls from 1,130 to 20 MiB (FC) and from 402 to 21 MiB (LC); at uu~→gggg it takes 0.12 s (FC) and 0.13 s (LC), from 0.32 and 0.20 s.

Plane kernels and the model subsets (merged with artifact-portability). The binary64 plane paths of loop_v2/trees.rs fill each kernel’s own model inputs, as run_interactions does: plane_interactions and plane_propagator take program.models[kernel] and fill state components model_offset + index in that order, and a propagator’s value width is inputs − 4 − models[kernel].len(). load_interactions reads each kernel’s (inputs, outputs, model indices) entry once: the indices must be increasing and inside the model block (StateLayout::model_block), and the (inputs, outputs) shapes select the plane or exact kernel per carrier. export_trees prunes the program first (prune_program) and compiles the plane applications of the kernels it keeps only, so a dropped kernel compiles no plane.

7.6 Next-to-leading colour¶

NLC keeps every class whose exact maximal degree over the sector’s Born basis is ≥ P − 2, and truncates the cells to degrees P, P−1 and P−2. No class is dropped on a literature-based expectation; the degree always comes from the exact seed table. Structurally:

  • gluon processes: NLC adds the quark-loop classes (P−1). The double-trace and off-diagonal weights of the same gluon-loop skeletons arrive through truncated seeds.

  • quark lines: NLC adds A^R, mixed and closed primitives, and every class whose exact degree reaches P−2.

Literature check (O14). In BDK’s q̄qggg colour sum [L hep-ph/9409393 eq. NLOCrossSection, l.1748-1772]:

  • against the leading (N_c²−1)² A_{5;1}, the other two orderings of A_{5;1} and two of the three A_{5;3} terms enter at relative N_c⁻², i.e. degree P−2, inside NLC;

  • the remaining A_{5;1}, A_{5;3} and A_{5;4} terms enter at N_c⁻⁴.

WP2.4 tests v2’s exact-N_c interference for uu~→ggg against this formula, with the partial amplitudes obtained from resolved-colour seed columns on the BDK colour structures. Revision 1’s claim that A_{5;3} enters only at N_c⁻⁴ was a misreading and is withdrawn.

NLC/FC cost ≈ 0.9–1.0: the value of NLC is accuracy, not speed. The tree NLC truncation (color/contraction_factors.py:100-108) is a different definition and is not reused for loops [V-s].

Opt-in, labelled, non-default modes [L 1209.0100 njet.tex:529-540, tab:timedsymgluons l.1231-1251; L-s 0907.1984]:

  • separate LC and (FC − LC) outputs for colour-expansion sampling;

  • integrated-equivalent full colour (NJet’s de-symmetrised colour sums). Valid only after integration over a phase space symmetric in identical final-state particles:

    • v2 generates loop seed classes only for the de-symmetrised orderings, and the seeds use the de-symmetrised colour matrix;

    • NJet reports 7 gluons going from 171 to 3.07 s;

    • labelled, never the default, never reported as pointwise FC; evaluated in WP4.7.

7.7 Directed colour correlations¶

V_{αβ,k} = B†K^{αβ}{BL}L_k + L_k†K^{αβ}{LB}B, with K_{LB}^{αβ} = (K_{BL}^{βα})† (MASTER_PLAN §2.17).

Status for loop-induced processes (m-lit): no Born, so the correlators act between loop amplitudes (a†K a on the amplitude basis), served by LIT-OBS as quadratic forms on the amplitude vector (full observable parity, RULED Q9; §7.14).

  • Each (history, direction) is a seed column. The second direction is seeded with K^{βα}, reduced, and conjugated after reduction. Results stay complex per history.

  • The colour operators come from color/correlator_matrices.py:295 [V-s], applied on the Born side.

  • The complete-family LC/NLC degree conventions (loop_runtime.rs:13-14 [V-s]) are kept.

  • Cost. Dressing and reduction scale with 2·N_hist columns: 42 at 7 legs with 21 pairs.

    • Directed tables by the seed-cell machinery (WP2.5). A directed table has |classes| × |basis| exact cells K[c, b] = <bra(b)|ket(κ_c)>. When every ket step is a gluon emission (dipoles, Casimirs, ordered emission histories), <bra(b)|ket(κ)> = <ket†bra(b)|κ>: observables.absorb returns each emission onto the Born side (the emission on a fresh label, contracted with the emitted one by SU(N_c) Fierz, colour.reduce_network), and the operator images ket†bra(b) replace the Born basis in the inclusive cell builder colour.seed_cells (primitives by integer cycle counting with the relabelling caches of §7.2, generic classes term-factored). The caches are shared by every table of a slice (_PrimitiveCells.rebased), so the tables of a complete family reuse each other’s overlaps, and the directed overlaps of counterterm and field cells share their literal structure overlaps (contract_cached). A ket with a quark-pair splitting keeps the generic contraction of the connected images (DirectedColour.generic_table), which is also the test oracle: the tables are equal cell by cell, exactly, in both directions, for every dipole of g g > g g, d d~ > g g and u u~ > g g g, ordered histories and emitter chains. Full colour builds one table per history (two when it is not symmetric); LC/NLC builds the |F|² tables of the complete family F plus the history’s own, and contracts every Born, counterterm and field structure pair of each family table for the family degrees.

    • Generation cost (measured, Python, exact; one dipole; generic contraction → seed cells):

Not measured, estimated [I]: uu~→ggggg (7,620 quark-ring classes × 120) needs about 5–30 min per FC table from the six-leg per-cell costs (0.17–0.71 ms per cell, ×3 for the larger rings), and its LC/NLC family about 1.5–6 h with the measured six-leg cache sharing (about four tables’ worth of work per table); the LC/NLC family degrees, whose counterterm and field overlaps grow with |F|² × Born structures × counterterm structures, are estimated at hours at seven legs (gg→gggg: most of its 349 s; its 36 tables alone take 52 s on the six-gluon classes built the same way). Full colour is therefore no longer a blocker for gg→ggggg (2 min per dipole, both directions), and is one for the full dipole set of uu~→ggggg only through those estimated hours; the remaining seven-leg cost of the LC/NLC families (tables and degrees) and of uu~→ggggg moves with the seed tables into the Rust generator (proposed for WP3.1’s goal and acceptance, WP2.5 open list; not yet confirmed).

    • Above the break-even, a generation-time cost model switches to schedule 3: F with amplitude-level (h, b) closures, plus a transposed NinjaRS reduction that returns each family’s integrals of all monomials once (request 2 in §11.5). Every observable then becomes a dot product.

    • The break-even is ≈15–20 columns at 6 legs and ≈45–60 at 7 legs [M/I Designs 1 and 2].

    • Schedule 3 is adopted only after a measured prototype, because the owner’s transposition study is a symbolic instruction count, not a timing (§11.5).

7.8 Caps¶

The loop path never passes max_sectors (color/plan_build.py:21 [V]), and the 12-gluon/int64 guard of color/adjoint_kernel.py is removed (WP2.4). Direct contraction is always available when FFT eligibility fails.

Verified for WP2.4 [V]:

  • loops/v2 calls neither color/plan_build.py nor color/adjoint_kernel.py. Its Born plan is the tree engine’s trace basis, and no caller in the repository passes max_sectors.

  • The seed FFT has no degree bound. It enumerates S_m only when |S_m| ≤ the Born basis size, the structural condition for a regular orbit, and contracts directly otherwise.

  • The native plan’s own bound is its factorial and u32 index storage.

  • color/adjoint_kernel.py has no gluon cap. The dense DDM kernel ((n−2)! entries, sweeps over S_{n−1}) uses int64 while its exact bound N_c^n·4^{n−2} fits, and exact Python integers otherwise. Above DENSE_ADJOINT_GLUONS = 12 an overlap is evaluated on its own (ladder_overlap: both ladders’ 2^{n−2} traces, integer cycle counting, about 6 s per entry at n = 13), so the tree DDM plan no longer refuses more than 12 gluons. The automatic tree basis choice still prefers the trace basis above that size; this is a resource preference, not a cap. Tests: every dense entry for n ≤ 6 at N_c = 2, 3, 5 equals ladder_overlap (all three accuracies), and the object fallback and a 13-gluon entry are checked.

7.9 Native colour cells (WP3.1 package C, RUST-MIGRATION.md §3.C)¶

The exact colour-cell stages run in rusticol-core (loop_v2::generate::cells, loop_v2::dipole_orbits; PyO3 v2_colour.rs; glue loops/v2/native_cells.py, loops/v2/dipoles.py). Every native stage equals its Python stage exactly, which stays the oracle (HANDOFF §0.4). No Symbolica state or licence is touched: exact numbers are symbolica::domains::{integer, rational} only (checked statically and by a no-key subprocess, tests/unit/test_loop_v2_native_cells.py).

Switches (rule 1: one flag per stage, dispatched inside the Python stage). native_cells.NATIVE_STAGES (default: all six; native_cells.native_stages(()) runs the oracle lane):

Stage

Switch site

What runs natively

"cells"

colour.seed_cells (the slice’s, the companion’s and the prune’s tables); observables.DirectedColour._table

CellEngine::cells: adjoint rings by face counts of their U(N_c) expansion, fundamental traces and quark rings (their reduced canonical tensors, _reduced_primitive) by exact contraction, generic classes term-factored (each distinct term structure contracted once per basis tensor, a class’s cells combined from those rows in parallel; equal values share one cell, so the seven-gluon companion’s 7.3 M cells hold a few hundred distinct values); relabelling caches on relabelled bras. _PrimitiveCells.native() is the twin engine; rebased copies share its caches both ways. Quark-ring seeds are canonicalised (colour._ring_relabelling) once per basis (native_cells._relabellings, dropped with the basis), so a table rebuilt on the same basis and classes (the degrees’, the liveness’, the LC prune’s) does not repeat it. Directed tables: the operator images ket†bra(b) of a history whose steps are gluon emissions are formed natively (cells::operator_image: connect, then absorb by the completeness relation τ^a_ij τ^a_kl = δ_il δ_kj − δ_ij δ_kl/N_c, generators normalised to Tr(τ^aτ^b) = δ^ab); a Born-side quark-pair splitting keeps the oracle’s images (DirectedColour.operator) with native cells; a loop-side splitting keeps DirectedColour.generic_table (Python, the reference route of §7.7)

The liveness of _prune_colour stays Python (no switch line is given to it; native_cells.live_classes is its tested twin). BornBasis.gram and contract_colour keep their Python bodies (twins native_cells.gram, contract_many).

Copies to keep in step (rule 3; RUST-MIGRATION.md §5.3 item 3). The "degrees" and "family" stages collect their key sets in Python copies of the oracles’ key rules, and both stages are on by default, so an edit to an oracle’s key rules has no production effect until the copy follows it. The owners of the oracles edit both, and the oracle tests (QCD controls only: an electroweak field-insertion or closure-term rule change is not caught by them) compare the two:

Rule 2 (fail closed). No stage has a per-request Python fallback: a native refusal raises. The one known refusal where the oracle returns a value is oracle defect 3 (a primitive class against a Born tensor with an open quark string: color.connections.overlap_traces drops the unglued bra string; strict xfail test_python_adjoint_ring_against_a_quark_bra_is_refused); no control reaches it (adjoint rings and fundamental traces arise only on pure-adjoint Born bases there). The routes that stay Python by construction (not fallbacks of a switched stage): Born-side splittings’ images, loop-side splittings’ generic tables.

Rule 9 (decodes). Consumer table: each seed or directed table built during generation decodes its own cells once (an extension only its new classes) for the Python consumers (_prune_colour’s liveness, SeedTable users, the exporter); the degrees decode no cell; the dipole operators decode their entries only when expanded (LoopSlice.dipoles, counted per entry). native_cells.decoded_cells() counts; the test asserts the generation’s count equals the cells of the slice’s and the companion’s tables.

C2: the batched seed-record projection for D’s _Exporter.seed_records. native_cells.project_records(slice_, columns, seeds, born_components, tables=None) -> (class_json: bytes, records_json: bytes): columns are the exporter’s SeedColumns, seeds its seed keys (combination, loop order) in plan order, born_components its dict, extended in place in first-seen order; tables maps id(column.table) to a NativeCellTable (default: encoded from the Python cells). The bytes equal json.dumps(records, separators=(",", ":")) of the oracle’s two lists exactly; a class no sector admits raises the oracle’s KeyError. D owns the plan’s call site (D3); the stored observable column sets’ seed records (export_plan(column_sets=...)) call it since generation-scale-2’s fix round 2 (plan_export._set_records, slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-26 ~15:10 item 4); the Rust API is cells::project_records (in-crate). Since generation-scale-2’s column_weights (merged with native-cells in its fix round 1), seed_records returns a third value, per column its seed-weight column (None when every column has its own): columns that differ only by their helicity rows share one weight list per class record, so D3’s call site passes each weight column’s first column (plan_export.weight_columns); test_loop_v2_native_cells.py checks both cases (sector columns, and g g > g g’s helicity-resolved columns with shared weights).

Measured (2026-10-26; this package merged on slice 392d3f4a, release native loop-native-native-cells-8ef63961 built with build_loop_native.py’s default codegen, 16 codegen units without LTO, not the shipped wheel’s one unit with thin LTO; loop_sm with the top, compiled once; QED = 0; one process at a time pinned to 12 idle cores of the shared host at load 120–280, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=12; the Python column is the oracle lane on the same inputs; evidence and stage digests in workspace/tmp/native-cells/oracle/p3/). Package C keeps no disk cache, so every stage time is the stage’s first computation in its process (cold for C’s in-process caches); the generation totals have the compiled model and the kernel caches warm (outside C), and no cold-cache generation total was taken. Every native table equals its oracle exactly where both ran; S5 of the slice and of its companion are equal in both lanes (u u~ > g g g g g) and to the earlier heads’ (g g > g g g g g).

LC pruning and loop families (investigation of slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-25 ~20:45 item 3: the top-free g g > g g g g g LC plan keeps all 4,707 FC families). Not a defect. A family is keyed by its propagators’ momenta and masses (§4), so a closed massless-quark loop shares its family with the gluon and ghost rings of the same topology: the prune drops the quark loops’ skeletons inside the family, and drops a family only when none of its skeletons is live, i.e. for closed loops of a mass class no gluon ring has (the massive top). With loop_sm’s top the families halve at every multiplicity; with particle_veto [t] they cannot, while the tries shrink alike and the LC plans with and without the top are the same:

Building the LC tries once, with keep, would remove the rebuild (generation-scale-2’s generator_input). With an observable’s tables the liveness dominates instead: at u u~ > g g g g g LC with T12’s family (the slice table and 50 directed tables as criteria) _prune_colour takes 129 s in Python, its native twin native_cells.live_classes on the same tables (their native handles) 1.25 s (3,120 of 7,620 classes live). _prune_colour has no switch line of package C (§5.2 of the migration plan); the line is the coordinator’s to assign.

7.10 Amplitude colour basis (loop-induced, M-LIT LIT-COL)¶

A loop-induced request has no Born to project the loop onto (blocks.born_orders == ()), so the loop amplitude stays a colour vector (M-LIT PLAN §2.a.2 items 1–3). colour.amplitude_basis(table, kets) returns an AmplitudeBasis:

  • T: the distinct literal tensors of the class expansions κ_c = Σ_t c_{c,t} |t⟩ (SeedTable.tensor; class order, then each class’s canonical term order), then those of the counterterm kets not already in T (sorted; native_cells.counterterm_tensors collects a slice’s from the _DegreeKeys counterterm keys, every site closed). Equal literal tensors are one element. The analogue of the Born-interfered seed basis (assemble._born_tensors).

  • Cells c_{c,t}: per class the (t, Laurent) pairs read off its own expansion, exact in N_c, its 1/√2 power folded (an odd power is refused, as in seed_cells). Nothing is overlapped, projected or inverted.

  • Metric G_{tt’} = ⟨t|t’⟩, exact in N_c: BornBasis.gram of T as a seed basis (AmplitudeBasis.seed_basis, also the basis of the seeded oracle F2), i.e. contract_colour with the relabelling-orbit cache; natively cells::gram.

  • Full colour only (M-LIT Q8): no N_c grade, no truncated metric; cells_at_three / metric_at_three substitute N_c = 3. T may be linearly dependent at N_c = 3; |A|² = a†Ga needs no inversion (§7.1), and per-component values a_t are not physical (checks use G-norms or G a).

  • Colour zero (AmplitudeBasis.colour_zero, the one exact zero of M-LIT, Q13): every c_{c,t} vanishes exactly at N_c = 3 and no counterterm ket carries a tensor (e.g. tr(τ^a) = 0 at h > g a). Every other zero is numerical.

  • Seed contraction: without a Born, LoopSlice._plan_contraction applies colour.amplitude_contraction (the symmetric-group seed FFT contracts Born amplitudes, of which there are none): "auto"/"direct" contract directly, a forced "fft" is refused typed (forced-seed-fft-unserved).

The native stage equals the oracle exactly (tensors, cells, ket elements and metric as formal-N_c Laurent polynomials), independent of the thread count (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_amplitude_colour.py: synthetic tables of every class kind built without generation, g g > h, g g > h g, u u~ > h g, g g > g g h, g g > z z g). The Born-interfered seed tables, plans and tree programs are unchanged.

7.11 Loop-induced |A_loop|² on route R1 (M-LIT LIT-AMP)¶

loops/v2/induced.py (Python oracle) and the native amplitude mode serve a request without a Born (SliceRequest.contribution = "loop-induced", routed by LIT-REQ):

  • Generation. LoopSlice._generate builds the families, schedules and CT program as for a virtual; sectors are loop × loop pairs (ℓ, ℓ′), ℓ ≤ ℓ′, weight κ = 1 or 2 (induced.loop_sectors; the pair type’s first slot holds the conjugated loop order); induced.bind attaches T (§7.10) and the exact colour-zero loop orders (an order with no live cell and no CT ket; an unrouted order must show the single-coloured-attachment rejection in a field-level recursion at that order, else no-loop-amplitude). No certified-scaleless companion is built (only the split pole selections read it).

  • Plan (route R1, schema 5). One-hot columns (h0, t), column = row·T + t: the column seeds its own row (column_rows = [[h0]]) with weight column t, whose class records hold c_{c,t} at N_c = 3 on one unit Born component (plan_export._Exporter.amplitude_seed_records). Dressing, tries, kernels and reduction are the seeded path’s, unchanged. Amplitude-mode plans are schema 5 with capability rusticol.loop-runtime.v5; seeded plans keep schema 4, binary FORMAT 3, capability v4 and their bytes (Q42). An exact colour zero (T = 0, h > g a) is a zero-column plan.

  • Native amplitude sum. loop_execution sums per (loop order, column) slot a = i/(16π²) Σ_f Ω_f over the point’s lanes in key order (families in plan order); the amplitude-mode result assembly is chosen once per call. A point returns only its amplitudes (with a check, their re-test and the budget Σ_f |ΔΩ_f|/(16π²) per slot), O(rows × T) values per loop order; raw lanes only with raw_lanes. The native trees give the rows’ unit Born components and the raw counterterm kets (TreeInputs::kets), mapped onto T by induced.ket_map (stored with the process).

  • Canonical squaring order. Written once here and implemented once per carrier class (Q41): |A|²_s = (1/avg) Σ_{(ℓ,ℓ′) ∈ s} κ Σ_h Σ_k Σ_{i+j=k} Re Σ_t conj(a_{ℓ,h,t,i}) Σ_{t′} G_{tt′} a_{ℓ′,h,t′,j}: sectors in order, their pairs (ℓ, ℓ′) sorted, then helicity rows h in plan order, then the Laurent coefficient k = [finite, 1/ε, 1/ε²] with i ascending, then t, then t′; each total divided by the average at the end. Binary64 runs interference::square_amplitudes (PyO3 square_amplitudes); DD and arbitrary precision square the exported amplitude vectors in Python’s Decimal (induced.square), operation for operation. The finite part of |A|² is exact only if a_{−1} = a_{−2} = 0 (O(ε) amplitude terms are not computed): the finiteness probe checks it.

  • Term floor (the scale of the estimates). Scales measured after the integration fail where families integrate to zero by themselves (Landau–Yang) or are finite at an order (massive loops, 1/ε²), M-LIT DECISIONS 2026-11-06 ~09:00 (1). The scale is the per-row term floor S_k(h) = max(S_term,k(h), S_term,0(h)), S_term,k(h) = Σ_t T_{h,t,k} √G_tt + ‖A^CT_{h,k}‖G with T{h,t,k} = Σ_f Σ_α |N_{f,h,t,α}| |I_{f,α,k}| / (16π²) and I_{f,α} the integral of monomial α of family f: natively one unit-numerator reduction per monomial, family and point (V2Options::term_scale, requested with the stability checks: C(R+4,4) lanes per family and point; TIRust’s moments give it without extra reductions), in the Python oracle its own unit numerators through the reducer (induced.term_values). The stability estimate’s floor at the |A|² level is S = Σ κ Σ_h Σ_{i+j=k} S_{ℓ,h,i} S_{ℓ′,h,j} / avg (induced.scale); budgets are quadratic in colour-metric norms (induced.quadratic_budget). Every zero other than the colour zero is reported numerically against E and S (Q13).

  • Probes (induced.probe, PLAN §2.a.7): per (loop order, row) the residues ‖a_{−k}‖_G (finiteness, k = 1, 2) or ‖a(ε_j → p_j/E_j)‖_G at every k (Ward, on a full-kernel slice, massless gauge bosons, zero widths outside the complex-mass scheme) against E_k = SAFETY·(‖δa_k‖_G of the re-test + the largest over rotations of ‖δa_k‖_G) + FLOOR_UNITS·u·S_k(h), the calibrated RECOMMENDED_CHECKS (rescaled re-test + one generic rotation); pass within ×10 E (Q12). The rotation budget (induced.rotation_errors) compares the raw lanes and the CT kets after removing each row’s little-group phase (from every Laurent coefficient), summed over the lanes so that no two cancel: a true residue rotates with its row’s phase, rounding noise does not. It is what covers the Furry zeros (g g > a a a, g g > h a), whose numerator coefficients cancel between the loop’s two orientations inside each family, so that their term floor is at rounding too (without it the DD probes of g g > a a a reported 6e28 and of g g > h a 4e29). A Ward residue stands on the PHYSICAL amplitude’s term floor (induced.ward_floors: the largest over the substituted leg’s helicities), as ward.py’s criterion does: the substituted amplitude’s own floor can be at rounding (g g > h: its numerators vanish term by term). The floor, a magnitude, is formed once per point in binary64 (induced.physical_floors: the term scale’s unit reductions cost 51 s in double-double against 3 s in binary64 on g g > z z g); the probes of a point run as one batch with the re-test and one batch of rotated runs (induced.probes). The amplitude is linear in the substituted vector, so c = i adds nothing to c = 1 (ward.WARD_FACTORS serves the Born interference’s real part).

  • Generation-time probes (induced.generation_probes, called by loop_service._loop_induced_probes for a loop-induced process only with generation.loop_induced_probes = true; Q12, Q7). Off by default (USER / DECISIONS 2026-11-08 22:34 (3), superseding Q12 (a)’s probe of every request as the default): nothing the artifact stores or evaluates depends on them (the plan is written from the generated process before they run; plan SHA-256 and binary64 values bitwise equal with and without them), so the default generation runs none of their stages and records loop_induced_probes = {"status": "off"} (not run, never a pass); the exact helicity-zero filter (Q10, it changes the artifact) keeps its own binary64 pre-screen, which shares probe_point / _probe_runs / physical_floors. When enabled: on a probe slice of the request with every non-zero external width fixed to 0 (the complex-mass scheme keeps its masses) on the full tree kernels (ward.ward_slice; the production slice itself when it already is one), at the generation validation point farthest from every tree pole (the smallest |s_I − M²|/M² over the leg subsets of a tree propagator and the model’s massive particles, recorded) lifted once to exact momentum conservation with mass shells at 2 × the working digits of the last carrier (induced.probe_point), so that every carrier evaluates the same exact point; the finiteness probe and one Ward probe per external gluon / photon species (its first leg; Bose symmetry relates the others), and the Goldstone probe of each massive-vector species (§7.12). Carriers (induced.probe_carriers): every probe runs in binary64 first; a probe whose binary64 verdict fails or whose run the backend refuses (induced.ProbePointRefused) runs again in double-double, and only those probes; the verdict (×10 the probe’s own estimate) is the first passing carrier’s, else the last one’s; the term floors stay binary64, formed once per point (double-double only where the binary64 run is refused, induced.probe_floors). The probes reduce on NinjaRS (induced.PROBE_REDUCTION, recorded as requested / effective / reason; never the run-time auto rule). A probe failing after the fallback (or refused in every carrier) refuses the process (internal key loop-induced-probe) unless generation.allow_failed_probes; the outcome is the generation filter loop_induced_probes (per probe: deciding carrier, ratio, fallback reason with the binary64 ratio or the refusal, time; the stage times: probe slice, lift, floors, native passes per carrier, Goldstone slices and probes, total; an exact colour zero records exact_colour_zero). Binary64 keeps about 13 orders of margin below the O(1) residue of a missing family, counterterm or R2 vertex (estimate floor 16 u S); a dropped R2 vertex of g g > a a fails the binary64 Ward probe by 1e10-1e11 times its estimate and the double-double one by 6e26 (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_probes.py). Cost (lit-probe, one pinned core per row, loaded host, agent-reported, workspace/tmp/lit-probe/gen/final): the probe slice’s generation (≈ one production generation, 3-5 s on loop_sm 2->3), the lift and the probe executor (0.4-1.4 s), the binary64 term floors and passes: validation 3.3-13 s on the loop_sm 2->3 rows against 2.5-14 s of engine generation; g g > h h g g 18 s, g g > h g g g 29 s, g g > a a g g 93 s, g g > z z z z 103 s (engine 5-11 s); no binary64 probe failed or was refused on these 17 rows (no fallback ran), worst ratio 0.22 against the limit 10. The double-double probes alone (the former default) took 5-195 s on the 2->3 rows, 441 s and 789 s on g g > h h g g and g g > h g g g, and 4,218 s and 4,468 s on g g > a a g g and g g > z z z z (1.1-46× the binary64 ones). On the EW UFOs the probe slice is a full generation of the process (e+ e- > g g g: 37 s of 43 s). The probe executors’ lanes are sized to the probe batch (induced.probe_lanes: the smallest power of two holding the largest batch; a binary64 chunk costs its full lane count however few points it holds): paired same-core A/B against 16 lanes, identical verdicts, binary64 floors and passes 1.5-1.8× faster (probes g g > z z g 15.5 → 10.4 s, g g > a a g g 149 → 96 s, g g > h g g g 80 → 44 s; workspace/tmp/lit-probe/gen/lanes-*.json).

  • Storage and runtime. The native record holds the amplitude record (induced.amplitude_record: T, G at N_c = 3 as exact rationals, the CT elements, the ket map, the helicity rows, the colour-zero orders and the request’s exact colour zero, AmplitudeBasis.colour_zero as generated: the record keeps no cells, so StoredAmplitude.colour_zero reads it rather than guess it from the orders); the stored view is induced.StoredAmplitude. The execution and physics metadata declare contribution_kind = "loop-induced", interference = "conj(loop)*loop", empty Born orders, full colour and the pole selections all and none. V2VirtualRuntime reads its contribution_kind (and physics.contribution_kind) from that metadata (m-lit Q36) and returns a VirtualEvaluation with contribution = "loop-induced", zero-length Born fields and the computed poles as a necessary-only cross-check; the Runtime facade serves the kind with virtual result semantics (and the CLI’s evaluate takes any v2 loop runtime as a virtual artifact); the “uv” and “ir” selections are refused typed; resolved and correlated outputs are LIT-OBS’s.

  • Mixed artifacts. One run may store Born-interfered (v4) and loop-induced (v5) processes together (process.loop_induced = auto routes each request): every process requires exactly one v2 loop runtime and the manifest their union (loop_artifact::is_loop_v2_manifest, the native loader’s and the SDK’s admission); the selected process’s capability is checked against its contribution (loop_v2_capability), and the native admission reports it. The native SDK (V2Runtime) serves both process types of any such artifact (m-lit LIT-SDK): a loop-induced process’s executor amplitudes and counterterm kets are added in the Python API’s order and squared by the one native square in binary64 (induced.native_square’s square_amplitudes) and in v2_decimal::square_amplitudes_python (Python’s induced.square, operation for operation) in double-double and arbitrary precision (v2_runtime/induced.rs); its Born counts are zero and “uv”/”ir” are refused in the Python API’s words. The reduction-backend policy (“auto”, the per-type defaults, the routes’ auto sets and the reason texts) has one definition, rusticol_loop_reduction::reduction_policy, which loops/v2/reduction.py reads through PyO3 and the SDKs’ rusticol_virtual_set_reduction applies.

  • SDK stability monitoring (m-lit LIT-SDK, the revision-2c ruling). The binary64 stability estimate has one Rust implementation, rusticol_loop_reduction::v2_stability: the exact rotations (Rotation, default_rotation and the rotation specifications, Python’s floating-point steps and Fraction.limit_denominator ported exactly), StabilityChecks, the Born-interfered budgets (_lane_budget, rotation_budget, the re-test deviations, the absolute sums), the loop-induced ones (quadratic_budget with the colour-metric norms, the little-group row phases, the cross-backend comparison, the term floor row_scales / scale, the finiteness ratio) and StabilityEstimate.from_checks. The Python API’s binary64 native points (plan_export.point_estimate) delegate to it (stability.native_estimate, NATIVE_BINARY64; the Python assembly stays the oracle and serves the extended carriers, the Python reference executor and raw-lane runs); the SDK runtime drives the same checks (v2_runtime/monitor.rs: the reference evaluation in the reduction check’s frame, with a loop-induced point’s term scale, one evaluation per exactly rotated batch, the cross-backend evaluation on the other backend, as NativeExecutor._runs) and reports each point’s public estimate in diagnostics_json (rusticol_virtual_set_stability_checks, additive, ABI version 2). The collection is a compile-time choice of evaluate_batch (COLLECT): an evaluation without checks runs today’s code. Not served natively: the split pole selections with checks, the extended carriers and the resolved / correlated outputs (their estimates stay the Python API’s; the SDK says why). Tests: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_sdk_stability.py.

  • Public surface (LIT-API, m-lit Q36, Q11 (b), Q13, Q17, Q18, Q2 (b)). Results are VirtualEvaluation / ResolvedVirtualEvaluation with contribution = "loop-induced": Born fields zeroed (born_orders = (), zero-length Born axes, no Born colour IDs), the pole selections {all, none} (the result types refuse “uv”/”ir”, pole_parts None). Lane diagnostics carry finiteness (max over (ℓ, h) and k of ‖a_{−k}‖G / S_k(h), induced.point_finiteness) exactly when the call computes the poles and requests stability checks, and None otherwise (lit-api-b, DECISIONS 2026-11-07 ~04:35 (2)): its scale is the per-point term floor S_k(h) (DECISIONS 2026-11-06 ~09:00 (1)), which needs the tensor moments I{f,α} of every family at the point (V2Options::term_scale: one unit-numerator reduction per family monomial and point on NinjaRS; measured at B = 128, binary64, one core: 1.32× a plain poles-on evaluate on g g > z z, 2.03× on g g > h, values bitwise unchanged); no generation-time floor serves another point. The checks form the term scale anyway (the floor of E), so the ratio costs nothing there; a call without checks pays nothing (timing is in poles = "none", Q11). Without it the computed poles are the necessary-only cross-check and the generation’s double-double finiteness probe judged the artifact (Q12). An exact colour zero’s lane detail states the colour-algebra fact (every colour coefficient of the loop amplitude vanishes at N_c = 3), not one mechanism. Every estimate E and S per sector (VirtualStabilityEstimate.absolute / magnitude, max E/S as scale; for loop-induced the pole estimates are E/S): a zero is “zero within the estimate”, never declared (Q13); the opt-in rescue metric "scale" accepts E ≤ target·S. process.loop_induced = include serves the Born and Born-less members of one request as separate processes (v4 and v5), never summed. The shipped self-test artifact assets/selftest_virtual/li (g g > h, _internal.selftest_virtual_li) runs in pyamplicol self-test without a licence and touches no Symbolica state.

Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced.py (rows vs analytic oracles and MadLoop, DD, Python oracle = native, F2 = 2|A|², finiteness and Ward probes, colour and numerical zeros, schema 5, the public route and relocation); tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_api.py (the result types, the reduction option, estimates, the self-test without licence). The estimate’s calibration on g g > h h and g g > z (NinjaRS): §10.4 ‘Loop-induced’, tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_stability.py.

7.12 Electroweak-induced rows, the width policy and the gauge probes of massive vectors (M-LIT LIT-EW)¶

  • Width policy (RULED Q7). Decided once per request at generation from its contribution (ew_policy.tree_width_policy, called in the tree program of LoopSlice._generate for every loop-induced request and every electroweak one): a Born-interfered electroweak request keeps require_zero_widths and its electroweak-width refusal unchanged (its plans and conventions byte-identical); a loop-induced request is never refused for a width: its tree propagators keep the model’s widths fixed (MadLoop’s loop-induced default), its loop propagators stay widthless (assemble._mass_values: real masses), and its UV/R2 counterterm vertices multiply the same widthful tree propagators; under the complex-mass scheme every particle of a width propagates with its complex pole mass in the trees and the loops, with complex couplings, and an unstable external state is refused (model_cms.require_stable_external_states, cms-external-width, in _member and in _generate). loop_service._loop_induced_request no longer applies the Born-interfered guard. The policy is the slice’s width_policy and the artifact’s conventions.width_policy (ew_policy.scheme_conventions; policy “fixed-tree-widths” with the particles a non-amputated tree current propagates with a non-zero width, or “complex-mass-scheme”, the dry run’s names), so every loop-induced artifact records its conventions (QCD-induced ones: mass_scheme and width_policy).

  • Probe widths. ew_policy.probe_widths (the rule induced.probe_request reads): outside the complex-mass scheme every non-zero external width is fixed to 0 for the generation-time probes (a fixed width breaks the Ward and Slavnov-Taylor identities), under it the complex masses stay; the production artifact keeps its policy.

  • Goldstone equivalence (loops/v2/goldstone.py, PLAN §2.a.7 “massive external vectors”): in ‘t Hooft-Feynman gauge (every electroweak request; a model compiled in it), k·A(V) = η M_V A(G) per (loop order, row) on T, with A(V) the Ward-substituted amplitude (ε_j → p_j/E_j) and A(G) the request with leg j’s vector replaced by its Goldstone (the compiler’s ir.goldstone_partners; admitted as an external leg only inside processes.model.goldstone_legs, a gauge probe, never a physical process), same loop orders. η is a field convention (−i for an outgoing Z in MG5_aMC’s loop models, as the tree-level Slavnov-Taylor test fixes it), so the probe reads its unit phase from Σ⟨b, a_V⟩_G, b = (M_V/E_j) a_G, and requires every row to hold with that one phase and unit modulus within ×10 (E_V + (M_V/E_j) E_G) (the two sides’ amplitude_estimates; the vector side on the physical amplitude’s term floor). Where the Goldstone side vanishes (h > z a) both sides must vanish within their estimates. induced.generation_probes (when the probes are enabled, §7.11) runs it on one leg per massive species with a partner in a ‘t Hooft-Feynman-gauge request, binary64 first and again in double-double for a species whose binary64 verdict fails or whose run is refused (record goldstone: legs, worst ratio, passed, the deciding carriers, phases; a Goldstone side the engine refuses is recorded as skipped with its refusal text; when every side is refused nothing is probed and the record is status “not-run” with the refusals, never passed); unitary-gauge (QCD-only) requests are checked by the both-gauges equality (validation, test_loop_v2_induced_ew_gauge.py). Cost: one more probe-slice generation per massive species and its DD probe (a a > z z: about 85 s and 45 s, against a production generation of about 70 s).

Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_ew.py (h > a a, h > z a, a a > h, e+ e- > h a, the complete a a > a a, a a > z z, a a > h h, e+ e- > h h and LI-E4 e+ e- > g g g vs MadLoop, Recola and the oracles in binary64 and DD; AP on h > a a and on LI-C1’s g g > a a; the dry runs: the Born-interfered electroweak-width refusal, the loop-induced e+ e- > h h served with the fixed-tree-width policy), tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_ew_widths.py (e+ e- > h h and e+ e- > g g g at the model’s Z width; LI-43 g g > e+ e- μ+ μ- with fixed tree widths vs MadLoop and OpenLoops; widthless loop propagators on h > z a and a a > a a; the six LI-C1 complex-mass rows; the unstable-external refusal), tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_ew_gauge.py (Goldstone equivalence with η = −i on a a > z z, its controls, h > z a, the all-refused record; the both-gauges equality of g g > h z and g g > w+ w−) and tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_ew_public.py (the public route on a a > z z: the artifact’s width policy and generation-time probes, Goldstone included, and the stored process vs MadLoop). Default tier: one parametrisation per test (the h > a a row and its AP, e+ e- > g g g at the Z width, h > z a widthless, the complex-mass e+ e- > g g g, the refused g g > z z, the both-gauges g g > w+ w−; every unparametrised test); the other 18 ids are loop_nightly (lit-ew-b, slice-status DECISIONS 2026-11-07 ~09:12 (5)). The TIRust side of these rows follows LIT-TIR.

7.13 Loop-induced on route R2 and the exact helicity-zero filter (M-LIT LIT-R2)¶

Route R2 is the production form of amplitude mode (RULED Q14 = (a); the spike’s route R2k, m-lit DECISIONS 2026-11-06 ~09:00 (3)); route R1 (§7.11) stays as its oracle (export_plan(route="R1"), NativeExecutor(route=...); R2 is the default of every loop-induced plan).

  • Dressed rows. A schema-5 plan may declare "dressed": true (written only then; in the binary member the columns DressedFlag/Dressed exist only in schema-5 members, so seeded members keep format 3’s bytes). Its leaves seed one row and one object column: a constant seed, the leaf object is the leaf weight w_s. An edge joins each source row with every row of its content (the rule of schedule F), so a step’s rows are the helicities of the legs it has dressed, and a trace step’s rows are Born rows (plan/links.rs derive, the seeded walk with the empty leaf row and this link rule; checked against the exporter’s rows when written with links=True). Objects carry one column; the accumulators keep route R1’s columns (row, t).

  • Per-row closure. Each trace step closes each object row r into the columns of its Born row h(r) with the amplitude vector of its seed key, acc[(h, t)] += U[key][w(t)] Tr_α O[r] (closure::trace_rows_into), U[key][w] = Σ_c x_c Σ K[c, w] exact on the one unit Born component (LoopProgramV4::key_vectors, the value a route-R1 seed takes on its row). The step and its key are derived at load (RowTrace: every leaf under a trace step shares one key); the choice between this closure and the seeded trace is made per step, never per lane or point.

  • One trie per amplitude vector (R2k). The exporter splits each family’s skeletons by the exact amplitude vector of their seed (Σ_c x_c c_{c,t} at N_c = 3; plan_export.vector_groups) and builds one suffix trie per group in the family’s frame (schedules.build_trie); their steps follow one another and share the family’s accumulators. Seeded families and class tries are walked by one function (plan_export.walk_trie; only the leaf objects differ). A trie of one vector carries one column where a single trie would carry T (R2 “plain” loses to R3 by 1.5-2.7x, the spike).

  • Frames chosen for dressed rows (m-lit DECISIONS ~09:00 (3)). The generator prices frames on seeded rows (rows shrink as legs are dressed); dressed rows grow from the leaf instead, and the STRUCTURED model priced on dressed rows picks frames 15-22 % worse than exact counts on g g > h g, g g > h h and g g > h g g (the spike). So a loop-induced slice is re-framed at generation (LoopSlice._frame_dressed_rows, before induced.bind): per family, among its frames (schedules.candidate_tries), the one whose class tries take the least modelled dressing work (plan_export.dressed_frames): the exporter’s walk with dressed rows, each step priced at the cheaper of its fused and split forms by the reference executor’s MAC counts (ReferenceExecutor._dress without numerics: exact rows and links), plus the per-row closures; a tie keeps the generator’s frame. The readings of every frame first get seed classes (colour.extend_seed_table, their vectors on the extended table’s cells); once the frames are fixed the seed table is rebuilt over the plan’s readings, so T holds the tensors the plan reads. Route R1 reads the same frames. The choice is recorded (LoopSlice.dressed_frames) and costs 0.005-0.5 s (g g > z z g: 0.49 s, 48 families). Modelled dressing work: g g > z z -8.4 % (7 of 7 families move), g g > z z g -9.7 % (48 of 48), g g > h g g -2.7 % (22 of 37), g g > h g -0.2 %, unchanged on g g > h, g g > h h, g g > a a and u u~ > h g (the spike’s exact counts: 9-10 % on g g > z z and g g > z z g, within 0.5 % elsewhere). An opt-in aligned family export frame (the generation option LoopSlice.generate(aligned_frames=True), recorded as dressed_frames["aligned"], m-lit lit-cache; amplitude mode only; no module state) restricts the choice to frames whose last entry holds the process’s highest leg (plan_export.aligned_frame), so a propagator shared by two families has the same shift mask in both and common propagators keep their order: the frame in which a persistent tensor store keyed on shifts meets a parent’s pinches across reduce calls. It costs modelled dressing work (g g > z z g +7.6 %, g g > h g g +8.6 % over the default frames) and is off by default: measured with the store it is not adopted (it moves values at rounding and with them TIRust’s fail-closed decisions; m-lit lit-cache report §6.2).

  • Costs (binary64, one thread, release native). With the generator’s frames, at three fixture points (one 16-lane chunk): g g > h g g R1 790 ms/point (modelled dressing 76.6 M MAC per lane, peak 0.72 GiB) against R2 105 ms (18.0 M, 0.61 GiB); g g > z z g R1 4264 ms (310 M, 1.24 GiB) against R2 1196 ms (144 M, 0.86 GiB). In the frames chosen for dressed rows, at B = 128 (paired same-core runs against the generator’s frames on a loaded host): g g > z z g 349-358 ms/point against 354-388, dressing 112-116 ms against 121-136 (-8 to -15 %; modelled 130 M against 144 M); g g > z z 7.2-8.7 ms against 8.4-10.0, dressing median -18 %; g g > h g g 42-51 ms, dressing unchanged within the ±5 % noise (modelled -2.8 %); evaluation peak 1.43 GiB (g g > z z g, B = 128); generation 4.8-5.3 s at 0.57 GiB, the frame choice included (0.4-0.55 s). The generation-time DD probes under R2 take 28.5 s (g g > h g g, 0.76 GiB), 198.6 s (g g > z z g, 1.18 GiB) and 10.2 s (g g > z z): the reduction dominates them.

  • Equality. R1 = R2 in the colour-metric norm of the amplitude vectors (test_route_r2_equals_route_r1): bitwise in binary64 on g g > h, g g > h (t, b), h > g g, g g > a a (both), g g > h h and u u~ > h g, ≤ 1.1e-16 on g g > z z and ≤ 2.7e-15 on g g > h g (the sums run in another order); ≤ 2e-28 in double-double.

Exact helicity-zero filter (loops/v2/helicity_filter.py; RULED Q10 = (a), Q13; DECISIONS ~09:00 (2) and ~13:45). A row is an integrand zero when every numerator N_{f,l,h,t}(q) and its counterterm ket vanish identically; rows that vanish only after the integration (J_z rules, Landau-Yang) are not.

  • Binary64 pre-screen (keep only): one binary64 evaluation at the generation point farthest from every tree pole with the probes’ estimate (induced.probes: re-test, one generic rotation, row term floors); a row above ten times its estimate at some loop order and Laurent coefficient is live. The rotation budget is needed: without it the rounding of a Furry zero, whose term floor is rounding too, looked live.

  • Exact test: the remaining rows’ numerators are dressed natively over F_p, p = 2^61 − 1 (rusticol_core::loop_v2::prime::Fp, arithmetic "prime", numerators only), at k random points of the dressing’s inputs: every block-current component, the external momenta (the last leg balances), and every base of the kernel constants’ exact factored form (KernelConstants: b^e = u_b^(e L_b), L_b the common denominator of b’s exponents; a prime under a square root takes its root mod p where it has one; a flipped mass under a fractional power its own variable). Each coefficient is then a Laurent polynomial in these values; cleared of every base’s negative powers (a nonzero monomial, the u_b being drawn nonzero) it is a polynomial of degree at most d (degree_bound: the largest family’s positions times the largest kernel term degree plus every base’s largest negative exponent, the term degree counting every input power, the positive constant exponents and a split term’s block components), so a non-zero row vanishes at a random point with probability at most d/(p − 1) (Schwartz-Zippel); k is the least count with rows × (d/(p − 1))^k ≤ p_fail (stated: generation.helicity_filter_failure_probability, default 1e-12, 0 skips the filter; d, k, p_fail and the bound recorded). Zeros that rely on relations the random point does not keep (on-shell conditions, spinor identities of the tree currents) stay live. The bound is over the random point for the numerator reduced modulo the fixed p; it does not count two deterministic steps before it: a non-zero exact coefficient that vanishes modulo p (p divides its numerator) and a prime under a square root read as its root modulo p (p divides the norm of an element of Q(√b)), both needing p = 2^61 − 1 to divide an integer built from the model’s constants. A constant with no value in F_p (p divides its denominator) keeps every tested row live (Unrepresentable, as the Rust carrier’s non-finite marker).

  • Counterterm kets: no exact tree program exists, so a row’s ket counts as zero only where the request has no counterterm ket at all (native_cells.counterterm_tensors); with kets no row can drop, so neither the screen nor the exact test runs (the verdict records the kets as present and no row tested; g g > z z g saves the 12.5 s the filter took there).

  • Q13: if every row would drop, every row stays live and the verdict (every_row_zero) is a diagnostic. A dropped row keeps its (row, t) columns without a row (column_rows [] in the plan; the loader admits at most one row per amplitude-mode column): its trace writes nothing, its columns stay zero and are not reduced. On route R2 the loader prunes the dressed steps to the Born rows a column reads (plan/live.rs, §7.14): the dropped helicities are neither dressed nor reduced.

  • Generation: loop_service._loop_induced_filter runs it before the probes (helicity_filter.generation_filter), records loop_induced_helicity_filter in the process’s generation filters, and exports the process again from its slice when rows drop (artifact.reexport_process).

  • Verdicts: g g > h a (8 rows) and g g > a a a (32) are integrand zeros row by row (the loop’s two orientations cancel inside each family; no counterterm ket): every row would drop, so every row stays live and both are reported as zero within their absolute estimates (with folding off; folded, the default since lit-fold, both are exact fold zeros, §7.15, and the filter is skipped). The requests with counterterm kets skip the filter at generation (g g > h, g g > z z, g g > z z g and g g > h g g among the measured ones; the verdict records the kets as present); called directly, the screen and the exact test show the J_z-forbidden rows of g g > h and every Landau-Yang row of g g > z are not integrand zeros, and the screen proves every row of g g > h g, g g > z z, g g > z z g (72 rows) and g g > h g g (16) live. Cost: the screen 0.01-0.12 s at 2→1/2→2, the exact test 1-250 ms (g g > a a a); before the counterterm-ket skip the filter took 12.5 s on g g > z z g (peak 0.78 GiB) and 2.0 s on g g > h g g; d = 33 (g g > h), 36 (g g > a a), 44 (g g > z z, g g > h g, g g > h a), 55 (g g > z z g, g g > h g g), k = 1, the bound ≤ 2.4e-17.

Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_r2.py (R1 = R2 on lit-amp’s nine rows in binary64 and double-double, dressed plans’ links and binary member, the degree bound, constants without a residue, the F_p test’s verdicts at two seeds, the filter’s Q13 diagnostic, dropped rows as columns without a row, a partial drop through the public generation and runtime).

7.15 F1 proportional-chain folding and exact fold zeros (M-LIT lit-fold)¶

USER 2026-11-08 ~22:39 “Yes, and allow exact zeros” (m-lit DECISIONS 22:39, binding). Loop-induced route-R2 plans only (schema 5, dressed); seeded plans (schema 4), route R1 (the oracle) and every Born-interfered plan are never folded (loops/v2/fold.py, plan_export.export_plan’s dressing, LoopSlice.fold).

  • What folds. A family’s chains (the leaves of its class tries: colour-ordered skeletons read in the family frame, never Feynman diagrams) that close into the same loop orders and whose weighted numerators N_j = w_j Tr_j are exactly proportional, N_j = r_j N_rep for every helicity row, loop order and coefficient with r_j an exact rational, are dressed once: Σ_j U_j N_j = (Σ_j r_j U_j) N_rep. Within one class trie (equal vectors) the representative’s leaf weight becomes w_rep Σ_j r_j; across class tries it keeps w_rep under the seed key Σ_j r_j x^(j) (an exact combination of seed classes, key vector Σ_j r_j U_j): existing schema-5 records (SeedKey.classes, leaf_weights), no loader or kernel change. The folded class tries keep the first-seen order of vector_groups; a family left without a fold is exported by the unchanged path (a process in which nothing folds keeps its plan bytes; generation.loop_induced_folding = false writes the unfolded plans and records nothing).

  • The exact test (the helicity filter’s machinery, §7.13; no physics rule: no vertex type, Lorentz structure, C-parity, model or particle name decides a fold). Every input is a free variable: block-current components, momenta (conservation kept), masses and every base of the constants’ exact form, including a prime under a fractional power (fold._FreeValues: never its root modulo p, so an irrational ratio varies between points and fails; the filter’s own fixed root would give sqrt 2 a constant residue, 2 being a square modulo 2^61 − 1). (1) Candidates: one chain-resolved probe (fold.ProbeDressing: each chain closes into its own column; families batched by output size, memory only) dressed natively over F_p at one random point; chains with equal ratios of two random linear projections form a group (a ratio outside F_p, i.e. complex, is none; a chain zero there is a candidate zero). (2) Exact ratios: the same probe in the exact rational carrier at a random point of small integers, pruned at load to a few helicity rows covering every group’s representative (fold._cover, plan/live.rs); r_j is the exact quotient of the first nonzero coefficients, kept when real and equal to its residue (never a rational reconstruction of a residue, which is not unique). (3) Certification: every identity N_j − r_j N_rep = 0 (N_j = 0 for a candidate zero) at k fresh F_p points, each a polynomial of degree ≤ d once the bases’ negative powers are cleared (the plan’s degree_bound), so k is the least count with m (d/(p − 1))^k ≤ p_fail (m identities, the union bound; p_fail = generation.helicity_filter_failure_probability, default 1e-12, 0 folds nothing). A failed identity leaves its chain unfolded. The deterministic caveats are the filter’s: an exact coefficient whose numerator p divides reduces to 0; a constant without a residue folds nothing. Seed 0 (recorded): regeneration writes the same bytes.

  • Exact zeros (Q13 relaxed for zeros the exact algebra proves). A group whose combined vector vanishes exactly (Σ r_j = 0 in one class trie, Σ r_j U_j = 0 across) is not exported; a family left without chains is not exported; a loop order (or the request) left with no chain and no counterterm ket is an exact fold zero, recorded in the amplitude record (fold_zero: exact_fold_zero, loop orders, the certificate) and served as exactly 0 by the empty plan, with the certificate in the result detail, inspect() and the SDK capabilities (fold_zero); the helicity filter is skipped there (exact_fold_zero). g g > a a a and g g > h a are exact fold zeros; every other zero (Landau-Yang, J_z, integrated zeros) stays numerical.

  • Dependent reduction lanes (F1d). A stored column o’ of accumulator k is c times column o of the same Born row when every trace step closing into k has U[key][w’] = c U[key][w] (exact key vectors; plan::Dependents, derived by the family’s first reduction from the plan’s data, never stored, as plan::Walk; per observable column, so valid on row-pruned copies). Such a column has no reduction lane (lanes_of); after the reduction its Laurent integrals (and re-test) are c times its representative’s (a real c scales both parts, bitwise for c = ±1) and its term scale |c| times (loop_execution::Formed): every consumer (assembly, read_native, SDK) sees the same lanes as before. The rule is a property of the plan’s exact key vectors, not of the fold: of the 65 loop-induced fixture rows’ unfolded plans one already has such columns, u u~ > d d~ h (its one family’s colour vector has two entries in an exact ratio: 1 of its 2 columns per Born row), which therefore reduces half its lanes with folding off too (values at rounding level, lit-fold report); every other unfolded plan has none and takes the unchanged path bitwise; seeded plans never. Folded, the dependent columns per Born row are e.g. 48 of 132 (g g > h g g), 252 of 648 (g g > h h g g), 660 of 1560 (g g > h g g g), 408 of 1032 (g g > a a g g); rows whose colour basis has one element (two coloured partons) gain nothing here.

  • Record (generation_filters["loop_induced_fold"]): enabled, prime, seed, points, degree bound, identities certified (and failed), failure probability and bound, families, chains before / after, groups, chains folded, zero groups, zero loop orders, exact zero. Timings stay out of it.

  • Census and costs: lit-fold report (workspace/reports/engine-v2/m-lit/lit-fold-report.md).

Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_fold.py (the option; g g > h g’s pairs across and within class tries, the bound’s derivation, values within rounding, R1 unfolded, determinism; g g > z g folds nothing; sqrt 2, a parameter and i never fold; g g > a a a and g g > h a exact zeros, through the public route; dependent lanes), test_loop_v2_sdk_induced.py (the SDK’s exact fold zero).

7.14 Loop-induced observables (M-LIT LIT-OBS)¶

Full observable parity in the core (RULED Q9 = (a); full colour only, Q8): every output of a loop-induced point is a quadratic form on its one amplitude vector a_{l,h,t} (§7.11), squared by the canonical square (induced.square, the native square_amplitudes in binary64, Q41) with the total’s average and loop × loop sectors; nothing is dressed or reduced again: one call is one native batch (and one per rotation), whatever its histories and spin source assignments (evaluate_correlated_many forms every (assignment, history) output on the same amplitude vectors), on the call’s effective reduction backend, which the executor refuses typed when it does not run it (NativeExecutor.runs(reduction=)) (loops/v2/induced_observables.py; runtime runtime.virtual.V2InducedObservablesRuntime, the Born-interfered runtime’s calls and result types with contribution = "loop-induced").

  • Colour-correlated. A declared history X (ColorCorrelator) has the directed matrix M_X[t, u] = <bra_X(t)|ket_X(u)> on the amplitude basis at N_c = 3 (color.correlator_matrices.literal_correlator_matrices: the connected images of the unit literal tensors, every Laurent term kept), computed at generation (induced_observables.declare, the declaration resolved on the basis’s legs, all_color_through_order expanded) and stored in the amplitude record (correlators, written only with a declaration, so a record without one keeps its bytes): a load forms nothing. The output per sector is (1/avg) Σ_h Σ_pairs (a_l† M a_l’ [+ a_l’† M a_l, l ≠ l’]), the analogue of B† K_BL L + L† K_LB B; it is squared as M = H + iK (H, K the Hermitian parts), a dipole being Hermitian (K = 0). "born" is G: |A|². The identity history is G exactly and Σ_{j≠i} M_{T_i·T_j} = −C_i G exactly (every basis tensor is a colour singlet).

  • Spin-correlated. A spin vector v replaces leg j’s wavefunction on both sides (the Born-interfered convention: v in place of the polarisation vector, the crossing phase applied by the engine). By linearity A(v) = Σ_λ c_λ(v) A(λ), c_λ = −v · conj(w_λ) on the leg’s own polarisation vectors at the point (the tree program’s source records: momentum transform, source helicity; HELAS vxxxxx/massive vectors; w_λ · conj(w_λ’) = −δ; a massive leg’s mass its on-shell sqrt(p²)), exact for v in their span, which is v · p_j = 0 (ε±, and p_j for a massless leg, whose part the Ward identity removes: Recola’s projection; a massive leg’s three polarisations). A part of v outside that span has no meaning on the helicity amplitudes: the output is that of the transverse vector v − r the projection reads (r = v − Σ_λ c_λ w_λ; for a transverse v the literal source on both process types), and r enters the estimate (Stability below); nothing is refused, so a binary64-built k_⊥, transverse to its rounding only, is served at every precision. The amplitude with the literal source (the Ward mode’s loop-side source on a full-kernel slice) agrees to rounding for a gluon and a massive Z. A spin class is checked at generation to be vector legs with four-component sources (the tree engine’s rule).

  • Resolved. Per helicity row |A(h)|²/avg with one colour-contracted component ("full"); color_resolution = "amplitude-basis" gives per basis element t Re(conj(a_t)(G a)_t)/avg (metric (E_t G + G E_t)/2), a basis-dependent split (T may be dependent at N_c = 3) summing to the row.

  • Single-helicity selection (Q39). evaluate(helicities=[...]) is the sum of the selected rows’ |A(h)|²/avg with the total’s average, so a complete selection sums to it; no parity halving or Bose row mapping (Q37). The executor prunes the dressing to the selected rows: route R2’s dressed steps are pruned per call to the trace rows whose Born row is kept (lit-dress: a family runs its pruned copy whenever that drops a link, and its template when every link is reached, so a selection dresses, closes, scatters and reduces exactly the restriction of its rows: its counts equal those of the plan whose columns keep the selected rows only, tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_row_restriction.py; before, a family keeping more than KEPT_SHARE = 1/2 of its links ran whole, as seeded plans still do, and dressed, closed and reduced every row: an unselected row’s TIRust refusal then failed a point of a multi-row selection; a fused step zeroes only the rows its links write where every consumer link reads one of them, dress::written_rows) (NativeExecutor.runs(rows=...), the PyO3 rows mask, LoopProgramV4::live_rows), and at load to the rows a column reads (the helicity filter’s drops). The selection also forms only its kept rows’ trees and counterterm kets (the amplitude-mode tree program restricts per call without observable columns, TreeProgram::live_rows, and at load for a plan keeping some rows; report counts tree closure rows, tree interactions), exports only their amplitude slots and kets (the PyO3 output’s amplitude_rows) and assembles and squares only them (induced.read_native; the SDK’s Induced::vectors_point likewise). The backward pass of prune_family keeps a trace step’s object rows whose Born row (RowTrace::rows) is traced; the leaves seed one constant row, so nothing dies forward; the pruned copy keeps its row closures. Seeded plans take the unchanged path (traced = None).

  • Stability. "born" without spin sources over every row is |A|² itself and carries the inclusive evaluation’s estimate (plan_export.point_estimate). Every other output: a rotation’s budget is the output’s own deviation at the rotated point (spin vectors rotate with the momenta; a row’s little-group phase cancels in a†Ma); the reduction check’s is the elementwise bound Σ (e^T|M||b| + |a|^T|M|e + e^T|M|e) from the re-test’s absolute amplitude errors; a spin vector with a non-transverse part of Euclidean size ρ (transverse_residual: |r|, less its part along p_j for a massless leg; exactly 0 when v · p_j = 0 in exact rationals) determines the transverse vector it stands for only to within ρ, so the budget spin-transverse (stability.TRANSVERSE, added like a reduction check’s) is the same elementwise bound for the coefficient changes |δc_λ| ≤ ρ |w_λ| (Cauchy-Schwarz: every transverse vector within ρ of v − r): ~1e-13 relative for a binary64-built k_⊥, of the output’s size for a v far from transverse, whose point is then returned with that estimate (the correlated calls take no rescue policy, rescue.RESCUE_SCOPE; escalating is the caller’s decision); S is the same |M| form of the row term floors (term scale + counterterm kets), never the output (Q13). The finiteness ratio is taken over the rows an output reads.

  • Mappings. A permuted mapped process reads the representative’s histories on its labels (mapping.MappedObservables), its momenta, spin legs and resolved rows relabelled by the member; its helicity selections name the member’s own rows (its resolved order and tree IDs), each read as the representative row it relabels.

  • Runtime. The observables run the artifact runtime’s current executor (clear replaces it) under its lock (the inclusive calls share it); the carrier forms are built once per precision.

  • Refusals. No colour-flow selection (full colour); an undeclared history or spin leg; color_resolution on a Born-interfered runtime.
