Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_observables.py (Recola’s loop-induced colour, spin and spin-colour correlations on g g > h g g and u u~ > h g g, tests/fixtures/loop/required/li/correlations, tools/loop_reference/recola_correlations.py’s loop-induced mode; the exact identities; the literal-source oracle; resolved and selection sums; double-double; refusals), rust/crates/rusticol-core/tests/loop_v2_plan_derive_bound.rs (dressed rows pruned at load and per call). The both-backends check (L6) is tools/loop_v2_observables_backends.py (runs once TIRust serves the loop-induced observable calls; its binary64 bound 10 max(E_N, E_T) takes the estimates of the rescaled reduction re-test and three generic rotations: with the cached reduction check alone the masters’ own rounding is missed, §10.4 (T1.T4 of u u~ > h g g at point 1 is 25 times its estimate), and one rotation is one sample of the dressing’s rounding, which no re-test repeats (against double-double, stability.RECOMMENDED_CHECKS leaves 3 of the rows’ 2322 binary64 entries beyond 10 E, up to 14.7 at a numerical-zero amplitude-basis anchor; two or three rotations none).

8. Helicities and spin¶

8.1 Catalogue, selection and identifiers¶

  • Catalogue. The full Cartesian helicity catalogue in leg order is kept (contracts §2.1).

  • Selection mask. Massless chirality conservation plus Born-zero rows. A row h with A0_b(h) = 0 for all b gives a zero seed and is dropped at the leaves, but only for observables whose bra is the Born (assessment R3).

  • Identifiers. Resolved helicity IDs keep indexing the full catalogue. structural_zero_helicity_count, hard-coded to 0 today (runtime/virtual.py:508 [V]), reports the dropped rows.

8.2 Summation¶

  • B and M sum the helicities of each block at the step that attaches it: objects carry only rows of undressed legs.

  • F keeps attached-leg rows and sums at closure. That makes it the natural producer of helicity-resolved outputs.

8.3 Parity halving (optional, wave 4)¶

Identity. Under three conditions, the conjugate helicity configuration gives U0(c,−h)·c_α(−h) = conj(U0(c,h)·c_α(h)) per monomial in the real monomial basis:

  • real external momenta;

  • real couplings and masses (no widths);

  • parity-certified kernels: tree, loop-segment and CT.

Hence C_α = 2 Re C_α^{half} [I, derived; the absorptive parts sit in the integrals, which are applied afterwards].

Implementation.

  • Restrict seed rows to h_j = + for one leg j chosen inside the last-dressed position of each family’s frame, so all earlier steps carry half the rows.

  • Apply 2 Re to the Born-weighted coefficients before reduction.

Gating and scope.

  • The certificate is a loop-level re-proof: the tree engine’s global_helicity_flip_equivalence_is_proven (models/external_catalog.py:465-472 [V]) extended to loop kernels, plus a numerical check on random points. It is never inherited (tree report §4).

  • It is invalid with chiral couplings, widths or the complex-mass scheme.

  • In the required set it applies to gg→gggg, gg→ggggg, uu~→ggggg and gg→tt̄gg only: vector-like QCD couplings, real masses, zero widths.

  • It does not apply to uu~→e⁻e⁺ggg, uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g or gg→tt̄e⁻e⁺g, which are generated with QED ≤ 2 and include Z exchange.

  • Expected gain: ×1.6–2 on dressing, ×1.25–1.6 per point, for those four processes.

8.4 Spin sources and correlations¶

  • Literal sources. Complex vectors replace the polarisation of the source legs in both the Born and the blocks (spin_sources.py:17-40 semantics [V-s]), and the source rows replace that leg’s helicity rows. Joint classes and spin-correlation tensors form seed columns. Non-transverse sources use full kernels (§3.2 item 2).

  • Asymmetric Ward mode (validation only, judge X2). The Born bra uses physical polarisations; blocks and CT = 1 currents use ε_j → p_j with full kernels. Seeds and blocks are computed separately, so this needs no new machinery. The renormalised loop amplitude must give zero interference, which tests UV + R2 completeness and gauge invariance per point.

  • Native Ward inputs at any multiplicity (M-QCD MQ-WARD; ADDENDUM H; user ruling 2026-10-28 ~16:10, Q4). NativeExecutor(..., inputs="native").evaluate(..., ward=...) runs the Ward mode on the native per-point input path (loops/v2/ward.py): the native trees take per point a loop-side vector per leg (inputs["loop_sources"], loop_v2::trees::TreeProgram::inputs_loop_side) and run the tree program twice, physically for the Born bra (the seeds’ Born components and |A0|²) and with the vector in the leg’s vector source slots (every helicity source, times its crossing phase; the targets are read from each program’s own source fill, SchemaSources::vector_slots) for the block rows, the counterterm program and the field insertions’ Born ket (Interference::evaluate’s born_ket); TreeInputs::loop_born = Re ⟨A0|M|A0′⟩ per squared Born order becomes PointResult.loop_born. The same call with inputs="python" is the oracle (_PointEvaluation(loop_sources=...)). It needs a slice on the full tree kernels (ward.ward_slice; refused otherwise, and on a stored process, whose record carries no kernel variant) and refuses observable columns natively. The check (ward.ward_check: per point and carrier one batch of the physical entry and every leg and factor, each row judged by ward.ward_row) uses ε_j → c p_j / p_j⁰ with c = 1 and i (of the size of a polarisation vector) and requires the Born (≤ 1e-12 binary64, ≤ 1e-24 double-double of the physical Born) and the virtual of every sector and Laurent coefficient to vanish: in double-double ≤ 1e-25 of the physical scale (the largest physical component), in binary64 by the user’s O1 rule (m-qcd PLAN §1.4 rules 2 and 3, the exact value 0 and the scale in place of the coefficient) with the Ward evaluation’s own reduction-direction estimate E: E ≤ 1e-9 of the scale (O1’s scope), the virtual ≤ max(1e-12 of the scale, E) and ≤ 10 E. Physically (no Ward value) the full kernels are the production slice’s transverse ones (double-double: bitwise on g g > g g and u u~ > g g g, asserted to 1e-25 of the scale). The parts need not vanish alone: R2 cancels a bare violation, and with massive quarks the local UV part’s mass counterterm is not gauge invariant without the bare self-energies (g g > t t~ g g, ε₁ → i p₁: 40 times the scale). A rotation check is no rounding estimate of a Ward evaluation: the leg’s helicity-summed bra against a helicity-independent ket makes each lane change by little-group phases under a rotation (ward_row refuses it). tools/loop_v2_ward.py (in the upstream pyAmpliCol repository; MadGraph7 does not carry it, as it needs the benchmark tooling) runs the check on a tools/loop_benchmark process (one batch per carrier: the physical entry and every leg and factor); tests/unit/test_loop_v2_ward.py holds the default tier (g g > g g, u u~ > g g g; native = Python inputs on the non-gauge control in double-double, bitwise) and nightly the ladder up to seven legs and the seven-gluon check. Campaign (stream point 0, every gluon leg of g g > g g … g g > g g g g, u u~ > g g g, u u~ > d d~ g, u u~ > u u~ g, u u~ > g g g g, g g > t t~ g g, u u~ > g g g g g; legs 1, 4, 7 of top-free g g > g g g g g; c = 1 and i): all pass; g g > g g g g g: generation 168 s, binary64 72 s and double-double 721 s for the batch of seven on 12 threads, 27 GB; the virtual at most 2.9e-10 (binary64, 0.5 of its estimate) and 2.8e-26 (double-double) of the physical scale, the Born ratio 9.8e-16 and 5.3e-32; the physical binary64 Born and finite part of this full-kernel slice at that point are the G1 production values (m1028a g1-values.json, native/full point 0) to 1e-16 and 2.8e-10 (its estimate 4.8e-9); the largest binary64 rule-2 ratio of the campaign is 0.65 (u u~ > g g g g); the check discriminates: in double-double the bare and R2 parts are each 5e-4 (g g > g g g g g) to 8e-2 (g g > t t~ g g, with the local UV part) of the scale and cancel to the virtual’s 1e-26 to 1e-31, so a wrong or missing R2 or UV term fails (records workspace/reports/engine-v2/mq-ward/records/).

8.5 Resolved outputs¶

  • Per helicity: schedule F, or one-hot seed columns (×H cost at 7 legs).

  • Loop-induced (m-lit LIT-API / LIT-OBS): ResolvedVirtualEvaluation.contribution = "loop-induced" has no Born colour axis (empty born_color_ids); its resolved and correlated outputs are quadratic forms on its amplitude vector (LIT-OBS, §7.14): per helicity row one contracted component ("full") or the amplitude-basis anchors (amplitude-<t>).

  • Per Born colour component: seed columns restricted to the component’s Born basis elements. Components still sum exactly to the inclusive result, and ResolvedVirtualEvaluation.total() equals inclusive. The kind is renamed if anchors change (§1.6). As built on the public surface (WP2.6, Runtime.evaluate_resolved through v2): colour is resolved at LC only (one component per Born basis element, ids basis-<i>); NLC and full colour return one contracted colour component per helicity row (id = the accuracy), as Runtime.evaluate_resolved documents for the legacy engine. Decision 3 of §1.6 (Born-basis anchors at every accuracy) is still for the user.

  • Leading-colour selection (MQ-SELECT, as built 2026-10-28; loops/v2/selection.py). Rule. Tree-engine parity at LC: the helicity IDs (h:<values>) and flow IDs (flow:<word>, ordinals in the tree runtime’s order: plan sectors, a folded trace’s reflection after its sector) are the tree engine’s, and an artifact lists and numbers the flows it computes as the tree runtime with the same selectors does (selection.request_flows: the tree engine’s plan with the request’s reference_color_order and max_color_sectors, kept as Selection.color_order/max_sectors, which select nothing; under a colour selection only its flows). A flow is a Born basis element with its outer flow, and a selection is one observable column (rows and basis elements of its bra): it equals the sum of its resolved entries, and a complete set sums to the inclusive value. Declared colour or spin correlations (or the Ward mode) with a selection are refused (selected-correlators), as in the tree engine (a spin source on a leg of fixed helicity would ignore the selection). A selected artifact reports helicity_coverage/color_coverage "selected". NLC and full colour keep their bytes and select helicity rows only (Full-colour selection (lit-fc-hel), below). Evaluation. evaluate takes helicities=/color_flows= on every runtime, and evaluate_resolved takes them as a filter of its rows and basis elements. Python and native slices export one selection column on first use. A stored process serves every selection with one column set and its executors, formed once from its stored resolved records without regeneration (MF-MASKS, M-FINAL; native_observables.SelectionTemplate): per row class (rows whose resolved columns read the same seed-weight column per basis element and sector; one at leading colour) and sector one seed column whose weights are every basis element’s seed-weight column concatenated in seed-weight-column order, and one interference column of every basis element. A selection is then the masks of one native call (V2Executor.evaluate(rows=, basis=, components=, families=), tree_columns(rows=, basis=)): the kept Born rows (every other row’s Born components vanish, as a spin source’s fixed row does, so its seeds and interferences are zero), the kept bra basis elements of the column interferences (PointSources.basis; the ket stays whole), the seeds’ kept plan Born components (the selected basis elements’ own; the others read zero, so each seed sums the selected basis elements’ terms in the order the per-selection set concatenates them, plus exact zeros) and the families with a leaf on a seed class with a kept term (Executor::evaluate_families dresses only those; the others’ lanes are absent). The companion of the certified-scaleless families takes the same row, component and family masks. Each selected value is the per-selection set’s (native_observables.selection_parts: the selected basis elements’ seed-weight columns summed on the selected rows, a plan of the live families only (live_families) and row-restricted; kept as the template’s oracle) bitwise up to the sign of a zero: u u~ > d d~ g and g g > g g g (and u u~ > g g g) at LC, single, several and every helicity row and flow, crossed ones and a subleading flow, binary64, the “ir”/”uv” poles (companion masks) and double-double (test_selections_are_masks_on_one_template). A new selection builds no native executor (counted) and retains no native heap: about 0.001 MB per new selection on one executor thread and 0.03-0.07 MB on eight (their heaps’ fragmentation, whatever the selection), against 0.7-1.7 MB per selection for a per-selection set, linearly (u u~ > d d~ g, u u~ > g g g, g g > g g g; 20 new selections after 12; test_new_selections_retain_no_native_heap). The LC stored observables record holds the flow catalogue (color_flows), the one byte change of LC artifacts. A runtime keeps the 8 most recently used selections (selection.SelectionCache; $PYAMPLICOL_LOOP_SELECTION_CACHE sets the count, 0 keeps none): masks of a stored process, a compiled column of an in-memory slice. An in-memory slice exports a new selection’s column instead (g g > g g g in double-double: about 16 s), so sampling should use a stored artifact. Generation. SliceRequest.selection (the public route’s selected_source_helicities, selected_color_sector_ids, reference_color_order, max_color_sectors) keeps the selected flows’ Born tensors (restrict_born_terms: basis, seed table, Born/counterterm/field bras and the tree program follow) and the selected block rows (restrict_rows); the colour pruning is ring-aware: a skeleton is kept when the plan’s reading of its ring (rotations and reflection) or its own reading is live for the selected elements (per-reading liveness alone lost 40 % of the double pole on one flow of g g > g g g); the inclusive pruning is unchanged. A tree-engine sector of a folded trace is two flows, the sector’s and its reflection’s. Leading power. A flow below the squared matrix element’s leading N_c power (u u~ > d d~ g, each quark joined to its own antiquark) is zero at evaluation; at generation it contributes exact zeros next to a leading flow, and a selection without one is refused (subleading-colour-flows, LoopSlice._refuse_inexact_flows). Leading is read from the slice’s own grading of the unrestricted Born (_flow_degrees: each item’s N_c power plus its coupling’s grades, so identical-flavour lines are graded correctly; within one Born order only a flow’s own term, since two distinct flows close fewer index loops and their cross term is below the mean of their own degrees; between two Born orders every pair), not from the Born roots’ U(1) grades (colour.leading_born_flows). With several Born orders a generation-time selection is exact only if none of its flows interferes at the leading power with an unselected flow: the restricted Born drops that term (bra and ket the selected flows), the evaluation-time selection keeps it (bra the flow, ket the whole Born; this is also the per-flow cross-order convention at evaluation). Such a selection is refused (interfering-colour-flows): u u~ > d d~ with QCD and photon Born amplitudes, where at QCD^2 QED^2 the flows (2,4,3,1) and (2,1,3,4) overlap at N_c^1, the leading power there (evaluation-time Born values ±8.5e-3, summing to the vanishing inclusive LC value); (2,1,3,4) alone is subleading-colour-flows, both together are the inclusive value. Evidence (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_selection.py): complete sets (flow thirds, helicity halves) sum to the inclusive value on the public artifacts of u u~ > g g g g, u u~ > d d~ g g, g g > g g g g and u u~ > g g g g g to 1e-28 in double-double and 1.8e-13 in binary64; generation-time selections equal the evaluation-time ones in double-double (identical-flavour lines included: u u~ > u u~, u u~ > u u~ g, on the public route its sectors 0 and 2); single helicities equal MadLoop’s SLOOPMATRIXHEL (MQ-REF quadruple precision: g g > t t~, g g > g g g) to 1e-12 per coefficient, one parity pair’s single pole held by parity within MadLoop’s own spread (PLAN §1.4 rule 1 (i)). Cost (binary64, one core, shared host, indicative; MF-MASKS, 2026-11-02, the per-selection set’s in brackets): u u~ > g g g LC, B = 128, inclusive 2.4 ms; one flow 1.10 (1.08) ms, one (helicity, flow) 0.84 (0.34) ms, one helicity 1.43 (0.52) ms, half the helicities 2.15 (2.39) ms; u u~ > g g g g LC, B = 32, inclusive 33 ms; one flow 9.6 (9.5) ms, one (helicity, flow) 8.7 (3.0) ms, one helicity 19.5 (5.0) ms, half the helicities 29 (24) ms; a generation-time (helicity, flow) selection 0.62 and 2.9 ms. These masks kept the family pruning of a flow selection but not the row restriction below (the dressing ran every Born row of the kept families), so a few-helicity selection cost 2.5-4 times its own set per point; a call keeping some Born rows now forms its own row restriction (Per-call row liveness, below) and costs what its set does, against no setup and no memory per selection: a new selection costs its masks and one row liveness (the template’s formation, once per process, about 0.1 s and 1 s there), where a per-selection set took about 0.1 s and 1 s and 66 MB each. Full-colour selection (lit-fc-hel, as built 2026-11-09; USER 2026-11-09 ~19:53, 2026-11-08 ~22:34). Rule. A Born-interfered virtual selects its Born helicity rows at every colour accuracy with the tree engine’s helicity IDs (h:<values>, h<index>); colour flows exist at leading colour only and are refused typed at NLC and full colour (selection.require_colour_flows); generation-time selections stay leading-colour only; the correlated routes keep refusing selections (the v2 rule of both process types, not a tree parity). At NLC and full colour the colour is contracted, so a selection keeps some rows with every Born colour component of each kept row: its seeds sum the kept rows’ Born components with the colour weights before the dressing (one seed column per sector), and a single helicity equals its evaluate_resolved entry bitwise up to the sign of a zero. Template. The stored resolved set at NLC and full colour has one column per row with the contracted component (basis null); the template is the leading-colour one with that component as the colour axis: per row class and sector one seed column of the class’s rows, masks = the kept rows (no basis or component mask). One formation serves every accuracy and both APIs (rust/loop-reduction/src/v2_runtime/template.rs: SelectionTemplate::form / masks, pure JSON over the stored records, no Symbolica operation; the PyO3 selection_template that native_observables.SelectionTemplate calls and the SDK’s V2Runtime::evaluate_selection both run it, so their binary64 values are bitwise equal by construction; PythonSelectionTemplate is kept as the oracle, test_the_native_formation_is_the_python_one); at leading colour it forms exactly the earlier template and masks. Nothing more (G4). A selected call forms its kept rows’ Born and counterterm trees and root closures (TreeRows), dresses the links those rows reach and reduces the lanes of the families they reach: every family that drops a link runs its pruned copy in seeded plans too (LoopProgramV4::live_rows, no share and no heap gate on the selection path); its dressing work, lanes and tree rows equal the loader’s row restriction of the same rows (test_a_selection_forms_only_its_rows, test_selections_are_masks_on_one_template). A resolved selection reads its kept rows’ (and at leading colour kept basis elements’) stored resolved columns only (template::resolved_subset; Python resolved_parts), its own column set kept among the runtime’s evaluation-time selections. The seeds sum the kept rows before the dressing, so a selection has one reduction lane per live (family, loop order) and sector, the same as the summed call less the families no kept row reaches: a one-helicity call cannot fall below the reduction share of the summed call. Rescue levels and stability rotations evaluate the selected rows only. Partition. A complete set of selections sums to the unselected value within the summation bound 2 gamma_n S (n the helicity rows) plus the reduction estimates of both sides: the summed call reduces one numerator per family, a selection its rows’ only, so the identity is held to the reduction rounding, not to the final summation’s alone. SDK. rusticol_virtual_evaluate_selected serves Born-interfered helicity selections (ordinary, per point, resolved) at every accuracy, leading-colour colour flows refused typed (the Python API’s color_flows=). Formation memory. The formation reads the stored records typed and borrowed (the observables record’s resolved columns and lanes, the seed records and interference programs as their stored JSON text, the plan’s seed records and leaf seeds only), and where the stored set reads the plan’s own seed records (full colour) the template names the plan’s seed-weight columns instead of copying them (template::plan_weights): u u~ > g g g g g LC forms its template in 0.6 s with +24 MB transient (a first form holding the records as JSON values took 10.8 s and +345 MB, which glibc kept after freeing, so the first selected call’s peak rose by 240-680 MB). The template keeps per family the colour components its seeds read, as bits (per-class component sets held its 1.9 M seed terms, 72 MB, at full colour seven legs), and a formed set’s plan loads as the stored plan with its seed records (LoopProgramV4::load_overlaid, V2Executor(overlay=); the SDK loads every column set so), never through a merged plan JSON (at full colour seven legs a 66 MB JSON, its 595 MB Python parse and the loader’s parse put the selected call’s VmHWM 140-190 MB above the summed call’s). Cost (binary64, public API, poles “none”, auto, one pinned core, the largest-Born helicity at the first point, median of three fresh processes of four calls; one helicity / summed ms per point): u u~ > t t~ g g FC (example 1, B = 8) 12.7 / 22.0 (0.58), its LC variant 4.9 / 7.5 (0.66), u u~ > d d~ e+ e- FC (example 2, B = 8) 64.0 / 108.2 (0.59), g g > g g g FC (B = 8) 8.0 / 18.6 (0.43), u u~ > g g g g g LC (B = 4) 269 / 826 (0.33) and FC 1377 / 3246 (0.42). The ratio is the summed call’s reduction share (one lane per live family and loop order on both sides: 0.27, 0.23, 0.21, 0.13, 0.12, 0.08) plus the kept row’s dressing, which is 14-32 % of the summed call’s dressing work rather than 1/H (a link carries the rows of its undressed legs, so most links serve many rows), plus one row’s trees and the per-call rest. A selection’s lanes are its rows’: a lane whose numerator cancels exactly in the helicity sum is a kept row’s own (example 2: one helicity 14,804 lanes, its row restriction 14,804, the summed call 14,802). VmHWM one / summed: 198 / 219, 186 / 186, 410 / 425, 186 / 192, 1044 / 1050 and 1479 / 1484 MB. A resolved selection of one row: 0.14 s and 187 MB (example 1 FC), 0.60 s and 293 MB (example 2 FC, whose unselected resolved call took 8.9 GiB), 6.8 s and 0.98 GB (u u~ > g g g g g FC); at leading colour a row keeps |basis| columns: 0.30 s, 188 MB on example 1 LC (17.6 GiB and 11.6 s unselected), 640 s and 21.8 GB on u u~ > g g g g g LC (120 columns dressed apart at B = 1; schedule B, §8.5 ‘Cost’). Native row restriction (as built 2026-10-28). A plan whose columns keep some Born rows only (helicity selections and helicity-resolved columns: column_rows) seeds zeros on the other rows, so the native loader keeps only what a kept row reaches (rust/crates/rusticol-core/src/loop_v2/plan/live.rs): forward, the row links from a live source row; backward, those into a row a later link or trace reads; then the split targets a kept part link writes, and the parts, groups, edges and steps left with one; each step’s modelled work and each family’s inputs are recounted, and the fused factors and split currents are built on the rows the kept links read (plan::ReadRows; not with a schedule-F or -M program, which reads them too). A tree program with observable columns of such a plan (TreeProgram::set_columns: the stored path; an in-memory slice’s plan_export.NativeExecutor passes no columns and runs the whole tree program, except in amplitude mode, which restricts at load without columns) then evaluates what those read (loop_v2/trees_rows.rs): the plan block rows of the read factor and current rows, each with its further terms (block_row_terms: a block current the tree engine splits into trees by flavour flow), and the root closures (Born and counterterm) of the kept rows, with the interactions and output slots of both interaction programs kept by backward liveness over their states; the other rows’ Born and counterterm components stay zero. Plans without a row restriction (inclusive evaluation at every accuracy) are untouched (paired A/B at B = 128, head/base 0.99-1.03 on u u~ > g g g FC and NLC and g g > g g g FC, values bitwise equal). Helicity-resolved columns are row-restricted at every accuracy, so evaluate_resolved at full and next-to-leading colour also runs the pruned program (equal up to the sign of a zero; checked bitwise before and after at LC, every resolved entry and runtime selection of the stored u u~ > g g g artifact in binary64 and double-double; the full-colour resolved rows are held against MadLoop’s per-helicity values at 1e-12). The derivation bound holds on the restricted plans (exported_plans_stay_within_their_bound, row_restricted_columns_stay_within_the_bound). Split block currents: on the stored public LC artifact of u u~ > w+ w- g (the u current of legs {1, 3, 4}) the helicity halves sum to the inclusive value and single helicities equal their resolved rows in double-double (test_helicity_selections_keep_split_block_currents); with the further terms dropped the halves give 1.34 times the inclusive finite part. Cost: one (helicity, flow) of u u~ > g g g LC at evaluation 1.07 -> 0.70 ms; what remains above the generation-time selection is the lane data of every Born and block row, the full states’ source fill and the column interference programs. Per-call row liveness (MF-MASKS-ROWS, as built 2026-11-04). Stored evaluation-time selections run masks on one template (MF-MASKS, above), whose columns keep every row, so the loader’s restriction never applies; a schedule-B call whose rows mask drops a seeded row forms the same restriction for itself instead (schedules M and F dress their own programs whole and form none: V2Executor::live_rows takes the schedule, only_schedule_b_forms_a_row_liveness). Executor::live_rows (plan::LiveRows, plan/live.rs) prunes each family the family mask keeps with the loader’s own prune_family, seeded by the call’s kept rows and the plan’s column rows, into a fresh copy at the lengths it keeps (a split part’s list keeping every link stays shared with the template, a shorter one is packed and interned; the families are pruned on the calling thread with one link interner, so the copies sit in one allocator arena and equal shortened lists are shared across families). Before lit-fc-hel, in a seeded plan a copy was kept only when it ran at most half its family’s row links (KEPT_SHARE; now the opt-in live_rows_keeping, no production caller), else the family ran whole on the masked seeds; since lit-fc-hel (G4) every helicity selection keeps a copy whenever it drops a link, as a dressed-row plan (loop-induced, lit-dress) did (the call evaluates exactly the restriction of its rows; a copy is a subset of its template), a family whose every link is reached runs its template; a family left without a step is not dressed (its lanes are absent, as under a family mask). The share rule also ran every family whole in a seeded plan when the kept copies together would hold more heap than the families they replace (their lists, steps, edges, fused links, groups and parts, the template’s shared part lists counted once); a selection keeps its copies (each is a subset of its template, so they add at most the listed families’ own heap, reported as row-pruned family bytes against row-liveness dressed bytes). A loop-induced row selection also forms its kept rows’ trees and counterterm kets only (an amplitude-mode tree program takes the per-call flags below without observable columns: its Born components are the plan’s units, so a dropped row’s closures only form kets the call does not read), exports only their amplitude slots and kets (amplitude_rows) and assembles and squares only them (induced.read_native, the evaluation’s amplitude_rows); before lit-dress the tree program formed every row’s counterterm kets, which entered the raw row-mask call’s |A|² (the Python API and the SDK squared the selected rows themselves). The fused factor and split current rows the dressed links read are recorded, so the chunk inputs build only those (ChunkInputs::with_rows). The tree program takes the matching per-call flags (TreeProgram::live_rows -> trees::TreeRows, trees_rows.rs; the loader’s prune is the same flags plus a retain): per interaction and output of both interaction programs the flags prune keeps for the read block rows and the kept rows’ closure inputs, with the program and its runtime left whole (run_interactions skips the others and whole dead steps), and the root closures skip the dropped rows. The executor keeps its latest liveness (one entry; a miss drops it before the next is formed, so a call never holds two) and returns it for a repeated rows and family mask, so a sampling loop on one selection forms the plan part once; a new selection forms it in 23 ms (a call there takes 0.5 s) on u u~ > g g g g and 0.6-0.8 s on u u~ > g g g g g (on the calling thread, at any thread count), against an executor and seconds for a per-selection set. Report counts: live-row links, row-pruned families, row-pruned family bytes, row-liveness dressed bytes. What the share rule kept (u u~ > g g g g g LC, 6,509,270 links): one helicity runs 80,214 links in 2,712 copies (17 MB of copies), one (helicity, flow) 14,024 (2 MB), half the helicities 4.9 M (416 copies, 5 MB), three quarters and all but one helicity every family whole (re-measured by lit-fc-hel for all but h37: 5.74 M links in 101 copies); since lit-fc-hel (G4) the half holding h36 runs 2.88 M links and all but h37 5.58 M, each in 2,712 copies (19.8 and 21.4 MB); u u~ > g g g g: one helicity 5,949 of 232,456 links (copies 1.4 of 1.7 MB: the steps’ own structures dominate there, so the gate counts links, not bytes). Unselected and flow-only calls form none and run as before (inclusive values bitwise equal). Peak (VmHWM of a fresh process running four calls of one selection, MB, median of three, base slice a7452422 | this package, binary64, poles “all”; u u~ > g g g g g LC, h36, at B = 2 / eight threads, B = 4 / one thread, B = 4 / eight threads): one helicity 1021 | 1023, 1058 | 1055, 1117 | 1102; one (helicity, flow) 827 | 812, 846 | 860, 882 | 876; half the helicities 1016 | 1043, 1054 | 1063, 1105 | 1117; three quarters 1035 | 1020, 1051 | 1065, 1104 | 1108; all but one 1026 | 1043, 1060 | 1071, 1103 | 1115; one flow 817 | 832, 852 | 856, 894 | 890; inclusive 1003 | 1006, 1038 | 1046, 1093 | 1092: every selection within 1.7 % (27 MB), inside the spread of the unchanged inclusive and one-flow calls between runs (about ±30 MB with glibc’s per-thread arenas; with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 every selection, the inclusive one included, within ±2.5 %). u u~ > g g g g, B = 32, eight threads (median of two): one helicity 342 | 326, one (helicity, flow) 280 | 274, half 340 | 328, all but one 350 | 324, one flow 280 | 278, inclusive 332 | 321. The executor’s one-entry cache keeps a call’s copies after it (17 MB for one helicity of u u~ > g g g g g). Earlier forms grew the peak: copies cloned whole and pruned in place (clone + retain, capacity kept) by 140-200 MB (+9-14 %) there, and a prune in parallel on the pool’s threads (copies spread over their allocator arenas) by about 50 MB at eight threads for one helicity. Selected values equal the per-selection set’s (selection_parts) bitwise up to the sign of a zero: u u~ > d d~ g, u u~ > g g g, g g > g g g and u u~ > g g g g in binary64 (“all”, “ir”; g g > g g g also “uv”), u u~ > d d~ g double-double “uv” and “ir”, g g > g g g and u u~ > g g g double-double, twelve selections each (single, several, all-but-one and every helicity, single and several flows, crossed ones, and the helicity with the largest Born on the points with its largest flow: a helicity whose amplitudes vanish, h0-h15 of u u~ > g g g, leaves only rounding, so a first-non-zero pick is no check), and the stored partitions of u u~ > g g g g, u u~ > d d~ g g, g g > g g g g and u u~ > g g g g g; test_selections_are_masks_on_one_template asserts the liveness engages exactly on row-restricted masks (live-row links) and that one helicity runs pruned copies (row-pruned families). Cost per point (binary64, ms; the largest-Born helicity, h9 of u u~ > g g g and h21 of u u~ > g g g g, and its largest flow; release natives loop-native-v2-slice-a7452422 vs this package’s, the timing rows on its build c5b85e79, whose dressing is the final one (later commits change how the liveness is formed, not what runs); shared host at load ~1000-1500, so indicative only): masked one-helicity and one-(helicity, flow) calls cost what the per-selection set does — interleaved in one process (best of 9-15 calls, one pinned thread) masked/set 0.89-1.19 and 1.01-1.03 on u u~ > g g g (B = 128), 0.98-1.00 and 1.01-1.05 on u u~ > g g g g (B = 32); at eight threads 0.79-1.31 (host noise). Before -> after (fresh processes, base and new alternating, one pinned thread, best of 5, four rounds): u u~ > g g g one helicity 1.94-3.16 -> 1.48-2.79 (set 1.22-1.87), one (helicity, flow) 0.92-1.84 -> 0.57-1.17 (0.56-0.93); u u~ > g g g g one helicity 27.0-44.4 -> 15.7-22.7 (16.3-24.0), one (helicity, flow) 9.5-16.7 -> 4.5-6.6 (4.2-5.8). Inclusive and one-flow calls are unchanged (paired fresh processes, best of 7, four pairs, new/base): inclusive 0.91-1.06 (u u~ > g g g g) and 0.82-1.04 (u u~ > g g g), one flow 1.01-1.07 and 0.99-1.19. At seven legs (u u~ > g g g g g, B = 4, four calls in a fresh process, one thread, median of three) one helicity takes 0.87 s per point against 1.53 s before.

  • Cost (WP2.5). Every resolved output is its own seed column per squared-order sector, dressed and reduced like the inclusive one: helicity resolution has H columns (Born helicity rows), colour resolution |basis|, helicity × colour H × |basis|. Measured: u u~ > g g g has 32 rows × 11 basis elements = 352 columns; the nightly check of its helicity × colour outputs at two points (Python reference executor and native, binary64) takes about 5 min, against seconds for the inclusive evaluation. Exporting their seed weights takes 3.9 s (244 seed keys; 0.9 s for the inclusive plan): plan_export indexes each column’s admitted Born entries and projected weights per (class, loop order) once, where a rescan per seed key, column and class took 53 s. At seven legs the counts reach up to 2^7 × 720 ≈ 9×10⁴ columns for gg→ggggg and 2^7 × 120 for uu~→ggggg, far above the schedule-3 break-even of ≈45–60 columns (§7.7), and helicity-only resolution alone (≈128 columns) is above it too. Resolved outputs at seven legs therefore need schedule 3 (each family’s integrals of all monomials once, every output a dot product); with schedule B they cost H × |basis| inclusive evaluations.

9. Flavour mappings¶

  • Representative-only programs. Identity-port members are records executed by the representative on the same momenta (AdmittedFlavorMember, loop_runtime.rs:467-470 [V-s]).

  • Admission keeps prove_flavor_relabeling (loops/flavor_mappings.py:186 [V]) and runs it on the prepared model before compilation (assessment R11).

  • Permutation aliases (e.g. u~ u for u u~) become relabelling tables: momentum and label permutations on the representative plan, with Bose transport as a special case and fermion signs from the same permutation parity as §3.3. This is the same mechanism as primitive templates.

  • As built (M-FINAL MF-MAP, loops/v2/mapping.py). A stored process serves (1) its explicit ProcessAlias records (the manifest’s alias records, published with LoopV2ProcessArtifact.aliases; the native admission takes a stored process that lists aliases when it is selected as itself), (2) a selector expression equal to its own up to a permutation within each side (the artifact selector’s precedence, artifact._select), and (3) process.flavor_blind members admitted by observables.admit_member: a proved species substitution, a side permutation, or both (process-groups.json, basis exact-loop-flavor, the representative-to-member permutation; a request with explicit aliases is never folded). Each is a FlavourMember of its representative evaluated at the permuted momenta, bitwise the representative’s value there. Correlations compose: a declared history (spin class) is read on the mapped process’s labels, relabelled onto the representative’s and served by the stored column of equal bra and ket (mapping.MappedObservables); a flavor_blind permuted member is folded only when every declared history and spin class has a stored image (loop_service._correlations_closed), otherwise it is generated on its own and serves all of them; for an explicit alias or an inferred side permutation one without a stored image is not served (available_color_correlations() omits it). A permuted member’s leg-keyed request fields must be invariant (no generation-time selection; photon tags by mode or by a leg set the permutation keeps). At leading colour a mapped process publishes the stored flows relabelled onto its legs as its Born anchors (its resolved components are the stored basis elements); helicity and colour-flow selection of it is refused. A process-group relation of another basis (numerical analysis) is refused at load and process.analyze_process_groups = "numerical" at generation (process-group-analysis). Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_mapping.py (two aliases and three members of 2→2 representatives, and an alias and a member whose permutations are three-cycles of u u~ > d d~ g’s final legs; inclusive, relabelled histories, spin source, resolved rows and double-double bitwise; alias and member equal to their own generation; the representative’s plan and PACBIN plan members byte-identical to its generation alone; a declaration not closed under a member’s permutation generates it on its own; LC anchors and resolved components of a permuted member).

  • Retired. The paired-program comparison of flavor_transport.py (contracts §2.7).

  • Composition. Correlations and spin sources compose with members, because member execution reuses the representative’s seed columns.

10. Precision and rescue¶

10.1 Carriers¶

  • One instruction stream for f64, DoubleFloat and Float. Dressing and closure are generic Rust. Segment builders are SymJIT (f64) and exact evaluators (DD/AP). Seeds and colour tables are exact rationals cast per carrier. Ingress is exact decimal → rational, and the invariant table is exact until cast (contracts K4, K6).

  • Trees. The tree recurrence lane gains DoubleFloat and arbitrary-precision prepared kernels built from the retained exact_expressions (tree report §7.3). Until the loop-request mode of the Rust recurrence (WP3.1) the per-point trees, Born components and counterterm scalars of the v2 path are formed in Python (LoopSlice._point): in binary64, or in Decimal at the carrier’s working digits for DD (32 + 20 guard digits) and AP, then cast once into the native carrier (WP2.3).

  • Native carriers (WP2.3). NativeExecutor.evaluate runs dressing, seeds and reduction in f64, DoubleFloat (Precision.double_double(), unit roundoff 2⁻¹⁰⁴) or Float (Precision.arbitrary(digits)); the Python reference path has no DoubleFloat arithmetic and refuses it. Native DD and AP equal the Python 60-digit reference (gg→gg, uu~→dd~g: DD within its own estimate < 10⁻²⁴, AP < 10⁻⁵⁵; test_loop_v2_stability.py). Outside f64 the lanes are scalar loops, so the executor uses the smallest lane count holding the batch.

  • NinjaRS. The fast engine for f64; the generic engine for DD/AP. Every carrier reads the same on-shell external invariants (§11.1), so the generic engine’s exact on-shell tests and the fast engine see equal inputs; lanes whose inputs reach the fast engine’s absolute 10⁻⁹ thresholds take the generic binary64 engine (§11.2, ‘Absolute thresholds’). Both engines refuse, typed (Unstable; the generic engine CutFailed { SingularParameter }), a lane whose box mu-expansion is predicted to lose more digits than the carrier keeps minus 14 bits: at near-planar 2 -> 3 points (the event plane containing the beam, a vanishing pentagon Gram determinant) the uncut lines’ leading coefficients d0 vanish and the boxes’ rational c4 cancel between the boxes, which before lost about twice the digits of log2(scale/|d0|) unseen (up to 1e17 off in binary64, 1e7 in double-double on loop-induced g g > z z z). The bound reads the lane’s geometry, its numerator’s leading coefficient along the box normal (helicity-summed parity-even interferences lose one division only, so Born-interfered g g > g g g at the same points is served) and the carrier’s precision, and is independent of the noise thresholds (active under reduction_unchecked). The binary64 fast engine uses it as a screen: a flagged lane is refused only when the first-order rounding estimate of its boxes’ mu-expansion rational terms (the moduli through the divisions by d0, times (k + 1) Σ R + 1) exceeds 2^-17 of the lane’s finite part, so that high-multiplicity lanes at regular kinematics, whose regular uncut lines add up to the binary64 budget without any cancellation, stay served; the generic engine refuses every flagged lane. Regular lanes never reach the screen’s cold stage (NinjaRS 71eddb15, its docs/box-mu-conditioning.md; M-LIT lit-ninja-planar). Before that bound (pin 5b6a8f57) both engines returned such values as success; the measured windows and the per-point fallback’s guard (defence in depth: double-double and arbitrary precision, limit max(target, 1e-5)) are in §12.2 ‘Reduction backend’, ‘Near-planar NinjaRS hazard’ and ‘Fallback guard’.

    • The generic engine’s numerator ingress is PolynomialNumerator, built from a Symbolica expression (ninjars-symbolica/src/polynomial.rs:258 [V]), one template per (N, R) and reducer, compiled on first use and cached. Measured compile cost (WP2.3; first minus second call of one lane, 7-point family; shared host): DoubleFloat 0.35–0.52 s at rank 6, 0.73 s at rank 7 (330 parameters), 2.6 s at rank 8, 10.8 s at rank 9; Float(256) 1.0–1.2 s at rank 6, 1.3–1.5 s at rank 7, 3.2 s at rank 8, 11.3 s at rank 9. It is paid once per executor, so a tensor ingress is not needed for it.

    • The generic engine’s workspace grows with the lanes of one call (about 18 MB per lane of a 7-point family at 256 bits), so buckets are reduced in chunks of 16 lanes (values unchanged).

    • numerica tracks the significant bits of Float masters: a master below the provider’s required bits fails its lane with ImpreciseResult instead of returning an unestablished value (imprecise_float_masters_fail_their_lane).

    • A generic-precision tensor numerator exists only in the CLI harness (ninjars-cli/src/case_check/harness.rs:1290, TensorGenericNumerator<T> [V]). Request 8 (§11.5) asks the owner to upstream it.

    • Float(128) needs Symbolica 9cdc2949 (NinjaRS guidance [V]), pinned since the coordinated re-pin (WP0.2). Since mf-symbolica (2026-11-04) the alphal00p Symbolica fork is gone: every crate pins symbolica-dev community 36cbac3a + symbolica-dev/symbolica#163 (ValentinHirschi/symbolica loop_me_pyamplicol dfe6bd97 since lit-sym-bump, b9eaa735 since lit-tirust-p3, 20a9da94 before; dependencies/README.md), which carries the fork commits we need (batched evaluation, DualNumber, complex-modulus Dual derivatives) plus state-minimal evaluator saves, deterministic integer factor signs, polynomial exponents bounded by the i32 conversion range, a journaled conditional cache in the direct evaluator translator (generated instructions unchanged) and native Python ComplexFloat operands at the more precise component’s precision. PyPI 3.0.3 (the release lock, without #163) still saves the producer’s whole Symbolica state, and every save numbers its symbols by the producer’s registry; every generation writer stores the native’s canonical form instead (symbolica_helpers.saved_evaluator, native canonical_saved_evaluator: only the referenced symbols, ordered by name and numbered 0, 1, …; payload byte for byte; checked to decode to the same evaluator), so stored bytes, sizes and loads depend neither on the installed Python Symbolica nor on the process history.

10.2 Triggers, cheapest first¶

As implemented (WP2.3; REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM C overrides the defaults below). An evaluation runs the checks its caller asks for, StabilityChecks(rotations, reduction_direction, rescaled) (loops/v2/stability.py), and none by default; with no check no estimate exists (PointResult.stability is None, in every carrier), and nothing is escalated automatically.

  • Rotation checks: any number of user rotations, each an exact rational orthogonal matrix (Rotation.about(axis, cos, sin), Rotation.from_axis_angle(axis, angle) via a rational unit quaternion), so the rotated point is exactly on shell. Each re-evaluates the whole point (trees, dressing, reduction, counterterms).

  • One reduction check: the reduction-direction check re-reduces every lane in the reversed frame (q → −q from the second propagator) with the coefficients reused exactly and cached masters, +0.84–1.0 reduction (§5.5); or its rescaled variant (rescaled=True, ReductionFrame::RESCALED), the same frame with every dimensionful input scaled by x = 7/10 (shifts by x, squared masses, μ² and invariants by x², degree-d coefficients by x⁻ᵈ) and the integrals scaled back by x^{2N−4}, exact at every Laurent order. It re-evaluates the masters at differently rounded arguments, so it also measures their own rounding, which neither the cached frame nor a rotation (same invariants) can see. Cost on uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g (7 legs, binary64, 16 points, one thread, shared host): finite only 13.4 ms/pt, + reversed check 16.1, + rescaled check 16.5 (reduction 3.2 → 5.8 / 6.3 ms/pt).

  • Budget and estimate: per check an absolute budget per squared-order sector and Laurent coefficient that lets no two lanes cancel (Σ_f 2|Ω_f − Ω′_f|/(16π²·avg) for a reduction check; for a rotation also the local components); E = 2 × (max over rotations + reduction budget) + 16 u S, with u the carrier’s unit roundoff and S the absolute sum of the contributions. StabilityEstimate returns E (absolute), E against each sector’s Laurent vector (relative) and per coefficient (coefficients, finite), each check’s own budget and the per-lane deviations; subset recombines fewer checks. A relative estimate ≥ 1 says the value has no correct digit.

  • Failed points: a failed lane (status, ImpreciseResult, non-finite numerator), also in a rotation check’s evaluation, fails its point alone: NativeExecutor.evaluate raises FailedPoints with every other point’s complete result.

  • The calibrated false-negative rates of every configuration are in §10.4. The IR-pole check and κ below are not wired as estimates.

  1. NinjaRS status. Lane status ≠ Success, a master failure, or a non-finite value. This is free. The fast engine has no cancellation test (NinjaRS guidance [V]).

  2. Reduction-side re-test of every family (default). For each (family, point, sector), the stored family polynomial is reduced a second time in a relabelled frame.

    • Relabelling. The propagators are rotated cyclically by a fixed per-family k_f ≠ 0. This maps q → q − V_{k_f} and permutes the shifts and the S-matrix.

    • Re-expansion. The polynomial is re-expanded by the exact affine map (loops/v2/poly_affine.py; in Rust, the same generic routine in the working precision, O(4·R·C(R+4,4)) operations).

    • Masters. Box and triangle masters hit the cache. Bubbles with swapped mass order miss, because they are keyed by ordered arguments (§11.2).

    • Estimate. |Ω_f − Ω′_f| is the per-family error estimate. This is MadLoop’s production check in the form recommended by NinjaRS guidance (b). Ninja’s authors recommend a global scaling or rotation test, not Ninja’s internal tests, as the accuracy estimate [L 1403.1229 main.tex:1642-1651]; the rescaling variant below is the scaling test applied per family.

    • Rescaling variant (measured in WP2.3). Replace c_α by x^{d_f − |α|}c_α, scale all invariants, masses and μ by a non-dyadic x so that rounding differs, and compare after undoing x^{4−2N+d_f}. Here d_f is the family numerator’s mass dimension. This is NJet’s scaling test applied per family [L 1209.0100 §Accuracy]. It recomputes the masters and so also tests them.

    • Cost. +0.75 R (relabelling, cached masters) or +1.0 R (rescaling), included in Table 1a: +12–25 % per point at 7 legs.

  3. IR-pole check per point and sector, kept as an additional signal.

    • The 1/ε² and 1/ε coefficients of the renormalised result are compared with Catani’s operator, built from the Born and the colour-correlated Borns (tree correlators) plus UV CT poles. Massive emitters use the massive dipole form (implemented, poles.catani_poles, §12.4); electroweak sectors use the QED analogue (poles.qed_catani_poles, WP3.2 EWI-6, §12.4).

    • It is free and catches missing counterterms.

    • It is not sufficient: pole residues involve only divergent integrals, so finite boxes, the R1 rational part and Gram-determinant failures in N ≤ 5 families pass it [I].

  4. Optionally, the generic engine’s κ cancellation test (guidance (a)).

Error budget. The point’s estimated absolute error is E = Σ_f |ΔΩ_f|, compared with the target accuracy × |Σ_f Ω_f + CT|. When the target is missed, the families with the largest |ΔΩ_f| are recomputed (§10.3) until the remaining estimate meets the target. Per-family locality makes this targeted.

Relaxation. The default (every family, every point) may be relaxed only after WP2.3 measures the false-negative rate of each trigger against Float(256) on ≥ 10⁴ points per required process. Possible relaxations are N ≥ 5 families, or sampled points with a reported rate.

10.3 Escalation¶

By REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM C the v2 path does not escalate by default: the caller re-evaluates a point (or the failed points of FailedPoints) in Precision.double_double() or Precision.arbitrary(digits) from its original inputs when the returned estimate misses its target. loop_v2/rescue.rs is not built.

Status (M-FINAL MF-RESCUE, user ruling 2026-10-31 Q9): optional convenience tier built, off by default. loops/v2/rescue.py runs a VirtualRescuePolicy (levels of carrier, rotations incl. gammaloop’s exact euler:α,β,γ, reduction check and a target on the estimate E; default binary64 → double-double → arbitrary(57) at 1e-5 with one rotation and the rescaled check) in the Python native evaluate only (no SDK, CLI or config). Whole points escalate, not single families: level 0 runs the batch; failed points (rotation failures included) and points whose estimate misses the target are re-evaluated at the next level from their exact inputs (never promoted), one point per native call so each escalated carrier builds one executor; the last level keeps a missed point with met = False. Statuses success (level 0) / rescued / failed, accuracy_established = met (an estimate’s verdict, not a certificate), VirtualEvaluation.rescue per lane (docs/user/python-api.md). The per-(family, point) ladder below stays the reference for a native tier; the legacy VirtualStabilityPolicy and its refusal plumbing are deleted (the SDK-side verification.rs is MF-CLEAN’s).

Escalation always starts from the original inputs and never promotes binary64 values (MASTER_PLAN §2.18):

  1. Per (family, point): recompute trees, seeds and that family’s trie (or its M closures) in DoubleFloat from the original decimals with the same source snapshot, reduce with the generic engine, and replace the lane. Per-family locality makes this cheap.

  2. Whole point in DoubleFloat, then Float(p) per policy.

Statuses:

  • They stay success / rescued / failed / accuracy-not-established, with one implementation (rust/loop-reduction/src/verification.rs); loops/stability.py is deleted.

  • Lane compaction replaces the whole-batch restart (loop_execution.rs:749-826 [V-s]).

  • The single-level defect (verification.rs:346-351 [V]) is fixed per decision 6 in §1.6.

  • The R2 strategy is fixed during rescue.

10.4 Expected rescue load and calibration¶

  • NJet needed quadruple precision for 1.37 % (6 gluons) and 8.63 % (7 gluons) of points with unitarity in double [L 1209.0100 njet.tex:1161-1227].

  • Ninja’s exact Laurent expansions avoid the OPP sampling part of that instability [L-s 1403.1229].

  • NinjaRS 0d0d7e7 lost 5×10⁻⁹–10⁻⁵ on ill-conditioned n = 7 lanes in binary64; the fix is in the pinned main aa6a6307 (guidance [V]; not re-measured here). The guidance expects many n = 7 μ² lanes to need DoubleFloat at a 10⁻⁸ target.

WP2.3 measures on 10⁴ points per process:

  • the rescue rate;

  • the rescue cost;

  • the false-negative rate of each trigger (relabelling, rescaling, pole check, κ).

Measured (WP2.3, O15; tools/loop_v2_stability_calibration.py, report tests/fixtures/loop/v2/stability_calibration.json). 2000 binary64 points per process and 400 DoubleFloat points (the first 400), native executor, against Float(256) (Precision.arbitrary(57): 77 working digits); RAMBO points at √s = 1 TeV made exactly on shell and momentum conserving in rationals, p_T > 20 GeV, ΔR > 0.4, μ_R = 1 TeV; two fixed rotations (rotations() in the tool) and one reduction check per evaluation, every combination recombined from the recorded absolute budgets (StabilityEstimate.subset). A false negative is a point whose true error exceeds E, both measured against the truth’s Laurent vector (E against the evaluated value would let a value with no correct digit, flagged by a relative estimate ≥ 1, count as missed). No point failed. The test bounds each rate (test_loop_v2_stability.py).

  • The cached reduction check alone misses the masters’ own rounding: the same masters enter both reductions. Its estimate/error ratio has q01 = 0.4–0.5 in binary64. A rotation keeps every invariant and so misses it too; the rescaled check sees it. A rotation re-evaluates the trees, dressing and counterterms, which neither reduction check sees (injected-numerator test).
