10.5 Optional labelled hybrid tier (needs sign-off)¶

Re-reduce flagged families in DoubleFloat from their binary64 coefficients (the OpenLoops 2 hybrid-precision analogue [L-s 1907.13071 §5]). It is off by default, never reported as DoubleFloat accuracy, and has its own status.

10.6 Kinematics improvement of the input points (m-lit lit-psimprove)¶

USER 2026-11-10 ~00:56 / ~01:56; DECISIONS 2026-11-10 01:30, 01:56, 02:29. The contract of an evaluation above binary64 is the value at the improved point of the given inputs: before anything is evaluated in a carrier, rusticol_core::kinematics_improvement (the one implementation: Python through improve_kinematics, the SDKs through V2Runtime::improve_kinematics) moves each point onto exact conservation and the external shells in that carrier’s arithmetic. Targets: exactly the leg masses the evaluation binds (TreeProgram::bind, V2Batch::leg_masses; a leg without one keeps its own p²).

  • Variants. MadLoop 2 "z-shift" (improve_ps.inc ORIG_IMPROVE_PS_POINT_PRECISION, faithful: refusal codes 100 / 200 / 300 / 400 + I / 500 / 999 in MadLoop’s order, the closed-form shifts, P2’s sub-threshold transverse momentum kept), MadLoop 1 "rescaling" (PSMC_IMPROVE_PS_POINT_PRECISION with FINDX / FUNCT, faithful: MadLoop’s step order, seeds 1, 1.1, 0.9, particle 1 at x², FUNCT’s derivative as coded, the error-code sum); it leaves the 3-momentum residual (x² - x) p₁ wherever x ≠ 1), and the frame-independent minimal-norm "projection" (Gauss-Newton x ← x - Jᵀ(JJᵀ)⁻¹c(x) on the n shells and 4 conservation equations, Euclidean metric, an in-house Jacobi-scaled Cholesky solve in the carrier; STOPPING RULE: stop when every defect is within the exactness bound below or when a step does not strictly decrease the scaled residual, which terminates without an iteration cap; a singular JJᵀ is refused, code 10001).

  • Chain. "z-shift" (the default, ONE constant DEFAULT_VARIANT) and "rescaling": MadLoop’s dispatch exactly (IS_PHYSICAL, the selected variant, on a refusal code the other), then THE FINISH (FINISH = the projection; USER 2026-11-10 ~19:20 ‘Projection after MadLoop’, DECISIONS 19:20 (F1), amending 01:56 (1) / (3) for that case): when the dispatch leaves a physical input inexact (its produced point misses the exactness record’s bounds, or both variants refuse), the projection continues from the dispatch’s point (the produced one, else the input; IS_CLOSE against the caller’s input); a point a MadLoop variant makes exact is MadLoop’s bit for bit (ORIG with beams along z); evaluated as given (typed, every attempt named) only when IS_PHYSICAL fails (MadLoop’s input test, no finish) or the projection refuses too (after a produced point, that point stands with its kinematics-inexact record); the record names every attempt and the producer. "projection": alone (no IS_PHYSICAL test, bounded by IS_CLOSE, no MadLoop variant after it). A forced variant (fallback = false, the developer entry) runs alone. An exactly physical exact input is passed unchanged (MadLoopParams.dat: ‘leaves the input PS point unchanged’).

  • Exactness record, not a fallback (01:56 (3)): the produced point’s defects max_k |p_k² - m_k²| / (REF_k S) and max_μ |Σ_in - Σ_out| / S (S = Σ|E|, REF_k = |E|+|px|+|py|+|pz|) are measured in the carrier against (2n + 5) u and 2n u (u the carrier’s unit roundoff: forming p² - m² costs 5 roundings of REF_k², an n-term sum n - 1 of S, a component formed from n legs n u S); above them the record carries the typed kinematics-inexact warning naming the variant and the residual. Both typed warnings are records: no failure, no rescue escalation.

  • Tolerances. Precision literals derived from the carrier: THRS_TEST = sqrt(u) (P2’s transverse momentum t·REF costs both initial shells ~t² REF²), CONVERGED = the Newton step’s own rounding 2 (n + 3) u Σ E / (|f’| |x|), MAXITERATIONS = ceil(log2 bits) + 1 (MadLoop’s 8 at 113 bits), CONSISTENCY = (3n + 6) u. Input-sanity bounds (THE READING, DECISIONS 02:29): IS_PHYSICAL (1e-6 conservation, 1e-2 shells) and IS_CLOSE (1e-2) bound the input relative to its own scale, independent of the carrier, MadLoop’s values; IS_PHYSICAL tests |BUFF| (MadLoop’s comparison is signed). Overriding them: the Rust Tolerances of improve / improve_exact and the Python entry pyamplicol.kinematics.improve(..., tolerances={"fourmom": ..., "onshell": ..., "close": ...}), whose exact output an evaluation takes with kinematics_improvement="off" (the composition that also forces a variant); the evaluation settings themselves are the two ruled ones (variant and binary64 switch), so the runtimes and the SDKs run MadLoop’s values (a question recorded for the coordinator in the lit-psimprove report).

  • What the MadLoop variants leave. The z-shift keeps each final state’s E, px, py and sets pz = SIGN(sqrt(|E² - pT² - m²|), pz): a slow final state (small |pz|) moves by ~sqrt(2 E dE) rather than by the input’s defect dE (F-GH C.md §0: 1.2e-6 GeV on the h h beam-frame points, whose point 0 value moves by 1.9e-8 relative at 16 digits; values above binary64 move by up to ~1e-8 there, as MadLoop’s do), and where a slow state’s rounded energy lies below its transverse mass the ABS leaves its shell off by 2 |E² - pT² - m²| (6 of the 24 beam-frame points of A’s theta scan in double-double, shell defects 5e-21 .. 1.2e-17 of REF S), flagged by the exactness record’s typed warning, MadLoop’s literal behaviour. The rescaling leaves (x² - x) p₁ off conservation wherever x ≠ 1, the z-shift refuses (200) every frame whose beams are not along z: there MadLoop’s dispatch produces PSMC’s point, which near a degenerate 2 -> 2 (sub-)box NinjaRS amplifies ~1/Gram where no rotation sees it (a rotation keeps the residual; g g > z z rotated + boosted at theta 1e-4: 5.3 off at double-double, met at estimate 1.6e-7, lit-ninja-fwd F1), so the default finishes it with the projection: the default and "projection" are exact in every frame (the slow-state shell defect of the z-shift above is finished likewise).

  • Where. At each carrier’s entry above the per-point fallback, the stability rotations, the tree fill and V2Batch: Python V2VirtualRuntime.evaluate (each level of a rescue from the original exact inputs; kinematics.LevelImprover, one point per carrier, reused) and the observables runtimes’ routes; the SDK in Runtime::improved_inputs before from_v4 / resolved_v4 / the induced and correlated entries. Key of ‘double-precision evaluations’ (G3): the carrier kind; binary64 only under kinematics_improvement_binary64. Runtime only: no artifact field, stored plans unchanged.

  • Trees. The Python tree runtime improves its higher-precision modes (precision above 16 and the correlated calls’ carriers, "arbitrary" at 16 digits included) toward the exact executors’ external masses at that precision, and binary64 under the switch through NativeRuntime::improve_f64_points (the binary64 instance, no Symbolica: an exactly physical binary64 point, tested with error-free FMA products and exact partial sums, passes unchanged; targets the binary64 masses of the external wavefunctions, external_masses_f64), the code the tree C ABI runs under rusticol_runtime_set_kinematics_improvement_binary64 (every f64 entry except the warm-up’s own point; additive, RUSTICOL_ABI_VERSION 1 kept), so Python and the C ABI give one point. Tree results are values only: the record is the warnings channel, the most recent improved call’s lines (kinematics_improvement::notes, for the Python tree runtime’s JSON records notes_json, one formatter: a summary and every typed warning; bounded, none while muted), read by rusticol_runtime_take_warnings_json and Python’s tree Runtime.take_warnings(), the typed warnings also as Python warnings. NativeRuntime::evaluate_with_precision (the native tree higher-precision lane) is reached by no public route (the Python tree runtime takes the exact executors above precision 16, the C ABI is binary64) and is not wired.

11. NinjaRS and oneloopmaster interface¶

Status (m-lit): NinjaRS is one of two reduction backends behind the V2Backend contract (its near-planar hazard, pin 5b6a8f57: §12.2 ‘Reduction backend’, ‘Near-planar NinjaRS hazard’, and the loop-induced "auto" fallback’s guard in the extended carriers there); TIRust (tensor-integral reduction, the loop-induced default) implements the same contract in every carrier, binary64, DoubleFloat and MPFR (lit-tir, lit-tir-mp: rust/loop-reduction/src/v2_tir.rs, feature tir, TIRust’s DirectWorkspace at the carrier’s precision). The executor’s backend is one enum (runtime::V2Backends) matched once per begin and per reduce (bucket chunk), never per point or lane, so evaluate is monomorphised once per carrier. The TIR backend computes one row of TIRust tensor moments per (family, point) run of lanes at the row’s true rank (Convention::OneLoop, TensorWeights::Components), permutes it once into NinjaRS’s layout and contracts every lane natively (finite, UV1+IR1, IR2 and the split UV slot; finite only without poles), as a sequential sum over the lane’s nonzero coefficients (a moment a lane does not read never enters its value). A row-layout contraction (the row’s slots laid out once, one dot product per lane and slot; the PLAN §2.b.2 item 4 GEMM) was measured and dropped: on 128 distinct served g g > z z points it saves 14 % of the reduction stage (paired median; 13 % from the contraction alone), below the 15 % lever rule (m-lit lit-cache report §2.1). TirOptions::profile (a measurement option, V2Executor.prepare_reduction(profile=True)) adds TIRust’s own stage profile to the report (“reduction: TIR geometry / masters / recursion / gather / output”); the count “TIR master requests” (the scalar-master rows TIRust’s calls request, DirectWorkspace::last_master_rows; the same with the store on, whose reuse is counted apart as “TIR store masters reused / computed”) is always reported. A method-choice row’s acceptance moments (the rescaled frame’s) are mapped back to the direct frame once per row (FrameMap::moments, the transpose of the lanes’ coefficient re-expansion, with the frame’s undo), and each lane contracts its own coefficients with them (m-lit lit-perf: one map per row instead of one re-expansion per lane; the served values are the direct ones, unchanged); the call’s check frame keeps the per-lane re-expansion. The binary64 gates take TirOptions::gate (default TIRust’s own 1e-12). TirOptions::store (opt-in, prepare_reduction(store=True)) shares TIRust’s per-subset results between the families of a point chunk through one iregi_rust::TensorStore per backend (every plan registered when prepare builds it, before the first reduce; every workspace attached; cleared once per point chunk in begin and per family-group call; entries are pure functions of exact keys, so every value is bitwise the store-off one); TirOptions::masters_census (with the store; refused typed without it) attaches a provider that declines every master and counts, per master family, the store’s misses and those that repeat an earlier miss up to MasterCache’s relabellings of the triangle and the box and the mass exchange of the scalar bubble (MasterCache keys its bubbles by argument order), the bound of a canonical masters provider. With the store, check passes (another frame, the method-choice acceptance, the rotation copy’s rows refused alone) run in workspaces without it, so a check recomputes every integral and keeps seeing the primary pass’s rounding. Both are measurement options, off by default: cross-family sharing through the store was measured below Q19’s 1.3x on the reduction stage (m-lit lit-cache report §6.2). Each row hands TIRust the S-matrix of §11.1 (InvariantInput::SuppliedInvariants: the same entries NinjaRS reads, the on-shell bound ones exactly the legs’ squared masses) and μ² itself (ScaleInput::MuSquared), so an on-shell leg next to a propagator of its mass (a top in its own gauge loop) stays on the exact on-shell branch in every carrier; the §11.1 contract holds on TIRust (massive-b reproducer: DoubleFloat = MPFR to 7.8e-32, TIRust = NinjaRS in MPFR at the on-shell neighbour to 6.6e-52; tests/unit/test_loop_v2_onshell.py). Rows the conditioning gates refuse fail closed with the gates’ reason; the extended carriers’ gates are binary64’s (TIRust’s default 1e-12; 1e-15 for the method-choice pass) taken to the carrier’s precision, g^(p/53) (v2_tir::carrier_gate), the same share of the significand, never the binary64 value itself; TIRust’s partial DD rescue and precision tiers stay off. In binary64 the gate-refused rows take TIRust’s a priori method choice (TirOptions::method_choice, on by default since lit-tir-mp; small-Gram expansions or the alternative PV, the alternative first within EXPANSION_TOLERANCE, DECISIONS 2026-11-07 ~10:05). TIRust leaves those values unchecked, so every such lane is accepted here only if its value in the rescaled rotation-by-one frame of the same row (masters recomputed at inputs rescaled by 7/10; the call’s check row when the call checks in that frame) agrees with the direct one within EXPANSION_TOLERANCE of its term scale, compared on every Laurent slot whatever the pole mode; otherwise it fails closed. A row the method choice refuses as well (a small-Gram expansion that does not converge because the Cayley determinant is small too, and an alternative PV whose modified Cayley determinant cancels) goes to the VERIFIED LAST RESORT (TirOptions::verified_last_resort, on by default since m-lit tir-uuzggg): plain PV at gate 0 in the unchecked mode’s third workspace, every lane of it then checked exactly as a method-choice lane (rescaled frame, TirOptions::acceptance = target/580), failing closed otherwise; its refusals are labelled ‘TIRust last-resort (gate-0 plain PV) lane refused by its check’ and counted as “TIR last-resort lanes refused by their check” (the measure kind stays MethodChoiceDeviation, the same frame deviation), its served rows as “TIR last-resort rows”. It is off where the method choice is off (the extended carriers: their gate-refused rows still fail closed) and irrelevant in the unchecked mode (which serves those rows unverified anyway); lanes the gates or the method choice serve are bitwise unchanged. Rationale: the gates bound the worst-case condition^rank of one subset, not the lane’s error; on u u~ > z g g g [QCD] every flat point was refused on rank-4 boxes of Gram conditioning 1e-4 to 5e-10 while the unchecked values were accurate to 1e-9 and better against NinjaRS double-double (tir-uuzggg report). The 580 calibration was derived on method-choice lanes and is carried over, not re-derived: over about 450 flat points of five processes no newly served point was beyond about 7e-9 of the reference at the default target 1e-5; coverage at much tighter targets is not demonstrated. User-visible: explicit "tirust" serves more points and the loop-induced "auto" falls back to NinjaRS less often (g g > z g g: fallbacks 12 -> 1 of 32). The frame is the rescaled one because a rotated frame alone is blind on some wrong lanes (massive boxes and pentagons the gates refuse on a massive sub-triangle: lit-tir report §H, 21 lanes served up to 1.9e-4 from a consistent truth at the earlier pin). Evidence at TIRust ac1e2342, every binary64 synthetic lane and check lane bitwise the same at the pin fefb5f2b (lit-tir-mp, lit-spike-tir’s synthetic set against NinjaRS at 60 digits on consistent inputs, cross-checked by TIRust at 256 bits): the rescaled acceptance refuses all 21 of those lanes, serves 33,430 method-choice lanes with a worst error of 1.3e-7, and refuses 1,079 lanes (3.2 %) the rotated acceptance would serve, 1,076 of them right to 1e-5 (its false-refusal cost); on the G1 rows g g > g g g and u u~ > e- e+ g g g the points it serves agree with NinjaRS to 3e-12 in the summed virtual, while many points of the 6-leg G1 rows still fail closed. The extended carriers keep the method choice off (TirOptions::extended_method_choice, not measured there): their gate-refused rows fail closed and the rescue ladder moves the point. A high-precision reference must take inputs consistent to its own precision: lift the exact sums or re-derive the non-bound entries from the lifted shifts; NinjaRS on the exact on-shell S-matrix with binary64 shifts that miss those shells by ~1e-16 moves by up to 5e-4 of a lane at any number of digits (lit-tir report §G, lit-onshell-probe). TIR’s check frame of a ReductionCheck never reverses (q → −q is bitwise blind for tensor moments): without rescale (the reduction-direction check) it is the cyclic relabelling of the propagators by rotation in the same loop-momentum frame, TIRust’s rotation copy (U3, DirectWorkspace::reduce_batch_with_rotation, m-lit lit-stab-t step C): the copy’s moments come from the direct pass’s own TIRust calls (gates and method choice; a row refused together with its copy takes one rotation-copy call of the method choice), bit for bit the separate pass in that frame (TirOptions::rotation_copy; Rust T11), with the lanes’ coefficients reused exactly; with rescale it is the rotation with the origin shift at inputs rescaled by 7/10, a second pass whose masters are evaluated anew (v2_tir.rs::tir_frame). A family outside TIRust’s capability query (DirectCapabilities::admits at the carrier’s precision, after the artifacts’ rank admission; v2_tir::capability_refusal) is refused typed with TIRust’s reason (the artifact runtime builds the plans once per call and carrier on TIRust, V2Executor.prepare_reduction, before any point); no TIRust limit is stated on pyAmpliCol’s side, and TIRust’s qualified domain (N ≤ 6, R ≤ 6) is reported, never enforced. Binary64 TIR touches no Symbolica state. The public choice is the reduction option of §12.2 (requested, effective backend and reason recorded per call and carrier, each rescue level’s carrier included; never a silent switch); NinjaRS’s internal fast/generic engine choice stays internal.

11.1 Hand-off per family and channel¶

Item

Content

Denominators

N_f lines: real shifts from leg masks; masses from mass ids (complex under the complex-mass scheme)

S-matrix

N_f × N_f from one canonical invariant table per event, on-shell bindings patched (below)

Rank

True structural rank; never over-declared, since over-declaring costs up to 981× in accuracy (guidance [V])

Numerator

C(R+4,4) complex coefficients scattered into TensorNumerator lanes; lane-major storage, coefficients_mut (ninjars:fast/tensor.rs:30-90 [V]); no text

DD/AP numerator

PolynomialNumerator (Symbolica expression) until the owner upstreams the generic tensor numerator (request 8)

Re-test

The same coefficients after the exact affine relabelling (§10.2), same bucket

Output

Raw Laurent [finite, 1/ε, 1/ε²] of μ_R^{2ε}/(iπ^{2−ε} r_Γ) ∫ N/ΠD, post-processed as 2 Re(i/16π²·Σ_f Ω_f) (rust/loop-reduction/src/lib.rs:5-9, 59-69 [V-s]); directed cross terms stay complex

On-shell external invariants (package precision-ap, 2026-10-25). An S-matrix entry whose arc is a single external leg, or whose complement is one (momentum conservation), is that leg’s squared mass at the point’s parameters, exactly the value its propagators take, never p(arc)² of the given momenta (families.onshell_leg). Python: _PointEvaluation._groups reads it from assemble._leg_masses (the exact value _mass_values gives the leg’s mass id). Native: ExactInvariants::square reads V2Batch::leg_masses (exact rationals: NativeExecutor._inputs passes them with python inputs; with native inputs TreeProgram::bind derives them from the external parameters, or for a derived mass from its parameter-program carrier output read exactly (TreeCarrier::exact), by the sources’ own mass lookup, SchemaSources::leg_masses), so the cast entry equals the cast propagator mass bit for bit. A leg whose mass is a derived parameter (loop_sm’s MW, any internal mass) is bound the same way (generation-scale-2 fix round 1, genericity audit M2): its invariants are the square of the value its wavefunctions and propagators take (Python: the one mass evaluator assemble._model_masses, at the working digits; native: the carrier value), see §16.2 WP3.1, items 3 and 4, ‘Derived masses bound on their shell’. Every other entry, the shifts, the trees and the wavefunctions use the momenta as given: nothing is projected or snapped inside the executor, and no tolerance is involved. Since m-lit lit-psimprove (§10.6) the momenta ‘as given’ to a carrier above binary64 are the improved point of the caller’s inputs: on it every bound entry equals p(arc)² of the improved legs to the carrier’s rounding, so S and the shifts agree (F-GH component I). All carriers bind the same entries. The structural proof of certified-scaleless families reads the same rule: Family.onshell_bindings calls onshell_leg, and the native families stage (the default, generator_input.NATIVE_STAGES) mirrors it in rusticol-core loop_v2::generate::families::certified_scaleless (its own single-leg arc test, equal on proper arcs; test_loop_v2_generate.py holds native and Python scaleless equal; it should call dress::onshell_leg at the next native change of that file). The staged validation’s oracle is _PointEvaluation._groups itself, so generation, the Python reference and the native executor share one rule (package onshell-consistency, 2026-10-26: the reference without the binding is O(1) wrong in binary64 and fails its C0 master at 40 digits on a binary64-rounded point; before precision-ap both binary64 routes agreed on that wrong value, which the staged validation could not see).

  • Why. oneloopmaster decides on-shellness by exact tests. Rounded momenta leave a leg off its shell by about 10⁻¹⁶ relative; the generic engine (DoubleFloat, MPFR, generic binary64) then evaluated the soft and collinear masters off shell, with log(p² − m²) in place of their poles: an O(1) error in every carrier but binary64 (b b~ > t t~ QED=2 [virt=QCD], massive b: binary64 3.0434, MPFR −50.574; g g > t t~ and g g > g g g at rounded RAMBO points likewise), and a 140-digit on-shell decimal point still left a massless leg’s C0 non-finite. Binary64’s fast engine hid the defect behind NinjaRS’s absolute 10⁻⁹ GeV² snap, which depends on units and energies (a 5 TeV massless leg rounds off shell by more).

  • Contract. Since m-lit lit-psimprove (§10.6) an evaluation in a carrier above binary64 (and a binary64 one under kinematics_improvement_binary64) returns the value at the improved point of the given inputs: each carrier first moves the caller’s point onto exact conservation and the bound shells in its own arithmetic (MadLoop’s default, "z-shift" with MadLoop’s fallback, finished by the projection where MadLoop leaves the point inexact: exact in every frame), then evaluates that point. On the improved point the bound invariants and the shifts agree to the carrier’s rounding, so DoubleFloat equals MPFR within 10⁻²⁴ on the same improved point, and the value of a rounded input differs from that of its exactly on-shell, momentum-conserving neighbour by the input’s own defect, about 10⁻¹⁴ relative (by up to ~10⁻⁸ where the z-shift moves a slow final state by ~sqrt(2 E dE), §10.6), with the record per point (the variant that produced it, its exactness record, or ‘evaluated as given’ with a typed warning). With the improvement off (kinematics_improvement = "off", and binary64 by default) the earlier physical-input contract holds unchanged: every carrier evaluates the same function of the inputs as given, binary64 within its accuracy (its stability estimate where that exceeds 10⁻¹²), and a point off its shells (or not conserving momentum) by δ moves the result at O(δ), amplified near degenerate kinematics (F-GH component I), so results beyond binary64 accuracy then need momenta on shell and conserving to that accuracy (exact rationals or enough decimals; tests/unit/test_loop_v2_onshell.py). The legacy engine binds the same invariants (on_shell_bindings, docs/LOOP_PHYSICAL_KINEMATICS.md).

  • Evidence. b b~ > t t~ QED=2 [virt=QCD] with a massive b: MPFR and DoubleFloat at the binary64-rounded reproducer point and at a rounded RAMBO point equal MadLoop (MG5_aMC 3.7.0, loop_sm default restriction, widths 0, quadruple-precision stability test forced, ImprovePSPoint 2) at the exactly on-shell points within 10⁻¹⁵ (relative) in the finite part and the single pole (3.04337313194461 and 0.584382517487585; 66.8536902819154 and 10.5488373076888); before the fix the same arbitrary-precision evaluations gave −50.574 and −806.48. g g > t t~, u u~ > t t~ g and g g > g g g agree in every carrier at rounded RAMBO points (before: O(1) off in DoubleFloat and MPFR, the massless double pole included, and IntegrationFailed at 140-digit on-shell decimals with a massless leg).

  • Binary64 at the reproducer is accurate to 6.6·10⁻¹⁰ (its reduction-direction estimate: 6.3·10⁻¹⁰ there, 4.2·10⁻⁹ at the exact neighbour): the fast engine’s (0, MT, MB) triangle family (the gluon correction of the W vertex) with original Ninja’s cut geometry, the momenta lying in the x–z plane. A boost along x restores 1.8·10⁻¹⁵, one along z does not (2.6·10⁻¹⁰); the generic engine in binary64 reaches 10⁻¹⁵. NinjaRS’s FastOptions::conditioned_cuts targets this geometry; it changes binary64 values and is not adopted here (open).

  • Catani. The single pole of this process (every carrier, and MadLoop) differs from pyAmpliCol’s Catani prediction by 0.45 % (0.584383 against 0.581745): [virt=QCD] loops are pure QCD (four vertex-correction triangle families here, MadLoop’s 12 diagrams), so no gluon joins the b and t lines (those boxes carry the γ/Z/W in the loop), while the operator includes the b–t colour correlations of the s- and t-channel interference. Without the W the two agree exactly. Pre-existing and independent of the carrier (owner: the "ir" pole prediction).

Complex pole masses (M-SM MS-CMS-N, 2026-10-29/30). Under the complex-mass scheme a particle with a width propagates with its pole mass CMASS_M = sqrt(M² − iMΓ), an internal parameter of complex type, with width ZERO (model_cms.complex_mass_model, MS-CMS, §6.8). The native trees read its two components like any derived parameter. A loop propagator whose mass parameter is internal and of complex type is a ["complex", o] plan mass of the parameter program (native_trees._parameter_program): not checked real and positive, bound to the square of its carrier value’s exact complex rational (TreeProgram::bind; BoundParameters::masses_imaginary and V2Batch::masses_imaginary, empty without a complex plan mass), the M² the tree propagators’ carrier value squares, and run complex by the reduction lanes. External legs keep real masses (stable states; the binder’s positivity check refuses a complex one). A Python-input batch gives a complex squared mass as an [re, im] pair (plan_export._mass_text, from MS-CMS’s _mass_values), and the kernel constants take the pole mass complex. A photon α ratio whose expression reads the imaginary unit (a complex-mass α, real by construction, e.g. the G_μ UFO’s Gfbar) takes its real part, as MG5_aMC’s double-precision rescale factor does; the complex conversion eCoup_DGmua0_UV_EW is a field coupling whose interference with the Born takes 2 Re of it, MG5’s real part. The binary64 fast-threshold record of a stored artifact reads |re| + |im| of a complex square (as v2_reduce does). With these the public route stores complex-mass artifacts (model_cms.NATIVE_POLE_MASSES = True): native point inputs (native-v2), relocatable bitwise. Records without complex plan masses are unchanged (an older native refuses the entry); the parameter program’s SymJIT plane bytes differ from run to run (pre-existing, also on 54ec03c5), everything else of the export is byte-identical on loop_sm controls. Evidence (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_native_complex_masses.py): CM10 (u d~ > w+ b b~ QCD=0 [QCD], loop_sm under CMS with Γ_t: resonant top in the Born, complex top loops and counterterms) with native inputs equals MadLoop CMS in quadruple precision at its four points, double-double to 7·10⁻¹⁴ on every coefficient, binary64 to 3.4·10⁻¹⁰, and the same request through the public route (mass_scheme = "complex-mass" on the shipped loop_sm) stores native-v2, relocates bitwise and its loaded artifact equals MadLoop CMS; CM08 (u d~ > e+ ve b b~ QCD=0 [QCD], G_μ UFO with Γ_t, Γ_W, Γ_Z, Γ_H) native = MadLoop CMS, double-double to 1.3·10⁻¹⁴, binary64 to 1.2·10⁻¹³ (nightly, about 18 min, 25 GB); CM09 (u d~ > e+ ve a [QCD QED], G_μ a0 under CMS, the photon tagged: complex conversion and α ratio) native = MadLoop CMS × MG5_aMC’s formula over the tagged photon with Re(eCoup_DGmua0_UV_EW), both sectors, double-double to 2.7·10⁻¹⁴, binary64 to 1.7·10⁻¹² (nightly, about 6 min, 7 GB). CM07, the [U4] acceptance process (g g > t t~ e- e+ g [QCD QED] s⁶e⁶, Γ_Z, Γ_W, Γ_H > 0, Γ_t = 0): with Γ_t = 0 the transform ties ymt := MT (MG5_aMC), so with the top propagating on MT the top Yukawa vertices of the EW loops read the loop line’s mass, which LeafWeights._require_mass_free_couplings refused (the tree reading flips that mass in the whole segment kernel; with the guard disabled, a diagnostic, the finite part and single pole were off by O(1)); with the top on its line mass LMASS_MT := MT (transform step 4b) it generates (2.7 min, 6.2 GB; export 2.4 min, 7.9 GB peak) and native = MadLoop CMS at its three points, double-double to 6.9·10⁻¹³ (finite), 4.5·10⁻¹⁴ (single pole), binary64 to 4.8·10⁻⁹ (nightly, about 10 min). On a loop_sm complex-top fixture the native lane binds M² − iMΓ to the carrier’s rounding in binary64, double-double and MPFR, agrees across carriers, and equals the Python-input lane at the card’s width (binary64 1.8·10⁻¹⁴ of the virtual, the parameter program’s binary64 rounding; double-double bitwise).

11.2 Batching, rank and masters¶

  • Buckets. One FastAmplitude::new(N, R, FastOptions::default()) per bucket; rank ≤ N + 2 is enforced (ninjars:fast/engine.rs:620-632 [V]).

    • Lanes are (family, point, sector, column), and every lane carries its own shifts, masses and S-matrix (FastInput, ninjars:fast/mod.rs:60-79 [V]).

    • So unrelated families share calls: 5–11 physical calls per batch instead of one per family (§11.4). The re-test reuses the same buckets.

  • Per-lane rank. The pinned NinjaRS (since aa6a6307; main b3a29c85) reduces a lane declared at rank n+2 at its own rank (FastNumerator::lane_rank), bitwise as declaring that rank, so buckets may merge by N. runtime/v2_reduce.rs still buckets by (N, true rank), with the same results; merging by N is open.

  • Master cache. A pyAmpliCol-side CachingMasters wrapper implements FastMasters (ninjars:fast/masters.rs:56-64 [V]) and is cleared per batch.

    • Keys are the exact bit patterns of the request arguments. This works because all S-matrices come from one invariant table per event.

    • Canonicalisation only where the outputs are invariant: C0 under the triangle’s symmetry group acting consistently on its external invariants and masses, and D0 under the dihedral relabelling of the box acting consistently on (p_i², s12, s23, m_i²). A0 needs none.

    • Bubbles are keyed by the ordered tuple [p², m0², m1², μ²]. BubbleRank2/3/4 return [B0, B1, B11(, B111, B1111)] for ordered arguments (ninjars:fast/masters.rs:16-26, fast/engine.rs:1817 [V]), and the tensor coefficients are not invariant under m0 ↔ m1: B1(p²; m0, m1) = −B0 − B1(p²; m1, m0). Revision 1’s mass-swap canonicalisation was wrong for unequal-mass bubbles and is withdrawn.

    • The canonicalisation is applied identically in cached and uncached runs, so they stay bitwise equal. WP1.6 tests unequal-mass bubbles on gg→tt̄ (top–gluon).

    • Integer master ids from generation are an upstream optimisation (request 4).

    • The measured redundancy at 7 gluons is 308,448 requests for 2,822 distinct masters (109×) [M recola-ninjars §5.3].

  • DD/AP. Same structure with the generic engine and its master provider.

  • Absolute thresholds (genericity audit 2, G2-M3; package onshell-threshold, 2026-10-27). On the pinned NinjaRS (41a4c00 when written; unchanged on main b3a29c85, run with the default threshold) the binary64 fast path compares its inputs with absolute constants in the model’s units, while the generic engines (SymbolicaMasters with with_onshell_threshold(None), runtime/reduction.rs) have none: OneLoopNativeMasters (ninjars-symbolica/src/oneloop_native.rs:27-49) sets squared masses and invariants with |re| + |im| < 10⁻⁹ to zero and a real invariant within 10⁻⁹ of a real squared mass onto it, and the engine (FastOptions::infrared_eps = 10⁻⁹) skips the bubble of two massless lines whose invariant is below it and builds its cut bases from momenta whose square is below it as light-like ones. A keV mass in GeV (m² = 10⁻¹²; or the electron in TeV units) thus became massless in binary64 alone: log m² turned into poles, and the result depended on the units.

    • Routing (interim, exact). v2_reduce::FastEngine hands every lane whose inputs reach one of these thresholds to the generic binary64 engine (reaches_fast_threshold): a squared mass or an off-diagonal invariant x with 0 < |re x| + |im x| < 10⁻⁹, or an invariant within (0, 10⁻⁹) of a real squared mass of the lane. The comparisons are exact on the given inputs, absolute (never relative to a scale: at s ~ 10⁶ GeV² a relative rule would move the electron mass) and keyed on no name or process; exact zeros, and invariants exactly equal to a mass (the executor’s on-shell external invariants, §11.1), never route. The rule runs per bucket and frame, on the frame’s own (rescaled) inputs, so a lane may take the fast engine in one frame and the generic one in the other. The routed lanes give the generic engine’s bits; every other lane, and every bucket without a routed lane, keeps the fast engine’s code path and bits (the loop_sm controls gg→gg, uu~→dd~g, uu~→tt̄, gg→ggg and uu~→e⁻e⁺gg are bitwise unchanged, with and without the reduction-direction and rescaled checks; no lane routes). Cost: per lane and frame, the n masses and n² − n invariants are compared with the threshold and each invariant with each of the n masses, O(n³) comparisons (no measurable cost: ‘Evidence’); a routed lane costs a generic binary64 reduction, and the first routed lane of each (n, rank) in an executor pays the generic engine’s one-time Symbolica template compile (measured for DoubleFloat at 0.35–10.8 s for rank 6–9, §10.1 ‘NinjaRS’; not measured for binary64, whose template is the same expression). Licence: the generic engine parses and evaluates Symbolica expressions, so a routed lane is the one binary64 reduction that touches the Rust copy of Symbolica; it runs under pyAmpliCol’s native library key, taken explicitly on the reducing thread (pyamplicol::unlock in FastEngine::reduce, besides the executor workers’ own guards), the exception to §12.1 (e)’s ‘binary64 needs no Symbolica’ (test_routed_binary64_lanes_run_under_the_package_key: unlicensed, permit held, completes with the key and aborts without it; the unrouted e+ e- > u u~ of the same artifact completes without it; on the caller’s own thread, as the Python reference path reduces, test_the_reference_reducer_takes_the_key_on_its_own_thread: a light bubble on V2Reducer('double', None, 'fast') is routed (take_exact_lanes = 1), completes with the key bitwise equal to the generic binary64 reducer and aborts without it, the heavy bubble completes without it; on a native without the explicit guard (the package’s 26a19255) the keyed run aborts in restricted mode, so the test pins the guard). When the package key expires (2028-03-01) such lanes need the user’s licence or Symbolica’s restricted mode, like DoubleFloat. Legacy engine (history: the engine and its production callers were removed by MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE, §13.3; runtime::PolynomialPlan stays as the Rust test oracle of the v2 reducer): runtime::PolynomialPlan’s binary64 fast plans (fast, fast-tensor; then the default engine’s) route by the same rule (reduction.rs FastPlan): a lane reaching the thresholds is reduced by the legacy generic binary64 plan of the same numerator, built on first use under the key, in chunks of 16 lanes, the rule applied to the invariants of the call’s s_matrix (the former production callers, physical_process.py and runtime/physical.rs, removed with the legacy engine, passed one with the external legs bound to their squared masses). A call without one (evaluate_decimal, evaluate_batch(s_matrix=None), the legacy Drell–Yan bare program) has its invariants formed from the binary64 shifts, which are not given inputs: below the thresholds they are rounding (a massless leg at a generic angle gives p² ≈ −7.3·10⁻¹¹ at E = 500), which the fast path’s snap sets to zero as it always did, and the generic plan would take for a slightly off-shell leg (the massless box O(1) off, or a non-finite C0 for the rotated Drell–Yan points: the re-audit of 2026-10-28, which found the first form of this routing doing so). Such a call routes on the given squared masses alone: a lane with a light squared mass is refused with the typed status light_mass_needs_invariants(threshold) (an InvalidInput naming the threshold the rule compared with; rounded invariants cannot resolve so light a mass, and an external leg’s squared mass is not given at all: a formed p² ≈ 0 may stand for a massless leg or for one of that mass; the remedy is the exact invariants or double-double), and every other lane keeps the fast plan with its snap of the formed invariants, the base behaviour and bits (the re-audit’s probes, the massless box and the rotated Drell–Yan points, now give the base native’s values digit for digit). Every lane neither routed nor refused, and every call without such a lane, keeps the fast plan’s code path and bits (the_legacy_fast_plans_route_light_lanes_to_their_generic_plan; without invariants the_legacy_fast_plans_without_invariants_route_on_the_squared_masses: the massless box at a generic angle keeps the fast plan and equals the generic plan given the exact invariants within 10⁻¹², while the generic plan at the rounded p² fails or is O(1) off; the light line is refused, and keeps its massless neighbour’s bits in one call; PolynomialPlan::take_exact_lanes counts, a test hook no production code reads; the legacy Python binding and runtime/physical.rs were removed with the legacy engine, §13.3). The legacy generation record carries no binary64_exact_engine entry (the record is informative; the runtime decides per lane). The executor’s report counts the routed lanes (binary64 lanes on the exact engine; V2Reducer::take_exact_lanes). Routing is per lane and per point because masses are runtime parameters and invariants per point. The artifact records what the generation parameters route: GeneratedProcess.binary64_exact_engine lists the masses of the process (loop lines of both plans and the external legs) whose binary64 square at the model’s defaults and the request’s fixed parameters lies in (0, threshold), the threshold being the engine’s own (runtime::fast_engine_threshold, the loop module’s V2_FAST_ENGINE_THRESHOLD), and the generation record keeps it as the filter binary64_exact_engine ({"threshold": "1e-09", "squared_masses": {"MT": "1e-12"}} for e+ e- > t t~ with MT = 10⁻⁶ fixed), written only when a mass is that light, so every other artifact keeps its bytes. The record is informative: the runtime decides per lane again, on the point’s invariants and on any parameter override (test_the_artifact_records_the_light_masses).

    • Evidence. e+ e- > t t~ [QCD] with MT = 10⁻⁶ (m² = 10⁻¹² in every loop line and both legs) at E = 500 GeV: the slice native (11542fd5) was 107 % off MPFR in binary64 with a reduction-direction estimate of 10⁻¹⁴ (silently wrong); with the routing (2 lanes) binary64 is within 1.1·10⁻¹⁵ of MPFR. u u~ > g g [QCD] (a closed light-top loop) routes 4 lanes and agrees within 1.3·10⁻¹³ (its estimate 7·10⁻¹³), but does not detect the snap: the closed light loop is smooth as m → 0, and the slice native’s fast engine was as close (1.2·10⁻¹³; the evidence audit), so it checks the routed path’s accuracy only; MT = 173 routes nothing. The legacy engine had its own routed check (e+ e- > t t~ with MT = 10⁻⁶ fixed, binary64 within 6.9·10⁻¹⁸ of MPFR), removed with that engine (MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE, §13.3). Routed lanes under the key: test_routed_binary64_lanes_run_under_the_package_key (above). tests/unit/test_loop_v2_onshell_threshold.py holds these (binary64 against MPFR under the user’s rule, DoubleFloat within 10⁻²⁴, on the four-light-line box of g g > g g within 10⁻¹⁷ (measured 2.05·10⁻¹⁸; MPFR(32) within 2.9·10⁻³⁵ of 64 digits there), no routing at MT = 173) and the unit independence of the dimensionless virtual: GeV against MeV (momenta, MT, MZ times 10³, G_F times 10⁻⁶, the scale times 10⁶) to binary64 accuracy, the light top routed in GeV and on the fast engine in MeV (m² = 10⁻⁶). tests/runtime_v2_reduce.rs: light internal masses (collinear-singular triangles of light lines, a box with a light line, the light bubble of a massless leg) are routed in both frames, equal the generic engine bitwise and DoubleFloat within 10⁻¹², while the massless lines’ integrals (what the snap computed) are O(1) off; fast lanes keep their bits beside routed lanes in one bucket; the pinned provider snaps exactly at the routing threshold; every lane (top, massless and light families) gives the same statuses and integrals scaled by x^(4−2N) in TeV, GeV and MeV (x = 10⁻³, 1, 10³; within 10⁻¹¹), the light lanes routed in TeV and GeV and on the fast engine in MeV; in units of a power of two (x = 2⁻¹⁰, 2¹⁰, every input scaled without rounding) the routing and every status are those of the GeV inputs exactly and the integrals agree within 10⁻¹², but not bitwise: the pinned binary64 reduction commutes with an exact rescaling only up to rounding (43 of 96 comparisons bitwise, at most 2.3·10⁻¹³ on the massless rank-4 box; power_of_two_units_scale_the_decisions_exactly): in that range a unit change moves the values by rounding and the routing and statuses not at all. Beyond it the fast engine was unit dependent through Ninja’s light-like spinors, which the routing cannot see (‘Large units’ under ‘Other thresholds’ below: O(10 %) errors from about 10⁴ times GeV-like units), until NinjaRS #10 (pinned since the mf-symbolica re-pin). The loop_sm controls gg→gg, uu~→dd~g, uu~→tt̄, gg→ggg and uu~→e⁻e⁺gg (native inputs, reduction-direction and rescaled checks) are bitwise the slice native’s (workspace/tmp/onshell-threshold/controls/). Binary64 runtime at B = 128 (one pinned thread, finite part, checks off, pooled medians, the evidence audit of 2026-10-28 against the slice 6da37352): g g > g g g g 421.32 → 418.63 ms per point (0.994), u u~ > g g g g 80.28 → 79.91 (0.995), every value bitwise equal, no lane routed; after the re-audit’s fix of the legacy no-invariant path (the v2 reducer’s rule only split into its two clauses), against the previous head 2fc09825 (paired rounds side by side on cores 248 and 254, swapped between rounds): 418.90 → 419.01 (1.000) and 78.77 → 79.56 (1.010; the reduction stage equal or faster, the difference in the unchanged native-tree stage), every value bitwise equal; merged with the slice f6619f34 (sdk-parity), against that slice’s native: 419.77 → 419.42 (0.999) and 81.24 → 81.19 (0.999), every value bitwise equal; merged with the slice 28a16255 (identical-flavour-lc, ew-leptons, gate-b128), against the slice native 5cb5ea83 (three paired rounds, cores 248 and 254 swapped between rounds, pooled medians of 15 blocks): 396.59 → 396.20 (0.999) and 74.66 → 74.88 (1.003), every value bitwise equal, and the loop_sm controls above bitwise the slice’s (630 values, no lane routed).

    • Binary64 masters at extreme hierarchies. A routed lane is only as accurate as oneloopmaster’s binary64 masters at its arguments (the fast engine’s own unsnapped masters are the same native evaluators). Measured at μ² = 10⁴ against 300 bits: A0, B0, C0 with light lines between massless legs and D0 with one or two light lines stay within 3·10⁻¹⁴ down to m² = 10⁻¹²; D0 with three or four light lines between massless legs loses accuracy about in proportion to s/m² (10⁻² and 10⁻³ at m² = 10⁻¹², the three-line figure from the review probe of the upstream PR, workspace/tmp/upstream-ninjars-onshell-threshold/correctness-probe.log); D0 and C0 rows with light lines beside a massive leg lose more (5·10⁻² at m² = 10⁻¹⁰ beside p² = 9·10⁴) and become non-finite at m² = 10⁻¹² (m²/p² ~ 10⁻¹⁷). Such a lane fails with the master’s reason (IntegrationFailed { … MasterFailed { integral: D0, failure: NonFiniteResult } }), so the point fails instead of taking the massless integral: g g > g g with MT = 10⁻⁶ (a box of four light lines) fails in binary64, which the snap had evaluated (there correctly, the light-top loop being smooth as m → 0) — DoubleFloat evaluates it (to 2.1·10⁻¹⁸ of MPFR, the same box’s conditioning). No escalation is automatic (requirements addendum C). Routed to oneloopmaster (stable small-mass forms). Light external quarks, and what the checks see (the evidence audit of 2026-10-28, re-measured on this package’s native): u u~ > t t~ [QCD] with MT = 10⁻⁶, beams along z, at (E, cos θ, φ, μ²) = (64, −0.8, 5.0, 1600) and (45, 0.9, 4.0, 8100): 10 lanes routed, the fast result bitwise the generic engine’s, binary64 2.52·10⁻⁶ and 1.32·10⁻⁶ from MPFR(40), while the reversed reduction check estimates 3.2·10⁻¹⁵ and 3.8·10⁻¹⁵ and one exact rotation (about z, 3/5, 4/5) 4.7·10⁻¹⁵ and 5.3·10⁻¹⁵: more than 10⁸ below the error, against the tenfold estimate rule (§10.4). Both checks evaluate the same masters (a rotation leaves every invariant unchanged; the reversed frame re-reduces with the cached masters), so neither sees a master’s own error; the rescaled check, which recomputes every master at 0.7 times the inputs, estimates 4.7·10⁻³ and 2.6·10⁻³. At (320, 0.35, 1.1, 90000), (150, 0.1, 0.3, 22500) and (900, −0.45, 2.0, 250000) the point fails with the C0’s NonFiniteResult (the audit’s measurement; the generic engine fails the same way on the base): fail-closed. Routed: the masters’ accuracy to oneloopmaster (above); the estimate gap to the stability owner (WP3.4/O1): an estimate that sees master errors on routed lanes (the rescaled check does, at the cost of re-evaluating every master). The user docs (‘Light masses in binary64’) recommend the rescaled check for light loops.

    • Upstream. OneLoopNativeMasters::with_onshell_threshold(Option<f64>) (default unchanged): NinjaRS PR https://github.com/alphal00p/ninjars/pull/9 (posted 2026-10-28 by the coordinator; merged on NinjaRS main 2026-11-03 as 27fb75d4, in the pin b3a29c85; workspace/reports/engine-v2/upstream/ninjars-onshell-threshold/). Not adopted yet: once the fast engine and the legacy fast plans take None, the masses’ and near-mass clauses of the rule go; the invariant clause stays for infrared_eps, which is still the fast engine’s massless-momentum threshold of its cut bases and of its scaleless-bubble skip (NinjaRS #10 made the light-like spinors threshold-free, so they no longer need it; see the spinor note below), and with it the key dependence of the lanes it routes.

    • Other thresholds on the binary64 path (completeness, read with this package). runtime/master_cache.rs keys rows on exact bits and canonicalises by exact relabellings: no threshold. NinjaRS’s fast::tensor_uv residue is exact algebra in the lane’s carrier (unit free). The v2 stability estimate (loops/v2/stability.py) is relative and nothing escalates automatically. FastOptions::relative_tolerance is relative; stability_threshold (10²⁰ DBL_MIN ≈ 2·10⁻²⁸⁸) is absolute but at the underflow scale, reached by no unit system short of 10⁻⁷⁰ GeV. The legacy engine’s binary64 fast path (lib.rs FastReducer, behind runtime/fast.rs) is routed as above. Unit dependent up to NinjaRS 41a4c00 and fixed by NinjaRS #10 (pinned since the mf-symbolica re-pin; the record below is the pre-fix evidence): Ninja’s light-like spinors (ninjars fast/geometry.rs:62-104, the cut bases’ e3, e4): a basis vector with |p⁰ ∓ p³| < infrared_eps takes the z axis’ spinor and drops its transverse momentum (up to (2E·10⁻⁹)^(1/2): a vector within ≈ (2·10⁻⁹/E)^(1/2) of the axis), and outside that window the spinor divides by √(p⁰ + p³), formed by cancellation near −z (relative error ≈ 2.2·10⁻¹⁶/θ² at an angle θ from the axis, unit free). No mass or invariant is near a threshold, so the routing cannot see either (the vectors are internal combinations of the loop’s momenta). Measured (a_rotation_check_sees_ninjas_lightlike_spinor_errors: a massless rank-3 box, beams along x, the outgoing legs at θ from the z axis, E = 500, no small invariant): the fast engine is silently off by 7.1·10⁻¹⁰ (θ = 10⁻³), 6.2·10⁻⁶ (10⁻⁵, cancellation), 8.8·10⁻⁶ (10⁻⁶, branch) and 8.8·10⁻⁸ (10⁻⁸), every lane ‘success’; the rotated point is within 10⁻¹⁴ and the generic engine within 6·10⁻¹⁵ in both frames; the rotation check’s difference equals the error and the reduction-direction check’s is 1.29–2.26 times it (both asserted, within 0.5–2 times and above 0.5 times the error), so both stability checks see it. With beams along z the same legs sit near a beam, where the box’s Gram determinant dominates and the fast engine returns Unstable for θ ≤ 10⁻⁶. Large units (the evidence audit of 2026-10-28; test_power_of_ten_units_keep_the_virtual_and_its_estimate). The same window makes the fast engine unit dependent at large factors. A beam along −z enters the cut bases as a difference of loop shifts (sums of external momenta in the family’s frame), so its p⁰ + p³ carries a rounding residue of about 10⁻¹⁶ times the energies: below infrared_eps (energies up to a few 10⁶ in the model’s units, so GeV-like units) the axis branch takes it and drops a rounding-size transverse momentum, which is harmless; above it the general branch divides the transverse rounding noise by √(p⁰ + p³) of the same noise, e3 and e4 are wrong at O(1), and the virtual is silently O(10 %) off, every lane ‘success’. Measured with every momentum and dimensionful parameter times f (the scale times f², G_F times f⁻²; nothing light, nothing routed), the virtual’s Laurent coefficients over the Born against DoubleFloat in GeV: g g > t t~ (beams along z, E = 400, the top at cos θ = 0.21, φ = 0.7) is within 4·10⁻¹⁵ for f = 10⁻⁵ to 10⁵, 2.2·10⁻¹ off at f = 7·10⁵ and 9.7·10⁻² at 3·10⁷, but 7.8·10⁻¹⁶ at 10⁶ (sums exact by chance); u u~ > d d~ g (fixture points 0 and 1) is within 7.5·10⁻¹³ for f = 10⁻⁶ to 10³ (the points’ own conditioning: the generic engine is 3.5·10⁻¹³ off at f = 1) and 2.6·10⁻² to 1.4·10⁻¹ off from f = 10⁴ (point 1, E = 7.8·10⁶) or 10⁵ (point 0) up to 10⁹ (point 1 fails Unstable at 7·10⁵). The generic binary64 engine is within 4.2·10⁻¹³ (3·10⁻¹⁵ on g g > t t~) and DoubleFloat within 2.4·10⁻¹⁴ at every factor. The estimates move with it: the reduction-direction check sees most of these points (8.4·10⁻² against 0.22) or fails them, but not all (u u~ > d d~ g point 1 at f = 10⁴: 7.9·10⁻¹³ against 6.8·10⁻²), and both reduction checks raise false alarms on exact values (the rescaled one, whose frame is 0.7 times the inputs, 0.43 on g g > t t~ at f = 10⁶; the reversed one 0.11 on u u~ > d d~ g point 1 at 10⁹). The exact rotation by 90° about x (beams along ∓y) removes all of it at every factor (within 3.7·10⁻¹⁵ and 2.6·10⁻¹³, estimates below 3.4·10⁻¹⁴ and 3.3·10⁻¹²), while the 180° rotation (the beams swapped on z) keeps it: the beam on −z is the cause, not a mass or an invariant, so no structural rule on the lane’s inputs sees it, and the routing above does not engage. The upstream note’s threshold-free spinor (the larger light-cone component, both copies geometry.rs and bases_x2.rs) removes it, measured with a scratch native of this head patched to it (upstream/ninjars-lightlike-spinor/experiment-larger-lightcone-component.patch, not a PR): g g > t t~ within 2.8·10⁻¹⁵ and u u~ > d d~ g within 7.6·10⁻¹³ at every factor, estimates below 3.2·10⁻¹⁴ and 2.9·10⁻¹², no point failing; the five strict xfails of the test XPASS. It is not bitwise: 214 of 640 loop_sm control values change, by at most 9.4·10⁻¹⁴ relative except g g > g g g point 0 (2.2·10⁻⁹), where it moves the binary64 virtual from 7.4·10⁻¹⁰ to 3.4·10⁻¹¹ of DoubleFloat (cut-basis vectors with |p⁺| < |p⁻| outside the window). Routed to the dedicated NinjaRS light-like spinor package (DECISIONS 2026-10-28 ~05:20 (3)), with this reproducer in the upstream note. Until the fix was pinned, models whose energies are of order 10⁶ or more in their units (keV or eV units; MeV with multi-TeV beams) needed GeV-like units or double-double in practice; the user docs (‘Units and the beam axis in binary64’) now state that no such limit remains. Since the re-pin on NinjaRS #10 the five strict xfails are plain cases (they pass), and the Rust test is inverted as the_fast_engine_is_accurate_near_the_beam_axis (fast, rotated and both checks within 2.4·10⁻¹⁴ at θ = 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁸; bound 10⁻¹³). Upstream note with a threshold-free spinor (the larger light-cone component; beam-axis bits unchanged): workspace/reports/engine-v2/upstream/ninjars-lightlike-spinor/NOTE.md. And the tree engine’s binary64 external spinors (rusticol-core/src/wavefunctions.rs:164,210: |m| < 10⁻⁸ in the model’s units takes the massless spinor in binary64 only, while the generic carriers test is_zero; the dropped components are m/√(E + |p|) against √(E + |p|), a relative m/(2E) (5·10⁻¹² for m = 10⁻⁹ at E = 100), below binary64 rounding only for E > 2·10¹⁵ m; the massive form divides by √(E + |p|) alone, so an exact mass == 0.0 test is the fix). Not this package’s files (the tree engine, rusticol-core): proposed to the coordinator for a tree-engine follow-up in the package report (‘For the coordinator’), with the measurement binary64 against DoubleFloat for an external fermion of m = 10⁻⁹ as its acceptance test; no value measured here is affected (m = 10⁻⁶ is above it).

11.3 Topology bookkeeping, and the user’s questions¶

Bookkeeping

Aspect

Rule

Identity

Canonical cyclic (leg mask, mass id) sequence (§3.3): Recola’s (ho, hm)

Canonicalisation

Key = minimum over rotations and reflections, at generation. Execution frames: per-family cost-optimal for B; leg-1 rule for F; cut-ordering frames for M. Oracles map frames with exact affine transforms

Selection

Structural rule plus certified-scaleless drop (§3.3); the drop is logged

Merging in the recursion

All partial results with equal key are summed: across block orderings, colour classes, species, helicities, sectors and columns. B: within (family, cut species, undressed contents). M: across families with equal prefix sets and undressed word. Never across denominators

Merging at closure

Species with equal masses, all cut species and all colour classes accumulate into one polynomial per (family, sector, column)

Merging at reduction

(N, R) buckets as lanes; master cache; optional stage 2 below

Born weighting

B: seeds at the leaves. M: seeds per ordering at the cut. Every state is Born-weighted and summed over the helicities of its dressed legs, so each family closes into the Born-weighted, helicity-summed numerator NinjaRS needs: one reduction per (family, sector, column), plus the re-test

Pinched topologies

Separate families; no lifting (MASTER_PLAN §2.13)

Lifting pinched families into parents (user guidance). Rejected in both forms:

  • Globally (multiply by the missing D_j): +2 rank and μ² per lifted line, and at most ≈2 lifts fit rank ≤ n + 2.

    • Cost model at gg→ggggg: 0.80 s (≤ n+1) and 2.7 s (≤ n+2), against 0.79 s for one reduction per family.

    • Probe errors: 3×10⁻⁴ (n = 6) and 8×10⁻³ (n = 7), against 10⁻⁷–5×10⁻⁶ for separate reductions [M recola-ninjars §4.1; recursion-literature §4.3].

  • Inside the recursion (merging members after their first step):

    • Even the idealised bound with no rank inflation only takes the 7-gluon dressing from 9.0×10⁸ to ≥ 4.0×10⁸.

    • The alignment it needs (OpenLoops’ pinch-invariant cut) costs 2.7×.

    • Families with N ≤ 4 cannot be lifted, and lifted hosts reduce at rank n+1 or n+2 [M otf/lift_bound.log].

Family-tree / integrand-sum reduction sharing cuts without rank increase (user guidance). The mathematics is exact: Ninja’s extraction is linear, triangles need no subtraction, and bubble and tadpole subtractions are linear in the parent residues [L 1203.0291 introduction.tex:98-117; V ninjars:fast/subtractions.rs per physics judge]. GoSam already reduces pinched diagrams together with their parent “with virtually no additional computational cost” [L 1111.2034 diagen.tex:100-130]. Three realisations:

Realisation

Gain on the NinjaRS stage

§2.13

API

Decision

(b2) per-member division / process-level cut lattice fed by family tensors: each family expanded on its cuts through NinjaRS’s own jets; geometry, subtractions and masters once per cut

≈1.15–1.3× (the expansions, 72–75 % of NinjaRS time with cached masters, are unchanged) [I, from the measured split in recola-ninjars §3.5]

Compliant

Default stage 2, if gated in

(b1) cut-restricted lift into parent groups: callback returns T_i = Σ_m N_m Π L_j^(i) with affine L_j on cuts containing line i; rank class kept

1.5× (n = 6), 2.0× (n = 7) at rotation-noise accuracy, on synthetic numerators [M recola-ninjars §4.2.3]

Needs an amendment (cut-reduced extra denominators)

None to start (cut is passed to callbacks, ninjars:fast/numerator.rs:58-66 [V])

Residue lattice with pyAmpliCol jets (Design 3)

Masters once per cut; best for many channels

Compliant

New NinjaRS lattice API plus private jets

Not adopted (private jet arithmetic duplicates NinjaRS; production would wait on an API)

Gate. Pursue stage 2 only if NinjaRS exceeds 30 % of the total after the master cache. At 7 legs FC the stage is 22–46 % of the target including the re-test (Table 1a), so stage 2 can bring ≈3–10 % overall with (b2) and ≈7–20 % with (b1). The master cache comes first: it alone removes 0.23–1.5 s at gg→ggggg [M].

Recola’s tensor-integral bookkeeping (user guidance). Adopted:

  • the identity (ho, hm);

  • canonical cut and orientation rules during the recursion (F);

  • species sharing by mass;

  • the counterterm flag in the current key.

Recola’s pinch sharing happens inside Collier’s call-position cache [L-s 1604.06792 §4]. That cache shares tensor sub-reductions as well as scalar integrals. The NinjaRS master cache shares only scalar masters, so it reproduces the scalar part of Collier’s sharing, not its tensor-reduction sharing. In integrand reduction the corresponding work (per-cut expansions) is per family by construction, and stage 2 (b2) is its analogue.

Recola’s “reduce numerator-independent integrals once, contract per (colour, helicity)” is unavailable to integrand reduction, which needs the numerator first. It returns through the transposed reduction (schedule 3, §11.5 request 2) for many-observable requests [V-s recola2 amplitude_rcl.f90:1470-1496].

OpenLoops on-the-fly reduction (user guidance). Its output, low-rank polynomials over fixed denominator sets, would be acceptable to NinjaRS; that is not why it is rejected. It is not adopted because:

  1. Speed. OpenLoops’ own benchmark finds reduction after dressing (OpenLoops2+Collier) faster, depending on the process; OFR is kept there for stability [L 1710.11452 OL_OFRED_paper_epjc.tex:3836-3846].

  2. Private mathematics. It would be private reduction mathematics next to NinjaRS, against the user’s reuse rule.

  3. Integrand-level validity. The del Aguila–Pittau step holds at integrand level only for N ≥ 4 [L-s 1710.11452 §4.1]. It needs Gram-determinant expansions and hybrid precision.

  4. More families. Pinch closure adds families: uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g goes from 244 to 422 [M].

A few integrand-level steps could bring rank > N+2 effective-theory numerators into NinjaRS’s domain. That belongs in NinjaRS if ever needed.

11.5 Requests to the NinjaRS owner¶

These may be pushed to NinjaRS main under the 20 October authorisation (MASTER_PLAN.md:96-103 [V]), in priority order:

  1. Coordinated re-pin to the new mains with per-lane rank: done (WP0.2). Still requested: an upstream test that lanes of unrelated families give bitwise the same result batched and unbatched.

  2. Transposed / multi-numerator reduction. H numerators share one geometry; equivalently, each family’s integrals of all monomials are returned once. This enables schedule 3 for correlations and resolved outputs.

    • The owner’s study (docs/audits/transpose-probe.md [V]) is a symbolic instruction count on a three-propagator, rank-3 toy, starting from Laurent callback heads.

    • It is a negative result at one numerator per changing point (:21). Its thresholds, H > 1.85 and H > 3.97 for fixed geometry, are explicitly not timing predictions (:45).

    • A measured prototype is required before schedule 3 is adopted.

  3. Per-(cut, lane) conditioning diagnostics: minimal uncut-denominator leading coefficient, Gram determinant. These feed the error budget (§10.2).

  4. Optional integer master ids in master requests, so the cache needs no hashing.

  5. Gated stage 2: process-level lattice in tensor-provider mode or per-member division; or, after sign-off, a layout-aware affine-product builder plus a cut-reference adapter.

  6. Optional coefficient-major TensorNumerator ingress, to avoid the closure transpose.

  7. Public jets API for (b2), if stage 2 is gated in: fast/tensor_jets.rs is private today.

  8. Upstream the generic-precision tensor numerator (TensorGenericNumerator<T>, now only in ninjars-cli/src/case_check/harness.rs:1290), so that DD/AP ingress needs no Symbolica expression.

  9. Opt-out of the native masters’ absolute on-shell threshold (OneLoopNativeMasters::with_onshell_threshold(Option<f64>), default unchanged; G2-M3, §11.2 ‘Absolute thresholds’): NinjaRS #9, merged on its main 2026-11-03 and pinned since the mf-symbolica re-pin (workspace/reports/engine-v2/upstream/ninjars-onshell-threshold/).

  10. Threshold-free light-like spinors in the fast engine (fast/geometry.rs Spinor::new: no absolute infrared_eps window, no √(p⁰ + p³) by cancellation near −z; §11.2 ‘Other thresholds on the binary64 path’): NinjaRS #10 (the larger light-cone component), merged on its main 2026-11-03 and pinned since the mf-symbolica re-pin; it changes the fast engine’s bits (upstream note workspace/reports/engine-v2/upstream/ninjars-lightlike-spinor/NOTE.md).

12. Artifacts and public API¶

12.1 Artifact¶

As built (WP2.6, loops/v2/artifact.py, generation/loop_artifact.py, rusticol-core/src/loop_artifact.rs):

  • Envelope. The schema-v3 directory, transactional writer and payload digests are kept; the runtime capability is rusticol.loop-runtime.v4 (known to VerifiedArtifact, not a tree-execution capability). An artifact of the removed legacy engine (rusticol.loop-runtime.v3) is refused typed at load and inspection (CompatibilityError, LEGACY_LOOP_ARTIFACT_REMOVED; MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE, §13.3). No backward compatibility (AGENTS.md, contracts K9).

  • Per process processes/<id>/:

    • loop-runtime.pacbin: the member schedule/loop-plan-v4.bin.zlib of kind LOOP_RUNTIME_PLAN = 12 (MadGraph7’s copy; upstream pyAmpliCol numbers it 11, which MadGraph7 had already given to DECLARED_PAYLOAD, the packed declared payloads released in MadGraph7 v0.3.0, so loop artifacts of the two copies are not interchangeable), the zlib stream of the plan’s binary member (M-FINAL MF-8G-1 item 5, “Binary plan member” below; before it, and with native_lowering.BINARY_PLAN off, schedule/loop-plan-v4.json.zlib, the zlib stream of the plan v4 JSON) of plan_export (families, tries, merged section when present, seed weights, block-row and Born layouts, kernels). Exact seed tables and counterterm columns are exact rationals inside it. A process with certified-scaleless families also stores their companion plan (LoopSlice.scaleless, §12.4) as schedule/loop-plan-v4-scaleless.bin.zlib (or .json.zlib), same kind; only the uv and ir pole selections run it.

    • execution.json (schema 4): runtime capability, plan SHA-256, the companion plan’s SHA-256 (scaleless_plan_sha256, null without certified-scaleless families), point_inputs and the generation request (process, Born bounds, exact loop orders, corrections, fixed parameters, colour accuracy and formal-N_c declaration, seed contraction, the resolved correlator declarations).

    • physics.json (schema 2): LoopV2ExecutionMetadata (Born orders; sectors with their (Born, loop) pairs, each a separate partial result; families; (N, R) buckets; colour accuracy and LC/NLC degrees; seed contraction; schedule B; model R2; carriers double, double-double, arbitrary; declared colour histories, spin classes and resolved capability; the served pole selections poles = ["all", "none", "uv", "ir"] (exactly these: any other declaration, e.g. ["all", "none"] of the internal pre-split format, is refused with a request to regenerate, since internal artifact formats are not kept backward compatible (AGENTS.md); a companion is stored exactly when its digest is declared; its digest and its legs, rows and sectors are checked against the process plan at admission, and at load the regenerated companion must have the stored digest); rotation and reduction-direction checks; caller-side rescue; scheme declarations), the legs and the Born helicity rows.

    • model/compiled-model.json at the root; process-groups.json lists exact flavour members (exact-loop-flavor, identity port) served by their representative.

  • Native admission (load_loop_v2_artifact, rusticol-core feature loop-v2): envelope, execution and physics declarations (unknown fields refused), the plan digest, and the validated program, whose families, buckets, legs, helicity rows, sectors and spin-class legs must equal the declarations. The legacy loader (the SDK’s) refuses v4 with the reason.

  • Kernels are exact polynomial term lists interpreted natively (loop_v2/dress.rs), not SymJIT applications: the plan holds no compiled code (§5.5; factor builds 0.16–0.72 ms/pt). Their terms are in a canonical order (reference_executor._term_order: the monomial, then the constant key, both compared as exact tuples; the order of WP2.5), so neither the plan nor any summation depends on Symbolica’s symbol ids. A content whose tree reading flips the sign of its outgoing massive fermion’s mass (TreeReading.mass_signs) binds its own copy of each kernel, whose numbered constants the batch values with the flipped mass (plan_export; before this the native executor was wrong on every process with an open massive quark line through the loop, e.g. uu~→tt̄ and gg→tt̄, which the Python reference already handled). Referencing a prepared model bundle’s compiled kernels stays a measured option, not needed for size (zlib already folds repeated kernels: gg→gggg publishes < 20 MB).

  • Portability (requirements addendum G; package artifact-portability on the integrated slice). Every reference is relative to the artifact root; the configuration records paths by file name only (every engine, artifact_writer._portable_paths); no user or host name is stored. Acceptance: tools/loop_artifact_portability.py and tests/unit/test_loop_artifact_portability.py. The tool’s check scans, copies the artifact to another path and evaluates both in fresh interpreters with other working, home and temporary directories and user names, compares bitwise and counts generation calls; --hold-permit adds concurrent unlicensed evaluations of the copy while a plain Symbolica process holds the restricted permit, --arithmetic/--precision select the loop carrier and --client the loop SDK; tree-capi runs a tree artifact’s own C example through the tree C API at both locations; cpu-matrix runs QEMU user-mode CPU models. The cross-host recipe is in its docstring.

    • (a) SymJIT IR, recompiled at load. A v4 loop artifact with native point inputs (point_inputs = "native-v2", native_process.NativeProcess) stores the plan (kind 12), the saved exact evaluators of its tree program (kind 2: the interaction kernels of the trees and of the counterterm program, and the parameter program) and one binary64 SymJIT plane application per saved evaluator (kind 1, point-inputs/kernel-<k>.symjit, point-inputs/parameters.symjit). They are storage-v4 IR at -O2 (native_trees._PLANE_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL; evaluator.jit.optimization_level does not apply), except a program whose -O2 code fails the plane check at a probe row, kept at level 0 if that passes (§15 risk 13); the stored IR keeps its level, which load recompiles at, so both are portable. Until a fixed SymJIT is pinned, the fallback is decided by the generating host’s SIMD code: a kernel plane certified at -O2 on a CPU class whose code does not show the defect runs unchecked on one whose code may. The parameter program always compiles at level 0 (native_trees._PARAMETER_PLANE_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL): it runs once per batch or scale, and level 0 has no peephole pass, so the defect cannot reach it on any CPU class. symjit_plane::SymjitPlaneKernel::load_bytes authenticates, recompiles for the loading CPU and seals them at load (loop_v2::trees::BinaryPlane); the native admission requires them.

      • Export (native_trees._plane_applications → _loop.compile_v2_plane → loop_v2::trees::compile_plane_application_checked): from the saved state’s binary64 evaluator (coefficients cast as the runtime casts them) through Symbolica’s Rust instruction export, so registered constants and fixed-argument functions (pi, …) keep their binary64 values. The model’s helper functions of the parameter program (pyamplicol_v2_canonical::c*, piecewise on pyamplicol_scalar_v1::equal with if_else/join) are inlined (symjit_plane::InlinedProgram, on an explicit stack without a depth limit), and the scalar primitives are bound as SymJIT external functions by name (scalar_primitive_defuns, at compile and at load). Each application is checked against its evaluator at generation, at two complex points off the real axis and at the real points it runs at (the parameter program: the request’s parameter values; WP3.2 status, ew-native), and refused on a disagreement. test_loop_plane_applications_equal_their_exact_states compares every stored one with Symbolica at the parameter program’s default inputs and at random inputs (1e-12).

      • Batch independence: SymJIT’s SIMD and scalar kernels of one application round differently in the last bits, so BinaryPlane pads the rows of a call to whole SIMD blocks (copies of the last row, discarded) and a point’s value does not depend on its batch (test_native_scales_may_change_per_point).

      • Reproducible generation: from empty and warm model caches the plan and every native member are byte-identical (test_native_members_do_not_depend_on_the_model_cache; the parameter program names its helpers in sorted order, since a compiled and a cached model list them differently), parameters.symjit included: SymJIT 2.28.3 (pinned since M-FINAL MF-UP) tags external calls deterministically (siravan/symjit#26; 2.27.3 tagged each with rand::random(), so the IR of a program calling the scalar primitives differed between two compilations, never between loads of one artifact; test_plane_applications_calling_primitives_are_byte_reproducible).

      • The plan’s kernels stay exact term lists interpreted natively (§5.5). The tree engine’s SymJIT -O2 kernels are storage-v4 IR as before.

    • Speed of the binary64 plane path. The interaction program fills a plane kernel’s input planes directly from the states (plane_interactions, plane_propagator in run_interactions). It works one plane at a time with contiguous stores, in calls of at most 1,024 rows (PLANE_ROWS, so a call’s planes stay in L2), on a buffer that only grows (plane stride = padded rows plus one cache line; PlaneRows::{planes, run}). Padding and the row-major accumulation order are unchanged, so the values are bitwise those of a row-major fill. A/B on one native and tree, the exact-state arm with native_trees._plane_applications patched to return nothing (tools.loop_benchmark pyamplicol <process> --inputs native --batches 128 --reps 3, full colour, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, both arms at once on two idle cores, then swapped; median ms/pt; release cu16 without LTO, so not the report’s absolute values):
