    • (b) What is scanned. Every file and every PACBIN member (zlib members decompressed) for absolute paths under common roots, the generating host’s home, working and temporary directories, the artifact’s own location, user and host names; native binaries; the member kinds and SymJIT storage version; the manifest target (portable-64le, no CPU features). The v4 artifacts of (f) scan clean.

    • (d) No regeneration. A sentinel counts calls of generation code (GENERATION_CODE, GENERATION_FILES: slice and plan generation, the model compile, GenerationBackend.generate, api.Generator.generate, the native generator’s and native DAG’s inputs, the native-trees export with its plane compile, the observables’ slice and column plans and the export of the stored observable columns; test_sentinel_entries_name_existing_generation_code resolves every entry) from before the first pyAmpliCol import to the end of the evaluation. On native-v2 artifacts it counts zero for every inclusive call: all four pole selections (the process stores the companion of its certified-scaleless families with its own tree program, native_process.NativeCompanion, PACBIN members point-inputs/scaleless/*; generation-scale-2), stability checks, double-double, set_model_parameters, per-order partials, and an exact flavour member served by its representative (the identity-port member listed in process-groups.json was proved at generation, loop_service._v2_member; the load reads it as artifact._stored_member). It counts zero for every observable call too (generation-scale-2, resumed run): colour-correlated (directed histories, also in “uv” with the companion’s columns, with stability checks, in double-double), spin-correlated and helicity-resolved calls and the correlation catalogue, with and without declared observables, and a member’s directed history. The process stores its observable column sets (native_observables.StoredObservables, PACBIN members point-inputs/observables*, every native-v2 process): per set (correlated: the Born metric and every declared history; resolved: per Born helicity row, and per Born basis element at LC) the seed records of its plan over the stored plan (export_plan(column_sets=...) forms them on the plan’s own exporter after the plan, so the plan is unchanged; a set equal to the plan’s own columns stores none, a set on the plan’s own seed-weight columns stores only its column fields), the plan’s Born components in the tree program’s numbering, the lanes of its columns, the same for the stored companion; the column interferences (loop_v2::trees::TreeProgram::set_columns: exact overlaps of the Born basis with the CT ket tensors under the column’s metric, the counterterm interference’s own cells for the Born metric (stored as null), a directed history’s operator and its swap, with the column’s LC/NLC degrees, kept rows and bra basis elements, entry lists and directed metrics stored once per set); and the vector spin-source slots of the trees’ and the CT program’s states with their crossing phases (a source vector replaces the leg’s wavefunction natively; the leg keeps its fixed row). A load builds StoredObservableSlice (no slice) and the observables package assembles the requested columns on the native interferences (observables._Assembly, ColumnPlan.checked). A declared process keeps every CT ket component in its tree program (keep_kets: a history can read a component the Born metric does not). Plan v4 column_weights: columns that differ only by their helicity rows have equal seed weights, so a plan may name per observable column its seed-weight column (plan_export.weight_columns; loop_v2::plan validates it, loop_v2::seeds reads each column’s weights through it) and its seed class records hold one weight list per weight column; the exporter writes it only when columns share (every inclusive plan’s bytes and digest are unchanged). Without it the six-gluon resolved interferences took 22.6 MB and the seven-gluon resolved set’s seed records were killed after 7 min at 38 GB. Cost for a process without declared observables (FC; both sets: the Born metric and 32, 64, 128 resolved columns): g g > g g g 1.8 kB of observable members (zlib; the native members 249 kB), generation 14.0 s against 14.1 s without them; g g > g g g g 2.6 kB (3.47 MB), 47.8 s against 47.9 s; g g > g g g g g (top veto) 5.5 kB (69.8 MB), its observables’ work in generate_process (583 s, process peak 11.3 GB) 0.12 s for the export and no seed records beyond the plan’s and its companion’s own (33.6 s and 5.7 s; one run, workspace/tmp/generation-scale-2/r2/obs7/). Cost with every dipole declared (fix round 2; FC, all T_i·T_j as directed histories, post_build_validation = false, loop_sm, one process per run, workspace/tmp/generation-scale-2/obs-cost/). Three stages made declared dipoles expensive; each is now native or gone, with its Python form kept as the oracle. (i) Metrics. A directed history’s metric (Born basis × CT ket tensors under its operator and its swap) was one Python contraction per (b, t) pair (DirectedColour.overlap, now the oracle), 96 % of the export. It is now one native table per direction (package C’s colour cells: NativeCells.directed images of the literal basis against every ket tensor, native_observables._Metrics). A metric is stored as its distinct cells with one index per (ket tensor, basis element) (schema 2, MetricCells::Table: the interference sums each distinct cell once per metric class; 29 distinct cells over 120 × 265 pairs at six gluons, 552 over 720 × 1,854 at seven). (ii) Column records. The column sets’ seed records were the exporter’s Python projection (_Exporter.seed_records, now the oracle). They are now projected natively by package C’s C2 native_cells.project_records on the directed tables’ native cells (plan_export._set_records, NATIVE_COLUMN_RECORDS, the slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-26 ~15:10 item 4 route; the plan’s own seed records keep D3’s call site). The bytes are identical: every PACBIN member of the six-gluon artifact equals the Python projection’s (the nondeterministic parameters.symjit aside), and test_stored_metrics_equal_the_oracle checks the bytes of the correlated set and its companion twin. (iii) Self-adjoint dipoles. A dipole took two seed columns (direct and swapped) and two metrics. A history with one gluon emission on each side, off two different legs and with the same emitted gluon, is self-adjoint when its swapped seed table equals its direct one with a nonzero cell (observables.DirectedColour._self_adjoint, compared on the native tables’ distinct cells and ids). The direct cells are s_i <b|T_i T_j k> and the swapped ones s_j <b|T_j T_i k>, with T_i† = s_i T_i (a colour charge is hermitian up to its convention’s phase) and T_i T_j = T_j T_i. Equal tables therefore give s_i = s_j, and the two directions agree on every tensor, the CT kets included. A self-adjoint dipole takes one seed column (2 Re, as a symmetric history) and stores one metric without evaluating its swap. The companion takes the slice’s decision, so the lanes are numbered alike, and checks its own tables against it. SELF_ADJOINT_HISTORIES = False keeps the two-column form (the oracle). Every correlated output of u u~ > g g g with all ten dipoles, at FC and NLC, in every pole selection, binary64 and double-double, is bitwise the two-column form’s (test_self_adjoint_dipoles_take_one_column, NLC nightly), and the stored swapped metrics equal the oracle’s per-pair overlaps. A correlated call reads half the lanes: the ten dipoles of u u~ > g g g at 128 points, finite only, one thread, take 5.56 s against 11.45 s (best of five). Six gluons (g g > g g g g, 15 dipoles; cores 232-239, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8, warm caches, two alternating runs per arm): generate_process 309.6 s at the audited head (12 threads), then 66.3 s after (i) (12 threads), 41.6 s after (ii), 39.7 s after (iii), and 38.5 s with the native comparison. Without declared histories it takes 35.0 s, so the dipoles cost +10 % (the whole generation: 45.7 s against 41.8 s, +9.4 %). The remaining 3.5 s are the directed seed tables (0.5 s), the swapped tables and their comparison (0.46 s), the column records (0.62 s; 27.2 s in Python) and the metrics (1.8 s for 15 tables; 3.6 s with the swaps, 240.8 s per pair in Python). Process peak 3.18 → 1.42 GB (1.35 GB undeclared); process PACBIN 14.9 → 5.83 MB (4.40 MB undeclared); the correlated-columns member 9.25 → 0.31 MB. g g > g g g (10 dipoles): the export takes 0.06 s of metrics (5.0 s per pair in Python). Seven gluons (g g > g g g g g, top veto, 21 dipoles; same cores and threads, one run per arm, one seven-leg job at a time): generate_process takes 784.1 s with all dipoles against 418.6 s undeclared (+87 %), and the whole generation 894.9 s against 518.2 s. Process peak 17.2 against 11.2 GiB, reached in the native projection of the correlated set. Artifact 182.6 against 88.3 MB: the observable members are 94.2 MB of the 177.3 MB PACBIN (correlated seed records 56.9 MB, companion seed records 17.1 MB, metrics 20.2 MB, all zlib). For comparison, fix round 2’s head (12 threads, before (ii) and (iii)) took 2,264.7 s at 30.7 GiB; its Python column records alone took 1,278.7 s (1,029.6 s for the process and 249.1 s for the companion twins). The extra 365.5 s at seven gluons are the directed seed tables (28.8 s, 21 × 1.3 s), the swapped tables with their comparison (28.8 s), the column records natively (34.5 s) and the metrics (252.6 s): 21 native tables of 720 × 1,854 generic cells at 10.4 s each (482.6 s with the swaps), which do not speed up from 8 to 12 threads because the engine’s serial phases over the 1.33 M (structure, basis) tasks of a table dominate (task registry, cache lookups and stores, value interning; loop_v2::generate::cells, the engine’s cells). Open, routed to package C (native-cells phase 2): the directed metrics at seven legs (all histories in one batched call, unit literal ket tensors by cycle counting as the inclusive CT cells are, native_trees._counterterm_program, or one metric per dipole orbit relabelled with C4’s orbit representatives), and the size of the correlated seed records (D’s and C’s record format, one weight list per class and column). Every PACBIN member but the correlated columns (and the nondeterministic parameters.symjit) is byte-identical to the oracle’s; the correlated calls of u u~ > g g g at FC and NLC (11 histories, all/uv/ir/none, double-double) are bitwise those of the per-pair list format (test_stored_metrics_equal_the_oracle checks the tables against the oracle). Binary64 observable calls run without a licence while the restricted permit is held, with pyAmpliCol’s native key disabled (test_binary64_observable_calls_touch_no_symbolica_state). The public O1 checks against the legacy records (test_loop_v2_artifact.py: FC/LC/NLC, members, u u~ > g g g with spin, binary64, double-double and 60 digits) run through the stored columns; against the former regenerated path (Python per-point trees) the stored columns agree within 3.1×10⁻¹⁴ of each output’s scale on g g > g g (all and “uv”, three histories, spin, resolved). The asymmetric Ward mode is a validation tool of the generated slice and is not stored. native-v1 (no plane applications) is refused at load (test_loop_artifact_with_retired_or_unknown_point_inputs_is_refused).

    • (e) Licence. Without SYMBOLICA_LICENSE, Symbolica’s restricted mode admits one thread per lock directory (by default the user’s): the first Symbolica state access of a process takes it and every other unlicensed process aborts. The Python package key (set_library_key in pyamplicol/__init__.py) unlocks only the Python symbolica module, not the Rust copy in _rusticol and the loop SDK; _rusticol touches no Symbolica state at import (the scalar primitives are registered by the decoders that need them).

      • Binary64 needs no Symbolica, except the lanes routed to the exact engine (§3.7): the native lane runs the plane applications and loading decodes no exact state (test_binary64_loop_evaluation_touches_no_symbolica_state: two concurrent unlicensed binary64 evaluations complete while the permit is held and the native key is disabled, PYAMPLICOL_NATIVE_LIBRARY_KEY=off). The exception (G2-M3, §11.2 ‘Absolute thresholds’; DECISIONS 2026-10-28 ~05:20 (4)): a lane whose squared masses or invariants reach the fast engine’s absolute 10⁻⁹ thresholds (a keV-scale mass in GeV) is reduced by the generic binary64 engine, which builds and evaluates Symbolica expressions under the package key, like DoubleFloat (test_routed_binary64_lanes_run_under_the_package_key, test_the_reference_reducer_takes_the_key_on_its_own_thread); with the key disabled such an evaluation aborts while the permit is held, and after the key expires (2028-03-01) it needs a personal licence or Symbolica’s restricted mode. There is no other exception at any model parameters, scale or pole selection (USER ~17:35, M-SM MS-MASTERS round 5): the parameter program’s plane takes the exact evaluator’s side of every branch cut at real inputs by construction (§3.7, the plane check), so nothing is checked at run time. Rounds 1–4 had checked the plane against the saved state once per new parameter key under the package key, which a width set to zero, a new mass or LogSwitch = 0 triggered; removed. The held-permit tests: g g > g g at αs = 0.12, MT = 172 and each of WZ, WW, WH = 0 (test_binary64_parameter_changes_need_no_key); the shipped EW self-test (e- e+ > e- e+ [QED] on loop_qcd_qed_sm) at MadLoop’s second and third points and scales (μ_R² = 4.9·10⁵, 1.96·10⁶) for every pole selection, bitwise equal to the keyed run and equal to double-double by the binary64 rule, and at MZ = 91.19, MW = 80.5 and LogSwitch = 0, equal to double-double (test_binary64_ew_evaluations_need_no_key); its stored parameter plane equals its state output by output at new scales, αs, α, epsIR = 0, LogSwitch = 0, MT, MZ and MW = 100 (a cut the plane had taken on the other side; test_ew_parameter_plane_equals_its_state_off_the_generation_values). Under the complex-mass scheme CM05’s nightly evaluates MadLoop’s four points at their four scales (μ_R = 1000, 700, 1400, 500) and equals MadLoop CMS (test_cm05_native_inputs_equal_madloop_cms); CM01’s binary64 at zero widths equals MadLoop’s zero-width virtual (test_cm01_masters_avoid_the_known_complex_mass_defects). Against the former exact-state evaluation the binary64 values moved in the last bits (instruction order and FMA; the g g > g g Born 56.50237664591928 → 56.502376645919256, DoubleFloat 56.502376645919255).

      • DoubleFloat and arbitrary precision use pyAmpliCol’s library key in the native code (user decision 2026-10-24 ~16:05). The workspace crate pyamplicol (rust/crates/pyamplicol, named after the package the key is issued for, publish = false) registers the key with Symbolica’s documented set_library_key! into a pub(crate) static and gives pyAmpliCol’s other crates thread-bound guards only (pyamplicol::unlock, unlock_thread). Guards are held while decoding saved evaluators, registering the scalar primitives, running exact kernels of the tree runtime (TreeRuntime::runs_exact_states: DoubleFloat, arbitrary precision, or binary64 on a CPU without SymJIT), in the executor’s generic reduction and every worker of the v2 executor’s pool (and formerly in the legacy virtual runtime, removed with the legacy engine, §13.3). Every native entry point holds one as well (package lic-gen, 2026-11-12): each #[pyfunction] and each #[pymethods] method, except plain field accessors, of _rusticol (tree bindings) and of its _loop module, and every call of the tree C ABI and of the loop SDK ABI (their guard helpers); the native pools that touch Symbolica state hold one per worker. Generation, check, evaluation and profiling without a personal licence therefore never take the restricted permit nor print the restricted-mode banner (before, an unlicensed generation of u u~ > d d~ [QCD] aborted while another unlicensed process held the permit: loop_kernel_terms parsed Symbolica atoms outside the guard of its worker pool). PYAMPLICOL_NATIVE_LIBRARY_KEY=off still disables every guard, so the held-permit tests of the key-free paths keep discriminating (tests/unit/test_unlicensed_generation.py). A personal licence is used as before; a rejected key leaves inert guards. Tests: test_unlicensed_extended_precision_loop_evaluations_run_concurrently (binary64, DoubleFloat and 32 digits concurrently and unlicensed while the permit is held, agreeing at an exactly massless point to 1e-12; with the key disabled DoubleFloat aborts), test_native_library_key_uses_symbolicas_documented_registration, test_native_library_key_equals_the_python_package_key (the two copies of the key, compared by digest). The v4 SDK (V2Runtime, generation-scale-2) inherits the guards through loop_v2::trees and the executor.

      • The permit. Symbolica keeps the restricted-thread lock in SYMBOLICA_LOCK_DIR, else $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/symbolica/locks, else the cache directory’s symbolica/locks. RestrictedPermit resolves it once (symbolica_lock_dir, or an explicit lock_dir) and passes it to the holder, its control and every instance it covers, so instances with a fresh HOME or without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR cannot take another permit. The tests use a private 0700 lock directory (private_symbolica_permit): the checks discriminate the same way, the user’s real permit stays free and the file runs beside other unlicensed test files. The tool’s --hold-permit takes the user’s real permit.

      • The tree engine needs no licence at any precision (unchanged): binary64 runs SymJIT applications and no Symbolica code (Python, and the C API although librusticol_capi.a links Symbolica through the loop SDK); other precisions go through the Python symbolica module, which the package key unlocks.

    • (c) CPU feature levels. SymJIT 2.27.3 needs x86-64 with AVX and FMA3: its AVX generator is chosen from the AVX bit alone but emits FMA3 (vfmsub231sd, SIGILL on SandyBridge-v2), and the shared epilogue emits vzeroupper for the SSE generator too (SIGILL on Nehalem-v2, qemu64). The SymJIT loaders refuse x86-64 CPUs without AVX and FMA3 with a compatibility error before compiling (symjit_plane::require_symjit_host_cpu); the tool reads the same features from the native extension (_rusticol._symjit_host_cpu). Upstream: SymJIT issues https://github.com/siravan/symjit/issues/22 (the FMA3/vzeroupper requirement) and /23 (Config::default() panics on a bad symjit.toml), pull requests https://github.com/siravan/symjit/pull/24 and /25, merged into v228 (4031c1a9, d37160b8), not in a release yet (crates.io 2.28.1; pyAmpliCol pins 2.27.3). The gate stays until a SymJIT release with the fixes is pinned. A v4 loop artifact holds both forms of its tree program, so on such a CPU binary64 runs the exact states (under the library key) instead of refusing the artifact; its values then follow that CPU’s class. QEMU 11.1 user mode on the native-v2 g g > g g artifact: Haswell-v4 recompiles the plane applications and is bitwise equal to the host; SandyBridge-v2 and Nehalem-v2 run the exact states without SIGILL or refusal and differ from the host in the last bits (at most 1.6e-15 relative), equal to each other (workspace/tmp/artifact-portability/r5/cpu/matrix.json). Bitwise identity across SymJIT classes is not expected (FMA contraction). AArch64: SymJIT generates AArch64 code, but no relocation check has run on AArch64 (expected to hold, untested). The Python API itself needs x86-64-v2 here (numpy 2 raises SIGILL on qemu64).

    • Environment independence. SymJIT’s Config::default() reads ./symjit.toml or $SYMJIT_TOML and panics on a malformed or unreadable file; our direct-application and plane loaders build their configuration explicitly (symjit_plane::explicit_loader_config); the SymJIT-internal call is fixed by pull request 25.

    • glibc floor (user decision 2026-10-28, slice-status DECISIONS ~07:40 and ~13:30; package glibc-floor). On Linux a native library needs the glibc symbol versions it links (ELF version needs, readelf -V), and the dynamic loader refuses it on a glibc that does not define one. The release natives (_rusticol.so, librusticol_loop_sdk.so) built by tools/developer/build_loop_native.py with the repository’s toolchain need at most GLIBC_2.38 and no ABI marker: the floor is glibc 2.38 (pinned by the tests, stated in the user docs, the SDK headers, Fortran module and README). Build: on x86-64 Linux the C dependencies (GMP/MPFR/MPC through gmp-mpfr-sys, and cc-crate objects) are compiled with CC="<cc> -mtls-dialect=gnu", after any flag of the compiler wrapper. TLS-descriptor objects (-mtls-dialect=gnu2, which some nixpkgs cc wrappers add in nix-support/cc-cflags-before) make the linked natives need GLIBC_ABI_GNU2_TLS, an ABI marker that only glibc builds carrying it define (BZ #33129: glibc 2.43, and the 2.38-2.42 stable branches after the backport, not the 2.42 release tarball), so no release number decides it; slice natives fb54246c..6e123fdb needed it because builds/cargo-v2-slice held GMP/MPFR compiled through such a wrapper (the native digest does not cover the C compiler). gmp-mpfr-sys neither reruns its build script when CC changes nor keys its cache by the actual compiler (only by the CC string), so a target directory whose recorded C settings (pyamplicol-c-dependencies.json) differ first drops its gmp-mpfr-sys outputs (cargo clean -p gmp-mpfr-sys); the first build on a host compiles GMP/MPFR/MPC from source (make and m4 on PATH). build-info.json records the C settings and each library’s glibc_version_needs (by release). Measured 2026-10-28: loop-native-glibc-floor-fd7838e4 (fresh target dir, package profile, C dependencies compiled through the gnu2-default nixpkgs gcc-wrapper-15.3.0) has 0 TLSDESC relocations in libgmp/libmpfr/libmpc (1,684 traditional TLS ones in libmpfr.a, against TLSDESC in builds/cargo-v2-slice’s), and both natives top at GLIBC_2.38 without marker; on a real glibc 2.40 (Nix python3 3.13.9) its SDK .so loads while loop-native-v2-slice-6e123fdb’s is refused for GLIBC_ABI_GNU2_TLS. loop-native-glibc-floor-91a4dd94 (the same target dir, env.sh’s cc, the slice profile: one codegen unit, thin LTO) exercised the drop of the stale gmp-mpfr-sys outputs and gives the same requirements. Python (pyamplicol/_native_loader.py, installed first by pyamplicol/__init__.py): a sys.meta_path finder hands pyamplicol._rusticol to an ExtensionFileLoader subclass whose create_module, before dlopen, looks each GLIBC_* version the file needs up in the version definitions of the glibc library it is needed from, as mapped into the process (/proc/self/maps): the loader’s own check (weak needs, VER_FLG_WEAK, which ld.so does not enforce, are skipped), so markers are decided by the running glibc build. A library not loaded yet is left to the loader. A missing version, or a process not on glibc (os.confstr('CS_GNU_LIBC_VERSION'), else gnu_get_libc_version), raises NativePlatformError (a DependencyError, not an ImportError, so except ImportError sites do not reword it; the one broad except Exception site, the direct-arena P-kernel compiler, re-raises it) with library, missing, required (the newest missing numbered release, None for markers only) and found. A loader error naming a missing glibc version at the two wired sites — the guarded pyamplicol._rusticol import (for the extension or a library it needs) and the Symbolica import in pyamplicol/__init__.py (the workspace’s community-release-python-9cdc2949 Symbolica itself needs GLIBC_ABI_GNU2_TLS) — becomes the same error with the loader’s text, and a dependency’s library gets its own remedy; other native code (numpy, the libraries of C++/ASM artifacts) keeps the loader’s error. Cost: the module import ~0.4 ms (warm), the check ~0.9 ms once per process (mostly /proc/self/maps), against ~0.27 s for import pyamplicol. C/C++/Fortran: a C/C++ client of the release shared library that defines RUSTICOL_VIRTUAL_SHARED stops at compile time on an older glibc toolchain (RUSTICOL_VIRTUAL_GLIBC_FLOOR_MAJOR/MINOR; exact, since every glibc release defines the numbered versions before it; omitted for an SDK built from source on an older host). Otherwise the floor is a numbered version that real symbols bind (__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38, hypot@GLIBC_2.35), so GNU ld, whose default for executables is --no-allow-shlib-undefined, fails a client’s link on a toolchain older than glibc 2.38 (undefined reference to `__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38'; only the symbol-less GLIBC_ABI_GNU2_TLS marker linked silently), and a client built on a newer glibc and run on an older one gets the loader’s version `GLIBC_2.38' not found: both messages are documented. Tests: tests/unit/test_native_glibc_floor.py. The pin asserts the staged natives’ measured requirement exactly (~13:30 ruling (b)): no marker, and the newest numbered need equal to the documented floor GLIBC_2.38, so a raise, a drop or a marker fails and names the docs to update; the other checks use stub libraries and stub libc.so.6 files linked by the test.

The process stores point-inputs/tree-program.bin.zlib (kind 12, zlib) instead of tree-program.json.zlib (and the companion’s under point-inputs/scaleless/): a container (magic PYAMTRP1; sections (name, encoding, payload)) of the program’s head (JSON, the parts Python reads: parameters, sources, layout), one JSON section per moved key (interactions, block_rows, born, counterterms, counterterm_trees, layouts, weights), and binary sections replacing their large arrays: the trees’ and the counterterm program’s steps as narrow columns (interactions.steps, counterterm_trees.interactions.steps; the counterterm program’s straight from its native DAG, V2Program.step_section, the trees’ from the native blocks DAG without a Python TreeRows, both pruned natively, tree_steps_prune), the counterterm overlap cells as a table of distinct Laurent cells and per (ket tensor, basis element) ids (counterterms.cells, formed natively by NativeCellTable.section; the interference reads it as MetricCells::Table, bitwise the list’s values) and the closure terms (born.terms, counterterms.terms). TreeProgram::load reads the container or the JSON program (the oracle; test_loop_v2_tree_binary.py: decoded program byte for byte, values bitwise; the pre-package native-member pins of test_loop_v2_fail_closed.py hash the decoded JSON and still hold); the SDK reads either member. At g g > 6g LC the JSON tree program was 13.1 GB, of which 7.56 GB overlap cells and 4.0 GB counterterm steps.

  • Counterterm-program build memory (MF-8G-1 item 4). The counterterm DAG’s builder holds about one copy of its interactions in every stage: the recursion’s interaction dedup set restarts per left current (all of one left current’s interactions into a mask are made in one iteration), the prune compacts in place, the N_c grade split expands in place from the last interaction, the reuse derivation keeps the classes of one mask at a time (a contract holds its mask) and its rewrite compares, then writes, without a copy, and the columns are written from the last row while the rows’ buffer shrinks behind (ColumnarDag columns zero-allocated, committed as written). The interaction program is emitted at the build (dag_input.emit_counterterm_program) with 4-byte rows when its bounds fit 32 bits (dag::program::Rows); the DAG’s columns are released once the program and the kernels’ representatives are read, the step section takes the program’s steps (V2Program.take_step_section, rows released as the columns form) and the export takes the emission (native_counterterm_trees pops it). PYAMPLICOL_LOOP_STAGE_MEMORY prints the resident and peak memory after each builder stage (profiling only). At g g > 5g LC the build’s peak over its base fell from 3.1 to 1.7 GiB (13.3 M interactions). The recursion looks its results and evaluation groups up in maps of the current mask only, and the reuse rewrite in maps of the current run of one result mask (no key crosses masks: a key’s inputs join to its result’s mask; a group’s id counts the groups before it, so ids are those of one map of the whole DAG; the rewrite checks the runs and the joins and otherwise keeps one map), and the builder input’s pair lookups use FxHash: the g g > 5g LC counterterm DAG (7.1 M groups) builds in 10.9 instead of 14.7 s (benches/loop_v2_dag.rs per stage, digests equal at 4-7 legs). With it, and the G1 harness wrapping its Python-tree timer on the class (Run._install_timers had built the slice’s Python tree runtime from the blocks DAG after the export and held it through the store), g g > 5g (8 threads, loaded host, tmp/mf-8g-1/m7/c9 → c11): LC generate 63 s / 3.25 GiB → 59 s / 3.25, export 47 s / 4.07 → 46 s / 4.08, store 34 s / 4.54 → 34 s / 3.85; FC 46 s / 2.72 → 44 s / 2.52, 70 s / 4.62 → 73 s / 4.47, 35 s / 5.52 → 35 s / 4.72; stored artifacts byte-identical. The LC/NLC prune releases the complete schedule build it rebuilt from (NativeGeneration.release, Arena::release: its tries and state natively, its decoded plan and seed stage; the rebuild shares only its skeletons), and the pruned plan’s view keeps the Python liveness instead of the native flags that held the build: the g g > 5g LC slice holds 2.77 instead of 3.08 GiB after generation, the export and store peaks fall from 4.73 / 5.21 to 4.16 / 4.62 GiB, the stored artifact byte-identical (test_loop_v2_generation_release.py).

  • Binary plan member (WP3.1 D, native-lowering; stored since M-FINAL MF-8G-1 item 5, native_lowering.BINARY_PLAN). ExportedPlan.binary() (loops/v2/native_lowering.py, rusticol_core::loop_v2::plan::binary, format 3: format 2 plus generation-scale-2’s column_weights) is the plan’s columnar encoding: one column per record field at its narrowest width, repeated per-content lists stored once, plan data only (no path, host or build information), deterministic, decoding to the model whose JSON is the plan JSON byte for byte. It is read by loop_v2::plan::read_binary, the member’s one reader, through the loader’s validation and derivations (bounded decode and derivations, fail-closed; the schedule-B row links stay derived at load). As built:

    • Stored form. ExportedPlan.stored() is the member; generate_process stores it as schedule/loop-plan-v4.bin.zlib and the companion’s as schedule/loop-plan-v4-scaleless.bin.zlib (kind 12, zlib stream; the member name and the magic LOOPPLAN tell it from a JSON, as the tree-program container’s do), and no plan JSON. GeneratedProcess.plan, NativeProcess.plan and NativeCompanion.plan carry the member, NativeExecutor loads it by default and V2Executor(plan) takes bytes (a member) or text (a JSON): LoopProgramV4::load_with reads a member through read_binary_with. plan_json is a property that forms the JSON from the member on each call (native_lowering.member_json) for the Python readers of plan records (the observable column sets) and for the tests’ JSON digests. A column set’s plan (the plan with the set’s seed records) loads from the member and the set’s overlay (LoopProgramV4::load_overlaid: the seed fields replaced on the decoded model, no merged JSON; the SDK’s every column set and the Python selection template and resolved selections; lit-fc-hel), the Python stored correlated and resolved sets from the merged JSON (native_observables.with_overlay).

    • Digests. plan_sha256 (and scaleless_plan_sha256) is the SHA-256 of the stored bytes (the member; a JSON’s text for a plan stored as JSON), so the admission digests the member as read without forming the JSON (O(member), and a later per-bucket decode stays possible); the plan JSON’s digest stays available through plan_json (equal for equal plans: the member is deterministic and decodes to the JSON byte for byte). This replaces the proposal’s JSON digest.

    • Readers. The Rust admission and SDK (loop_runtime::read_loop_program_v4_json, ..._scaleless_json) and the Python artifact.read_plan read the member where stored, else the JSON member; read_plan_json gives the JSON of either. The JSON form is the oracle’s stored form and is read for that reason only (no compatibility promise for artifacts written before the member, AGENTS.md; the Rust doc comments of LOOP_PROGRAM_V4_MEMBER and plan_sha256’s reader still say ‘artifacts written before it’ and change with the next Rust increment) (BINARY_PLAN = False stores and loads JSON plans; tests/unit/test_loop_v2_plan_member.py: member decoded to the exporter’s JSON, the same loaded program, bitwise equal evaluations on member and JSON with and without poles and in “uv”, stored and loaded members, a JSON-stored process loaded and evaluated alike).

    • Open (reader side, MF-8G-2b): the zlib inflation of a plan member is not bounded by a declared length (as for every zlib member today); a per-bucket decode would read the member’s sections lazily (not done: the compact forms below brought the loaded plan within the 2->6 target without it).

  • Load (M-FINAL MF-8G-2 items 2 and 4, MF-8G-2b). A stored process reads its large members on demand through the handle it opened at load (coordinator ruling 2026-11-02 ~16:45): artifact.load_native_process opens the loop-runtime.pacbin once, verifies its payload digests through that handle, reads the record and the small members (one member enumeration with the in-memory reader, artifact._native_members), and keeps the plan, the companion plan and both binary tree programs as native_trees.StoredMember (logical member, payload offset and length, SHA-256, and the shared read-only handle). Every read (StoredMember.payload: the executor’s first build per arithmetic, the ‘uv’/’ir’ companion, the correlated and resolved column sets, plan_json) is a positional read through the handle with the digest checked; the executor inflates the payload itself (program_bytes in v2_executor.rs, loop_artifact::inflate_loop_v2_member), and the Python view inflates a tree program only up to its head section (inflate_loop_v2_section). LIFETIME RULE: the handle lives as long as the loaded process (one open descriptor per loaded process); moving, renaming, deleting or replacing the artifact after Runtime.load changes no result (the handle keeps the loaded file; the generator publishes a regenerated container as a new file, write_pacbin_atomic); a container rewritten in place (the same file truncated and written) fails the digest check and is refused with a ValueError (load it again); without positional reads (os.pread) the members are read at load (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_load_memory.py, test_loop_v2_stored_process.py::test_a_loaded_process_does_not_depend_on_its_artifact_path). No tree program is json.loadsed or re-dumped at load; the in-memory load (read_native_process) and the JSON forms stay the oracles (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_load_memory.py, test_loop_v2_tree_binary.py, test_loop_v2_plan_member.py). Resident forms: a split step’s edges release their row links (each link held once, by the parts); a split part’s links are packed column by column at the narrowest width (plan/packed.rs, 3 bytes per link up to eight legs) and shared by the parts with equal links (plan::LinkInterner: g g > 5g LC has 648,105 parts but 610 distinct lists); plan leaves and seed-class terms index their distinct exact weights; tree-program interactions hold u32 state components and accumulator offsets and index their distinct weights (the loader refuses a program that does not fit); the binary64 tree runtime keeps the distinct weights only; the fast reducer reduces a bucket in calls of 1,024 lanes (the evaluation base between blocks). Values are bitwise unchanged (7-leg and 4-6-leg controls at B = 1, 16, 128). Rust Arithmetic / Runtime::set_arithmetic, results’ decimal_json(); C ABI rusticol_virtual_set_arithmetic, rusticol_virtual_result_decimal_json, rusticol_virtual_correlated_result_decimal_json (additive, ABI version 2); C++ set_arithmetic / decimal_json, Fortran set_arithmetic / %decimal_json, the packaged single-file Rust wrapper; UMAMI serves points with status “accuracy not established”. Tests: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_sdk_extras.py (g g > t t~ and u u~ > d d~ g FC: C, C++, Fortran and UMAMI clients bitwise in binary64, Decimal-equal in double-double and arbitrary(32); through the C ABI also double-double and arbitrary(32) in uv/ir and the leading-colour resolved rows of u u~ > g g; the packaged Rust wrapper compiled, linked and run; Rust via the opt-in nightly id), rust/loop-reduction/sdk/tests/v4_extras.rs. Not served: the stability rescue (Python API only, Q9), LC helicity/colour-flow selection and history subsets. mf-small3 (2026-11-02): the Python API reads the uv/ir companion lanes inside the working-digit scope too (before, outside it, ~1e-28 off the SDK), the safe Rust API refuses per-leg spin sources of another length than 4 per point (typed invalid argument; the C ABI’s flat buffer was already checked), and the UMAMI extension reports layout version 2 (PYAMPLICOL_UMAMI_VIRTUAL_VERSION; its options lost verification_json with ABI version 2; _v1 names kept). Binary64 runs the stored SymJIT applications and needs no licence; two binary64 cases evaluate saved Symbolica states natively under pyAmpliCol’s own package key (no user licence either): light-mass lanes (§12.1 (e)) and x86-64 CPUs without AVX and FMA3 (§12.1 (c)). Loop-induced selections (m-lit lit-sdk-b, the USER’s F1). rusticol_virtual_evaluate_selected (additive, ABI version 2 kept; C++, Fortran, the packaged Rust wrapper, the safe Rust Runtime::evaluate_selected and UMAMI’s UMAMI_IN_HELICITY_INDEX / PYAMPLICOL_UMAMI_V1_IN_COLOR_RESOLUTION) serves the Python API’s helicities= and color_resolution= of a loop-induced process with the tree C ABI’s selector conventions: the amplitude-basis anchors (induced_outputs::anchor_metric, an explicitly basis-dependent split, PLAN §2.a.10), the global and per-point helicity selections (|A(h)|²/avg with the total’s average, Q39; per-point selections evaluated as one batch per distinct row) and the resolved selection; a call that reads some rows dresses only those (InducedCall::row_mask, the executor’s live_rows and the tree fill’s TreeProgram::live_rows, as the Python binding’s evaluate(rows=...); the Python API’s evaluate(helicities=...) and evaluate_resolved(helicities=...) dress the selected rows only too, V2InducedObservablesRuntime._resolved_key, so a lane refused in an unselected row fails a point in neither), and the Python API’s binary64 anchors run the same Rust form (induced_anchor_form). Colour flows are refused (full colour, Q8); a Born-interfered process’s leading-colour selection stays the Python API’s. Tests: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_sdk_selection.py. Parity with the Python API (sdk-parity, second genericity audit M2, m3 and the SDK advisories). Model parameters (at open and update_parameters, every client) follow V2VirtualRuntime._checked_parameters, whose rule is now one function per language (assemble.check_model_parameters, v2_runtime::checked_parameters): the whole mapping is validated before anything is applied, and an unknown name (not an external parameter of the artifact’s model, model/parameters.json, the Python API’s compiled.ir.parameters of nature external), the renormalisation scale’s parameter (the native record’s scale_parameter, resolved at generation as the Python API resolves it, not by name) and a parameter fixed at generation at another exact value are refused with a typed ModelParameter error carrying the Python API’s message (C RUSTICOL_VIRTUAL_INVALID_ARGUMENT, C++ VirtualError::status(), Fortran ierr and error_message, evaluate_v2_artifact ValueError); a refused update changes nothing. The fixed set is every external parameter fixed at generation (LoopSlice.fixed_parameters: the request’s, as given, and the model’s external parameters the preparation fixes besides, from the prepared model’s structure.fixed_parameters, e.g. a colour declaration’s external scheme constants; the names an applied source restriction removed from the model are unknown names to every client already), recorded in the native record’s fixed_parameters and applied by every runtime; before (fix round 1), the record held the request’s alone, so an external scheme constant at another value entered trees whose counterterm colour continuation was built at the fixed value (toy: loop_sm with lhv external, loop_v2_ufo_variants.external_scheme_constant_ufo). Every client refuses an empty name first (the Python API’s TypeError; Rust InvalidArgument, C RUSTICOL_VIRTUAL_INVALID_ARGUMENT, evaluate_v2_artifact ValueError, same text), reads the values next (as Python’s Decimal of ASCII text: no fractions, an infinity or NaN not finite, other digits or whitespace than ASCII refused, by the Python API’s runtime.virtual._number too; v2_runtime::decimal_parameter), then the names, both by name, so a mapping with several refused entries gets the same message everywhere; a complex value is the Python API’s CompatibilityError (Rust Compatibility, C RUSTICOL_VIRTUAL_RUNTIME_ERROR, as "direct" R2). The stored-process view (native_process._ProcessView, NativeProcess.executor(..., externals=...)) applies the same rule; the native record carries the model’s external parameter names (externals) and the names of the fixed set the model preparation fixed (preparation_fixed_parameters), so a stored view alone refuses unknown names (before, NativeProcess.executor without externals, the benchmark’s --load path, dropped a misspelt name) and every client says who fixed a refused fixed value (the request’s [loop.preparation] fixed_parameters, or the model preparation: a scheme constant, not a run-time parameter; assemble.fixed_refusal, v2_runtime::fixed_refusal); a record of an older build has neither, and its views check no names. Before, the SDK silently replaced a caller’s value of a fixed parameter by the fixed one and overwrote the scale parameter, and applied an update value by value. The slice’s per-point evaluation (LoopSlice._point_parameters, the reference executor’s twin) applies the same rule. The default R2 strategy "auto" (the C ABI’s and C++ wrapper’s default) selects the model R2 of a v4 artifact as the Python API does ("direct" is refused); before, open_v4 refused every strategy but "model". The tree and closure stages run on the executor’s pool (V2Executor::install), so the runtime’s threads bound covers them (before, the global rayon pool); the Python API’s native executor (plan_export.NativeExecutor, the PyO3 V2Executor’s Trees::fill) binds its batch and runs the same stages on its own pool too (before, 2 -> 11 threads at threads=1 with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8). Scale-dependent batches: see §12.1’s parameter program. Tests: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_sdk_parity.py (g g > t t~ with WT fixed: the Python API, evaluate_v2_artifact, a C client and the slice refuse WT = 1.4915, MU_R and an unknown name with the same text, a mapping with one refused entry changes nothing, and accepted values (WT at zero, an unread MH, αs, MT = 150 at a point on shell there) are bitwise the Python API’s; the C++ and Fortran wrappers compile and report the refusal; on the renamed-model harness’s scale variant muR is refused as the scale and MU_R as unknown; threads=1 starts no global rayon pool), rust/loop-reduction/sdk/tests/v4_parameters.rs (the safe Rust Runtime: an ignored test run with --ignored and PYAMPLICOL_V4_GGTT_ARTIFACT, failing without it; error kinds checked; the parity file’s opt-in nightly id test_the_rust_sdk_follows_the_python_api runs it on its artifact given a private PYAMPLICOL_SDK_CARGO_TARGET_DIR) and the unit test of checked_parameters. Evidence: the C client (tools/loop_artifact_portability.py, CLIENT_SOURCE) equals the Python API bitwise at both locations of a relocated g g > g g artifact, and two unlicensed SDK instances run while another process holds the restricted permit (test_loop_artifact_portability.py, the former strict xfails); the C client equals the Python API bitwise in all four pole selections, the finite part identical in all four (test_loop_v4_sdk_selects_poles_like_python), and evaluate_v2_artifact does at g g > g g and d d~ > g g with the default and a caller-set αs (test_rust_runtime_equals_the_python_api). A v2 artifact still carries no API bundle (recorded as a configuration adjustment).

12.2 Public API and configuration¶

As built (WP2.6). The planned changes below are kept in the history of this file; what exists is:

  • Surface.

    • Generator(RunConfig) with process.loop_coupling_orders: generate publishes plan v4 (Born-interfered; plan v5 for loop-induced processes, §7.11) (loop_service._generate_v2) and plan is the v2 dry run (_plan_v2, loop_graph_count 0 per process). v2 is the only one-loop engine (MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE, §13.3): loop.engine (TOML, override, CLI --loop-engine) is refused with the reason, and so is a rusticol.loop-runtime.v3 artifact at load and inspection.

    • Runtime.load dispatches a v4 or v5 process to loops.v2.artifact.V2VirtualRuntime, which implements the RuntimeBackend calls evaluate, evaluate_resolved, evaluate_correlated(_many), set_model_parameters and set_spin_correlation_vectors; a v3 process still loads VirtualRuntimeBackend.

    • The result types (api/virtual_results.py), with the additions below.

    • The C, C++, Fortran, Rust and UMAMI SDK ABI is unchanged; rusticol_virtual_open dispatches a plan v4 artifact to the native V2Runtime (ordinary binary64 virtuals, §12.1 SDK), legacy artifacts as before.

  • Options added.

    • Pole selection PoleSelection (pyamplicol.config, re-exported by pyamplicol.api), one string-valued option across TOML (evaluation.poles = "all" | "none" | "uv" | "ir", default "all"), CLI (--poles {all,none,uv,ir}), API (poles= on evaluate, evaluate_resolved, evaluate_correlated(_many)), result types (VirtualEvaluation.poles, ResolvedVirtualEvaluation.poles) and the artifact declaration (physics.json poles). "none" is the finite part only: poles None (LaurentCoefficients), also for correlated and resolved outputs, from the same artifact; the finite part is bitwise the same. Booleans and unknown selections are refused. "uv" and "ir" (WP2.10, §12.4) return the selected origin’s pole parts, and pole_parts (one VirtualPoleParts per point: uv and ir, each component a Laurent triple per sector, and per helicity and colour component for resolved output; pole_part(origin, component)) both origins by component, for inclusive, correlated and resolved calls.

    • [evaluation.stability_checks] and per call stability_checks=VirtualStabilityChecks(...) (REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM C: any list of exact rotations or a rotation count, and the reduction-direction check, optionally rescaled; none by default, and then no estimate; recommended VirtualStabilityChecks(1, True, rescaled=True) = stability.RECOMMENDED_CHECKS, §10.4): one VirtualStabilityEstimate per point (per helicity row and colour component for resolved output); CLI --stability-rotation SPEC (repeatable), --stability-rotations COUNT, --stability-reduction-direction, --stability-rescaled. Escalating the arithmetic stays the caller’s decision; the [evaluation.stability] rescue policy (and its CLI options) was removed with the legacy engine: any non-default value is refused at configuration time (config.models.EVALUATION_STABILITY_REMOVED) and a Python VirtualStabilityPolicy at load. A non-positive mu_r2 raises for the whole call, also with on_failure="return" (invalid input). A scale at which a counterterm coupling is not finite in the lane’s carrier (mu_r2 = "1e-400" in binary64; the native parameter program refuses the whole batch, “a counterterm coupling’s diagnostic is not finite”, raised as the typed NonFiniteCountertermError, a ValueError, since mf-small3: trees::nonfinite_counterterm) fails only its own points: the runtimes re-run such a batch per exact scale (runtime.virtual.isolate_scale_failures, failure path only) and fail that scale’s points with the reason, as the Python reference path fails them (SourceBindingFailure); test test_loop_v2_scale_failures.py (mf-small, closes HANDOFF §9.16).

    • on_failure (status since 1.0.3, m-lit ux-besteffort / ux-polish; USER-NOTES 2026-11-11 items 7-9): "best-effort" (the default; config evaluation.on_failure null, CLI --on-failure, every native SDK’s set_on_failure), "return", "raise" (the default before 1.0.3). Best-effort lane status: a point no configured alternative accepts (the backend’s own acceptance checks, auto’s per-point fallback, the last rescue level) is evaluated again on that point only with the reduction_unchecked machinery (reduction.with_fallback(best_effort=True), _best_effort; SDK best_effort.rs) and returned with lane status "best-effort" (valid False, has_value True; VirtualBestEffort: bounded refusal, uncertainty, source, backend_deviation, gram_conditioning (ux-polish item 4: the backend’s lane measures as data, V2Backend::take_lane_measures -> PointResult::measures -> V2Runtime PointFailure / PyO3 refusal_measures -> plan_export.Refusal; SDK diagnostics "refusal_measures"); SDK status 5 RUSTICOL_VIRTUAL_BEST_EFFORT, uncertainties, diagnostics "best_effort" / "warnings"); a point with no value stays a failed lane. The uncertainty is the estimate of the call’s checks together with the recommended checks (guard rotation + rescaled reduction direction; reduction.best_effort_checks, same rule in the SDK), run on the refused points only (ux-polish: one rotation alone covered 220 of 722 u u~ > t t~ g g best-effort points). ResultWarning metadata: result.warnings / has_warnings carry the best-effort and failed points (one entry per kind; also the captured dependency log events of generate / check, source "symbolica" / "ufo-model-loader", and since ux-clean "ufo-model": a UFO model’s own compile-time Python warnings, symbolica_log.ufo_source_warnings); nothing is printed, logged or warned per point; result.emit_warnings() is the opt-in single NumericalAccuracyWarning. "return": a failed point is None with its reason, the other points are unaffected, no best-effort evaluation. Accepted points take no new path (bitwise, same cost).

  • Diagnostics as built. VirtualColorContraction: requested is the request’s "auto", "direct" or "symmetric-group-fft", algorithm is what the native executor ran: "symmetric-group-fft" (the certified pairs of the stored seed Fourier record, regular_kernels their count; MQ-FFT, §7.3) or "direct" (no "diagonal" was added). ProcessPhysics reports helicity_coverage = "all" and structural_zero_helicity_count = 0: the plan keeps every Born helicity row, structural zeros included (u u~ > d d~ g keeps all 32), and does not count them yet. Per-point diagnostics carry the carrier, precision and colour contraction; the schedule, per-family estimates, rescue tier and stage times are not reported (WP2.7, with the live report).

  • Reduction backend (m-lit LIT-API, Q17 / Q18; PLAN §2.b.4). [loop] reduction = "auto" | "ninjars" | "tirust" is the generation default, recorded in the request record (SliceRequest.reduction, only when not "auto"; the plan does not depend on it); [evaluation] reduction, Runtime.load(..., reduction=), reduction= on every evaluation and CLI --loop-reduction override it. loops.v2.reduction.resolve chooses once per call, carrier and route (each rescue level’s, before any point): "auto" takes the per-type default (loop-induced TIRust, Born-interfered NinjaRS), else NinjaRS with the reason; an explicit backend that cannot serve is refused (ReductionUnavailable, a CompatibilityError, key reduction-unavailable). A backend serves a call when the artifact admits it, the native extension’s capability query reduction_backends() (JSON: backend → carriers; absent: NinjaRS at every carrier) has it at the carrier, and the call’s route runs it (reduction.Route: SUMMED, the summed evaluate and its rescue levels through the native executor, V2VirtualRuntime._evaluate_level; RESOLVED, evaluate_resolved, evaluate_correlated(_many) and the leading-colour selection of evaluate through V2ObservablesRuntime). The route check is the one guard of every route: the effective backend is always one the route’s executor runs. One choice list (config.ReductionBackend) and one validator (config.models.reduction_request) serve the configuration, the API, the slice request and the result record. Every lane diagnostic records VirtualReduction(requested, effective, reason), built with the lane (V2ObservablesRuntime takes the resolved choices as reductions; no finished result is rebuilt). Both routes run both backends (lit-tir): the effective backend reaches the native executor calls of the call through reduction.running (a context variable set once per call and carrier; the executors’ call sites read reduction.executor_options(), which is empty for NinjaRS, so a NinjaRS call passes what it passed before). Route.auto holds the backends "auto" may take on a route: both on both routes (m-lit F3, USER 2026-11-08 ~14:40 / ~15:40, superseding DECISIONS 2026-11-08 11:17), so "auto" takes TIRust for loop-induced processes. Per-point fallback and target (m-lit lit-tirust-default, F3 (a)-(d)). The one definition is Rust’s reduction_policy (R7): resolve returns a Choice with fallback = NinjaRS when "auto" takes TIRust and NinjaRS serves the call (never for an explicit backend or a TIR-only artifact); auto_default(contribution, admitted) is the one helper resolve, V2Runtime::open, the SDK capabilities and the Python inspect record read; fallback_served / fallback_failed / cross_refusal are the reason texts; DEFAULT_TARGET (1e-5) and target() the target accuracy and its validator. The fallback runs after the primary call, on the points it refused or failed (also in the binary64 monitoring’s own evaluations), from their exact inputs at the call’s carrier (binary64 for a binary64 call, double-double / arbitrary precision for those calls: the same precision as the call, user ruling 2026-11-08): loops.v2.reduction.with_fallback in Python (V2VirtualRuntime._evaluate_level, V2ObservablesRuntime._run), with_fallback in the SDK (V2Runtime::on_other, the cross-backend check’s kept backends); a call without a fallback runs once (no per-point branch on the Born-interfered path). Each fallback point records its own VirtualReduction (Python lane diagnostic) or "fallbacks" entry (SDK diagnostics); its cross-backend check is not run (R6). Fallback guard (m-lit lit-fallback-guard, DECISIONS 2026-11-09 05:56 (1) and 11:53). In the extended carriers (reduction_policy::fallback_guarded: double-double and arbitrary precision; USER 2026-11-09 ~11:53 ‘Double-double+ only’: in binary64 the protection is lit-ninja-planar’s conditioning bound in NinjaRS’s fast engine, and a binary64 fallback point is served as before, with no estimate) every point the per-point fallback SERVED runs a ROTATION RE-TEST (reduction_policy::FALLBACK_CHECK = “rotation”, since DECISIONS 2026-11-10 19:20 (c): the evaluated point, i.e. the caller’s exact inputs improved in the carrier, and on the correlated route its spin sources, rotated exactly by FALLBACK_ROTATION, the recommended checks’ default_rotation(0), and evaluated again on the fallback; each returned output’s deviation is its error. It replaced the cached reduction-direction re-reduction, which missed the double-double near-forward cut-stage losses of a nearly degenerate 2 -> 2 (sub-)box, e.g. g g > z z at theta 1e-4, suppressed rows 5.5e4 off at cached estimate 5.6e-6, rotation 2.6e-3 of the row; the false-rejection sweep on the regular double-double sets, the li streams’ fallback points and every stream point re-tested as if served, workspace/tmp/lit-ninja-fwd/c/, found none. Like every rotation it keeps the masters’ invariants and an input’s own shell / conservation defect, which the default kinematics chain removes, §10.6) at the call’s own carrier (never escalated, USER 2026-11-08 ~20:55), and fails TYPED when the check’s relative estimate (StabilityEstimate.relative: each squared-order sector against its largest Laurent coefficient, the target’s metric) exceeds the guard’s limit, the call’s target never below 1e-5 (reduction_policy::fallback_limit = max(target, FALLBACK_FLOOR 1e-5), USER ~11:53 ‘it’s fine to relax the target precision to 1e-5 or so’; fallback_accepted: the estimate is a number at most the limit; the call’s target is a rescue level’s own target on that level and the SDK’s rusticol_virtual_set_reduction_target). Its one reason is reduction_policy::fallback_rejected (the fallback, the primary’s failure, the check, the estimate, the limit with the target and the carrier), read by Python (loops.v2.reduction.text("rejected")) and the SDKs. The estimate is recorded per point as an additive field: VirtualReduction.guard_estimate (Python), "guard_estimate" of the SDK’s "fallbacks" entry; an accepted point keeps the fallback’s value bitwise and the call’s public estimate stays its own checks’ (none without checks). Python (with_fallback, one implementation for _evaluate_level and V2ObservablesRuntime._run): the call’s checks run the guard’s rotation first (RECOMMENDED_CHECKS) -> reused (StabilityEstimate.subset(["rotation-0"]), no second rotated evaluation); no checks -> the fallback’s evaluation runs it and the result is returned as an evaluation without checks returns it (no estimate, no finiteness ratio); another rotation first (every default rescue level’s euler:0.1,0.2,0.3) or the reduction checks alone -> the served points are evaluated once more with the guard’s rotation alone; a point whose rotated evaluation fails is a fallback failure. The SDK (V2Runtime::evaluate_extended_guarded / evaluate_induced_call_guarded) evaluates the rotated points (and spin sources) in the carrier beside the fallback’s run, the inclusive |A|^2 through v2_stability::induced_estimate, every other output as |rotated output - output| in the assembly arithmetic (PointOutputs.budgets). The guard decides on the outputs the call returns (DECISIONS 2026-11-09 14:30, RULING Q7; USER 2026-11-08 ‘only the selected helicities are evaluated and nothing more’ holds for the guard’s re-test too): the summed value, or on the resolved, correlated and selected calls (V2ObservablesRuntime._run; the SDK’s resolved, correlated and selected calls) each output, from the fallback’s evaluation of the call’s own rows (the row mask of the call: no other row is dressed or re-reduced). One rule, reduction_policy::fallback_estimate (read by Python through reduction_fallback_estimate, loops.v2.reduction.fallback_estimate): per output and squared-order sector its magnitude (largest |Laurent coefficient|), its largest absolute estimate E of the reduction check alone and its largest term scale S (GuardSector); each output against its own magnitude, an output that VANISHES (its magnitude within the estimate’s own rounding floor FLOOR_UNITS u S, a numerical zero: ‘zero within the estimate’, RULED Q13; no new constant) against the largest returned output of the point in that sector; the largest ratio is the point’s estimate (NaN on any NaN). For one output this is the "relative" metric of its own estimate, so the summed route is unchanged. The per-output estimate is the one the Python API’s observables form with the reduction check alone (induced_observables.InducedColumns.evaluate: point_estimate for the inclusive |A|^2 of every row without spin sources, PointOutputs.estimate otherwise: the |M| form e^T|M||a| + |a|^T|M|e + e^T|M|e of the re-test’s errors over the |M| form of the term floors, both moved onto a spin assignment by the coefficient magnitudes). SDK (with_fallback of sdk/src/lib.rs for every caller, given the call’s arithmetic; the SDKs monitor binary64 only, so the guard always runs its own check): the fallback’s evaluation of the served points carries it, one evaluation per served point as in the Python API: the summed calls V2Runtime::evaluate_extended_guarded, the resolved, correlated and selected calls V2Runtime::evaluate_induced_call_guarded / evaluate_columns_guarded (induced_call_with collects the re-test of the call’s outputs; monitor::call_guard_estimate is the binary64 port of the Python per-output estimate: InducedShape::magnitude_form = _bound, spin_moved = _spin_errors); the monitored run in the carrier (induced_points_with with the reversed re-test and the term scale) is read in binary64 into these functions at V2Precision::unit_roundoff, as the Python assembly reads the executor’s budgets as floats; status Failed with the reason (not AccuracyNotEstablished). Only a loop-induced process has a per-point fallback (reduction_policy::resolve: a Born-interfered call’s default is NinjaRS, no fallback), so the guard serves loop-induced processes only (a guarded call of a Born-interfered process is refused, never reached). On the same exact inputs the SDK’s guard estimates are the Python API’s, bitwise or a few ulps apart, and the values bitwise (summed: g g > z z z stream points 44 / 57 in double-double: 23.147763305988818 vs 23.14776330598882, 31.352350506280747 on both sides; the g g > h h near-forward points; workspace/tmp/lit-fallback-guard/fix1/probe8.json; the routes: fix3/probe9.json): the ulps are the colour-metric norms of the inclusive |A|^2, which the SDK forms in binary64 (InducedShape::g_norm) and the Python assembly in the carrier (induced.quadratic_budget). A binary64 input of the SDK is its double’s exact value, a text of the Python API is read exactly; a shortest decimal text lies up to half an ulp from its double (docs/user/native-apis.md), which moves an estimate at a near-planar point (point 44: 142 from the stream’s text, 23 from its double; both rejected). Points TIRust serves get no added work (no re-reduction, no estimate, no record): the SDK’s resolved, correlated and selected primary runs only test one per-call flag per output (induced_call_with’s guarded, no monitoring, no allocation), and a call without a fallback (explicit, Born-interfered, TIR-only) runs once; the paired same-core re-time at the final head is in the lit-fallback-guard report (Done 4). Near-planar NinjaRS hazard (DECISIONS 2026-11-09 05:56 ‘NINJARS DEFECT CONFIRMED’; records workspace/tmp/ninjars-dd-zzz/{A,B}.md, C/out/). Since NinjaRS 71eddb15 (lit-ninja-planar) the box mu-expansion’s conditioning bound refuses these lanes typed in both engines (§11 ‘NinjaRS’; double-double: g g > z z z stream points 44 / 57 and the tilts eps 0, 1e-14, 1e-13 refused, workspace/tmp/lit-fallback-guard/fix3/probe14.json), and the fallback guard is defence in depth on what the fallback still serves. Before it, NinjaRS (pin 5b6a8f57) returned finite, badly wrong values reported as success (Python) / AccuracyNotEstablished (SDK) at near-planar 2 -> 3 points (the event plane contains the beam: pentagon Gram ~0) for pentagon families of rank = n (all-vector quark loops), in both engines: the generic (double-double / arbitrary) box mu-expansion (ninjars-symbolica/src/box_kernels.rs divide_mu / Plans::new, guarded only by the noise-level value_checks.rs Negligible test) and the fast binary64 engine’s d0 test at 1024 eps (ninjars/src/fast/engine.rs ~l.1186-1215, a rounding-noise test, not a conditioning bound). Measured windows (g g > z z z stream point 44 tilted by eps out of its plane, C/out/tilt.json; constructed planar points of six rows, C/out/pr-*.json; truth TIRust 78 digits on the same binary64 texts): binary64 served wrong from ~5e-7 (2e-2 off at 1e-7, 3.6e-7 at 1e-6) down to at least 1e-12 with a point-dependent lower edge (point 44 refused at <= 1e-12; the six rows served 2.8e12..1.5e17 off at 1e-12, ‘nj_b64’; every measured row refused at eps 0); double-double wrong at eps 0 (1.3e7 at point 44, tilt.json ‘nj_dd’; 3.8e-3..1.7e3 on the six rows, ‘nj_dd’), 3.3e-6 at 1e-14, <= 2.1e-10 from 1e-13 up. Affected as measured: loop-induced g g > z z z, z z g, z g g, a a g, a g g, W+ W- g; unaffected as measured: the rank-4 pentagon rows (h h h, h z g), Born-interfered g g > g g g, five Born-interfered NLO EW rows (B.md §2.3). Estimates on the wrong points, per check and carrier: the guard’s check alone (cached reduction direction), double-double, 9.7..142 on four stream points (C/out/checks.json ‘nj_dd_dir’; from ~20x above the error to ~9e4x below it: no proven bound); the recommended / rescue-level checks, double-double, 22..852 (A/out/ddcheck.json) and 27..892 (B.md §2.1 / §3); the recommended checks, binary64, 3.0..236 at the wrong tilt points (C/out/tilt.json ‘nj_b64_chk’). Explicit "ninjars" calls without checks (and the SDKs’ unmonitored NinjaRS calls) were exposed until that bound; NinjaRS’s response to an input point’s own shell and momentum-conservation defect is seen by neither the bound nor the guard’s cached check (g g > h h near-forward binary64 texts: the suppressed +- helicity rows 1.1e-4 .. 9.3e11 off in double-double and at 60 and 80 digits, while TIRust at 80 digits stays within 2.3e-6 of the exact point’s; on exactly on-shell, momentum-conserving points NinjaRS at 60 and 80 digits agrees with TIRust at 80 digits to 3e-37, the latter’s own error): the near-forward hazard below. Near-forward NinjaRS hazard (F-GH; M-LIT lit-ninja-fwd; USER 2026-11-10 ~18:54 / ~19:20, DECISIONS 18:54 / 19:20). 12.4 Pole selection: poles = "all" | "none" | "uv" | "ir" (user request 2026-10-23)¶

The user asked that the UV/IR pole selection of NinjaRS 41a4c00 and oneloopmaster 5b710437 reach the user settings of the one-loop matrix elements, so that a user can compute or access only the IR or only the UV poles, not just no poles. The mode is a runtime option of an evaluation; one generated artifact serves all four modes, as it does finite-only (REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM B, I). Code: loops/v2/poles.py, runtime/v2_poles.rs (an interim local copy of the UV-residue functional proposed upstream as NinjaRS fast::tensor_uv, see Cost), runtime/v2_reduce.rs (Poles::Split).

Regulators. Every pole of the Born-virtual interference is split by origin with two regulators: P/ε = P_UV/ε_UV + P_IR/ε_IR, and D/ε² = D/ε_IR². At one loop the double pole is always infrared.

Mode

Poles returned

Notes

"all" (default)

P_UV + P_IR and D (ε_UV = ε_IR)

The existing result, unchanged bit for bit (re-pin checked bitwise, §12.4 validation)

"none"

none (absent, not zero)

Finite-only mode (poles="none"; a bool is refused) with all its savings: one Laurent column per lane, no pole CT slots, no Catani check

"uv"

P_UV of the BARE loop (the unrenormalised amplitude, the reduction’s UV poles); the double pole is 0

User decision 2026-10-23 ~19:20 (REQUIREMENTS_ADDENDUM I). The counterterms’ UV poles are the selected uv and r2 components and pole_origins; bare + counterterm UV = 0 where renormalisation is complete

"ir"

P_IR and D of the RENORMALISED virtual

Catani’s operator; the poles of "all" where renormalisation is complete

Invariant. The finite part is identical, bit for bit, in all four modes and every carrier. The selection never touches a finite term: the reduction runs exactly as in "all" (its combined columns are those of "all" bit for bit), and the R2, counterterm and field finite parts are those of "all".
