—

  • Certified-scaleless families. A scaleless family (§3.3: the massless bubbles {k², (k−p_i)²} with a quartic partner in QCD) integrates to zero, B0(0;0,0) = 1/ε_UV − 1/ε_IR, so the combined result never needs it. Its UV and IR parts are local but not separately zero, and without them the bare UV pole is not local: at g g > g g the generated families alone give 35.47 (α_s/4π)·Born, a point-dependent number. With them the bare UV pole is 10 (α_s/4π)·Born, the Feynman-gauge value −[(n/2)δZ_3 + (n−2)δZ_g]·2 for n = 4 and six loop flavours. Generation therefore keeps them as a companion slice, LoopSlice.scaleless, with its own schedules and seed table and shared blocks, Born, counterterms, kernels and colour degrees (LC/NLC pruned like the main slice). The uv and ir selections dress and reduce it: on the Python path in the same reducer call, natively with a second plan v4 (NativeExecutor.scaleless, schedule B). Its lanes’ combined Laurent values are set to exact zero and only their UV residues enter, so "all" and "none" never dress it and the combined bare sum is unchanged. The plan v4 artifact (WP2.6) must carry this second plan, so that one artifact serves every mode.

  • Bare loop. The UV residue of a lane, the 1/ε_UV coefficient of μ^{2ε}/(iπ^{d/2} r_Γ) ∫ N(q)/Π_i((q+V_i)² − m_i²), depends only on the integrand’s large-q behaviour. NinjaRS’s ninjars::fast::TensorUvResidues (residue_at, NinjaRS #7, on its main since 2026-11-03) expands 1/D_i = Σ_k (−1)^k (2q·V_i + c_i)^k/(q²)^{k+1} (c_i = V_i² − m_i²) to total degree −4 and integrates the angles exactly: ⟨q^β⟩ = Π_μ (β_μ − 1)!! g_μμ^{β_μ/2}/(2^k (k+1)!) for |β| = 2k. A degree-r block contributes only if r ≥ 2N − 4. It costs O(C(R+4,4)) per lane from the coefficients already in the lane, in any carrier, and in the re-test frame too. It equals the sum of the reduction coefficients times oneloopmaster’s UV master residues: A0 and the tadpole tensors (UV only), B0 and the longitudinal bubble moments ((−1)^r/(r+1)), scaleless bubbles included (B0(0;0,0) = 1/ε_UV − 1/ε_IR); C0, D0 and dB0 have none. tests/runtime_v2_reduce.rs checks this lane by lane against NinjaRS’s generic engine with PoleSelection::UV and ::IR, at binary64 (10⁻¹⁰) and DoubleFloat (10⁻²⁶), massive and massless families, including a scaleless bubble whose combined integral vanishes. This is master-integral algebra, which belongs upstream (HANDOFF §1.7): runtime/v2_reduce.rs calls NinjaRS’s fast::tensor_uv; the interim local copy runtime/v2_poles.rs was deleted at the mf-symbolica re-pin.

  • Local counterterms (r2, uv_local): UV by origin. They renormalise couplings and masses: loop_sm has δg_s (MS-bar, top decoupled) and the on-shell δm and δy. These are IR finite; δm^OS has no IR pole, only its derivative does.

  • External fields. The model’s external-field factors (UFO particle.counterterm, δZ/2 per leg) are on-shell field renormalisation constants written with one ε. A massless leg’s δZ = Z_UV(1/ε_UV − 1/ε_IR) vanishes, and loop_sm omits it. A massive leg’s δZ_Q = −(α_s C_F/4π)(1/ε_UV + 2/ε_IR + …) appears as 3/ε. A UFO model does not state the origin. The renormalised virtual is UV finite (bare_UV + uv_local + Σ_legs Z_i^UV·Born = 0), so the UV part of the field factors of a sector is fixed as above and the IR part is the rest. This does not hide a missing counterterm: an incomplete UV renormalisation makes the "ir" poles miss Catani’s operator, exactly as "all" does. It is also not a mere definition: for loop_sm in Feynman gauge (§6.8) the field UV part equals the textbook constants of every external leg, Z_g^UV = (α_s/4π)(5/3 C_A − 4/3 T_F n_f) with the six loop flavours and Z_q^UV = −(α_s/4π) C_F for massless and massive quarks. test_loop_v2_poles.py checks this per sector against the Born, independently of the residue, on g g > g g, u u~ > g g g, u u~ > u u~ (four quarks), Drell-Yan (no δg_s) and the massive g g > t t~ and u u~ > t t~. The bare loop’s UV/IR split of massless legs depends on the gauge (Z_i^UV does); its sum does not. Consequently the cancellation bare_UV + uv_local + fields_UV + r2 = 0 that the result shows (the user’s renormalisation check) holds by construction of fields_UV. Its falsifiable content is three independent checks: the bare-loop UV residue against NinjaRS’s generic engine with UV-selected masters, bare_UV + uv_local + Σ_legs Z_i^UV(textbook)·Born = 0 (the test above), and the "ir" poles against Catani’s operator. A model-generic, independent field-UV part would need each external leg’s self-energy UV residue, which the recursion does not generate (external-leg corrections are replaced by the field factors, §3.3); it is not attempted.

  • Models with pole regulators (M-SM MS-POLES). MadLoop’s electroweak UFOs (loop_qcd_qed_sm and its G_μ variant) state the origin: their CT parameters are linear in two external parameters, epsUV and epsIR (UFO/SLHA TECHNICAL 1 and 2, default 1), e.g. (epsUV − epsIR) for a massless δZ and (epsUV + 2 epsIR) for a massive one; no finite part reads them. poles.pole_regulators finds them by code (not by name) when both are adjustable external parameters of the request that only pole coefficients read (poles.model_pole_regulators: a model that uses those codes for a parameter a tree coupling or a finite part reads has none); the native record stores them (pole_regulators), and every lane that sets the IR regulator refuses one its tree program does not bind (plan_export._regulated, V2Runtime at load). The complex-mass transform keeps them external (model_cms step 5 exempts them from the restriction card’s ones: linear, no dead branch), so the split holds under both mass schemes. In "uv" and "ir" the counterterm program is then also evaluated with the IR regulator at 0 at the point’s parameters (poles.regulated_parameters; MadLoop’s epsIR = 0 run): its r2, uv_local and field components are their UV parts, and the IR parts are the rest, CT(epsUV, epsIR) − CT(epsUV, 0), for every component and sector (split_sector(..., counterterms_uv)), with no remainder. An evaluation at (0, epsIR) instead would count twice a pole term that reads neither regulator (the UFOs’ dMB_* massive-b corrections of their EW CT parameters, UV in MadLoop’s epsIR = 0 reading). Every lane forms the second evaluation: native point inputs (NativeExecutor.reduce, a second native tree pass), Python inputs (_PointEvaluation.counterterm_twin, the point’s trees in Python at the regulated parameters), the observable columns (observables._Assembly._local_uv; stored columns: one more pass of the tree program for the column interferences, V2Executor.tree_columns, no loop dressing or reduction, StoredColumns._evaluations) and the SDK’s plan v4 runtime (v2_runtime.rs, bitwise the Python API). bare + counterterm UV = 0 is then a test of the model’s counterterms and the bare residues, and the "ir" virtual is bare_IR + CT_IR. "all" and "none" never form it (their values are unchanged bit for bit). Oracle: the counterterms’ UV part equals MadLoop’s UV-CT component at epsIR = 0 and their IR part MadLoop’s epsIR = 1 minus epsIR = 0 virtual, on loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu’s restrict_with_technical card at its own masses (u u~ > e- e+ and g g > t t~ with QCD and QED corrections, MS-REF’s *_ew_tech and *_ew_tech_ir0 runs), and bare + CT UV vanishes to 10⁻¹⁶ of the bare UV pole, asserted at 10⁻¹² (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_ew_pole_split.py, nightly). Open: the difference reading and an evaluation at (0, epsIR) differ only by the dMB_* terms, which vanish at MB = 0, where the oracle runs; the choice rests on MadLoop’s epsIR = 0 definition, not on a massive-b comparison. Without regulators (a model without them, one of them in fixed_parameters) the split is the remainder definition below; an electroweak request records which one applies (scheme_conventions’ pole_split: “regulators” with pole_regulators, or “remainder”), and an electroweak artifact written before MS-POLES (no pole_split entry, no native pole_regulators) carries the remainder: regenerate it.

  • Selected values (user decision 2026-10-23). In "uv" the virtual’s poles are the bare loop’s UV poles, the unrenormalised amplitude’s (P_UV of bare, double pole 0), with the renormalised virtual’s finite part. The other components carry their UV parts: uv (UV_local plus the field UV part) and r2 are the counterterms’ UV poles, so virtual + uv + r2 poles is the renormalised virtual’s UV part, zero where renormalisation is complete. ir_poles is None. In "ir" the virtual’s poles are the renormalised virtual’s IR poles, those of "all" (Catani’s operator), and the components carry the IR parts: bare_IR, the field IR parts, and UV_local and R2 IR parts that are zero for a model without pole regulators (with them, their CT(epsUV, epsIR) − CT(epsUV, 0), e.g. the (epsUV − epsIR) vertex terms). Both rules are poles.select_sector, shared by the inclusive assembly (assemble._PointEvaluation._assemble) and the observable columns (observables._Assembly.result).

  • Richer access. In "uv" and "ir" both parts cost the same, so PointResult.pole_origins[origin][component][sector] returns both origins’ Laurent values of every renormalised component (with the combined finite part) besides the selected components: the strict origin split, so the two origins of each component add up to its poles in "all", and pole_origins["uv"]["virtual"] is the renormalised virtual’s UV part (not the "uv" selection’s virtual, which is pole_origins["uv"]["bare"]’s poles). The selection pays for this split in both modes: the "ir" values alone equal the "all" poles, so "ir"’s extra cost buys pole_parts.

Catani’s operator (poles.catani_poles; design §10.2 item 3, oracle O9) is the IR-pole prediction in "all" and "ir". It now covers massive emitters (Catani, Dittmaier, Trócsányi 2001). Per ordered pair (j, k) of coloured legs it adds (1/C_j)[C_j (μ²/s_jk)^ε V^(S)_jk + Γ_j]⟨T_j·T_k⟩, with:

  • V^(S) = 1/ε² for two massless legs; 1/(2ε²) + ln(m²/s_jk)/(2ε) for one massive leg of mass m; ln ρ_jk/(v_jk ε) for two massive legs, where v_jk = (1 − m_j²m_k²/(p_j·p_k)²)^{1/2} and ρ = ((1−v)/(1+v))^{1/2};

  • Γ_j = γ_j/ε for a massless leg and C_j/ε for a massive one. γ_j follows the leg’s spin and representation (poles.strong_gamma): 3/2 C(R) for a fermion, 2 C(R) for a scalar, and β₀ for the gluon (the massless adjoint gauge vector), with β₀ = 11/6 C_A − Σ_s w_s T(R_s) over the request’s eligible species (poles.strong_beta0, assemble._strong_beta0): the massless coloured species perturbative in the strong order and not vetoed, one entry per particle-antiparticle pair, weighted 2/3 (Dirac fermion), 1/3 (Majorana), 1/6 (complex scalar), 1/12 (real scalar); for QCD this is 11/6 C_A − 2/3 T_R n_f with n_f the light flavours of the request (a vetoed b gives four). Another coloured vector, a representation without C(R) or T(R), or a species the weights do not cover gives no prediction (genericity audit m3).

The massless arithmetic is unchanged. The massive form reproduces the provider poles of g g > t t~ (MadLoop, Recola, OpenLoops) and the virtual’s poles of u u~ > t t~ and g g > t t~.

Dipole operators per relabelling orbit (WP3.1 C4, placement (a) of RUST-MIGRATION.md §10 item 6). The colour correlators ⟨b|T_i·T_j|b′⟩ at N_c = 3 over the Born basis are built at generation in rusticol-core, stored, and expanded at load with index arithmetic only (no Symbolica, no licence, no basis tensors). For a permutation g of identical external adjoint labels that maps the basis onto itself, g·b = s_b b″, the entries obey C_{gi,gj}[gb, gb′] = C_ij[b, b′]/(conj(s_b) s_b′); the group is generated by the transpositions of identical labels verified exactly. Seven legs: g g > g g g g g 4,320 representatives (133 kB) for 21.8 M entries, u u~ > g g g g g 26,384 (538 kB) for 3.2 M (phase-0 measurement).

  • Rust API (rusticol_core::loop_v2::dipole_orbits, for generation-scale-2’s I5c in-crate): DipoleOrbits::build(legs: &[Leg], basis: &[Tensor], classes: &[Vec<Label>]) (one-term basis tensors without √2 normalisation; classes are the candidate label sets, the external adjoint legs of one particle; colour conservation Σ_{j≠i} T_i·T_j = −C_i checked exactly); to_json() / from_json(&str) (from_json runs validate() before any table of the index space is allocated: format; coloured legs with strictly increasing labels and representations 3, 3̄ or 8; c²B² and B² by checked arithmetic; scales starting with one and holding no zero; generators permuting the legs and the basis; representatives in range and off the diagonal; and the necessary cover bound Σ_reps |O(i)||O(j)||O(b)||O(b′)| ≥ c(c−1)B² from the generators’ leg and basis orbits, with its Born-metric analogue; a crafted member is a typed InvalidArgument, never an abort); tuple_count() / entry_count() (checked c²B², c(c−1)B²); every table of the index space is allocated fallibly (try_reserve_exact), so a host that cannot hold the expansion gets a typed refusal too; expand(visit(i, j, b, b′, &Rational)) (every entry once, i ≠ j coloured-leg indices; fails on overlapping or incomplete orbits); expand_dense(zero, cast) (dense [i][j][b][b′] in any carrier: binary64, DoubleFloat, MPFR) and expand_f64(); pairs() (the (label_i, label_j) order of LoopSlice.dipoles); expand_gram (the Born metric ⟨b|b′⟩ at N_c = 3); check_conservation(); digest() (SHA-256 in LoopSlice.dipoles order).

  • Stored form (FORMAT = "pyamplicol-dipole-orbits-1", JSON, portable: no path, user or host state): {"format", "coloured": [[label, representation], …] (coloured legs in leg order), "basis": B, "generators": [{"legs": [k′ per coloured-leg index k], "basis": [[b″, scale index] per b]}, …], "scales": [[re, im] exact texts; index 0 is 1], "representatives": [[i, j, b, b′, "p/q"], …], "gram": [[b, b′, "p/q"], …]}.

  • Python binding (loops/v2/dipoles.py): build(slice_) (at generation), stored(orbits) -> str, load(text) (licence-free), operators(orbits) (= LoopSlice.dipoles() exactly), matrices(orbits) (binary64, keyed and ordered as operators), slice_operators(slice_) (the "dipoles" switch).

  • For I5c (generation-scale-2): the artifact writer stores dipoles.stored(dipoles.build(slice_)) as a member at generation; the native runtime reads it with DipoleOrbits::from_json and never expands it: NativeExecutor(catani=True) contracts the Born vectors over the stored orbits by one traversal per point group (loop_v2::dipole_correlations::Correlator, M-FINAL MF-8G-3; the dense operator would be ≈ 13 GB at eight gluons); no load-time regeneration and no Symbolica. Not wired into the artifact by package C (the writer and NativeExecutor are generation-scale-2’s).

QED operator and joint requests (WP3.2 EWI-6, poles.qed_catani_poles). The same form with T_j·T_k → Q_jQ_k (all-incoming charges), C_j → Q_j², γ_f = 3/2 Q_f², γ_s = 2 Q_s², massive legs soft only, and the prefactor α/2π with α of the model’s photon couplings (poles.qed_coupling: α_Gμ on the G_μ UFO, the coupling of the loops, not α(0)). The correlator is Q_jQ_k times the colour-summed Born interferences the sector’s QED correction dresses (poles.dressed_born: squared Born orders plus QED² equal to the sector, cross orders included). A request’s prediction is the sum of one operator per correction (_PointEvaluation._ir_poles, poles.sector_sum: QCD with α_s/2π and ⟨T_j·T_k⟩ over the Born orders plus QCD², QED as above); a correction without an operator, or one operator without a prediction, gives None, never a partial sum (a joint QCD + QED request got 0 before). The strong and the electromagnetic corrections are the coupling orders that the gauge bosons’ vertices carry, never their names (ew_policy.correction_orders, genericity audit m1): the strong order is the one every minimal gauge vertex of the massless adjoint vector carries (with a coloured particle-antiparticle pair or two more of itself), the abelian one the one every three-point vertex of the photon with a charged particle-antiparticle pair carries; a model whose orders are spelt otherwise takes the same operators, the same electroweak classification and the same α_s rule. The slice request has no order-name default either (second genericity audit m7): SliceRequest.corrections left unset (None) is the model’s strong correction (ew_policy.request_corrections, resolved by assemble.resolve_request when the slice is generated or its model prepared), and a model without one is refused with a typed GenerationError; the public routes name the corrections ([process] loop_coupling_orders). Sectors the operators predict (poles.predicted_sectors, assemble._predicted_sectors). The poles of a complete one-loop amplitude of order L are Σ_c I_c A0_{L−2c} over every coupling order c with L_c ≥ 2, but a request computes the loops of its corrections only (MadLoop’s loop selection: a QCD correction has no gluon-photon box). A sector is therefore predicted only if, for each of its loop orders L and each such c, either c is requested and the tree of order L − 2c is a Born amplitude of the slice or provably absent, or c is not requested and that tree provably does not exist; and if every Born interference a requested correction dresses in the sector pairs with a requested loop order (the operator sums over all of them: the cross-order correlators of a joint request). A tree of an order outside the Born program is absent when the order lies within the request’s Born bounds, or when an external leg has no admitted vertex whose orders fit within it; otherwise one tree DAG of the process within that order decides (artifact.born_amplitude_orders, the request’s veto, once per slice at the first prediction: e⁺e⁻ → tt̄h has no tree of order g_s²e). Sectors without a prediction are absent from ir_poles (None when no sector is predicted). Nor is a sector predicted where a requested correction’s loops leave out soft exchanges its operator sums over the Born amplitudes it dresses (mq-ewjoin, MQ-VALIDATE finding F1; poles.separated_exchange): such an exchange between charged legs runs through the lines that join them in a Born tree, and a line of a species no requested correction circulates (the W or Z between the quark lines of u d > u d h at QCD = 0) is not in the computed loops. Grouping the charged legs of each tree by the other lines gives its partition (assemble._born_partitions, a recursion over the Born DAG’s currents, skipped when no such line separates charged legs). With one partition for every tree a non-abelian operator matches the computed loops (the cross-component ⟨B|T_j·T_k|D⟩ vanish: u b > d t, u c > u c h), with several it does not (u d > u d h: Z and W exchange, single pole 0.1–0.3 off while the virtual equals MadLoop; u g > d t b~ and u b > d t g: the gluon on either line); an abelian operator needs one component per tree. Every unpredicted sector has a typed reason (poles.sector_predictions: uncorrected-exchange, uncomputed-born-pair, separated-exchange; LoopSlice.unpredicted_sectors). This fixes the misleading prediction of mixed QCD × EW sectors of QCD-only requests routed from ew-lines (slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-25 ~13:30): on u u~ > d d~ with gluon and photon Borns and QCD corrections the operators’ sum in QCD⁴QED² was twice the virtual’s single pole (the gluon Born’s QED poles that the left-out gluon-photon boxes carry); QCD⁶ stays predicted and equal to the virtual (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_catani_scope.py). precision-ap’s b b~ > t t~ at QED² with QCD corrections (0.45 % from the b-t boxes with a photon or a W in the loop) is no longer predicted either. External photons (WP3.2 EWI-6b; the user’s decision [U9] of 2026-10-25) couple with α(0) in electroweak requests: see ew_policy.external_photon_scheme below; under that convention they add no γ_γ (qed_catani_poles, convention "alpha0"), and the conversion term’s pole is IR. Before EWI-3 opens electroweak generation the operator is checked on stand-in points (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_qed_catani.py): the providers’ poles of g g > t t~, u u~ > e⁻e⁺g, g g > t t~ e⁻e⁺ and g g > t t~ e⁻e⁺g at O(α) (MadLoop ≤ 10⁻¹², every validated provider within the fixtures’ 2·10⁻⁸) and of the MadLoop G_μ controls e⁻e⁺ → μ⁻μ⁺ and e⁻e⁺ → uū (≤ 10⁻¹²). The joint g g > g g on loop_qcd_qed_sm, which generates, has its QCD⁶ poles equal to the prediction. The ε_UV/ε_IR split of the counterterm poles on the G_μ UFO waits for EWI-3.

Electroweak guards (WP3.2 EWI-0b, loops/v2/ew_policy.py, called from LoopSlice.generate). An electroweak request (a correction other than the model’s strong one, identified by the gluon’s vertices; or a perturbative colour-singlet species) is refused with a typed GenerationError if its Born or loop-side trees propagate a particle with a non-zero width, coloured or not (ElectroweakWidthError, listed key electroweak-width; the user’s decision [U8]: fix the widths to zero, or use the complex-mass scheme, §6.8). On-shell external photons (WP3.2 EWI-6b, ew_policy.external_photon_scheme) couple with α(0), the convention MG5_aMC applies outside the UFO (1804.10017 §2; export_fks.write_rescale_a0gmu_file, the G_μ branch) and the user’s decision [U9]: every output of the point is multiplied by (α(0)/α)^n for n such photons (_PointEvaluation.average, which divides the slice’s spin, colour and symmetry average by it: Born, loop lanes, counterterm and field components, Catani’s correlators, stability budgets and the observable columns all take it), and each photon leg carries the field-like factor −(δZ_e^{Gμ} − δZ_e^{α(0)}) of the electromagnetic correction, the model’s eCoup_DGmua0_UV_EW (assemble._alpha0_field_rules; the field component adds −2 n DGmua0 Born, MG5_aMC’s term). α is the photon couplings’ (poles.qed_coupling, α_Gμ), α(0) the adjustable 1/α(0) at SMINPUTS 1 (aEW0M1 of MG5_aMC’s G_μ loop models under restrict_a0; the default card fixes it to zero). The conversion parameter has no structural marker in a UFO: MG5_aMC applies it by that name, so v2 does too. Per leg (MS-PHOTON; m-sm/PLAN.md Q1 (a), MG5_aMC’s !a!). Only the tagged photons take the convention: SliceRequest.external_photons ([loop] external_photons) is "final" (default: final-state photons, isolated photons), "all", "none" or a list of 1-based legs (initial legs allowed; a listed leg that is no on-shell photon is refused, listed key external-photon-legs), resolved by ew_policy.photon_tags; ExternalPhotons.legs holds the tagged legs only, so (α(0)/α)^n, the conversion field insertion (filtered to the tagged legs, not the species) and the native binder’s photons leg list run over them, and a request without a tagged photon needs neither 1/α(0) nor the conversion counterterm (the refusal, listed key external-photon-scheme, applies to tagged photons only and names the remedy for the model: untagged photons, or restriction = "a0"). An untagged photon keeps the loops’ coupling: the QED operator adds −γ_γ/ε per untagged photon (poles.UNTAGGED_PHOTON_CONVENTION, γ_γ over the massless, non-vetoed charged fermions at the point, _PointEvaluation._photon_gamma), so the joint prediction stays complete. Default rationale: an initial photon is a PDF photon (α(0) would shift it by ~3.3 % per photon and give the wrong IR pole); MadLoop standalone converts none, MG5_aMC converts exactly the tagged ones, and only with the electromagnetic correction (QCD-only requests convert nothing). scheme_conventions records tagged_photon_legs, untagged_photon_legs and the option; a request at the default records no option (request records keep their bytes). Acceptance: PI01–PI04, PI01’s "all" twin, VJ03, VV05, VV06, LL08 = raw MadLoop × MG5_aMC’s formula over the tagged legs with Python and native inputs, rule 4 per leg (test_loop_v2_external_photons.py::test_photon_rows_equal_madloop_with_the_formula_over_tagged_legs, nightly). A model or request that cannot take the convention is refused (ExternalPhotonError, naming the reason): no electromagnetic correction requested, no conversion parameter, no adjustable 1/α(0) the loops’ coupling leaves free, 1/α(0) fixed to zero, or a particle_veto of a species perturbative in the electromagnetic correction (the conversion is one parameter over the whole electroweak content). The native point inputs take the convention in the photons’ sources (WP3.2 EWI-N; until then the listed refusal external-photon-alpha0 of package fail-closed, G2-m4): the parameter program’s output α(0)/α (native_trees._parameter_program’s photons record, on the inputs 1/α(0) and those of the photon coupling, checked real, finite and positive per point by the native binder, which names 1/α(0) otherwise) and every source of the photon legs (helicity, spin and loop-side sources, in the trees and the counterterm program) multiplied by its square root (loop_v2::trees::TreeProgram::scale_photons, after the spin and loop-side sources are written). Every amplitude is linear in each leg’s source, so every output (Born, loops, counterterm kets, field insertions, observable columns) takes (α(0)/α)ⁿ and the plan’s average stays the slice’s: _NativePoint, V2Runtime and the SDKs divide by it; the conversion is a field insertion, exported as every field coupling. 1/α(0) is a runtime parameter of the stored process. Native = Python inputs within 1.1·10⁻¹⁵ (u u~ > a g) and 3.4·10⁻¹⁵ (u u~ > a a) of the virtual, and the native virtual = MadLoop’s converted one within 6.4·10⁻¹³ and 4.4·10⁻¹³ per coefficient (test_loop_v2_external_photons.py::test_alpha0_native_inputs_equal_madloop_and_the_python_inputs). MadLoop references on loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gμ (tests/fixtures/loop/required/uux_ag_ew.json, uux_aa_ew.json; pure G_μ standalone, converted with MG5_aMC’s formula and MadLoop’s own DGmua0) agree to 6.3·10⁻¹³ (u u~ > a g) and 2.7·10⁻¹³ (u u~ > a a) per coefficient, with the IR poles equal to Catani’s without γ_γ and cancelling UV poles; the photon’s Ward identity holds on u u~ > a g (O10’s asymmetric mode, ε_3 → c p_3 on the loop side: every renormalised component ≤ 2.1·10⁻¹² of the physical scale in binary64, the α(0) field term 6·10⁻¹⁷; a literal vector gives every part ≥ 10⁻² of it) (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_external_photons.py, nightly). The width check runs on the Born and block DAGs before their kernels and the counterterm lowering. QCD-only requests are not guarded and their plans are unchanged.

Listed generation refusals (package fail-closed, 2026-10-27; second genericity audit, genericity-audit-2/REPORT.md). An unsupported structure is refused with a typed error naming a listed rule, decided by a structural criterion (never process strings, names, PDG codes or leg and line counts), and the dry run lists both tables. Loop admission (loops/v2/refusals.py, LOOP_ADMISSION_REFUSALS, LoopRequestUnsupported, a GenerationError): colour-accuracy-nc-exact (§3.3: a guard only since package identical-flavour-lc; LC and NLC compile with the N_c grade split, so their blocks have one grade, identical-flavour lines included, and the rule refuses only blocks that still mix grades, i.e. a loop-request DAG compiled without the split), veto-unlabelled-counterterms (WP3.2 EWI-5 interim, item (3) of EWI-5’s “Open (found here, outside the lepton signs)”: a particle_veto removing a loop species of a requested correction on a model whose counterterm terms of that correction are not all labelled with their loop content, refused in the model preparation prepare_request_model, before any tree, so the dry run reports it) and fermion-line-representation (G2-m1): the blocks sign coloured fermion lines by their colour flow and colour-singlet ones by their Wick order (generation.fermion_ordering), so a vertex joining fermions of different sign ownership (a leptoquark u e S vertex: one line changing colour representation) has no sign; LoopSlice.generate refuses, before any tree, a request that can use such a vertex: an oriented kernel admitted as the DAG admits it (veto, order limits of the Born and the blocks) whose inputs are both currents producible from the legs (a tree vertex) or one such current and a species perturbative in a requested correction while its result is such a species or a contact auxiliary (a loop vertex: the loop line in and out), the producible currents the fixed point of the admitted kernels (an over-approximation of the trees, so a vertex any tree or loop uses is found), naming the vertices; the native DAG builder refuses the same merge, and a block whose coloured fermion ends do not pair, as DagError::Unsupported with the listed key FERMION_LINE_REPRESENTATION (loop_v2::dag::ADMISSION_REFUSALS), which dag_input raises as the same typed error; and loop-vertex-outside-tree-model (fail-closed-2, a guard): loop lines read their vertices’ colour and Lorentz structures from the request’s tree model, so a vertex of the loop model whose couplings at an order vanish identically at the model’s restriction is no loop vertex there: ct_sites.restricted_to_zero (the counterterm root closure’s rule of WP3.2 EWI-5, now with the source helpers a coupling calls inlined with their exact bodies, ScalarFunctionLibrary.inline, before the internal parameters are resolved; decided from the coupling values, never names) gives ct_sites.vanishing_loop_vertices, which families.ModelLoopCatalogue(vanishing=...) leaves out (0.08 s per generation on the G_μ UFO; on its default restriction, Wolfenstein inputs zero: the six W vertices of the off-diagonal CKM elements, each a complexconjugate of a zero element that the prepared native model keeps, and their charged-Goldstone Yukawas); any other loop vertex the tree model does not hold at the order a loop position takes it is refused when the position is used (colour.SeedColour.states, naming the vertex, its particles and orders), where it raised an untyped ValueError (g t → t u u~ with QCD and QED corrections at the G_μ default restriction, slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-28 ~03:50: its loops now pass the catalogue and the slice generates and evaluates, LoopSlice.generate: 150 families, 282 s, 8.7 GB, its poles the Catani operator’s; the stored-process path, artifact.generate_process behind pyamplicol generate and Generator, then refuses it at native export with the listed plane-mismatch at its UV_GTTLEW counterterm, epsilon power 0, after about 355 s and 8.8 GB, the open EWI-N refusal of g g → t t~ [QCD QED], measured by the fail-closed-2 evidence audit). Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_restricted_zero.py (the vanishing set at the default restriction equal to the loop model’s tree vertices of which the compiled tree model holds no term, the tree compiler’s own zero test, and of the native model’s vertices exactly the six off-diagonal W⁺ vertices and t̄ d G⁺, t̄ s G⁺; on the renamed ckm variant of loop_renamed_models, CKM elements, Wolfenstein inputs and vertices renamed: the same vertices by particles and orders, and no W vertex at restrict_ckm; the reproducer’s generation stopped after its loop schedules, its catalogue without them; the refusal with the rule disabled; the reproducer’s slice, nightly); the loop_sm byte pins below are unchanged (no loop_sm vertex vanishes), and so is the plan of u u~ → t t~ with QCD and QED corrections on the G_μ UFO; the plans of the G_μ controls with closed light-quark loops (g u → g u, g g → t t~, u u~ → e⁻ e⁺ g, e⁻ e⁺ → u u~ with their QED corrections) change on purpose: the closed s and b loops, whose catalogue entries differed only by the vanishing W vertices, now form one closed-loop class of multiplicity 2 (§4.3; g u → g u: 108 → 100 reading skeletons, 82 → 74 plan contents), and every component (Born, bare, R2, UV and its parts, virtual) is bitwise identical in binary64 at a point for g u → g u, g g → t t~ and e⁻ e⁺ → u u~, while for u u~ → e⁻ e⁺ g the Born, R2 and UV components are and the bare part and the virtual move by at most 1.2·10⁻¹⁵ of their largest coefficient (the merged class’s summation order). Native export (native_trees.NATIVE_EXPORT_REFUSALS, NativeExportUnsupported, a generation GenerationError through artifact._not_storable): besides the generation-scale keys, plane-mismatch (G2-M4: the SymJIT plane check’s disagreement, loop_v2::trees::compile_plane_application_checked → PlaneMismatchError(message, output, row, imaginary, real_axis), names the output: a kernel by its class and index (vertex or propagator kernel of the tree or counterterm program), a parameter-program output by its key, a derived coupling derived_coupling_<term id> by its UFO coupling, vertex and particles, a counterterm coefficient with its epsilon power and N_c grade (native_trees._PlaneOutputs); it refused g g → t t~ [QCD QED] on loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu (a counterterm coefficient UV_GTTLEW of the parameter program) and the MW-card-input loop_sm variant of the renamed-model harness (a W derived coupling) until WP3.2 EWI-N made the check independent of the parameter declaration order: complex rows off the real axis and the request’s parameter values as the real point, with the native counterterm couplings on MadLoop’s side of real cuts (DECISIONS 2026-10-26 ~21:10 item 6, confirmed by the user 2026-10-27 ~19:20; WP3.2 status, ew-native); external-photon-alpha0 (G2-m4, above) was listed until EWI-N exported the α(0) convention natively. Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_fail_closed.py (both rules through LoopSlice.generate, the public API and the CLI, each export layer, the toy leptoquark UFO loop_v2_ufo_variants.leptoquark_ufo in both DAG lanes and the native key), test_loop_v2_ew_policy.py::test_stored_external_photon_requests_reach_their_trees, test_loop_genericity_renamed_models.py::test_plane_mismatch_names_the_parameter_program_output (at the former real probes as the real point), test_loop_v2_ew_native.py (the check’s rows, EWI-N); test_loop_v2_fail_closed.py::test_plans_the_guards_do_not_refuse_keep_their_bytes pins the plan, companion and native-member digests of six of the controls below (measured on the slice 6da37352; equal at 59d47cb3 and 11542fd5 except the native trees of g g → u u~ u u~, whose counterterm program takes ew-epsilon’s root-closure reading signs at 6da37352: 192 four-block term signs); on the eleven loop_sm controls the guards admit (u u~ → d d~ g at LC, NLC and full colour, u u~ → d d~ s s~ at LC and NLC, u u~ → u u~ at LC, g g → g g g at LC, and full colour of u u~ → u u~ g, g g → u u~ u u~, u u~ → e⁺ e⁻ g and d d~ → g g) the stored plan, the companion plan and every native PACBIN member are byte-identical to 11542fd5’s (the six pinned ones also to 6da37352’s), except the parameter program’s SymJIT plane (parameters.symjit), which differs between two runs of 11542fd5 itself.

Stock loop_sm on the public route (package mq-model, m-qcd PLAN MQ-MODEL, 2026-10-28). (1) Source repair: loops.covariant_model.repair_source_declarations moves a vertex (tree or counterterm) whose particles are all scalars from a constant Lorentz tensor of other (scalar) slots to the model’s unique tensor of its spin signature and the same exact constant (loop_sm’s four-G⁰ V_1001: SSS1 → SSSS1), recorded under pyamplicol_source_repairs in the derived source and in the structure’s diagnostics; it runs in prepare_loop_request_model on the vertices the request reaches (so a source whose reached vertices have no defect, e.g. loop_sm under a QCD-only Born scope as in the frozen legacy captures, is prepared byte for byte as before; idempotent, a no-op on the checkout’s scalar-arity view, tools/loop_reference/model_compatibility.py, which stays the independent oracle: the same derived collections) and on the compiled model the public route publishes (with_source_repairs in generation.loop_service._prepare); any other slot mismatch is the listed lorentz-slot-arity when a request reaches the vertex. (2) Shipped model and declaration: MG5_aMC 3.7.0’s loop_sm and all its restriction cards ship verbatim (assets/models/ufo/loop_sm, PROVENANCE, MANIFEST); a bare shipped model name is a model source when no such path exists (_internal.packaged_models); loops.shipped_profiles holds loop_sm’s [loop.model] declaration keyed by the sha256 of the source’s declarations (schema version and record collections after the repair: one digest for the shipped copy, the MG5_aMC directory and every restriction), used when neither the card nor the source declares one. (3) A one-loop request without color.accuracy is full colour (user ruling Q1; config.ColorConfig.accuracy = None resolves in RunConfig). (4) Listed QCD refusals (user rulings 2026-10-28 ~15:25): loop-induced (no Born amplitude in the limits), coloured-width (naming restriction = "no_widths" and WT = "0"), dirac-weyl-closure (the tree DAG’s closure guard; lifted for loop requests by MQ-5F, whose loop Born records the class as a marker root, and since then the tree lanes’ dag_ordering.DiracWeylClosureUnsupported, no loop admission refusal), lorentz-slot-arity, majorana-fermion and multi-fermion-contact (model preparation); and product-wide process refusals (processes.refusals, ProcessRequestUnsupported, a ValueError, listed as process_request_refusals in the dry run): decay-process (one initial-state slot, ProcessRequest.parse) and madloop-syntax (NLO brackets, order constraints, /, $, decay chains, @N, naming the run-card setting). (5) pyamplicol self-test generates u u~ → e⁻ e⁺ / Z [virt=QCD] on the shipped loop_sm-no_b_mass through the public route and holds it to MadLoop (_internal.selftest_virtual). Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_stock_loop_sm.py (the public route on model.source = "loop_sm" with no [loop.model] and no colour setting bitwise equal in binary64 to the tools-view route for u u~ → e⁻ e⁺ and, nightly, the eleven further QED-Born requests of the MQ-MODEL list on the shipped copy and the MG5_aMC directory; Drell–Yan / Z and e⁺e⁻ → tt̄ against MadLoop: double-double within 2.8·10⁻¹³ and 1.3·10⁻¹⁴, binary64 within 10⁻¹² of double-double; every key in a dry run or at model preparation). Campaign rows on the public route (generation through Generator on model.source = "loop_sm", evaluation through Runtime.evaluate with the O1 checks, judged by MQ-VALIDATE’s §1.4 rules against MQ-REF’s MadLoop references; driver and records in workspace/reports/engine-v2/mq-model/public-route-campaign/): D01, D05, D12, D15, D16, D18, D21, F01 and F03 on the 5F* recipe (default restriction, MB = ymb = WT = 0) pass rules 1–4 (and 6 where the row lists it) at every reference point, double-double within 1.4·10⁻¹³ of MadLoop; the binary64 out-of-scope listing of D16 is route specific (the public route’s estimates put its single pole in scope, within E); D19’s single pole differs from Catani’s prediction by the same amount on both routes while equal to MadLoop’s (MQ-VALIDATE); F03 on no_b_mass was dirac-weyl-closure until MQ-5F, which admits it (records in workspace/reports/engine-v2/mq-5f/). The multiparticle row M01 (p p > t t~ on loop_sm-no_b_mass, m01_public.py): one public generation (37 s) holds the six concrete processes (d, u, s, c, b q q̄ and g g → t t̄; p is the model’s massless partons), the set of MadLoop’s SubProcesses P0_uux_ttx and P2_gg_ttx; each, loaded from that artifact by its expression, is bitwise equal to its own single-process generation (Born, the six components per sector and the totals, binary64 and double-double, at four reference points), and the gating variants M01@P0 (u u~ → t t~) and M01@P2 (g g → t t~) read from it pass rules 1–4 at every point (double-double within 1.2·10⁻¹⁴ of MadLoop). A loop artifact records the model’s spelling (loop_sm’s gluon is G), so loops.v2.artifact._select follows the public spelling rule of requests (processes.model.resolve_model_particle_name): the exact spelling first, then a unique letter-case-insensitive match (as the tree selector’s lower-cased tokens, rusticol-core normalize_process_expression), and a folded match that is not unique names the stable ids. The committed built-in-sm prepared-model pair was stale against models/builtin (f355f343 after the f9874045 regeneration, on loop too), so stage_packaged_prepared_models refused every wheel build in both modes; it is regenerated with the release flow of .github/workflows/release-prepared-models.yml run on x86_64 Linux (tools/release/prepare_release_prepared_models.py bootstrap-wheel, the bootstrap runtime on PyPI dependencies, tools/ci/eager_portability.py produce --asset-mode release; the HEFT pair was current), and the one portable SymJIT storage-v4 O2 bundle fills both architecture slots of both stores through the backend’s writer (write_release_packaged_prepared_model_asset; the portability contract audits no producer/consumer architecture equality). A mass alias that resolves to an exact zero (loop_sm’s Me, MC, MB where a restriction or a fixed parameter zeroes them) is named ZERO in the covariant structure (build_covariant_structure): the published Community 3.0.2 HepKit, the wheel’s pinned Symbolica, keeps the alias’s source symbol where the integration kernel’s (9cdc2949) exports ZERO, and the v2 families refused it as a derived mass of value zero (_model_masses); native.to_json() is now byte for byte the same under both (loop_sm under seven restriction and fixed-zero cases; unchanged under 9cdc2949; test_structural_zero_mass_alias_is_named_zero_under_either_hepkit emulates the published HepKit). Evidence: a release-mode host wheel (pyamplicol.host-wheel=true) of the branch head installed into fresh venvs, one with only its pinned PyPI dependencies and one with the Community 9cdc2949 Symbolica, passes pyamplicol self-test (python, model-assets, rusticol-python, native-sdk, physics-f64, physics-virtual: MadLoop to 2.8·10⁻¹³, generated in 9 s) under env -i (workspace/reports/engine-v2/mq-model/wheel-selftest/).

The QCD+QED loop models on the public route (package ms-model, m-sm PLAN MS-MODEL, wave 1 part, 2026-10-29). (1) Goldstone-flag source repair: the legacy UFO object library’s Particle.anti binds goldstoneboson to its line argument, so MG5_aMC’s loop_qcd_qed_sm and loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu declare G⁻ without the flag of its partner G⁺; repair_source_declarations (rule antiparticle-goldstone-flag, found by the library fingerprint _lost_goldstone_flag, never by a name; not restricted by within, particles belong to every request) restores it, records it under pyamplicol_source_repairs and is idempotent, so the public route needs no compatibility = "gmu_particle_anti", which stays accepted (satisfied as it is on a repaired source). loop_sm has no such antiparticle: its declarations digest e2512823… is unchanged. (2) Shipped models (Q5 (a)): loop_qcd_qed_sm as downloaded (MG5_aMC model database, loop_qcd_qed_sm.tgz sha256 7b7b9b2c…) and loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu as the Python-3 conversion of its Python-2 download (…_Gmu.tgz sha256 7655cb63…; package-relative imports, .iteritems() → .items(), a Python-3 write_param_card.py; no declaration changed: the converted copy has the declarations digest of the workspace reference copy), every restriction card byte for byte, without caches, backups, AppleDouble or hidden files and the SMWidth tool (PROVENANCE ufo-python3-conversion-v1). (3) loops.shipped_profiles declares both by their declarations digest after the repair (1b9f6550…, 588cb07a…): joint QCD and QED corrections, complete UV and R2, the HV / four-dimensional / on-shell electroweak scheme; the scheme differs from loop_sm’s, so MQ-NC’s scheme-gated N_c data never attaches (EW LC/NLC keep colour-declaration-coverage). A modified copy (massive-muon, b-mass variants) has other declarations and keeps a declared [loop.model]. (4) ufo-python2 (models.source_refusals, a ModelError): a UFO directory whose import fails is Python 2 when one of its modules is not Python-3 source (compiled, not imported) or the failure names a Python-2-only attribute or builtin; the model loaders raise it, and the dry run, which compiles no model, finds the first case without importing. (5) Tree API: the NLO UFO scalar helpers arg, crecms, grreglog, recms, regsqrt are registered (the models call them in counterterm expressions only), so the tree models compile as supported; tree MEs from their prepared kernel packs equal MadLoop’s Borns of e⁻e⁺ → e⁻e⁺, e⁻e⁺ → tt̄h, gg → tt̄, uū → e⁻e⁺g and gg → tt̄e⁻e⁺ to ≤ 2.3·10⁻¹⁵. (6) pyamplicol self-test also evaluates an EW virtual from a shipped prepared artifact (assets/selftest_virtual/ew, _internal.selftest_virtual_ew: e⁻e⁺ → e⁻e⁺ [virt=QED] on loop_qcd_qed_sm, the public route’s output, native point inputs, portable: scan clean, relocated bitwise without a licence) against MadLoop (5.4·10⁻¹⁵); loading a v2 artifact reads its compiled model with Symbolica, so without it the check is a named warning. Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_ew_public_models.py (nightly: the public route on the shipped models, no [loop.model], no compatibility profile, no tools/ import, is bitwise equal in binary64 to the tools view for e⁻e⁺ → μ⁻μ⁺, uū → e⁻e⁺, uū → dd̄, gg → tt̄, ud̄ → W⁺g, uū → ZZ and uū → γg (a0), and gg → tt̄ equals MadLoop’s gg_ttx_ew rows).

UFOmodeldb as the source of the QCD+QED loop models (package ms-ufodb, m-sm PLAN MS-MODEL follow-up, user rule 2026-10-30: https://github.com/mg5amcnlo/UFOmodeldb is the ground truth). The shipped loop_qcd_qed_sm and loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu are UFOmodeldb’s (commit 6ca4b120; loop_qcd_qed_sm.tgz sha256 b6a60603…, loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu.tgz sha256 9f3668e7…; the G_mu model with the same Python-3 conversion). Against the MG5_aMC online-database copies of item (2) above the one declaration that changed is the coupling R2_ZZHH (CT_couplings.py, (2+2*cw**2 …) → (1+2*cw**2 …); UFOmodeldb fix 1f13c48f / 6ca4b120), which enters the R2 vertices Z Z H H and Z Z G0 G0 only. The shipped profiles list the new declarations digests first (580c029a…, b580d14a…) and keep the downloads’ (1b9f6550…, 588cb07a…): same scheme, one coupling value. A counterterm vertex is a tree vertex inserted once and the bare loops use tree couplings only, so a request none of whose trees holds those vertices has the same plan on both (artifacts of VV02, SC07, VH01 on either model: byte-identical but for the compiled model and the run-to-run parameters.symjit); of the M-SM rows only SC10 (z z > h h, new, MadLoop QP on both models) reaches them (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_ufodb_models.py); Recola, whose R2 terms are its own, equals MadLoop on the UFOmodeldb model to 2.2e-11 of the finite part and differs from MadLoop on the download by 3.7 % to 2.7 times it, so the fix is right. Tests and the reference toolkit load the UFOmodeldb copies under workspace/reference/models/ufodb-6ca4b120/; the shipped EW self-test artifact is regenerated from the new model (same values bitwise).

The UFOmodeldb issue-1 model patch in the shipped QCD+QED models (package ms-ufo-patch, user rule 2026-10-30 ~12:45; gist ValentinHirschi/81a26a3c…, ufomodeldb-issue-1.patch sha256 4b5b1ef0…, applied with patch --fuzz=0 -p1; PROVENANCE ufomodeldb-issue-1-patch-v1, -python3-v1, -python3-fold-v1). (1) R2_G0tt_{d,s,b} split by loop content ([W+, G+, q] and [G+, q], coefficient sum kept): the engine inserts every R2 vertex once, so its values do not move (bitwise on TT04, SC09, LL10; one ulp of the R2 component, ≤ 3e-17 of the virtual, on TT05 and TT06: the vertex coefficient is the same sum formed from other terms), while MadLoop’s exports now call R2_G0tt_b_WG and equal Recola (the rule-1 madloop_omitted_r2 correction is gone). (2) Exactly unitary CKM: on the ckm restriction (SC03) values change by O(lambda^4); on every other restriction the CKM entries are exactly 1 and 0 as before, but the unpatched UFO’s CKM33 = '1' of type complex resolved to a float (1.00000000000000) and the patched CKMc23*CKMc13 resolves to the exact 1, so rows with V_tb in W couplings or counterterms move at the last bits of those constants (cancellations amplify it to ≤ 2.1e-11 of the virtual: VV07, V301, VV01, CM08; a CKM-only variant reproduces it, the R2 split alone is bitwise neutral there). (3) The G_mu charge counterterm’s b-mass term: eCoup_a0_UV_EW + eCoup_DGmua0_UV_EW = eCoup_Gmu_UV_EW with MB ≠ 0 (ST04, SC04, TT06, SC03 move, = Recola), unchanged bitwise at MB = 0. The patch writes it as module-level X.value[k] += '...' statements, which ufo-model-loader 1.0.1 does not certify (it then certifies no value of the model: “source helper complexconjugate lacks a certified body”); the shipped G_mu model and the reference copies fold them into the constructors (tools/developer/fold_ufo_value_appends.py, every UFO value string identical by import). (4) restrict_with_b_mass.dat of G_mu gains SMINPUTS 1 = 0 (aEW0M1’s default; no value changes). The new term ( 0 if MB == 0 else … reglog(MU_R**2/MB**2) … ) exposed a lowering defect: with MB a fixed parameter the dead branch formed 0^-2 and no evaluator could be built (“infinity coefficients”; SC08 and ST03 hit it on the unpatched model already). ScalarFunctionLibrary now forms only the taken branch of a conditional its bindings decide (decided_number: exact numbers, the library’s predicates and symbolica::if), as Python’s lazy conditional does; values and exported plans are bitwise unchanged on the rows that evaluated before (tools route). The shipped EW self-test artifact, regenerated because its compiled model changes with the patch, has a 14 % smaller runtime (loop-runtime.pacbin, the dead branches of the MB == 0 conditionals gone) and one of its twelve values moves by 6.4e-16 (a single pole; the same on the unpatched model, so the reshaped scalar evaluator’s rounding, not the patch); it still equals MadLoop to 5.4e-15. Evidence: old-vs-new generations of 65 M-SM rows on the QCD+QED models (all but the composite MP rows, the CM01 and LL02 controls and the loop_sm rows SC05, CM10), bitwise equal except the rows named above; MadLoop QP and Recola on the patched model for LL10, TT04, SC09, TT05, TT06, ST04 and SC04’s e^6 sector agree to ≤ 5.3e-11 and with pyAmpliCol (workspace/reports/engine-v2/upstream/ufo-patch-validation.md); SC03’s IR single-pole remnant is exactly the documented tau-mass residual MTA^2/(2 sw^2 (s − MW^2)) (α/2π) Born (the EW counterterms omit the tau mass, a retained limitation). UFOmodeldb 60ee58bb (2026-10-30) took the b-flavour R2 split alone; the shipped models keep the full patch (coordinator ruling ~13:40). Shipped profiles: patched digests first (0dc17624…, 97f39eeb…), then UFOmodeldb 60ee58bb’s (1555635e…, 14ddd943…), 6ca4b120’s and MG5_aMC’s; tests and the toolkit read workspace/reference/models/ufodb-6ca4b120-patched/ (the unpatched copies remain as conftest controls).

Listed keys of every refusal a one-loop request reaches (package ms-model, m-sm PLAN MS-MODEL items 4, 5 and 7, after EWI-7, 2026-10-30). Three tables in loops/v2/refusals.py share LoopAdmissionRefusal (key, feature, rule, remedy, owner, follow-up) and the dry run lists each (estimated_coverage.loop_admission_refusals, loop_configuration_refusals, loop_internal_refusals): (1) admission keys, now also external-photon-scheme (ew_policy.ExternalPhotonError, a LoopRequestUnsupported; conditions and remedy per leg stay MS-PHOTON’s), feynman-gauge (ElectroweakGaugeError and ew_policy.require_loop_gauge’s no-gauge-1 refusal of a request whose loops need gauge 1), antiparticle-metadata (covariant_model._validate_pairs, the generalisation of the repaired Goldstone-flag mismatch) and anomalous-veto (ct_recursion.AnomalousVetoError, [U2]); (2) configuration keys (LOOP_CONFIGURATION_REFUSALS, decided from the run card and the model’s declarations before any tree): loop-model-declaration, loop-model-corrections, loop-model-completion (models.loop_declaration), undeclared-corrections, scale-parameter, veto-external-particle, tree-only-model, and the _feature_blockers / _v2_blockers texts fft-basis-trace, colour-selectors, process-group-analysis (numerical analysis only; process-aliases was lifted by M-FINAL MF-MAP, §9), direct-r2, relation-discovery, evaluator-backend, evaluator-tuning, covariant-multiplets (each a ListedBlocker, a str with its key: the dry run shows the listed text, generation raises the first as LoopRequestUnsupported); the LC/NLC “explicit source colour data” text is colour-declaration-coverage; (3) internal keys (LOOP_INTERNAL_REFUSALS): engine conditions met during the generation of an admitted request, carried by the error classes as refusal_key (fermion-sign, reading-sign, unlowered-counterterm, counterterm-coupling, loop-kernel-catalogue, counterterm-completeness; M-LIT lit-ew-blocks adds block-colour-flow, colour.BlockColourFlowError: two blocks of one block current and word whose colour flows differ, e.g. pure-electroweak u u~ > d d~ s s~ with QCD loops) and typed at the generation boundary (refusals.keyed_error: LoopEngineRefusal, a GenerationError with key); a native export refusal surfaces as NativeExportRefused with the export’s feature key (artifact._not_storable), not as text in a plain GenerationError. The dry run also calls the checks of an electroweak request that need only the model and the Born DAG (loop_service._plan_policy_checks: external_photon_scheme and the width policy ew_policy.require_zero_widths on the Born currents; the width and complex-parameter policy and their keys are MS-CMS’s). Multiparticle requests (Q2 (a), loop_service._born_members): a concrete process of a multiparticle request with Born members that has no Born amplitude is skipped with a typed loop-induced record (the dry run’s skipped_members, the artifact manifest extension loop_skipped_members); since M-LIT LIT-REQ a request none of whose processes has a Born is routed loop-induced and only process.loop_induced = "skip" refuses it (loop-induced; the paragraph below). Plan export (plan_export._trace_groups): a trace step reads its sources at the largest source storage and contracts at the largest content degree, so a family whose rings peak at different positions (an N = 2 family of u ū → ZZ [virt=QED] on G_μ: rank 1, a trace step at 1 + 1) was refused at load (“a trace step above the family rank”); such a step is now one step per source storage, summed by the accumulator, and a step within the rank is unchanged (every plan the loader admitted before is exported byte for byte as before). Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_refusal_keys.py (every configuration key in the dry run and as the typed generation error; the model-level keys on loop_sm, the modified-model keys, the EW keys on the shipped QCD+QED models; the multiparticle dry run and generation, a stored member bitwise equal to its own generation; internal keys and NativeExportRefused; the trace-step split); user docs docs/user/electroweak-and-madloop.md.

Loop-induced requests (package lit-req, M-LIT PLAN LIT-REQ, rulings Q2 (b), Q4 (a), Q7, Q8 (a), Q13, 2026-11-06). A concrete process is loop-induced iff no Born DAG root exists within its coupling-order limits (_member; structural). process.loop_induced (ProcessConfig, TOML, CLI --loop-induced, LoopInducedPolicy) routes it in loop_service._born_members: auto (default) serves a request none of whose members has a Born loop-induced and skips the Born-less members of a request with Born members (loop-induced record, as before); skip serves none (a purely loop-induced request is refused loop-induced, naming the key); only serves the Born-less members and skips the Born ones (born-in-loop-induced-mode; refused when none is left); include serves both kinds as separate processes of one artifact, never summed (the former loop-induced-include-pending refusal was retired by LIT-API). The slice request of a loop-induced member (_loop_induced_request, sharing _slice_request with _v2_request) has SliceRequest.contribution = "loop-induced" (recorded only then, so Born-interfered records keep their bytes), full colour only (loop-induced-colour-accuracy), no Born orders, and loop orders inferred by assemble.reachable_loop_orders + loop_service.loop_induced_orders: the field-level family recursion (native, the Python recursion its oracle) runs on every order of the box bounded by process.max_coupling_orders and, for an unnamed order, by the largest power of an (n + 2)-leg tree (_tree_order_bounds); its reached orders are those of the admitted and certified-scaleless routings plus the exact colour zeros, orders reached only by routings the selection convention drops for a single coloured attachment (Tr T^a = 0 in any model; the recursion’s rejection log carries no orders, so they are found by halving the target set while a group logs that reason: one extra run when none exists); minimal keeps every reached order of the least weighted degree by the model’s hierarchy (coupling_order_hierarchies, as MG5_aMC’s WEIGHTED guess, which also counts the zero-colour loop diagrams it later filters), explicit every reached order; nothing reached is no-loop-amplitude (skipped in a multiparticle request). The dry run’s record (_loop_induced_coverage) lists the kind, limits, loop orders, loop x loop sectors, colour_zero_loop_orders and exact_colour_zero (every loop order a colour zero: h > g a, z > g a, served by LIT-AMP as the exact zero with its colour record, PLAN §1.2) and the width policy (Q7: fixed widths in every tree propagator, no coloured-width refusal on this branch, also in the storage re-check of artifact.generate_process; loop propagators widthless; the complex-mass scheme everywhere, unstable external states refused by require_stable_external_states ahead of the routing; an electroweak loop-induced request takes the same policy, the Born-interfered electroweak-width guard does not apply to it: LIT-EW, §7.12). Generation serves them in amplitude mode (LIT-AMP, §7.11; the former loop-induced-engine-pending refusal is retired). Evidence: tests/unit/test_loop_v2_induced_request.py (the PLAN §1.3 table on loop_sm and loop_qcd_qed_sm, native = Python recursion, every key value on p p > z z and g g > h, the colour zeros, widths, refusals).

Engine defects found by the M-SM campaign (package ms-validate, m-sm PLAN MS-VALIDATE, 2026-10-30; docs/performance_reports/loop/data/msm-findings.json F1, F2, F9). (F1) A schedule-B step’s rank is its largest source storage plus its largest content degree, which can exceed every single ring’s summed degree (trie.rank) where a trie node joins rings of degree-0 and degree-1 vertices (Higgs, Goldstone, W and Z rings: h h > h h, u u~ > z h, w+ w- > w+ w- [virt=QED]); plan_export._Exporter.family writes the family rank as the largest of both, so the loader admits the steps (a family whose steps stay within the trie rank is written as before; a raised family is reduced at the higher rank, where ms-model’s _trace_groups split by source storage keeps the rank when it applies). (F2) A UFO conditional whose test reads only exact numbers (a parameter fixed at generation against a literal) is decided at lowering and only its taken branch lowered, as Python evaluates it: ‘0 if MB == 0 else …/MB’ at MB = 0 no longer builds 1/0 in the untaken branch, which the evaluators refused as an infinite coefficient (c_UVtxbWp1EW: t t~ > w+ w-, g b > t w-, b b~ members of p p > …); ms-ufo-patch landed the same fix independently (ScalarFunctionLibrary.decided_number, above), which the merge keeps (this package’s decided and its test are dropped). The decided conditionals change the parameter programs of the QCD+QED UFOs, so their binary64 EW values move in the last bits (on the unpatched model the EW self-test’s single pole -0.004058402964848439 -> -0.004058402964848442; Born and finite part unchanged): the shipped EW self-test artifact is regenerated with it and stays the public route’s output. (F9) The exact runtime’s massive Dirac source takes |p| = |pz| on the z axis (symbolica_exact._massive_dirac): the residue of sqrt(pz^2) at 50 digits put an on-axis leg along -z on the branch with pp3 = |p| + pz > 0 and zero transverse momentum, a vanishing spinor (the binary64 carrier’s Python inputs of b b~ > w+ w- with MB = 4.5 gave a Born of 1e-49). Evidence: the campaign rows (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_msm_nightly_*.py), test_loop_scalar_frontend.py::test_conditional_decided_by_its_bindings_forms_only_the_taken_branch, test_source_wavefunction_metadata.py::test_massive_dirac_sources_on_the_beam_axis_do_not_hang_on_rounding.

Counterterm slots (S_slot of the CT recursion, §6.1; WP2.2, integrated at a18b7599). "all", "uv" and "ir" evaluate every slot. "none" switches the pole slots off and, in the native CT program, skips the currents that feed only them (WP3.1 item 1). "uv" needs the UV_local pole slots for the counterterms’ UV poles, and "ir" cannot drop them either, because they fix the IR part of the field factors. So the switch is has_poles(selection) for every pole slot (poles.has_poles): _PointEvaluation passes it to the CT program, which sets the slot switches with CountertermRecursion.parameter_values(poles=has_poles(selection)) (a bool derived from the selection, not a selection; ct_closure.py, assemble.py); the site closure of the slice binds the counterterm couplings at every ε power except in "none" the same way.

Masters and caches. In every mode the fast engine’s per-batch cache holds the combined masters of its never-switched provider. NinjaRS refuses a UV- or IR-selecting provider in the fast engine, and MasterCache and ProfiledMasters forward that capability (requires_scaleless_bubbles). The adapter itself refuses a master selection with the fast engine. The generic engine’s selection (ReduceOptions::masters, binding master_poles) applies to its uncached SymbolicaMasters and is the oracle and cost reference below.

Carriers and estimates. The residue is computed in the lane’s carrier (binary64, DoubleFloat, MPFR), and in the reduction check’s frame (rescaled frames scale it back like the integral). In MPFR it first lifts its inputs to the engine’s working precision (BucketEngine::precision). An evaluator’s exact coefficients and masses can carry a low binary precision under Symbolica’s loose tracking, and an MPFR product rounds to the smaller precision of its factors. Without the lift, the native MPFR residues at a rotated g g > g g point kept 2–3 significant bits: bare UV 53.27 at 32 digits and 49.88 at 50 digits, against 43.22. The split-mode rotation estimate in MPFR found it (test_split_estimates_in_the_extended_carriers), and a unit test with 2-bit exact inputs covers it (v2_poles.rs). Binary64 and DoubleFloat inputs are borrowed unchanged. Stability estimates are formed on the selected coefficients: the reduction check compares the selected lane values of both frames, and rotations re-evaluate the mode.

In "uv" the reduction check is blind to numerator errors; bracket "uv" with a rotation. The selected single pole is the bare loop’s UV residue, an exact functional of each lane’s numerator coefficients, shifts and masses that does not depend on the reduction frame. The reduction-direction check (reversed or rescaled) re-reduces the same coefficients, so for this coefficient it sees only the residue’s own rounding, not an error of the coefficients themselves (tree rows, dressing, kernel constants). Measured at u u~ > d d~ g (first point of tests/fixtures/loop/required/uux_ddxg.json, binary64, one rotation and the reduction check, true error against DoubleFloat per sector and coefficient): the reduction check alone underestimates the "uv" single pole’s error 7.7× (rescaled 3.9×; 1.4× at the second point), while it brackets "all" and "ir", whose poles contain the reduced masters (error/E ≤ 0.15). A rotation re-evaluates the numerators and brackets every mode there (error/E ≤ 0.17 in "uv", ≤ 0.07 in "ir", alone or with the reduction check). So a "uv" estimate needs at least one rotation check; with the reduction check alone it is a lower bound of the residue’s rounding only. tests/unit/test_loop_v2_poles.py::test_a_rotation_brackets_the_split_poles_in_binary64 checks that the rotation’s estimate alone and the combined one bound the true error of every coefficient and sector at that point, in "uv" and "ir", with no margin; the reduction subset alone fails it in "uv". Flooring the "uv" single-pole estimate by the lanes’ single-pole reduction budget, so that the reduction check alone brackets it, is open (WP2.10).

Cost (tools/loop_v2_poles_cost.py; ms per point, complete native evaluation, reduction in parentheses). Setup: binary64, schedule B, one thread pinned to an idle core, 16 lanes, 16 exactly light-like rational points, random block rows, Born components and kernel constants. Seven legs (gg→ggggg, uu~→ggggg; §0.1 targets) were not measured. From five to six legs the companion build grew 16× and the slice generation 12×. If the same growth held, an estimate for WP3.1 planning (not a measurement) would be about 15 min of companion build at gg→ggggg, 15–20 % of the generation, plus a few minutes of export. The companion’s quartic partner positions take every split of the other legs. Decision (coordinator, DECISIONS 2026-10-23, under the user’s relaxed generation budget): the companion is kept as built, always generated and stored, so that one artifact serves every mode; its evaluation cost falls only on uv/ir. Folding it into the main plan, which would share seeds and factors (open, below), remains the optimisation if WP3.1’s seven-leg generation measures the share as too large; a generation option without the companion (artifacts refusing uv/ir) was not chosen.

  • "all" and "none" are unchanged: same fast engine and same plan, and the companion is never run.

  • The UV residue column costs less than this host’s noise: 0.1–0.2 ms/pt at five legs on a quieter host (build 0af1e5d3). This is after the monomial tables are built once per bucket; built per lane they cost +0.9 ms/pt at gg→ggg.

  • The companion dominates the uv/ir overhead: 31 ms/pt for its 6 families at gg→gggg, against 65 ms for 7 families before massless tadpoles were dropped. Its seeds, factors and dressing are repeated outside the main plan. Folding it into the main plan v4 (families flagged and skipped unless split) would share seeds and factors; that is an open optimisation, measured here before it is done.

  • The upstream route, NinjaRS’s generic engine with UV- or IR-selected masters, costs 9–12× the fast engine’s reduction and 2.5–3.5× its complete evaluation (table; gg→gggg 467 against 51 ms/pt of reduction). It returns one selection per reduction, so ir (which needs the combined poles for the field split) would also need the fast run. It would still need the companion, and its binary64 finite part is not the fast engine’s bit for bit. It is therefore the oracle of the residue, not the production path.

  • Upstream extension (brief trigger: generic engine much slower). The fast route needs the UV residue of every lane next to the fast engine’s combined poles. That residue is master-integral algebra, so it is proposed to NinjaRS as ninjars::fast::tensor_uv (TensorUvResidues, tensor_uv_residue; any Symbolica float carrier). Branch pyamplicol/fast-tensor-uv-residue, commits 40dca4c and 68945a3 (the multiprecision input lift, as in the local copy) on main 41a4c00, in the local clone workspace/tmp/poles-uvir/upstream/ninjars. Both are also kept as workspace/reports/engine-v2/ninjars-fast-tensor-uv-residue-68945a3.patch (git am onto 41a4c00), with the passing test logs ninjars-fast-tensor-uv-residue-40dca4c-tests.log and -68945a3-tests.log: tensor_uv_residue 2/2 and fast::tensor_uv 4/4, then 5/5. It is not pushed: pushing it or opening the PR waits for the coordinator’s go, and NinjaRS main is not touched. Its minimal reproducer crates/ninjars-symbolica/tests/tensor_uv_residue.rs shows that the fast engine’s combined poles can be split without selected masters. It checks the functional against the generic engine with PoleSelection::UV on tadpoles, bubbles (massive and scaleless light-like), a triangle and boxes (massless and massive) with dense integer numerators, and checks that finite shapes have no residue. The README section on separate UV and IR poles states the split IR = combined − UV, which includes the dropped scaleless bubbles. Merged as NinjaRS #7; the mf-symbolica re-pin deleted the interim local copy runtime/v2_poles.rs.

Validation (one point per process; tests/unit/test_loop_v2_poles.py, rust/loop-reduction/tests/runtime_v2_reduce.rs):

  • "all" is bitwise the result before the re-pin. Checked on g g > g g, u u~ > d d~ g and u u~ > t t~: Python path, native binary64 and DoubleFloat, finite only, and the re-test estimates. After merging the slice tips 42c6117d (observables) and 45875b87 (artifact-api), and with the public wiring and the observable-column split, "all" is again bitwise each tip’s result with its own native (same three processes; plus g g > g g observable outputs: native inclusive, dipole and directed columns, the Python path’s, and finite-only helicity-resolved outputs).

  • The finite parts are identical in all four modes, in binary64 and DoubleFloat (g g > g g, g g > t t~) and with MPFR at 32 digits (g g > g g; test_finite_parts_are_identical_in_every_mode).

  • UV + IR parts give the combined poles of every component, to 10⁻¹². The double pole is IR. The renormalised virtual’s UV part vanishes, and its IR poles (the "ir" values) are those of "all", also at LC and NLC and for correlated, directed and resolved outputs. The "uv" values are the bare loop’s UV poles, and the counterterms’ UV poles cancel them. For a model without pole regulators these identities hold by construction of the field UV part, and the three items below are the independent evidence; with them (MS-POLES, “Models with pole regulators” above) the UV cancellation is itself a test.

  • "ir" equals Catani’s operator on g g > g g and u u~ > g g g (massless) and on g g > t t~ and u u~ > t t~ (massive, stable top), to 10⁻¹⁰. The massive operator and the virtual reproduce the provider poles of g g > t t~ (MadLoop, Recola, OpenLoops) to 2·10⁻¹⁵.

  • −("uv" values + uv_local) = −(bare_UV + uv_local) equals Σ_legs Z_i^UV·Born (Feynman gauge, textbook constants) on g g > g g, u u~ > g g g, u u~ > u u~, Drell-Yan (photon vertex, no δg_s), g g > t t~ and u u~ > t t~, to 10⁻¹⁰ (observed ≤ 4·10⁻¹⁵ by the evidence audit, also on u u~ > d d~ g and u u~ > u u~ g). In units of (α_s/4π)·Born, bare_UV is 10 (g g > g g), 58/3 (four quarks) and 8/3 (Drell-Yan).

  • The residue equals the generic engine’s UV-selected reduction lane by lane: binary64 to 10⁻¹⁰ on synthetic lanes and 3·10⁻¹⁴ on g g > g g, DoubleFloat to 10⁻²⁶.

  • The Python reference path equals the native executor in split mode. The stability estimates exist in every mode and carrier (binary64; "uv" and "ir" with a rotation and the rescaled reduction check in DoubleFloat and MPFR at 32 digits).

  • A relocated copy of an artifact gives bitwise the original’s "uv" and "ir" values and pole parts (the stored companion plan, §0.2; test_artifacts_hold_no_host_paths_and_load_relocated).

Found on the way (pre-existing, not a pole-selection defect): at massive external legs the native executor’s family integrals differed from the reference path’s (g g > t t~, top width 0: native double pole −0.0666 against −0.1133; the reference path equals MadLoop to 2·10⁻¹⁵). The slice’s mass-flipped kernel copies (reference_executor.mass_flips, WP2.6) fixed it: after merging 45875b87 the native executor equals the reference path at g g > t t~ in "all" and "ir" (test_native_executor_at_massive_external_legs), and the massive processes of these tests now run natively (binary64, DoubleFloat). Catani’s operator takes the legs’ masses from the model’s runtime values (a symbolic mass bound to 0 is massless), not from p² of the given momenta. Rounded inputs give a massless leg a p² of ±10⁻¹⁷ (the post-build validation’s points) or O(10⁻¹¹) (decimal momenta of a 500 GeV point), which the massive branches read as a mass: the log of a negative argument, or v = 1 and log 0. With MB symbolic and bound to 0 that made "all" and "ir" raise at g g > b b~ (audit finding). It is fixed and tested by test_catani_takes_the_masses_from_the_model and test_symbolic_mass_bound_to_zero_at_rounded_momenta. Since the CT recursion became the default CT route (WP2.2, merged at a18b7599), the latter generates with counterterms="sites": the recursion’s lowered couplings refuse a symbolic mass bound to 0. The latter is natively and on the Python path equal to Catani’s prediction, and natively bitwise equal to the slice tip 45875b87 in "all". ρ² is computed as m_j²m_k²/(p_j·p_k)² / (1+v)², so 1 − v does not cancel at small masses. Where the operator makes no prediction (a vanishing invariant, a massive pair at or below threshold, a coloured leg whose mass is not a runtime parameter), ir_poles is None rather than an error. A top width in the loop propagators (complex mass, no CMS counterterms: WP3.2) also moves the single pole of g g > t t~ by 10⁻³ relative to Catani’s, so the IR-pole prediction is made only for stable coloured legs.

Public settings (WP2.6 surface, §12.2). PoleSelection has ALL, NONE, UV, IR; TOML evaluation.poles, CLI --poles and the API poles= take any of them, a runtime option of one artifact. V2VirtualRuntime.evaluate passes the mode to NativeExecutor.evaluate (the reducer’s Poles::Split and the companion plan in uv/ir):

  • VirtualEvaluation.values holds the selection (finite part bitwise that of "all"; "uv": the bare loop’s UV poles, the double pole exactly zero, equal to pole_part("uv", "bare")’s poles; "ir": the renormalised virtual’s IR poles, the poles of "all" to rounding);

  • VirtualEvaluation.pole_parts[point] (VirtualPoleParts, None for failed points and under all/none) holds both origins for the components virtual, bare, uv, r2, uv_local, uv_external_fields (PointResult.pole_origins); pole_part(origin, component) reads one as [point][sector] Laurent triples; for_order keeps them; the CLI prints them as a table (human output) or pole_parts (JSON);

  • stability estimates are formed on the selected coefficients (the "uv" double pole is exactly zero and so is its estimate, 0.0; relative is the whole-sector bound); in "uv" the reduction check alone does not see numerator errors, so a rotation check is needed to bracket the selected single pole (Carriers and estimates); tested in binary64 (a rotation brackets "uv" and "ir" against DoubleFloat), DoubleFloat and MPFR;

  • the artifact stores the companion plan (§12.1), so loading needs no extra generation for uv/ir; an artifact written before the split (poles declared ["all", "none"]) is refused at admission and load with a regeneration message (AGENTS.md: no backward compatibility; tested by rewriting a current artifact’s declaration);

  • correlated and resolved outputs (V2ObservablesRuntime, observables.NativeObservables and the Python path) take all four. Their columns also run on the certified-scaleless companion: ObservableSlice.scaleless() is the same observables on the companion slice (at LC/NLC with directed histories rebuilt unpruned and pruned for them, as of prunes the slice), and ColumnPlan.scaleless() its column plan, which numbers its lanes as the main plan does (checked). The assembly (observables._Assembly.result) splits every output’s poles per column with poles.split_sector: the UV finiteness of the renormalised amplitude holds for every linear functional of it, so the field-factor rule applies per column. ResolvedVirtualEvaluation.pole_parts and .total() (summed parts) follow; _sum_results sums the origins. Checked: native = Python (10⁻¹¹), UV + IR = all and finite parts bitwise for the inclusive, a dipole and a directed history at full colour and a directed history at LC; resolved sums = inclusive split (tests/unit/test_loop_v2_poles.py, test_loop_v2_artifact.py).

The slice-level option stays LoopSlice.evaluate(poles=...) and NativeExecutor.evaluate(poles=...), with one spelling: a PoleSelection or its value (poles.pole_mode; a bool is refused), and the binding’s reducer option is "all", "none" or "split". The SDKs take the same four selections for plan v4 artifacts (rusticol_virtual_set_poles, §12.1 SDK); plan v1-v3 handles take “all” only.

13.3 Deleted (MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE, 2026-10-29)¶

The user ruled (2026-10-28 ~16:10, M-QCD Q3) that v2 is the only one-loop engine and the legacy per-diagram engine is removed now, not after gate R3. Package MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE did so; the table below is the original plan (line ranges [V-s contracts §5], now gone). What was removed, decided by a def-level static reachability graph from the production entry points, loops/v2, the retained tests and tools: LoopEngine/loop.engine (refused with the reason in TOML, overrides and CLI), the legacy branches of loop_service (graph plan, compile, flavour transport, directed preparation and validation), LoopProcessArtifact/LoopExecutionMetadata, runtime.virtual.VirtualRuntimeBackend, 37 modules under loops/ and the legacy names of the shared ones (CT matching in counterterms, PreparedLoopRequestModel.compile and the primitive certificates in compiler, scale bindings, field-CT matching), the PyO3 legacy runtime (NativeLoopProgram, PortableLoopPlan, NativeVirtualRuntime, CoefficientPlan, DualBornWeights, …), the loop crate’s VirtualRuntime, physical backend, schedule, dual weights and state batches, the SDK’s plan v1-v3 engine (a v3 artifact is refused typed; resolved/correlated/spin/verified SDK calls refuse with the plan v4 reason) and the core’s plan v3 loader. Kept as test oracles: FeynKit’s diagram catalogue (tools/loop_reference/feynkit_loop_graphs.py, used by O7), the Rust PolynomialPlan (the v2 reducer’s Rust tests), control_models.py; the legacy engine’s values are frozen captures under tests/fixtures/loop/legacy/ (O1, O2 and the captures of the former live comparisons: reduction/, ew_families_*, gg_gg_non_default_parameters, gg_ttx_model_defaults, gg_gg_qcd_qed_sm). All 2→2…2→4 controls through Rust v2 equal O1 and O8 in three carriers. CT recursion = site closure. Observables and public API pass.

E0

Before any EW timing work (WP3.4), the v2 generator counts families per mass assignment, skeletons, trie nodes, buckets and NinjaRS reductions for gg→tt̄e⁻e⁺g (EW), with uu~→e⁻e⁺ggg (EW) as a control. The G1-calibrated prediction must be within the gate (≤ 1.24 s) with ×2 headroom; otherwise EW-specific work (species sharing by mass, M for EW classes) is scheduled first.

R3

Required set: ≥ 2 providers per process within their mutual agreement; O9 per point; re-test and rescue rates reported; MASTER_PLAN §5.8 speed gates against production-mode providers (protocol columns also reported).

D

Legacy deletion.

16. Implementation plan¶

Sizes are in agent-days: S ≤ 3, M 4–8, L 9–18. Every work package owns its files exclusively; shared files are split by function as stated. Dependencies on the assessment’s no-regret packages (test harness WP01, release builds WP02, massive-quark CT admission WP08, R6/R7) are external.
