      • Generation does not depend on the process history (v2 tree stages and loop kernel records):

        • Cause. Symbolica numbers symbols in creation order and sorts the terms of a sum by the bytes of their packed ids (AtomView::cmp_terms compares get_term_cmp_slice; ids are packed little-endian in 1, 2 or 4 bytes). The normal form of a tree stage, and the evaluator built from it, therefore depended on the absolute ids of its slot and parameter symbols, i.e. on every symbol created before it in the interpreter (the model compile, earlier generations), and so did the binary64 rounding of TreeRows (350 of 866 rows of u u~ > g g g differed in the last bits between histories). The loop kernel records had the same cause (next items); counterterm scalars and model values were identical across the measured histories. A list of expected binary64 misses then held only in the process history it was measured in. Minimal reproducer (workspace/tmp/observables/determinism/repro/repro.py): create N unrelated symbols, then a, b, c; E("a + b + c") normalises as a+b+c for N = 0 and as c+a+b for N = 141 (this build defines 369 symbols at start, so a, b, c get ids 510, 511, 512, packed as FE 01, FF 01, 00 02).

        • Mechanism (assemble._canonical_stage). Each stage is renamed onto canonical symbols allocated in whole blocks of 2^16 whose first id is a multiple of 2^16 (padding symbols fill the gap, about 0.2 s per block), so canonical symbol k sorts by k’s own bytes in every process. A positional renaming onto consecutive ids would not suffice: ids that straddle a byte boundary reorder. The stage inputs are positional (ParamBuilder.add_parameter_list), so input k becomes canonical symbol k by swapping the namespace in the id-independent canonical string and parsing it back, linear in the stage’s size (0.6 s for u u~ > g g g, 3.7 s for g g > g g g’s stages of up to 12 MB). Stages that retain model functions (above their inlining size; no tested process has one) take the general path: one replace_multiple renames the symbols, then a second the function heads, because a replacement does not descend into a call whose head it replaced. Function heads that carry Symbolica attributes keep their ids (none in the current models; WP3.1’s deterministic generator owns that case, open list).

        • Loop kernel records (reference_executor.ExactKernel, _term_order). A kernel output is read term by term from expand() of the catalogue’s exact expression, whose term order follows the ids of the kernel’s input and parameter symbols; both executors sum the terms in record order, and the plan numbers the kernel constants in order of first use. The records therefore moved with the history too: after 250 unrelated symbols 685 of the 1594 exported kernel outputs of u u~ > g g g changed (term order in 517, constant numbering in the rest), and 6 of its 19 binary64 totals moved by up to 7.4e-13 relative; u u~ > u u~’s changed after 77 symbols (measured after 0, 77, 250, 300, 1000 and 3000 unrelated symbols on the legacy controls g g > g g, u u~ > d d~ g, u u~ > u u~, u u~ > u u~ g, u u~ > g g g and u u~ > t t~). Each output’s terms are now sorted by (monomial, constant key), both built from exact numbers, parameter names and Symbolica’s canonical strings only, so the records, the constant numbering and the binary64 sums are independent of the ids (the term sets were already equal across histories). In a process that loads the compiled model and generates one control first, the canonical records equal the former ones for the first five controls (input symbols are created in position order) and differ for u u~ > t t~; in the binary64 O1 census processes (below) 377 of the 860 values moved in the last bits, with unchanged statistics but for two more four-leg resolved rows above E = 1e-12.

        • Guards. Each canonical block is checked when it is created (_check_canonical_block): a sum of probe symbols at offsets 0, 1, 255, 256, 257, 511, 65280 and 65535 must normalise in the order of the offsets’ bytes, which every misalignment by 1 to 2^16 − 1 ids breaks (checked for all of them), so a wrong id assumption or a change of Symbolica’s term order raises instead of silently restoring history dependence. Tests: test_canonical_stages_do_not_depend_on_the_process_history and test_misaligned_canonical_blocks_are_refused (fast tier: both renaming paths on a synthetic 400-input stage, with and without a retained model function, after 0 and 300 unrelated symbols: equal normal forms and binary64 evaluator bits, while the raw stages’ normal forms differ), and test_generation_does_not_depend_on_the_process_history (three fresh interpreters, after 0, 250 and 300 unrelated symbols: identical exported plan programs, kernel records included, identical kernel constants and bitwise identical binary64 totals of u u~ > g g g, while the probe’s kernel records in Symbolica’s own order still differ after 250; without the canonical stages the totals gave three different results after 0, 77 and 300, without the canonical kernel order they differed after 250).

        • Stability estimates do not depend on PYTHONHASHSEED: the observables and the inclusive rotation budgets (assemble.rotation_budget) sum their lanes in insertion order (before, in a set union’s order, 24 of 63 binary64 estimates of g g > g g and d d~ > g g LC at their first legacy point, directed, spin and inclusive, both executors, differed in the last ulp between seeds 1 and 2; none now).

        • Evidence. u u~ > g g g generated alone (model loaded or compiled in the process), after d d~ > g g, and after g g > g g, d d~ > g g and u u~ > d d~ gives bitwise identical tree rows and binary64 T12 (native and Python) on both renaming paths. Binary64 bits of v2 evaluations moved once with the canonical stages; accuracy did not (true binary64 errors of the 16 slice points against 200 bits: geometric mean 8.5e-15 with the raw stages in one process history, 9.3e-15 canonical; only u u~ > u u~ g’s values change, two up and one down; its fresh point gives 3.21e-13, and 1.59e-13 to 3.21e-13 with the raw stages, by history).

On the slice’s raw stages the strict bracket failed after 77, 141, 300 and 3000 unrelated symbols (3.12–3.21e-13 against 3.05–3.11e-13) and passed after 0 and 1000 (2.74e-13 against 3.06e-13, 1.59e-13 against 3.40e-13): it passed in the suite only through the suite’s process history.       • O10, what it shows (gauge invariance, UV + R2 completeness). The Ward interference vanishes as a complex number; an inclusive output projects it to its real part, so the test runs c = 1 and c = i (ward=(j, c)). With c = 1 alone the test would see only that real projection, in which R2 and UV can appear to vanish on the QCD controls. Measured at the test point (200 bits, Python): on u u~ > g g g the bare interference for c = i is 3.3 to 20 times the physical scale (by leg and Laurent coefficient) and the R2 part cancels it to 1e-50 (c = 1 + 2i: the same picture), so the bare amplitude alone is not gauge invariant and R2 restores the identity; the test asserts R2 above the physical scale there, so a missing or wrong R2 fails it. On g g > g g R2 vanishes for every gauge vector (exactly zero, c = 1, i, 1 + 2i). The UV parts (uv_local, external fields) are built on the Ward-sourced trees and vanish with the tree Ward identity (below 1e-77 of the physical scale at 200 bits, 1e-14 in binary64); the test holds each to the Ward bound on its own, so a UV part read with the physical source fails it. Non-gauge control (ward=(j, v), a literal complex vector on the loop side; binary64, both executors): the virtual is of order of the physical scale and R2, uv_local and the fields are each above 1e-2 of it (measured 0.1 to 0.7), so every part sees the loop-side source. g g > g g family lanes vanish one by one; u u~ > g g g lanes cancel across families (their absolute sum is 1.2e3 to 2.7e3 times the physical scale); binary64 leaves up to 3.5e-10 of the physical scale (Python, leg 5, c = 1), within the bound.

A compile of loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu after a tree evaluation wrote V_35’s colour as f(c1,c2,c3), a cold one f(c2,c3,c1), with the index bindings, LC transition/closure proof digests and oriented-kernel colour expressions derived from it; the kernels’ Horner forms (collect_factors, collect_horner) followed the symbol order; Spenso contracts a tensor network in an order that follows the ids, so scalar_gravity’s three-graviton kernels came out in other (equal) nestings when the index symbols had been created in another order; and ufo_model_loader evaluated internal parameters and couplings in binary64 in the history’s order (loop_sm’s yb one ulp apart). Mechanism (_internal/physics/canonical_order, the general form of assemble._canonical_stage’s pool): CanonicalRenaming renames an expression’s symbols, in the natural order of their canonical names, onto canonical symbols from 2^16-aligned blocks (a second block of Spenso tensor heads, tagged spenso::tensor, shares the renaming’s index k, so the two never tie); canonical_plain prints colour and Lorentz records (models/tensors.py), canonical_apply runs the kernel pipeline (compiler_kernels._canonicalize_oriented_kernel_component), compiler_kernels._execute_dense_network runs every model-compiler network (oriented kernels, contact partials and finals, contact trees direct and staged, custom propagators; their tensors collected in DenseTensors) on canonical symbols, and loading._canonical_loader_values re-evaluates the loader’s internal parameters and couplings with its own function on canonical symbols. The compiled-model payload (CompiledModel.to_dict: cache file, an artifact’s compiled-model member and model digest, the prepared bundle’s compiled-model digest) no longer carries the wall-clock conversion_seconds and phase_timings; the compile that measured them keeps them on its object, a loaded model has none. Evidence (workspace/tmp/model-determinism/): loop_sm, loop_qcd_qed_sm, loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu, MG5 sm, the bundled sm, scalars and scalar_gravity UFOs, the massive-muon Gmu variant and the built-in SM, each compiled cold and after ten histories (a second cold process, 100 and 65,300 unrelated symbols, a tree evaluation, a v2 loop generation, index symbols created in reverse, another model’s compile plus 65,300 symbols plus reversed indices, a compile into another cache in the same process, 1 and 32 threads): byte-identical cache files in all 90 comparisons; g g > g g and u u~ > d d~ g (LC and FC) cold in three histories, with 16 threads and warm: identical plans, native members (but parameters.symjit, SymJIT’s random tag) and cache files, bitwise-equal FC values, all equal to the base 18ed6674’s plans, members and values; S1/S4/S5/S8 of g g > t t~, u u~ > d d~ g, g u > w+ d and g g > g g unchanged. Bytes that moved against the base, once: the colour and Lorentz record strings and what derives from them, 9 Z f f̄ kernels’ Horner forms, and binary64 parameter/coupling values that the base rounded in its history’s order (loop_sm 3 values, 1 ulp; loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu 76 values, up to 8 ulp; EW values move in their last bits accordingly). Cost: about 0.45 s and 170 MB (Symbolica symbol table) once per process for the two blocks; a cold loop_sm compile 3.1 → 4.2 s, u u~ > d d~ g generation with its model and CT compiles 25.0 → 29.3 s (both pinned, cold cache). Tests: tests/unit/test_model_determinism.py (two fresh interpreters compile the bundled sm UFO cold and after a perturbing history: byte-identical cache files; a three-graviton network summand whose Spenso network differs with the index creation order while _execute_dense_network’s does not; the renaming’s round trip; misaligned blocks refused). Open: loops/v2/catalogue.py runs its loop-kernel networks on the original symbols (spin-2 loop species only would show it); assemble keeps its own pool (the shared one would save a block per generation process; assemble’s owner); attributed heads other than tensor heads keep their ids (none in current models); prepared model bundles (.pyamplicol-model) were not measured.

Validation is opt-in; at 2->5 the binary64 reference is not measured, and binary64 errors there reach the 1e-9 cap (the onshell-consistency requirements audit reads 2.9e-10 to 5.6e-9 maximal errors from the G1 2->5 records), so a 2->5 validation needs a relative_tolerance that binary64 resolves (the cap is max(tolerance, 1e-9)).       • coupling orders: the service reads the Born amplitude orders from the Born DAG before any loop generation (artifact.born_amplitude_orders, compiled as build_tree_blocks compiles the slice’s Born) and derives one exact loop order per Born amplitude order and correction (loop_service.v2_loop_orders), passed to the slice as a sequence; a correction the source model does not expand perturbatively is refused as the legacy graph generator refuses it (“requested corrections require declared NLO model support”; loop_sm declares QCD only — the slice would otherwise admit no QED loop species and return a vanishing QED correction).       • widths: v2 virtuals are real on-shell (loop propagators carry no width; the model counterterms renormalise the real mass). A coloured particle that a tree current propagates with a width other than a compile-time or fixed zero (the t-channel top of g g → t t̄ at loop_sm’s WT = 1.4915) mixed two schemes: the Born moved by 1.5e-6–3.7e-6 relative while the single pole over the Born moved by up to 2.7e-3 and the finite part by 2.8 % (the colour-correlated Borns should move at O(Γ²) only), against a legacy engine that ignores every width. Such a request is now refused, by the dry run and before any loop generation on the Born DAG, and after generation on the loop-side tree currents (artifact.require_zero_coloured_widths), naming the fix: fix the width to zero in [loop.preparation] fixed_parameters (the legacy convention). A resonant coloured particle needs the complex-mass scheme (WP3.2). A width that only loop propagators would carry (u u~ → t t̄) does not enter. The runtime refuses unknown parameter names, the scale parameter (mu_r2 sets it) and a value other than the one fixed at generation (before, WT = 1.4915 passed to an artifact generated with WT fixed to zero was silently replaced); other known parameters are accepted even where the process does not use them, as by the legacy engine (e.g. WT or WZ for u u~ → t t̄: bitwise-identical results). Test (test_coloured_widths_in_tree_currents_are_fixed_to_zero): g g → t t̄ refused at the default WT by the dry run and the generation; with WT fixed to zero the public v2 virtual equals the legacy engine evaluated at the model’s default parameters (WT = 1.4915) at the three exact points and scales of the gg→tt̄ provider reference, in binary64 (1e-12) and double-double (1e-24) against legacy in double-double, and at 60 digits (1e-40) nightly (test_coloured_width_fixed_to_zero_equals_legacy_at_sixty_digits); runtime WT ≠ 0, MU_R and unknown names are refused. Currents of all legs but one carry an external momentum and are amputated, so they do not count (u u~ → t t̄ is admitted at the default WT and equals legacy there, as the audit measured). Integrator: WP2.2 (work/v2-ct-recursion, adopted at 09d70e76) selects full tree kernels for coloured widths and model-supplied propagators by its own criterion (blocks.ward_breaking_fields, which does not exist on this branch or the slice); keep one criterion when both are integrated: the public path fixes coloured widths to zero (this refusal), and the full-kernel branch remains for custom propagators. Make DESIGN WP2.2/WP2.6 and docs/user/configuration.md agree.

Measured on the g g → g g correlated record: Born within 4.1e-51 of legacy at 200 digits, virtual 8.1e-31. Nothing is numerically wrong; WP3.1’s native point inputs evaluate the Born in the carrier and make the label exact.

The legacy observables capture (tools/loop_reference/legacy_observables_capture.py) validates with relative 3e-9 / absolute 2e-12, and the non-default-parameter test generates its legacy oracle without post-build validation and evaluates it in double-double. Legacy users of correlated outputs need the looser validation tolerances; the legacy engine is retired by WP3.6, so this is recorded, not fixed.

      • leanness (AGENTS.md): the writer no longer re-reads and re-hashes the staged plan member; a generated process serialises and hashes its plan once (GeneratedProcess, frozen, is what the generation cache keeps; NativeExecutor(plan_json=...) takes its plan JSON at load and at clear()), and a regenerating load digests the compiled model once (generate_process(..., model=...)). The v4 admission, flate2 and read_loop_program_v4_json are behind rusticol-core’s loop-v2 feature; the plan-v4 runtime capability itself is defined in the ungated engine.rs, so rusticol-core alone compiles in every feature configuration (just rust-test’s --no-default-features --features f64-compiled included). Still parsed twice per load: the admission validates the stored plan against the declarations, and the native executor parses the regenerated plan (digest-equal) for each carrier it builds. The second parse disappears with WP3.1, when the admitted program is the executed one (no regeneration).

      • integration of WP2.2 with this branch (loops/v2/assemble.py): the request model preparation is assemble.prepare_request_model (one function, called by LoopSlice.generate and by the dry run; since lit-ewprep it takes the generation’s preparation_cache.PreparationMemo: one preparation per recipe, the program lowered once per model, see the lit-ewprep entry above); ct-recursion’s LoopSlice.generate uses the locals fixed and declaration, which become model.fixed_parameters (bound as _fixed here) and request.colour_declaration.

      • interim (§12.1): loading a v4 process regenerates its slice (≈ generation time: gg→gg 9 s; reused within one interpreter) until WP3.1 stores native point inputs; the SDK evaluates v4 only after WP3.1.

      • proposed for WP3.1 (WP2.6 proposes, the coordinator confirms; WP3.1’s goal and acceptance are not edited here): Goal add “native programs for the per-point inputs of a v4 process (tree recurrence in loop-request mode, Born components, counterterm scalars) stored as further PACBIN members under a new point_inputs value, their SymJIT applications as IR recompiled at load (storage-v4 plane kernels), and the SDK (Rust/C/C++/Fortran) evaluating v4 artifacts”; Accept add “a v4 artifact loads without regenerating its slice and gives bitwise-identical binary64 values after relocation with the same native build; SDK smoke tests on the v2 controls equal the public runtime”.

      • superseded (user ruling 2026-10-28 ~16:10, M-QCD Q3: the legacy engine was removed instead, MQ-LEGACY-REMOVE, §13.3); the former default-switch criteria: (1) R3 passed for QCD (required set against ≥ 2 providers, O9 per point, rescue rates reported, MASTER_PLAN §5.8 speed gates against production-mode providers); (2) every public capability the default serves today runs through v2 or is refused with its reason (EW and mixed orders via WP3.2; aliases); (3) native point inputs (WP3.1), so loading needs no regeneration and the SDK evaluates v4; (4) the whole unit suite green with engine = "v2" as default, legacy-only tests pinned to engine = "legacy".

The native export compiles each stage of the runtime schema in chunks of whole output currents (≤ 2¹⁵ outputs) and saves and releases them one at a time. At gg→ggggg the export peak falls from 13.0 to 7.0 GB at equal time (390 s with generation’s 6.4 min before it) and equal per-point cost (0.79 s of trees and Born, 12.2 s with the bare loop). The process peak falls only from 18.2 to 17.5 GB, because the native tree runtime now sets it: about 5.6 GB at load for 265 MB of saved evaluators, plus 5 GB during the evaluation. The runtime now keeps the saved stages and decodes, casts and drops one at a time per carrier, which lowers the peak to 16.3 GB. What remains is the binary64 stage evaluators (≈ 4.3 GB) and the evaluation (+5 GB). For 8 legs T0 therefore stays near 200 GB [E]; the interaction program (below) replaces it.

      • Native trees as an interaction program (native_trees._interaction_program, loop_v2::trees; the default TREE_LANE). The blocks DAG is evaluated interaction by interaction. In each runtime stage, every interaction adds its exact colour weight times its vertex kernel to its result current; each output slot then copies the sum or applies the propagator kernel. The kernels are the model’s own component expressions (vertex_component_expression on [left, right, p_left, p_right, model], propagator_component_expression on [value, p, model]), one saved exact evaluator per shape (gg→gggg: 4 vertex and 1 propagator kernel; u u~ > d d~ g: 25 and 10). They run batched over the interactions and points that share them, in every carrier, so the program grows with the DAG instead of with T0’s per-output expressions.

  • WP3.1 Rust migration D, native-lowering (branch work/v2-native-lowering; workspace/reports/engine-v2/wp31/RUST-MIGRATION.md §3.D; phase 0 accepted 2026-10-25 ~01:05, phase 1 part 1 here; D3, the lowering in Rust from B’s arena, is next):

    • Plan model, JSON writer and binary member (D2, phase 0). rusticol_core::loop_v2::plan::binary::PlanModel holds a plan v4 in the loader’s file form; PlanModel::json writes json.dumps(program, separators=(",", ":")) byte for byte (keys in the exporter’s order, ensure_ascii escapes; the plan holds no float), PlanModel::binary the columnar member of §12.1 (proposed kind 12), which loop_v2::plan::read_binary reads with a declared, bounded decoded size (no decompression bomb), a derivation bound refusing what the derivations would trust beyond the plan’s tables, fallible probes of the decoded model and of the derivations’ peak, and fallible copies: never a panic or an allocation abort, an error instead.

    • Loader hardening (phase 1). LoopProgramV4::load (the production JSON load of the executor and of load_loop_v2_artifact) goes through the same bound: a fused entry’s q-degree above its content’s is refused before the segment layouts (whose recursive monomial index overflowed the stack), a decimal power of ten of 2^32 or more before numerica’s panic, vertex ids and ranks before the tables they size, and the derivations’ peak must be granted (a probe); the scalar-sized tables (row links, content rows, the vertex table) are reserved fallibly. A JSON is not bounded per byte (it cannot be padded). A read decodes on one thread wherever an allocation can fail before the host’s memory is exhausted (an address-space or data limit, strict overcommit): the parallel decode’s per-thread state (lazily created malloc arenas, rayon’s queues) escapes the probes, and under an RLIMIT_AS with the default pool it aborted on valid members. Elsewhere the chunks’ state is allocated fallibly and a section whose chunks cannot run is decoded again sequentially; a pool that cannot start leaves every read on one thread instead of refusing it. The probe is conservative (§0.2 portability): at g g > g g g g g FC the bound is 6.60 GB and the probe, with its margin, 7.4 GB, against a measured derivation peak of 3.29 GB (peak/bound 0.39-0.66 over the exported plans, tests/loop_v2_plan_derive_bound.rs); a host whose address space for the load lies between the real peak and the probe (an RLIMIT_AS/ulimit -v, common in batch jobs, or RAM plus swap under Linux’s heuristic overcommit, which refuses one allocation beyond it) refuses with an error an artifact it could load before. This grows at 2→6; tightening the bound (or probing the derivations in pieces) is a D3 / phase-1 part 2 item. Cost (rule 8; the build profile matters: the package’s natives are build_loop_native.py’s default, 16 codegen units without LTO, the slice’s natives the shipped codegen, one unit with thin LTO). Same profile (the slice 392d3f4a rebuilt at 16 units without LTO by the evidence audit, V2Executor construction, cores 216-227, 12 rayon threads): the g g > g g g g plan loads in 0.5566-0.5573 s against 0.5485-0.5512 s (+1.0-1.6 %), the u u~ > g g g g plan in 0.1428-0.1433 s against 0.1384-0.1394 s (+2.8-3.5 %). Across profiles (the package’s native against the slice’s thin-LTO one, so the profile’s share is not separated): u u~ > g g g g g FC (QED = 0, 69.2 MB, best of 3, alternating rounds) 2.575-2.592 s against 2.431-2.462 s (+5-6 %; at six legs the cross-profile cost is +3-4 % and +7 % where the same profile gives +1.0-1.6 % and +2.8-3.5 %), of which the derivation bound is 0.09 s (the probe is one mmap/munmap; a fixed glibc mmap threshold changes neither side, so the probe’s large free does not slow the derivations); g g > g g g g g FC 12.21-12.36 s against 12.22-12.24 s (the bound 0.10 s of it). No gate is affected; the load’s own cut is the derive (Open, below).

    • D1, leaf weights (conventions.LeafWeights; Python, output-identical). Generation asks eps_s for every reading (F and B: the refusal loop) and the export for every F leaf; fermion_sign now computes it once per distinct contents tuple (_fermion_sign, the full rule unchanged; a refusal is raised again at every call) and takes a fast path for a tuple without a fermion line (per content, once: no fermion loop line, no fermion block, no block holding a coloured fermion end; the sign of a closed ghost loop or +1). The fast path copies the inputs of the full rule (_content_kind: fermion loop lines, fermion blocks, blocks holding a coloured fermion end): any new input of _line_parity or _require_mass_free_couplings (WP3.2 EWI-5, e.g. Koszul signs of colour-singlet lines through the loop) must make _content_kind fermionic too, and check_leaf_weights of the package’s test file is the guard (both methods’ docstrings say so). Every reading’s sign and every leaf weight equal the full rule on the controls (main and companion readings, refusals included) and at seven legs. Measured (sites form, cores 216-227, the two loops replayed on the generated slice): g g > g g g g g 1,620,990 readings, 1,333,047 distinct tuples, 1,295,550 readings on the fast path, 285,840 signs kept; refusal loop 33.3 → 8.6 s, the export’s weight calls 19.4 → 7.6 s, 36.5 s saved. u u~ > g g g g g (QED = 0): 207,540 readings, no fast path (the quark line runs through every loop); 5.5 → 5.1 s and 3.1 → 0.3 s, 3.2 s saved.

    • D2’ switch (plan_export.ExportedPlan). ExportedPlan.json() is written by the native model, read from the exporter’s Python records (V2PlanModel.from_program: a serde deserializer over the Python objects that accepts only records the writer writes back as json.dumps writes them, i.e. the loader’s types, every record’s keys in the writer’s order (the loader’s file form declares its fields in that order), every key the writer always writes present (an absent option as None, which it writes as null) and no None under a key the writer omits when absent (a step’s rows, an edge’s links, the plan’s column_rows and column_weights, the only keys a record may lack; binary::OMITTED_WHEN_ABSENT, qualified by record), an error naming the record otherwise, so an accepted program’s native JSON is json.dumps’s byte for byte and an exporter change of key order or of an optional key’s presence fails loudly instead of being normalised; the writer (json::write), the member’s traversal (visit_plan) and the derivation bound (derive::bound) destructure the file form without .., so a field added to the loader does not compile until all three carry it), and ExportedPlan.binary() is its member; native_lowering.NATIVE_JSON (default on) switches the JSON back to ExportedPlan.python_json(), the oracle. The switch is inside ExportedPlan, so the main plan, the companion’s plan and the observables’ column plans take it alike; byte identity holds on every control of tests/unit/test_loop_v2_native_lowering.py for all three (schedules B, F and M, written and derived row links, mass flips, helicity-resolved columns, the stored form with the tree program, electroweak and six-leg controls).       • Loop species from the families (B2). The kernel catalogue takes the species the families route (assemble._family_loop_species: the cut species and loop lines of the admitted and certified-scaleless families’ routings, with the members of merged closed-loop flavour classes), not the loop particles of the root counterterm rules (none at a lepton leg 1; NLOCT UV rules declare none); species no family routes get no kernels (a unitary-gauge W with joint corrections on g g > g g).       • Colour-singlet line at the root (B4-root). History (WP3.2 EWI-1, superseded by EWI-5): a lepton line closing at the root vertex took the tree engine’s merge sign of its two ends (FermionOrderingSign.tree_sign, then SiteClosure._singlet_root_sign), and a process with more than one colour-singlet fermion line (more than two lepton legs) was refused before any tree was built, wherever its lines sat (require_one_singlet_line, FermionSignError; also in SiteClosure): the tree engine signs every merge of currents holding singlet fermions with their Koszul sign, which the blocks’ rows carry inside a block but neither the root closure nor the loops’ leaf weights then applied between blocks. With interleaved lines (uū→e⁻μ⁻e⁺μ⁺: supports {3, 5} and {4, 6}, sign −1) the Born closure was 0.53 times the tree runtime’s amplitude (uū→e⁻e⁻e⁺e⁺: 0.34), and so were the Born and the virtual, silently, on 8b52179b too; the earlier check refused only singlet lines attached directly at the root. Both helpers and the refusal are gone: the root closure (SiteClosure._root_sign) and the loops’ leaf weights (LeafWeights._line_parity) apply the Koszul signs between blocks with one rule, conventions.colour_singlet_sign (“Koszul signs of colour-singlet fermions”, below). The Born closure’s currents enter the loop-aware reachability (assemble._born_block_requests; within the Born’s own orders when they exceed the loop orders’ cap, an order the request leaves open bounded by its largest tree power from the model’s vertices, _tree_order_bounds: n − 2 for renormalisable vertices, a two-point vertex carrying the order refused) and the tree blocks’ order bound takes the Born’s where larger (_block_order_bounds).

The tree engine reads the current of tree particle p on the UFO leg of p; a W vertex has no leg for the tree particles of the families’ (incoming-field) attachments, so the root closure (Born, CT roots) and loop segments read it through the model’s conjugate rule, whose couplings and Lorentz structures are the vertex’s own complex-conjugated with the chiral projectors exchanged (ct_sites.ConjugateVertices, conventions.TreeReading.vertex; the colour stays the vertex’s incoming reading; the conjugate must be unique at the same coupling orders with one colour structure each, and a ghost on such a vertex is refused, by both readings). The counterterm-site oracle (O6) reads its open sites the same way, so the site scalar plan computes the conjugate rules’ couplings (SiteClosure.read_entries); a site term whose coupling the scalar plan does not compute is refused (LoopSlice._terms_of) and the evaluations read the couplings strictly: before, the R2 of every open W site vanished silently on the sites route (ud̄→e⁺ν_e: R2 0 against −3.08·10⁻⁵, 67 % of the virtual’s scale). Reading the vertex’s own couplings on swapped spinor legs (the first attempt) is wrong for complex or chiral couplings: with loop_sm’s Wolfenstein CKM and a massless b, g u > w+ b missed Catani by 59 % and the Born closure of u b~ > e+ ve differed from the tree runtime by the phase V_ub*/V_ub; with the conjugate rule both agree (≤ 4·10⁻¹⁶, a real global sign). (2) Those UFO object libraries lose the Goldstone flag of the G⁻ (Particle.anti() passes it positionally into line), so unitary-gauge trees kept a G⁻ beside the W⁻ (b t̄ → W⁻h, b t̄ → W⁻Z wrong by O(1)); the compiled flags are closed under conjugation (compiler_gauge.close_goldstone_flags).

    • Status, ew-leptons (EWI-5; colour-singlet fermion lines through the loop; test_loop_v2_ew_leptons.py, the ladder of test_loop_v2_ew.py):

      • Koszul signs of colour-singlet fermions (B4 in the loop and at the root). A block row carries the tree engine’s Koszul signs of colour-singlet fermions (generation/fermion_ordering.py): it is the block current’s coefficient of the product of its singlet sources in source order. The loop leaf weights (LeafWeights._line_parity) and the root closure (SiteClosure._root_sign) complete them with one rule, conventions.colour_singlet_sign: the Koszul sign of concatenating the blocks’ singlet supports in the order they are read (loop contents, or the root vertex’s legs), times the merge sign of the open singlet ends each line joins outside the blocks, listed (antiparticle, particle) as the tree engine’s two-fermion merge takes them (the block of incoming field f holds the external end of anti(f), open_end_orientation). Every singlet line is then listed (antiparticle, particle) inside the blocks and through the loop alike, so the Wick sign of every diagram is kept up to one sign per process, which the Born shares. It is the tree engine’s merge_sign composed over the blocks (its identity is tested against an independent inversion count in every block order, and against FermionOrderingSign.tree_sign); no vertex property enters, and no count of lines is assumed: any number of singlet lines, mixed with any number of coloured lines (the colour flow owns their order, the ring-sign rule unchanged). SiteClosure.fermion_ends holds the singlet ends (SINGLET_END), so the D1 fast path of LeafWeights reads every block holding one with the full rule (check_leaf_weights passes on the four-lepton processes). Lifted: ct_sites.require_one_singlet_line and the refusal of a singlet line through the loop; still refused: a line joining a coloured and a singlet end, two ends of one orientation (Majorana-like), vertices with more than one fermion line (four-fermion contacts; the user’s decision 2026-10-26 ~07:55 keeps these and Majorana fermions unsupported). The “loop fermion vertex couples through the mass of the line it emits” refusal blocks no vertex of loop_sm, loop_qcd_qed_sm or loop_qcd_qed_sm_Gmu (default and full restrictions, unitary and ‘t Hooft–Feynman gauge: no vertex coupling depends on the mass of one of its fermion legs; their Yukawas are written through ymX).

      • Counterterm roots on a mixing line’s Goldstone side. A root vertex of the loop model that the request’s tree model does not hold because its coupling vanishes at the restriction (the electron Yukawa [e+ e- G0] at the G_μ default restriction) has no promoted copy in the lowered model and contributes nothing, so CountertermClosure.build skips it instead of refusing, but only when every coupling of its loop-model entries vanishes identically in the lowered model (ct_sites.restricted_to_zero, the one restriction rule since fail-closed-2, which the loop catalogue applies too, “Listed generation refusals”: the source helpers inlined with their exact bodies, internal parameters resolved to the restriction’s external ones, ct_sites.vanishes_identically); any other such root vertex is refused (UnloweredCountertermError, also for a vertex the tree model holds, e.g. a massive lepton or top at leg 1).

      • The tree engine’s reading of colour-singlet loop segments (the Goldstone basis). The tree engine reads every vertex all-outgoing: the current of each outgoing tree particle on that particle’s leg, with its outgoing momentum (generation.runtime_schema: “sum all-outgoing momenta … negate physical incoming momenta first”). The loop segments read fermion legs that way (TreeReading), boson legs by their incoming fields with incoming momenta, and the colour seeds read the incoming colour flows. The tree engine’s value is the segment’s times L(π legs, −p)/L(legs, p) (L the Lorentz structure, π the exchange of each boson leg with its antiparticle’s leg on a vertex closed under conjugation, the identity on one read through its conjugate rule, which takes the antiparticles’ legs already) times the colour tensor’s sign under the transposition of its adjoint generators (conventions.colour_transposition_sign: −1 per f; 1 for d, T between swapped ends, identities and two-index traces; other tensors refused), one rule for every vertex, and the segment kernels carry it (catalogue._CatalogueBuilder.reading_sign; a vertex where either factor is not ±1 is refused, typed LoopKernelCatalogueError). On the SM’s coloured vertices the two factors cancel (the momentum-odd three-gluon vertex against its f; the quark–gluon and four-gluon vertices have neither). It is −1 exactly on Z G⁰ H, W∓ G⁰ G± and W∓ G± H in loop_qcd_qed_sm(_Gmu), loop_sm and MG5’s sm. The first version kept every coloured vertex at 1 on the SM argument; the second genericity audit (G2-M6) showed that silently wrong for a coloured vertex whose colour does not compensate its momenta (a W coupling of a coloured scalar pair, W/Z couplings of scalar leptoquarks, a chromomagnetic dipole). With the one rule such a vertex takes its colour-singlet copy’s sign (test_coloured_segments_take_the_sign_of_their_colour_singlet_copy, a toy extension of the G_μ UFO: W sq̃~ sd̃ as W G H, −1; the gluon’s and photon’s scalar vertices as A G⁻ G⁺, 1; the chromomagnetic dipole as the photon’s, −1; the old rule gave 1 on W sq̃~ sd̃ and the dipole), and every vertex term of loop_sm, loop_qcd_qed_sm, the G_μ UFO in both gauges and HEFT keeps its sign (QCD catalogues and artifacts unchanged). On the vertices closed under conjugation these are the field signs of G⁰ negated (s(G⁰) = −1, s(G⁺)s(G⁻) = 1, all others 1); W∓ G⁰ G± and W∓ G± H, read through their conjugate rules, take the ratio alone and are no field signs (as field signs they would contradict each other). The Goldstone Yukawas’ lone chiral projectors were matched to the tree engine’s readings (EWI-4a, models.tensors; the legacy loop path keeps the textbook readings with the exchanged projectors, which is why it agrees with MadLoop), and blocks, Born and counterterm trees come from them. A ghost vertex has no tree reading (it is read first: the gluon’s ghost vertex is no sign kinematically): it takes the product of the field signs of its other legs, solved over GF(2) from the closed boson vertices of every colour that have a reading sign (_FieldSigns; −1 on the ghost-G⁰ vertices, whose G⁰ blocks come from the tree engine; s(g) = 1 from the three-gluon vertex, so the gluon’s ghost vertex keeps 1), so the ghost lines share the basis. Before it, the loops mixed the textbook basis of these segments with the tree engine’s Goldstone Yukawas and blocks: the Z–G⁰–H triangles on an open fermion line had the opposite sign of legacy and MadLoop (O2 rel 2.0 on exactly those families of e⁻e⁺→μ⁻μ⁺ with massive muons and of e⁻e⁺→tt̄; 41 of the 127 families of e⁺e⁻→tt̄h, the last one a ghost-G⁰ bubble with a G⁰* → tt̄ block), the massive-muon control missed MadLoop’s bare part by 10⁻⁷ and g g > t t~ e- e+ EW missed MadLoop, Recola and OpenLoops by O(1) in the finite part. Independently, ew-epsilon (EWI-7b) found the same reading difference at the counterterm root of the Levi-Civita R2 of a Z with gluons (SiteClosure._reading_sign: (−1)^(momentum degree) times the colour flows’ transposition sign on all-self-conjugate vertices); the two rules are one statement: the colour factor is now one helper, conventions.colour_transposition_sign with conventions.ReadingSignError (accepting the bare UFO strings of the root’s entries and the namespace-qualified ones of compiled vertex terms), which ct_sites imports since ew-epsilon’s integration (its private copy, with the same tensors, signs and refusals, is gone; ct_sites.ReadingSignError is the shared class). One fermion classifier as well (G2-m2): conventions.fermion_end / fermion_ends (colour singlet → SINGLET_END, (anti)triplet → ±3, any other representation a typed FermionSignError) for the external ends, the root sign and the leaf weights, which had classified a sextet or octet fermion block as a singlet at the root, dropped an octet external fermion from the ends and refused it untyped (ValueError) in the leaf weights (unreachable on the slice’s models: the tree engine refuses such fermions too). The analysis: the segment emulation from catalogue kernels equals the textbook Feynman rules for any external spinors, the tree engine’s m⁻m⁺ → Zh equals the textbook only with the G⁰ Yukawa negated (Feynman = unitary), and a VSS probe (V_59 → P(1,2) alone) shows the tree engine feeding the external G⁰’s outgoing momentum.

Its counterterm couplings are not split by loop content (V_UVepemAEW: no label, one coupling of the W, Z and photon loops; R2_eeACp: labelled [e⁻, Z], its photon part inside), so no veto rule over the UFO’s terms can remove the W and Z loops from them; the model-supplied counterterms are the production path, so the fix needs a UFO whose counterterms are split by loop content (the C1 certifier could certify a veto’s UV poles, not the on-shell finite parts). veto-unlabelled-counterterms remains, its owner and follow-up updated; the strict xfail test_qed_poles_of_photon_only_mumu_on_loop_qcd_qed_sm_are_catani remains the refusal’s negative control.

      • The plane check (G2-M4; the relaxed ruling, slice-status DECISIONS 2026-10-26 ~21:10 item 6, user-confirmed 2026-10-27 ~19:20; options (b) and (c) together). loop_v2::trees::compile_plane_application_checked compares each saved evaluator’s binary64 SymJIT plane application with its exact evaluator at two complex rows off the real axis (real parts 0.5 + frac(k/φ), imaginary parts ±(0.25 + 0.5 frac(k/ρ)), one row per half-plane) and at the real points the caller gives (real_points; compile_v2_plane(state, level, compress, real_points)). Off the axis no input-dependent argument sits on a branch cut, so the rows certify the translation (a constant or function read wrongly changes an output at O(1)) whatever the inputs’ order, names and values. The parameter program’s real point is the request’s parameter values (native_trees._request_points: the generation’s fixed values, else the defaults, as batch_parameters binds a batch without a caller’s values), where it certifies the real-axis evaluation: the side of a cut an argument sits on at real masses, and the branches of the predicates. A program reading a branch cut, a power with a slot exponent or a discontinuous predicate (truth, equal, less, less_equal) of its inputs without a real point is refused (engine::real_axis_sensitive_outputs, read through the inlined helper bodies; constants’ branch cuts such as the kernels’ √2 and the continuous exp, sin, cos, abs, conj, real_part, imaginary_part do not count): the tree kernels, whose inputs are complex currents and couplings, hold none. The floor of the comparison is per output (1e-12 of the output’s largest part over the rows), so a small output is not compared against a large one’s size. A refusal stays the listed plane-mismatch (PlaneMismatchError(message, output, row, imaginary, real_axis); row and imaginary None for the missing real point). At other real parameter values the translation adds +0 to each non-constant argument of a cut function (symjit_plane::canonical_cut_row; under round-to-nearest x + 0 = x except −0 + 0 = +0), so the −0 imaginary part that SymJIT’s negation and ±i products give a negated real, where Symbolica’s evaluator has +0, becomes +0, exact arithmetic’s and MadLoop’s side (CM01 with its widths zeroed at run time put the electroweak counterterm couplings’ arguments on their cuts, where the plane had taken the other side: finite part 3.9·10⁻⁵ against MadLoop’s 1.8·10⁻³; M-SM MS-MASTERS, risk 13). The translation keeps the jumps of every conditional (IfElse, Goto, Label), in symjit_plane and in symbolica_helpers._symbolica_instruction_program_repr for the tree adapters’ text route: SymJIT 2.28.3 (siravan/symjit#31, pinned since M-FINAL MF-UP) translates a branch the request’s values do not take as faithfully as the one they take (2.27.3 to 2.28.2 defined a common subexpression at its first occurrence, which could lie inside an untaken branch, so until then the translation dropped the jumps and the Join selected between branches all evaluated; risk 13). An argument real only where some complex-mass widths vanish reads its real projection when they are exactly zero, in every carrier (ct_recursion._RealArguments.zero_width_cases; its exactly zero imaginary part could come out as a residue of either sign otherwise, risk 13). The real points still certify the translation and the predicates’ branches at the request’s values (with pole regulators also with the IR regulator at 0, the split selections’ regulated pass); nothing is checked at run time. The parameter program compiles at level 0, the kernels at -O2. Every probe row also runs in a call of its own, a SIMD block of equal lanes as a batch runs it: a block mixing rows that take other branches is replayed in scalar code, which hid a SymJIT SIMD NaN in CM05’s parameter program. A program failing the check at level ≥ 1 is compiled again at level 0 and kept if that passes; the defect is SymJIT’s AVX times_complex on aliased registers, upstream PR prepared (risk 13).

      • Evidence for the choice. (i) SymJIT gives a negated real a −0 imaginary part where Symbolica’s evaluator gives +0 (its product with the real constant −1; sqrt(-x) at x = 2: −i√2 against +i√2, also through Symbolica’s own JIT, which uses SymJIT); neither is a translation error, so (a), a SymJIT change, would only move one convention, and a real probe placed on a cut refuses a correct translation. The former real probes (0.5 + frac(0.618 (k + 1)), assigned by input index) put sqrt(1 − MW²/MZ²) on its cut whenever the probe of MW exceeded MZ’s, so the verdict depended on the declaration order (loop_sm with MW a card input; G_μ: c_UVepemA1EW, UV_GTTLEW). (ii) With the off-axis rows every kernel and parameter program of g g > t t~ EW, e⁻e⁺ > μ⁻μ⁺, e⁻e⁺ > u ū, g t > t t t~ and u ū > e⁻e⁺ g EW (G_μ) passes, which (c) alone would have accepted; the request’s real point then still refused their counterterm couplings (c_UVepemA1EW ε⁰ imaginary part −2.1469·10⁻³ in the plane against −3.5745·10⁻³ in the exact evaluator, UV_GTTLEW, c_UVuxuA1EW): a bisection of the coefficient found (MZ⁴(−3 + 4(1 − MW²/MZ²)))^(1/2) of the Z’s B0 helpers, a negated real at the card’s masses, i.e. a binary64 value on the other side of the cut than double-double and arbitrary precision and the Python lane (MadLoop’s). The real-axis row is what certifies the binary64 values, so the check keeps it.

      • Counterterm couplings on MadLoop’s side. The native lane’s counterterm and field couplings (the scalar plans’ columns in native_trees._parameter_program, values and diagnostics) take the counterterm lowering’s convention (ct_recursion._RealArguments, §EWI-3: MadLoop’s helpers take +0 for an exactly real argument) in its signed form: every branch-cut argument (of a logarithm, a square root, a fractional power, or a parameter a helper’s body reads through one, cut_parameters) that is manifestly real and not manifestly non-negative (is_nonnegative: non-negative numbers, π, e, even powers of reals, rational powers of non-negatives, their sums and products) reads through the real projection, value unchanged, +0 in every evaluator; arguments manifestly non-negative (QCD’s log(μ²/m²)), not manifestly real, or of a helper parameter its body reads through no branch cut (cond’s values) keep their form, so the QCD and loop_sm programs keep their bytes (test_plans_the_guards_do_not_refuse_keep_their_bytes, all six pins; a first form that also projected every helper argument changed four of them). The Born couplings and the tree model’s derived parameters are off the cut at real masses and unchanged.

      • Oracles. Native = Python inputs on the same exported plan (Born and every component per sector, binary64, in the sector’s virtual): g g > t t~ EW 2.2·10⁻¹⁵, e⁻e⁺ > μ⁻μ⁺ 9.5·10⁻¹⁶, u ū > d d̄ QED 1.7·10⁻¹⁵ (test_electroweak_native_inputs_equal_the_python_inputs; not bitwise: the Python lane forms the trees at the working digits and its couplings at 32 digits); u ū > d d̄ QED through the public API stores point_inputs = "native-v2" and relocates bitwise without a licence (artifact-portability’s check); validate --inputs native on g g > t t~ EW and the e⁻e⁺ > μ⁻μ⁺ control through native inputs (the strict xfails of EWI-4b and EWI-5 flipped); the renamed-model harness’ loop_sm MW-card-input variant takes the native route; every lifted rung of the electroweak ladder exports its native point inputs (the ladder asserts it; g g > t t~ e⁻e⁺ g EW in 379 s), and e⁻e⁺ > u ū, g t > t t t~ (the Goldstone–vector mixings), the massive-muon e⁻e⁺ > μ⁻μ⁺ (G⁰, H and G± on the lepton line) and u ū > e⁻e⁺ g EW give native = Python inputs to 1.1·10⁻¹⁵, 6.0·10⁻¹⁵, 2.2·10⁻¹⁶ and 5.1·10⁻¹⁴ of the virtual (one point each, binary64).

      • External photons (continuation 1). On-shell external photons of electroweak requests take native inputs: the listed refusal external-photon-alpha0 is gone (the α(0) convention in the photons’ sources, “Electroweak guards” above); u u~ > a g and u u~ > a a equal MadLoop natively (6.4·10⁻¹³, 4.4·10⁻¹³) and the Python inputs (1.1·10⁻¹⁵, 3.4·10⁻¹⁵ of the virtual), the photon’s native Ward run (its loop-side vector scaled as its source) vanishes within 8.3·10⁻¹² of the physical scale with the non-gauge control equal to the Python lane’s to 5.4·10⁻¹⁵ (test_external_photon_ward_identity), a missing 1/α(0) is refused by the native binder naming it, and u u~ > a g with QED corrections through the public API stores native-v2 inputs and relocates bitwise (test_loop_v2_ew_native.py).

      • Open. Arguments that are mathematically real but not manifestly so (e.g. a product of complex couplings) and sit on a cut at the card would still be refused at the real point (none on the controls); the plane’s complex products contract with FMA, so such an argument can carry a rounding-noise imaginary part there.

16.3 First vertical slice (gate S1)¶

Scope.

  • gg→gg in FC and LC with mb = 0 as in the provider references: 24 families = 12 massless + 12 top [M revision/mb0_all.log]. The control model with massive c, b and t is used only for O7.

  • uu~→dd~g in FC; uu~→uu~ and uu~→uu~g for fermion signs.

  • QCD corrections in loop_sm, model R2 and UV, all three Laurent coefficients, double and arbitrary precision.

Path through the new engine. No FeynKit diagram generation is used in this path; FeynKit appears only in oracle tests.

  1. Model and kernels (WP1.1): prepare_loop_request_model, then the loop kernel catalogue (gluon, ghost, light and massive quark loop lines; QCD CT site kernels; transverse and full variants).

  2. Trees (WP1.2): all needed blocks (loop-aware reachability) and the Born per (basis element, helicity), from GenericDAGCompiler in loop-request mode.

  3. Families and schedules (WP1.3): loop-prefix recursion, certified-scaleless drop, families, B tries, F graph, M states (LC).

  4. Colour (WP1.4): generic seed classes, exact K; FC; LC for gg→gg with QCDR2Continuation.

  5. Dressing (WP1.5): Python reference executor, F, B and M, exact and f64.

  6. Reduction (WP1.6): NinjaRS v2 adapter, fast engine in f64 and generic engine in AP, cached masters, re-test.

  7. Counterterms and fields (WP1.7): site closure, then UV_local, R2 and fields.

  8. Assembly (WP1.8): fermion signs, six components, 19 totals, IR-pole check, per-family error estimate.

Appendix A. Literature basis and alternatives considered¶

The user asked for a literature pass to make sure the structure is promising. The sibling reports read the primary sources ([L-s] below). For this document I re-checked, in source:

  • van Hameren’s complexity statement;

  • the OpenLoops 2 pole and performance statements;

  • NJet’s timing and de-symmetrisation tables;

  • Ninja’s accuracy caveat;

  • BDK’s colour sum.

I also searched for 2023–2026 developments [L*] and measured the providers on this host in both modes [V]. No newer program contradicts the structure:

  • GoSam-3.0 (arXiv:2507.23549) is about effective field theories and speed;

  • arXiv:2502.07060 is a GPU tree-level Berends–Giele code;

  • there is still no production SIMD/GPU one-loop code.

Structure

Evidence

Verdict

Born-seeded open loops with on-the-fly helicity sums and merging (OpenLoops 2)

Merging ≈2×, plus a further 2–3× from the on-the-fly treatment. Parent–child recycling is lost because the seed carries whole-diagram colour [L 1710.11452 l.1405-1411]. A-posteriori reduction is faster than OFR depending on the process [L l.3836-3846]. Defaults return I-operator poles “for performance reasons”; actual poles need multiple evaluations [L 1907.13071 OL2.tex:4881-4885, 6455-6457]. gg→tt̄gg 0.60 s on an i7-4790K [L tab:perfnew]; 0.49 s production on this host [V]

Adopted as schedule B, over BG blocks instead of diagrams; OFR rejected

Recursive loop currents keyed by propagator history (Recola)

(ho, hm) keys, canonical cut rules, colour flows [L-s 1211.6316 §2.2; recola2 source]. Generation on this host: 8–63 s for the 7-leg V+jets and tt̄ processes, 2,035 s (gg→gggg), 10,220 s (uu~→ggggg) [V]. Tensor integrals are 2.4–29 % of its time [M]. Production mode is 3.1–5.9× faster than the IR-pole protocol in steady state [V]

Adopted for generation keys and schedule F; its amplitude-level economics only through the transposed reduction

Born-weighted per-topology numerators into Ninja (MadLoop5)

Coefficients 36 s/helicity vs Ninja 0.78 s at gg→tt̄ggg [L 1604.01363 App. B]. Ninja tensor layout identical to NinjaRS [V ninjars:fast/tensor.rs:1-6]. Loop groups: 1,168 published for gg→tt̄gg; MG5 3.7.0 exports here have 1.6–3.9× our family counts [V]

Interface and checks adopted; per-diagram structure rejected

Grouped or cut-dependent numerators (GoSam, Samurai, Ninja)

Cut-dependent integrands are legal [L-s 1006.0710, 1403.1229 §3.1]. Ninja’s master cache [L-s 1403.1229 §3.3]. GoSam reduces pinched diagrams with their parent at almost no extra cost [L 1111.2034 diagen.tex:100-130]. Ninja’s internal tests are not an accuracy estimate; use scaling or rotation tests [L 1403.1229 main.tex:1642-1651]

Master cache and per-family re-test adopted; grouping only as gated stage 2

Tensor recursion per primitive and helicity (van Hameren)

O(n⁴2ⁿ) per ordered amplitude and helicity, competitive with unitarity up to n = 10 [L 0905.1005 introduction.tex:56-99, results.tex:142]

On-the-fly helicity summation removes the extra 2ⁿ from explicit helicity sums

Unitarity over BG trees (NGluon, NJet)

n⁶ observed, n⁸ asymptotic [L-s 1011.2900]. FC 7 gluons 171 s, 2u5g 195 s for two evaluations including the scaling test; 1.37 % / 8.63 % quadruple precision at 6 / 7 gluons [L 1209.0100 njet.tex:1161-1227]. De-symmetrised (integrated-equivalent) FC: 7 gluons 3.07 s [L tab:timedsymgluons]

Independent cross-check; per-point scaling-test practice adopted as the per-family re-test; de-symmetrised FC as a labelled opt-in

HELAC-1Loop

Loop as (n+2)-point tree; R2 as one-insertion trees [L-s 0903.4665 l.790]; colour and helicity sampling

Counterterms as trees and the (n+2)-point sign convention adopted; sampling rejected (exact per point)

Colour decompositions

DDM ring, BDK primitives and NLO colour sum, Ita–Ozeren, Reuschle–Weinzierl, Kälin [L/L-s hep-ph/9910563, hep-ph/9409393 l.1748-1772, 1111.4193, 1310.0413, 1712.03539, 1908.02695]

Seed compressions, the LC face rule, the O14 test

Leading colour in production (BlackHat, NJet)

LC ≈ 10 % off for Wbb̄ [L-s 1712.05721]; subleading sampled separately [L-s 1312.7140]

Exact LC/NLC by degree; LC and FC−LC as opt-in outputs

Forward-limit / Q-cut sewing of (n+2)-point trees

Integrands with linear propagators or loop-momentum relabellings [L* 1509.02169, 1512.02860, 2301.08043]

Rejected: not a fixed-denominator polynomial per family without a canonical cut; with one, it reduces to the Recola construction used here

Colour-dressed unitarity; numerical loop integration; loop-tree duality

Colour sampling, own reduction or no master integrals [L-s 0911.1962, 1111.1733]

Rejected

GPU / SIMD virtuals

No production one-loop SIMD or GPU evaluation; virtuals become the bottleneck after GPU trees [L-s 2303.18244, 2609.23500]; LoopFest 2024 Kokkos tree and one-loop abstract without details [L*]; GPU tree-level BG [L* 2502.07060]

Data-independent lockstep lanes are a distinguishing lever (≥ 16 lanes, §5.4)

Collier cache

Pinched sub-integrals and tensor sub-reductions computed once per event by call position [L-s 1604.06792 §4]

Scalar-master cache only; tensor-reduction sharing has no integrand-reduction analogue except stage 2

  • Binaries, points, settings. These are the campaign’s (workspace/reference/runs/required/<process>/):

    • the OpenLoops driver in openloops-run/ (OpenLoops 2.1.5, loop libraries from the public repository, loop_optimisation -O0 as in the OpenLoops default configuration);

    • a scratch copy of the Recola driver that adds one irpoles command, built against the same Recola 2.3.0 tree (self-reports 2.2.5) with COLLIER 1.2.8 (revision/recola_driver_modes.f90).

  • Modes.

    • OpenLoops protocol: truepoles 1, which sets coli_cache_use = 0 and polecheck_is = 1 (init_ui.F90:455-463) and forces full re-evaluation in the stability rescaling (stability.F90:479-483). OpenLoops production: truepoles 0.

    • Recola protocol: compute_ir_poles = 1, which makes three compute_amplitude calls per point (process_computation_rcl.f90:152-190), with the campaign’s cache setting. Recola production: compute_ir_poles = 0, cache on. A third mode, no poles and no cache, separates the two effects:

      Process

      No poles, cache on

      No poles, no cache

      Poles (protocol)

      uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g

      0.035 s

      0.061 s

      0.186 s

      uu~→e⁻e⁺ggg

      0.25 s

      0.32–0.36 s

      1.02 s

  • Timing. Single pinned idle core of this host; the driver’s own timer; point 1 evaluated untimed for initialisation, then points 2, 3, 1. Recola’s cached production rows are quoted from the second timed point on.

  • Equality checks. Finite parts: OpenLoops production = protocol bitwise on all points. Recola cached = uncached to ≤ 1×10⁻¹².

  • Ratios, protocol / production.

    • OpenLoops: 2.85–3.03 on all six processes measured.

    • Recola: 3.1–5.9 in steady state; 2.2–5.9 including the first timed point, which pays the cache set-up.

Review resolution¶

Two adversarial reviews of revision 1 were received: literature (L1–L9) and NinjaRS implementation (N1–N11). Both judged the design “sound with fixes” with no fatal issue. Every issue is resolved below; disagreements are marked Rebuttal, with evidence.

Literature review¶

#

Severity

Issue

Resolution

Where

L1

Major

Provider timings were protocol-mode (OpenLoops truepoles 1, Recola compute_ir_poles 1, partly uncached), so margins were inflated ≈2.5–5×

Re-measured production mode on this host for six processes (OpenLoops) and five (Recola), with the campaign’s binaries and points [V]. OpenLoops production is 2.85–3.03× faster than protocol, e.g. gg→gggg 2.92–2.96 s (reviewer’s estimate: ≈3–4 s). Recola production is 3.1–5.9× faster in steady state, e.g. uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g 35 ms (reviewer: 41 ms from the harness). Table 1b gives production and protocol columns. Gates use 1.3 × best production. “20–50× / 100–250×” removed. The V+jets processes are treated as speed-critical (G1 includes uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g and uu~→e⁻e⁺ggg). The baseline choice is decision 7. MadLoop production builds were also re-timed during this revision (lower values quoted).

§1.3, §1.5, §1.6 (7), §5.4, §14 (G1, R3), §15 (1, 15), App. C

L2

Major

Absolute cost model unvalidated; inconsistent range arithmetic; 1–2 G complex MAC/s assumed

One recipe for every row, applied in a script. Both ends now come from the same schedule-B model (structured vs dense kernel constants, 1.7–1.8× apart) instead of B-in-one-model / M-in-another. Rust kernel probe: 1.3–1.8 G complex MAC/s per core at 16 lanes for the split, fused and register-blocked forms; 0.4–0.9 G at 8 lanes. Gate G0 (new WP0.3) measures the kernels on real trie shapes in wave 0/1, before WP2.1. V+jets in G1. All v2 times labelled targets. Recomputed ranges confirm the reviewer’s arithmetic: with re-test, mb = 0, gg→gggg 0.17–0.47 s, gg→ggggg 3.4–9.0 s, uu~→ggggg 1.0–3.0 s; with a massive b, 0.25–0.64 / 4.8–12.4 / 1.1–3.2 s. Even at the upper ends every measured row passes its gate; the thinnest is uu~→e⁻e⁺dd~g at 1.7× against Recola production.

§1.3, §5.4, §14 (G0, G1), §16 (WP0.3, WP2.7)

L3

Major

Default accuracy checks weaker than published practice

Per-family re-test of every family of every point is the default: relabelling plus loop-momentum shift with cached masters (MadLoop practice, NinjaRS guidance (b)); exact rescaling variant (NJet’s scaling test per family). Costed in Table 1a (+0.75–1.0 NinjaRS pass, +12–25 % per point). Error-budget escalation per family. Relaxation only after O15: false-negative rates against Float(256) on ≥ 10⁴ points per required process (WP2.3). The IR-pole check is kept as an additional signal, explicitly not sufficient.

§10.2, §10.4, §14 (O15), WP2.3

L4

Major

gg→tt̄e⁻e⁺g (QCD and EW) not quantified

QCD counted with the generic enumerator: 579 families (629 with a massive b), 3,990 skeletons, 2,840 trie nodes, 9 buckets, hexagons at most, NinjaRS 10–14 ms, target 0.035–0.092 s against OpenLoops production 0.43 s and MadLoop 3.0 s. EW estimated [I]: ≈1,450 families (MadLoop’s EW/QCD loop-group ratio 2.5), heptagons through the lepton line, target 0.07–0.32 s against best production 0.95–1.0 s. Replaced by exact counts at the new gate E0 before any EW timing work, with an EW proliferation risk (15 #14). Provider EW/QCD ratios on this host: OpenLoops 2.2–2.6, Recola 1.4–1.7, MadLoop 2.3.

§1.3, §11.4, §14 (E0), §15 (14), WP3.2

L5

Minor

A_{5;3} misread (claimed relative N_c⁻⁴)

Example deleted. NLC prunes only by exact computed degree. Two of the three A_{5;3} terms enter at P−2 [L hep-ph/9409393 l.1748-1772]. New O14 test against BDK’s colour sum.

§7.6, §14 (O14), WP2.4

L6

Minor

Parity halving over-claimed

Restricted to gg→gggg, gg→ggggg, uu~→ggggg and gg→tt̄gg with real masses and zero widths. Excluded for the three processes with Z couplings and for complex masses.

§1.3, §8.3, WP4.1

L7

Minor

B-over-M choice rests on one uncalibrated model; “F ≈ 30× B” mislabelled

M is implemented in the Python reference executor (WP1.5) for LC and certified classes, with exact operation counters. G1 decides B vs M per class from counts × G0 throughput. M in Rust is a planned package (WP2.8). The 30× was the Design 1 model’s F/M (29.1); corrected. M’s memory (≈85 MB/lane, ≈1.4 GB at 16 lanes) is stated as affordable, not a cap.

§1.4, §1.6 (5), §2.2, WP1.5, WP2.7, WP2.8

L8

Minor

FC headline silently assumes certified colour compression

Stated in §1.3 and §7.2 (generic seeds add 0.4–2.4 s at gg→ggggg). The DDM and trace certificates are the first items of WP2.4.

§1.3, §7.2, WP2.4

L9

Minor

Inaccurate statements

(a) OFR: its output is acceptable to NinjaRS; rejection now rests on speed, private mathematics, integrand-level validity and family growth (§11.3). (b) MadLoop gg→gggg: 285 s graph generation + 8,354 s export + 20.6 s compilation (§1.5, §4.4). (c) Recola generation: 2,035 s (gg→gggg) and 10,220 s (uu~→ggggg), not “seconds to minutes” (App. A). (d) “B matches the best recursive class” restated precisely against open-loop, tensor and unitarity classes and M (§1.4). (e) Integrated-equivalent de-symmetrised full colour added as a labelled opt-in (§7.6, WP4.7).

as listed

NinjaRS-implementation review¶

#

Severity

Issue

Resolution

Where

N1

Major

Fermion sign of a skeleton never specified

Explicit rule using the tree engine’s conventions: the skeleton is treated as an (n+2)-point tree with the cut pair ranked n+1, n+2; the tree engine’s Koszul/orientation merge_sign at each ring step; per-class pairing parity for coloured lines (color/plan_replay.py:671-701); −1 per closed fermion or ghost loop at sewing. Implemented in conventions.py by calling generation/fermion_ordering.py. Oracles O13: uu~→uu~, uu~→uu~g, ee→μμ and e⁺e⁻→e⁺e⁻ at NLO EW (lepton lines in the loop), added to O1, WP0.1, S1 and WP3.2. The Majorana limit is stated.

§3.3, §14 (O13), WP0.1, WP1.8, WP3.2

N2

Major

B’s asymptotic class overstated

§1.4 states B = Θ((n−1)!·4ⁿ): it beats open-loop and tensor recursions but is asymptotically worse than unitarity (crossover n ≈ 30–50) and M. M (Θ(n!·2ⁿ·n⁴)) is the planned asymptotic production path (WP2.8, not optional), adopted per class at G1 and by default for n ≥ 8. B stays the default for n ≤ 7 until G1. The trie’s 3.0× sharing gain over unshared dressing is acknowledged; the remaining structural gains are listed in §1.5.

§1.4, §1.5, §2.2, WP2.8

N3

Major

Master cache returns wrong tensor bubbles under mass-swap canonicalisation

Bubbles (BubbleRank2/3/4) are keyed by the ordered tuple; only C0 and D0 are canonicalised, under symmetries that leave their outputs invariant. WP1.6 acceptance adds gg→tt̄ (unequal-mass top–gluon bubbles).

§11.2, WP1.6

N4

Major (generic models)

Selection rule, counts and oracles disagree

Generation follows the §3.3 rule. Two-position rings with a quartic partner are generated; families are dropped only with a structural scaleless certificate (all masses zero, all invariants structurally zero) and logged. Verified: FeynKit gives 52 gg→gg families in the control model = 4 mass classes × 12 + 4 scaleless bubbles [V]. QCD counts are unchanged; EW/BSM massive quartic rings are kept. O2/O7 compare modulo certified zeros.

§3.3, §4.2, §14 (O2, O7), WP1.3

N5

Minor

Loop-request mode under-specified

(a) The three pruning layers (dag_compiler.py:131-133, 341-378) are replaced in loop mode by one loop-aware reachability test from the family recursion’s position table. (b) Blocks are keyed by the full CurrentIndex incl. ColorState (sector_id, line_groups, basis_key). (c) Agreed: the transverse YM replacement is exact for blocks with transverse sources and is kept there; full kernels for loop segments, CT = 1 currents and Ward/non-transverse sources. WP1.1 owns the full-kernel flag and the selection hook in compiler_entry.py.

§3.2, §3.7, WP1.1, WP1.2

N6

Minor

Slice configuration does not match references

gg→gg slice at mb = 0: 24 families. Components are compared with the single instrumented MadLoop run (and legacy), not with “providers’ mutual agreement”, which now applies only to full results.

§16.3

N7

Minor

Rescue trigger 3 not in the timings

It is now the default and is budgeted in every target (+0.75–1.0 R).

§1.3, §10.2

N8

Minor

Parity-halving claim contradicts its own condition

As L6.

§8.3

N9

Minor

Cost assumptions not stated

Stated: C-parity folding of closed quark loops (×1.75 FC dressing without it); ghost loops inside the 1.2–1.35 factor; ≥ 16 lanes; certified colour compression. “20–50×” removed. Object counts compared honestly in §1.5 (9,180 skeletons / 7,619 nodes vs 26,975 diagrams at gg→gggg). Rebuttal (partial): a separate like-for-like OpenLoops 2 operation model is not built. The speed gate is a measurement, and production-mode OpenLoops timings now exist for every OpenLoops-covered required process (Table 1b), which is a stronger baseline than another unvalidated model. The expected advantage is decomposed instead (cut choice 2.1–2.7× in the same model; blocks; seeds; reduction), and G1 measures it.

§1.3, §1.5, §7.2

N10

Minor

NinjaRS claims overstated

tensor_jets is private (fast/mod.rs:46), so (b2) needs a public jets API (request 7). The transpose study is described as a symbolic n3/r3 instruction count, a negative result at one numerator per point, thresholds “not timing predictions” (transpose-probe.md:21, 45); schedule 3 needs a measured prototype. DD/AP ingress via PolynomialNumerator from a Symbolica expression (polynomial.rs:258, compile cost measured in WP2.3); upstreaming TensorGenericNumerator<T> (harness.rs:1290) is request 8.

§2.4 (18), §7.7, §10.1, §11.3, §11.5

N11

Minor

Wording and genericity

Collier’s cache shares tensor sub-reductions; the master cache only scalar masters (§2.3, §11.3, App. A). OFR reason fixed (§11.3). M memory: ≈85 MB = 65 MB accumulators + ≈20 MB chunked states (§2.2, §5.3). CT arity m ∈ {2, …, k_max}, witness attachments ≤ k_max, and divergent witnesses from R_f ≥ 2N − 4 derived from the model; effective theories refused without declared completeness (§6.2, §6.3, §6.6). Complex-mass master defects added as risk 13. Majorana limit stated (§3.3).

as listed

Further corrections made while resolving the reviews (not raised by either reviewer):

  • NinjaRS stage for gg→tt̄gg. The histogram model gives 19–27 ms (massless b), not revision 1’s “≈50 ms [I]”.

  • LC/FC ratio in the providers’ configuration. It is 0.37–0.42 for the gluon processes, not 0.27–0.30, which holds only with a massive b. Both are now stated.

  • MadLoop loop groups. The literature reviewer’s check “families equal MadLoop’s loop groups” holds against the published MadLoop 5 table (1,168 vs 1,164). The MG5 3.7.0 exports on this host carry 1.6–3.9× more groups than our canonical families (§11.4).

  • Shared build directory. env.sh points CARGO_TARGET_DIR at the shared workspace/builds/cargo. A first kbench build landed there and was removed (only the kbench* files this revision created); the reproduction recipe now sets the target directory inside the scratch tree.
